The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--Rödl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure $σ_s$ which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass $(s-2)/(2s-2)$. A Gaussian tail argument proves both sharpness of the recurrence exponent and the fact that this atom is the largest possible for any $s$-nice recurrent set. The result sharpens the recurrence separations of Bourgain and Mountakis, answers a question of Mountakis about the maximal mass of an atom at zero, and answers a question of Forrest about separating the various degrees of nice recurrence. In the appendix we give a self-contained proof of the Density Frankl-Rödl theorem.

papers.title: Kleinian groups generated by two elliptics of even order
papers.abstract: Let $Γ<\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ be a non-elementary discrete group generated by two elliptics of even order, with a nontrivial relation in the corresponding free product of cyclic groups. We classify the possible compact orbifold cores of $\mathbb H^3/Γ$, together with their cusp data and marked meridians. They are finite meridional fillings of the two-bridge link and Heckoid models of Akiyoshi--Ohshika--Parker--Sakuma--Yoshida. Their weighted graphs have at most two standard tunnels, whose weights in the two-tunnel case are $2$ and an odd integer. The original generators are powers of primitive meridians which generate $Γ$, and we determine the possible meridian placements for all even orders. The groups are geometrically finite, their conformal boundary components are turnovers, and each oriented core with its cusp data determines its complete hyperbolic holonomy up to Möbius conjugacy. The proof uses trace rigidity, dihedral surgery, half-turn symmetries, and an index-two cover.

papers.title: On the Planar Optimal Transport Problem
papers.abstract: We develop a complex analytic framework based on rotation of gradient graphs for the study of quadratic cost planar optimal transport with uniform densities. Using this framework we carry out the construction, characterization, and approximation of non-degenerate optimal transport maps up to the boundary. We also identify obstructions for continuous optimal transport and construct discontinuous optimal transport maps with prescribed analytic singular sets.

papers.title: An Elasticity Complex for Kirchhoff--Love Shells
papers.abstract: We develop an elasticity complex for Kirchhoff--Love shell theory, based on the linearized Gauss--Codazzi equations as compatibility conditions for shell strains. The resulting shell complex forms a fine resolution of the sheaf of infinitesimal rigid motions, so its cohomology groups are determined by the corresponding sheaf cohomology. Remarkably, the complex also reveals an Airy potential representation of equilibrium stress fields. The framework further identifies natural boundary conditions for both kinematic and dynamic variables. Finally, we establish a Hodge--Morrey--Friedrichs decomposition for strain and stress fields on shells with boundary.

papers.title: On the tensor product of semistable Hermitian adelic vector bundles over an adelic curve
papers.abstract: We prove tensor semistability for Hermitian adelic vector bundles on proper adelic curves whose underlying fields are countable and of characteristic zero. The central estimate concerns the canonical integral Specht lattice of a rectangular partition with fixed height: its logarithmic covolume, divided by its rank and tensor degree, tends to zero. We prove this estimate from monic seminormal norms and an exact hypergeometric law weighted by the square of a Vandermonde product for tableau prefixes. Constant adelic Specht bundles and equivariant contractions then yield the slope inequality for every geometrically semistable subspace of a finite tensor product. The correction is the measure of the Archimedean places times a sublinear Specht term and vanishes in the limit as the auxiliary degree tends to infinity. An instability-filtration argument completes the reduction to arbitrary factors and identifies the tensor product Harder--Narasimhan filtration. The number field specialization gives the Bost tensor semistability conjecture in all ranks.

papers.title: Totally odd clique immersions in graphs with bounded independence number
papers.abstract: We prove that every $n$-vertex graph with at least one edge and independence number at most an integer $a\ge2$, where $n\ge a$, contains a totally odd strong immersion of \[ K_{\left\lceil (n+a-1)/(2a-3/2) \right\rceil}, \] with every branch path of length at most $2a-1$. We also prove that every graph $G$ with independence number at most $a$ and no totally odd strong $K_t$-immersion with branch paths of length at most $2a-1$ satisfies \[ χ(G)\le\left\lfloor \frac{(2a-3/2)(t-1)-a+2}{2} \right\rfloor \] where $t\ge2$. These bounds reduce the leading denominator coefficient in the general order bound from $9/4$ to $2$ and the colouring coefficient for independence number two from $3/2$ to $5/4$.

papers.title: Limit distributions and bootstrap for smooth adapted Wasserstein distances
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide limit theorems for the Gaussian-smoothed adapted Wasserstein distances. Let $\widehatμ_n$ be the empirical measure of independent paths with law $μ$ on $(\mathbb{R}^d)^T$. Let $P = μ* γ_σ$ and $P_n = \widehatμ_n * γ_σ$, where $γ_σ= N(0,σ^2 I_{dT})$ is a Gaussian measure with mean zero and covariance matrix $σ^2 I_{dT}$. We first assume that $μ$ is compactly supported. For every $1 < p < \infty$ and fixed $d, T$, and $σ> 0$, we show that $\sqrt{n}\,\mathrm{AW}_p(P_n,P) \Rightarrow Q_{P,p}(G)^{1/p}$, where $G$ is the Gaussian limit of the density fluctuation and $Q_{P,p}$ is the minimum adapted $p$-energy for the linearized continuity equation. We prove full-path bootstrap consistency and the convergence of the first and $p$-th moments. The limit and the bootstrap hold for noncompact laws as well, for all $1 < p < \infty$ under appropriate tail and structural conditions. For two-sided bounded density perturbations of strongly log-concave laws, the bandwidth is not restricted for $1 < p \le 2$. For $p > 2$, we give sufficient tail conditions and provide a Gaussian counterexample where root-$n$ tightness fails for small bandwidths. Our proof is based on a two-endpoint local expansion of bicausal transport. As an application, we provide asymptotic error bounds for optimal stopping values under the smoothed model using the bootstrap quantiles.

papers.title: Spaces of ratios of schemes and étale cohomology
papers.abstract: We introduce the arithmetic topologies on the spaces of ratios for log schemes and prove the basic properties of their cohomologies.

papers.title: Optimal User-Level Private Stochastic Convex Optimization and Mean Estimation with Heavy Tails
papers.abstract: We study stochastic convex optimization with heavy-tailed stochastic gradients under $(\varepsilon, δ)$-user-level differential privacy, which protects each user's entire collection of samples. Instead of assuming a uniformly bounded Lipschitz constant, we only assume bounds on the second- and $k$-th moments of the random sample Lipschitz parameters. This allows for unbounded, heavy-tailed stochastic gradient distributions and can lead to sharper excess risk bounds. We characterize the minimax optimal excess population risk up to logarithmic factors. Our algorithm achieves the optimal rate with only $\widetilde{O}(1/\varepsilon)$ users. As a byproduct of our algorithmic developments, we obtain tight bounds for user-level private mean estimation under norm-moment assumptions, improving over the guarantees of Esfandiari et al. (2022) and Zhao et al. (2024). Finally, for mean estimation under the directional-moment assumption of Agarwal et al. (2025), we close their remaining approximate-DP gap by removing the additional $d/\varepsilon$ user requirement and attaining the optimal sample complexity up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Lattices of Minimal Covolume in $\mathrm{SL}_2$ over Dyadic Local Fields
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the minimal covolume among lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ for each finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_2$. Using the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ on its Bruhat--Tits tree, we investigate the shape of the fixed subtrees of finite subgroups, particularly cyclic and dicyclic subgroups of $2$-power order. We determine which larger vertex stabilizers can occur at boundary vertices of the fixed subtrees of dicyclic subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $2.A_4$. We use these results to construct graphs of groups defining lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ and prove that these lattices attain the minimal covolume. This extends a result of Lubotzky and Weigel, which treats finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for odd primes $p$.

papers.title: On p-Group Actions and Index Divisibilities
papers.abstract: We prove a mod-$ p $ divisibility result for indices of elliptic operators assuming a smooth action by a finite $ p $-group on the base manifold of dimension $ n\le 2(p-1) $ with no stationary points and which lifts equivariantly to the operator bundles. We show as one consequence that if such manifolds are spin or stably almost complex, with the group action lifting to the relevant structure, then their class in the relevant bordism theory modulo $ p $ is fully determined by one genus, and indeed vanishes for $ n<2(p-1) $. We show as another consequence that there exists no closed connected $ 24 $-dimensional spin manifold $ M $ satisfying $ {\hat{A}(M)=1}, {\hat{A}(M;T_\mathbb{C}M)=0} $, and for which there exists a smooth non-trivial action by the monster group, resolving a question of Hirzebruch.

papers.title: Uniform counting of quadratic fields with local conditions
papers.abstract: We sharpen the uniform counting estimates of Bhargava, Thorne, and the author for quadratic fields with prescribed local conditions. Combining the Burgess and Pólya--Vinogradov bounds, we improve the dependence of the error term on the primes supporting the local conditions and make explicit the factors previously absorbed into an arbitrary $ε$-power of their product. The resulting estimate has an absolute implied constant.

papers.title: Retracts of well-filtered co-sober spaces are co-sober
papers.abstract: Xu and Zhao asked whether co-sobriety is inherited by the image of a continuous kernel operator, and more generally whether it is inherited by retracts. Both questions have recently been answered in the negative by Xu, Xu, Ji and Qiu. We prove that both questions have positive answers whenever the ambient space is, in addition, well-filtered; in particular they hold for every sober co-sober space. It follows that the ambient space of any counterexample to either question, such as that of Xu, Xu, Ji and Qiu, must be co-sober and not well-filtered. We give an example of a kernel-operator image that is not a direct instance of the inheritance results of Wen and Xu, and we identify the step of the argument that uses well-filteredness.

papers.title: A Generalized Framework for Structured Low-Rank Approximation and Completion
papers.abstract: We formulate a generalized version of SLRA, consisting of general affine constraints, which subsumes the problems of structured low-rank matrix approximation and completion as special cases. We characterize its critical points and propose an algorithm to approximately solve the general problem. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithm for stock-price forecasting, computing approximate gcd of polynomials with noisy coefficients, and time-series denoising.

papers.title: Sub-Riemannian flow matching
papers.abstract: We study sub-Riemannian conditional flow matching (SRCFM) for generative transport with prescribed velocity constraints. Training uses paths between sampled source and target points whose velocities lie in the allowed horizontal directions at each state. A neural network takes time and the full state as input and predicts the coefficients of these directions, and the horizontal frame then determines the full velocity used for generation. We describe constructions based on Heisenberg geodesics and joint endpoint equations in free step-two Carnot groups. We propose a scalable piecewise algorithm that computes horizontal paths directly from their endpoints. A straight segment sets the horizontal coordinates, and a loop in those coordinates corrects the remaining vertical displacement. We verify the algorithm's endpoint accuracy to numerical precision in high-dimensional tests. Synthetic experiments illustrate approximate distribution transport along horizontal trajectories. On resized MNIST, we use the same construction to generate images from Gaussian inputs with fewer controls than pixels.

papers.title: A Unified Bregman Projection Framework for Solving Multi-Split Multiple-Set Implicit Convex Feasibility Problems
papers.abstract: We study the multi-split multiple-set implicit convex feasibility problem (MSMS-ICFP), in which the constraint sets are generated by point-to-set operators and the feasibility conditions are imposed both in the original space and in several image spaces connected by bounded linear operators. We analyze the generalized proximity function, built from weighted Bregman distances and Bregman projections, introduced by Censor and Dey. For translation-type point-to-set operators, we establish the continuity and Lipschitz continuity of the corresponding Bregman projections, the continuous differentiability of the proximity function with an explicit formula for its gradient, and global and local Lipschitz estimates for this gradient. We then propose a generalized simultaneous projection gradient algorithm. In the nonconvex case, the gradient norms of the iterates converge to zero and every accumulation point is stationary. When the proximity function is convex and the solution set is nonempty, the iterates converge in norm to a solution, with an $O(1/k)$ rate for the proximity values, an $O(1/\sqrt{k})$ rate for the gradient norms, and a linear rate under a quadratic growth condition. Cyclic and block-iterative variants are also analyzed. Numerical experiments, including a cooperative sensor network localization problem, illustrate the theory and show that, in contrast with frozen-set implicit projection methods, the proposed gradient schemes remain convergent when the translation operators are expansive.

papers.title: A constructive inverse for the Jordan--von Neumann operator on abelian groups
papers.abstract: For an abelian group $G$ and a real Banach space $X$, we study the inhomogeneous Jordan--von Neumann equation $\mathsf{Q}[f] = g$, where $\mathsf{Q}$ is the quadratic difference operator of the parallelogram law. We characterize the functions $g$ in the image of $\mathsf{Q}$ and, under a summability hypothesis, recover a solution explicitly by an iteration on the diagonal followed by a propagation argument; neither regularity of $g$ nor divisibility of $G$ is required. As a consequence we obtain a sharp stability estimate of Forti--Găvruţa type for the quadratic functional equation.

papers.title: Minimal norm of regular vectors in the root lattice of a crystallographic root system
papers.abstract: For a crystallographic root system $Φ$ with Weyl group $W$ and root lattice $L = \mathbb{Z}Φ$, we determine the minimum norm of a vector of $L$ having trivial stabilizer in $W$, and we prove that the vectors attaining it form a single orbit of $W$. Although this is a minimization of a quadratic function over the lattice points of a cone, the minimizer in the dominant chamber is always unique: it is $ρ+ λ$, where $ρ$ is the Weyl vector and $λ$ is $0$ or the minuscule weight in the class of $ρ$ modulo $L$. In particular, the optimal vector is the Weyl vector exactly when the Weyl vector lies in $L$. We give explicit formulas for the families $A_n$, $B_n$, $C_n$ and $D_n$, with elementary proofs, and the values for the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$. Finally, we explain the coincidences between the minimal norms by the folding of Dynkin diagrams.

papers.title: A Cubic Obstruction to Sums of Tripotent and Square-Zero Matrices
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring of characteristic $2$, and let $λ$ be a central unit of $R$. We prove that an element $a\in R$ satisfying $a^3+a^2+λ=0$ cannot be expressed as the sum of a tripotent element and a square-zero element. The proof does not require the summands to commute. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$, this gives counterexamples in every order divisible by three, including order twelve, and proves the optimality of the known uniform exponent four in those orders. We also give constructive proofs that every matrix of order four or five over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is a sum of a tripotent and a square-zero matrix, and deduce a complete criterion in order three. Combining the cubic obstruction with the quartic obstruction for idempotent-plus-cube-zero decompositions, we obtain two-way incomparability of the corresponding decomposition classes in every positive order divisible by twelve.

papers.title: Unboundedness of regular del Pezzo surfaces over imperfect fields
papers.abstract: Over an F-finite field, regular del Pezzo surfaces are bounded. Over a non-F-finite field of characteristic two or three, regular del Pezzo surfaces are unbounded.

papers.title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
papers.abstract: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in\ZZ_{\ge0}$ as $λ$-lengths of essential simple ideal arcs based at a distinguished cusp of a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.

papers.title: Synchronized Normalized Solutions for a Critical Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg System
papers.abstract: We study positive synchronized normalized solutions to the critical Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg system: \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{aligned} -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u) &=λ_1|x|^{-2a}u+β_1|x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u\\ &\quad+|x|^{-bp}\left(μ_1|u|^{p-2}u+να|u|^{α-2}u|v|^γ\right),\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N,\\ -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla v) &=λ_2|x|^{-2a}v+β_2|x|^{-bq}|v|^{q-2}v\\ &\quad+|x|^{-bp}\left(μ_2|v|^{p-2}v+νγ|u|^α|v|^{γ-2}v\right),\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N, \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation*} subject to the prescribed weighted masses \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx=ρ_1^2,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}v^2\,dx=ρ_2^2, \end{equation*} where $N\geq5$, $0\leq a<\frac{N-4}{2}$, $a<b<a+1$, $α,γ>1$, $α+γ=p=\frac{2N}{N-2(1+a-b)}$, $2<q<p$, $β_i,μ_i,ρ_i>0$ for $i=1,2$, and $ν>0$. The associated Lagrange multipliers $λ_1,λ_2\in\mathbb R$ are unknown. Under suitable algebraic compatibility conditions, we establish existence and multiplicity results for positive synchronized normalized solutions. The construction is based on synchronized reduction and critical energy estimates involving a finite-mass Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg extremal. In the mass-subcritical regime, we find two positive solutions with opposite energies when $β=β_1ρ_1^{q-2}=β_2ρ_2^{q-2}$ is sufficiently small. In the mass-critical and mass-supercritical regimes, we obtain a synchronized Pohozaev ground state below the critical energy threshold for sufficiently small $β$ and for all $β>0$, respectively. All these solutions satisfy $λ_1=λ_2<0$.

papers.title: A tight upper bound on non-overlapping codes
papers.abstract: Non-overlapping codes (also known as cross bifix-free codes or strong comma-free codes) have now been studied for over 60 years as part of information theory, with regular new applications appearing and much recent interest. Let $X$ be a $q$-ary non-overlapping code of length $n$. The paper contains a self-contained proof that \[ |X|\leq \left(\frac{q-1}{qe} +O(n^{-1/4})\right)\frac{q^n}{n} \] as $n\rightarrow\infty$ with $q$ fixed, where $e$ is the base of the natural logarithm. The constant $(q-1)/(qe)$ improves, by a factor of $(q-1)/q$, the best previously known bound due to Levenshtein (1970). Indeed, constructions of large non-overlapping codes show that this constant is best possible. The paper builds on work by Fimmel, Michel, Pirot, Sereni and Strüngmann (2019), and by Stanovnik, Mo\v skon and Mraz (2024).

papers.title: Exactly Proper Forcing
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of exact properness, a strong form of properness for uncountable models, and prove iteration theorems and the consistency of forcing axioms for this class. We discuss examples of posets in the class and give some applications of the forcing axioms.

papers.title: What Can Postselection on Halting Decide?
papers.abstract: A probabilistic program can produce an answer on some runs and continue forever on others. Suppose it halts with positive probability on every input and we count only the runs that halt. Aaronson et al. showed that if the correct answer must be more than twice as likely as the wrong one, such programs decide exactly the problems solvable with a finite list of halting questions chosen in advance. They asked what happens when the correct answer need only be more likely than the wrong one. We prove that the resulting class is exactly $\boldsymbol{Δ^0_2}$: the halting questions can now be asked one at a time, with each answer helping to determine the next question. This remains true if the program must halt with probability at least 99%, or with any other prescribed rational lower bound below one. Our main technical result is the exact query bound when the program gives two guarantees. Suppose it halts with probability at least $ρ$ and, among the runs that halt, the correct answer has probability at least $a$. For rational $0 < ρ< 1$ and $1/2 < a < 1$, these programs decide exactly the problems solvable with at most $n$ halting questions chosen in advance, where $n$ is the largest integer satisfying $ρ(a/(1-a))^n \le 1$. Every value of $n$ occurs, and different values give different classes. The proof measures how much additional halting probability a change of answer requires, and counts these changes as in Ershov's hierarchy. The results extend to quantum machines with computable gates.

papers.title: On the Cauchy problem for $σ$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $σ$-evolution equation $$ u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-Δ)^σu+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(τ)/b(τ) dτ$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(τ)/b(τ)dτ\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.

papers.title: Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
papers.abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining ordinary spectral flow on fixed-point spaces with minimal-overgroup nullities, we obtain a lower bound on the number of exact-stabilizer bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and requires endpoint invertibility only on the chosen fixed space, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings. When the restricted Hessians have finite Morse index, the criterion involves only indices and nullities. We also treat varying form domains under explicit transport assumptions and regular matrix Sturm--Liouville systems. As our principal application, we consider a Newtonian nine-body family consisting of two interlaced squares with fixed satellite masses and a varying central mass. We prove analytically that central configurations with two nonconjugate exact reflection stabilizers bifurcate at a common mass in $(142,150)$, displacing the central body from the centre of mass. The family contains a reported counterexample to Moeckel's linear-stability conjecture; our bifurcation proof is independent of that stability assertion.

papers.title: Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices
papers.abstract: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice $L$ equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra $V_L$, generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.

papers.title: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
papers.abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.

papers.title: Splitting and Alternating Minimization Methods for Training Orthogonal Deep Feedforward Networks
papers.abstract: Training deep feedforward networks with weight matrices constrained to layer-wise Stiefel manifolds serves as an effective regularization technique to improve generalization. However, the simultaneous presence of orthogonality constraints and nonsmooth activation functions poses severe theoretical and computational challenges for standard stochastic gradient and Riemannian optimization methods. In this paper, we propose two splitting and alternating-based algorithms to train orthogonal deep feedforward networks (OrthDFNs). By introducing auxiliary variables, we decouple the nested nonsmooth compositions and manifold constraints into a structured equality-constrained optimization problem. To solve this model, we develop OrthALM, an inexact augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) that employs a proximal alternating minimization scheme to solve its subproblems. Crucially, every block coordinate subproblem admits an exact, closed-form solution. We establish a rigorous convergence theory for OrthALM, proving that every accumulation point of the generated sequence is a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) point of the regularized, reformulated problem. Furthermore, we introduce OrthADMM as a practical, proximal-free variant that executes a single inner alternating sweep per multiplier update to accelerate computation. Extensive numerical experiments show that OrthALM attains lower training error and constraint residuals than OrthADMM in most configurations. OrthADMM achieves competitive test accuracy and the lowest reported runtime in most comparisons with the selected baselines.

papers.title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
papers.abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov, the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.

papers.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
papers.abstract: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval, and outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$. Near this threshold $a_*$ the distance between the two modes is of order $(a-a_*)^{1/2}$, and the width of the interval is of order $(a-a_*)^{3/2}$. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one. The proof bounds the sign changes of the first and second differences of the finite walk, including those created at the boundary, and passes them to the limit.

papers.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
papers.abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-δ_k+o(1)})$ where $δ_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.

papers.title: Species sampling priors through exact augmentation
papers.abstract: Discrete random probability measures are central to Bayesian nonparametric modeling. In practice, their use often favors a few tractable priors with full weak support. Full support alone, however, does not specify how prior mass reflects beliefs about clustering, recurrence, discovery and other sample features. We develop a novel and general construction of species sampling process (SSP) priors from an index distribution and finite allocation probabilities, linked to these sample characteristics. Every proper SSP admits an exact two-stage representation through an almost surely finite index and a finite conditional measure. Averaging over the index recovers each realized SSP on every measurable set. Reversing this identity constructs priors whose tie probabilities, expected occupancy and discovery rates can be assessed without evaluating the infinite weights. We characterize compatibility among index laws, schedules and weights, and construct light-tailed, heavy-tailed and multimodal families with full weak support under suitable hyperpriors. A prior with paired weights combines full weak support with invariance under size-biased permutation in its defining order, an explicit finite index law and partition prediction. Exact simulation, recursive reweighting and finite posterior augmentation follow. Examples distinguish prior elicitation, exact averaging and fixed-level approximation.

papers.title: An Elementary Proof of the Binary Goldbach Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].

papers.title: Fourier inequalities and sign uncertainty II
papers.abstract: Building on our earlier work, we present an $L^2$-$L^1$ inequality for radial Fourier eigenfunctions, relating this to the sign uncertainty principle of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane. We also propose a generalisation of the aforementioned uncertainty principle, and draw a connection with entropic uncertainty.

papers.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
papers.abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $Λ$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $Λ$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.

papers.title: Separately continuous maps into regular spaces and continuity of operations in separable semitopological groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every regular separable feebly compact semitopological group is a topological group. This answers a question of M. Tkachenko (2014) and extends the separable case of the author's 1994 theorem on Tychonoff pseudocompact groups to regular spaces. The proof rests on a new result: if $X$ is a separable Baire space, $Y$ is feebly compact and $Z$ is regular, then every separately continuous map $X\times Y\to Z$ is strongly quasicontinuous. Previously this was known only when $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are Tychonoff. Using topological games of Banach-Mazur type, we extend the group theorem to regular separable Baire groups from a wider class of spaces, which contains all $p$-spaces, all feebly compact spaces and all products of a $p$-space with a feebly compact space. We also obtain local versions: the theorem holds for locally separable, locally feebly compact groups.

papers.title: Separating the Polar of Sets of Uniqueness from the Polars of All $H^{(d)}$-Sets
papers.abstract: We construct a perfect set of uniqueness on the circle carrying a continuous probability measure which annihilates every $H^{(d)}$-set, simultaneously for all finite dimensions d. This gives a strict inclusion between the polar of the compact sets of uniqueness and the polar of the union of the classes $H^{(d)}$, answering a question raised in earlier work on these polars. The construction uses random binary increments of size comparable to the reciprocal of a product of square roots. A Gaussian sampling estimate gives a uniform Fourier-tail bound for all pseudomeasures supported by the resulting set, and also bounded atomic approximation and spectral synthesis. A separate energy estimate, stable under deletion of a small number of increments, yields full support for every limiting quasi-independent image of every positive measure absolutely continuous with respect to the constructed measure.

papers.title: OC-OPD: Observation-coordinated Supervision for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Reverse and forward Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences provide complementary supervision in on-policy distillation: reverse KL refines the student's active token rankings, and forward KL allocates mass to teacher-supported candidates. At student-generated prefixes, we form a four-observation matrix by treating the student and teacher as both candidate sources and evaluators. The diagonal self-observations measure uncertainty, while source-centered cross-observations recover the two KL objectives. We establish an exact identity equating the Fisher inverse-metric coupling of their logit gradients with the sum of these contrasts, yielding a common local descent direction for distinct positive distributions. Observation-coordinated on-policy distillation (OC-OPD) uses observations to set preferences, closed-form bargaining to coordinate gradients, and distributional discrepancy to scale the update. Across three heterogeneous student settings (non-thinking generation, thinking generation, and base-model initialization), OC-OPD achieves strong gains in mathematical reasoning and transfers effectively to out-of-distribution scientific question answering and code generation. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/RuoranXu/OC-OPD.

papers.title: A comparison of parallel iterative methods for ILU triangular solves
papers.abstract: Exact triangular solves parallelise poorly, limited by the size and number of the level sets, so on GPUs the factors from incomplete LU (ILU) factorisations are often solved approximately with parallel iterative methods. We compare four such methods: a Jacobi method, an Incomplete Sparse Approximate Inverse (ISAI), GMRES polynomials, and AIRG, a reduction multigrid built on GMRES polynomials, for which we introduce a parallel coarse/fine splitting that bounds the diagonal dominance ratio of the fine-fine block. We test them with ILU(0) and ILU(1) factors of canonical PDE problems and 91 SuiteSparse/Matrix Market matrices, the latter on a single GPU. AIRG is the most robust on the PDE factors, with nearly flat iteration counts under refinement and no per-problem tuning, but has the largest setup and memory costs. GMRES polynomials are more robust than the Jacobi method at a similar cost. As the inner solve of an ILU preconditioner with tuned inner iteration counts, ISAI gives the largest median speedups over a hipSPARSE exact triangular solve (4.5$\times$ and 6.8$\times$ for ILU(0) and ILU(1)), though this was dominated by smaller problems; on the largest ILU(1) problems all four methods give similar median speedups of 2.0-2.6$\times$.

papers.title: Tiling circular $n$-boards with squares and (1,1)-fences
papers.abstract: We show that the number of ways to tile a circular $n$-board (an annulus divided into $n$ curved unit square cells) with appropriately curved unit squares and curved (1,1)-fences is a Lucas number squared if $n$ is even and an odd-indexed Lucas number otherwise. A curved (1,1)-fence is composed of two curved unit squares separated by a gap in the shape of another curved unit square. This combinatorial interpretation of the Lucas numbers squared and the odd-indexed Lucas numbers allows us to obtain various identities concerning these sequences in a quick and lucid manner.

papers.title: Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals: Absorption Probabilities and Conic Intrinsic Volumes
papers.abstract: Let $(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process in $\mathbb R^d$ whose coordinate processes $(U_t^{(i)})_{t\in\mathbb R}$, $1\le i\le d$, are independent, centered, and have covariance function $\mathbb E [U_s^{(i)}U_t^{(i)}]=e^{-|t-s|/2}$. For every $T>0$, we obtain an explicit formula for the probability that the convex hull $\mathrm{conv}\{U_t:0\le t\le T\}$ contains the origin. We obtain a similar formula for a circular Ornstein--Uhlenbeck loop whose covariance is the normalized $T$-periodization of this kernel. For each fixed dimension $d$, we determine the precise long-time asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities, which decay as explicit constants times $T^{d-1} e^{-T/2}$ as $T\to\infty$. We also show that, as $d\to\infty$, the absorption probabilities in both models undergo a transition from $0$ to $1$ around $T=2d$, with a common Gaussian limiting profile on the scale $\sqrt d$. We also obtain explicit formulas for the probability that $σZ$ belongs to the convex hull of Brownian motion or Brownian bridge on $[0,1]$ in $\mathbb R^d$, where $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian vector and $σ\ge0$. The large-$σ$ asymptotics recover the known formulas for the expected volumes of these convex hulls. Finally, we compute the conic intrinsic volumes of the closed positive hulls of deterministic Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals and their circular analogues in Hilbert spaces. Their Grassmann angles coincide with the corresponding Ornstein--Uhlenbeck absorption probabilities. After suitable rescaling, the small-time limits of these conic intrinsic volumes recover the formulas of Gao--Vitale and Gao for the intrinsic volumes of the Brownian body and its Brownian-bridge analogue.

papers.title: Bayesian Inference in Partially Observed Critical Systems
papers.abstract: We ask how much of a large random system must be observed to infer a global average with controlled uncertainty. For the random transposition shuffle, a conjugate Bayesian estimator of the average displacement, computed from $m$ sampled cards, has relative uncertainty $1/\sqrt{2m}$, independent of the deck size $n$. Because the configuration is a single draw from equilibrium, a floor $R_n$ remains, and no relative tolerance below $κ\sqrt{R_n}$ can be certified, even by a census. For the shuffle $R_n=(2n^2+7)/\bigl(5(n-1)^2(n+1)\bigr)$. Before equilibrium, a certificate built on the displacement loses sight after about $\frac n4\ln m$ steps, half as long as the count of fixed cards in the same sample. At the two-dimensional Ising critical point the floor of the energy vanishes, whereas that of the magnetisation stays near $0.072$, with mean-field limit $\sqrt2-1$. For correlated fields, the usual 95\% interval can cover the ensemble mean in only 7\% of cases, and no bound on the floor from one realisation holds under stationarity alone.

papers.title: The maximum spectral radius of connected graphs with prescribed order and size
papers.abstract: In 1986, Brualdi and Solheid asked which connected graph of prescribed order and size has maximum adjacency spectral radius. We complete the classification for every feasible pair of parameters. We prove that no graph outside the dense and star threshold families is extremal, including at ties, and settle the range $n\le e+1$, where the star candidate is not defined. The final comparison \emph{between} the dense and star candidates is supplied by Damnjanović's Propositions~4.1--4.2, not reproved here. We combine an exact Bellman recursion with dense-core domination, fractional complete-split bounds, and a virtual-star inequality. Three remaining comparison families (J), (K1), and (K2) are established analytically and by exact polynomial and Sturm certificates. The exact certificates are implemented in Python/SymPy and SageMath.

papers.title: The \(\mathcal A_α\)-Spectral Turán Problem for \(s\)-Clique Tensors of \(K_{r+1}\)-Free Graphs
papers.abstract: For integers $3\leq s\leq r$ and $0<α<1$, we study the maximum spectral radius of the convex combination of the degree and adjacency tensors of the $s$-clique hypergraph of an $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graph. For $n\geq r$, every extremal graph is complete $r$-partite. For all sufficiently large $n$, uniformly in $α$, the only possible extremal graphs are $T_r(n)$ and $K_1\vee T_{r-1}(n-1)$. There is a unique parameter $α_n$ at which both attain the maximum; the former is uniquely extremal below $α_n$ and the latter above it. Writing $c=((r-1)/r)^{s-1}$, we show that $α_n=c+(s-1)c/n+O_{r,s}(n^{-2})$. The limiting maximum after normalization by $n^{s-1}$ is $\binom{r-1}{s-1}\max\{r^{1-s},α(r-1)^{1-s}\}$. A sharp row-quotient bound at $α=c$ identifies the limiting part proportions; local comparisons then determine the exact integer part sizes.

papers.title: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
papers.abstract: We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.

papers.title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
papers.abstract: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we obtain its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1<p<\infty$. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1<p<n$, a weighted exponential integrability of Trudinger type when $p=n$, where the Hardy term is replaced by its Leray logarithmic correction, and a weighted Hölder seminorm when $p>n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for $F_o$-radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction and, for $1<p\le n$, on a splitting of the transformed function into its $F_o$-spherical mean and a mean-free part. Since $F^2$ is not a quadratic form unless $F$ is induced by a scalar product, the reduction of the radial part through spherical harmonics, used in the Euclidean case, is not available; we control the radial part directly, through a convexity inequality for $F^p$ with a quadratic remainder and sharp one-dimensional estimates, and the mean-free part through a Poincaré inequality on the boundary of the Wulff shape. For $p>n$ we use an anisotropic Morrey representation formula.

papers.title: Pattern-dependent stability of binary exponential perturbations
papers.abstract: We study how the arrangement of binary frequency perturbations affects the stability of exponential systems on an interval of length one. For frequencies $λ_n=n+s_nδ$, with $s_n\in\{-1,+1\}$, we represent synthesis in Fourier coordinates by a shifted-sinc operator $N_{δ,s}$ and identify its Gram operator as $G_{δ,s}=N_{δ,s}^*N_{δ,s}$. The optimal squared synthesis bounds are $1\pmρ_{δ,s}$, where $ρ_{δ,s}=\|P_-T_{2δ}P_+\|$ measures the interaction between the two sign classes. Using the finite-matrix representation of periodic perturbations, we prove that, for each fixed $0\leqδ<1/2$, the minimum lower bound among $p$-periodic binary patterns converges to the worst binary lower bound as $p\to\infty$. At Kadec's critical amplitude $δ=1/4$, the alternating pattern has a positive lower bound, whereas a step pattern reduces to a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has lower bound zero. Every fixed periodic pattern nevertheless remains a Riesz basis. We discuss the resulting periodic extremal questions and record a direct perturbation estimate giving explicit stability neighborhoods around stable reference patterns.

papers.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
papers.abstract: We count the integral solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with $|x_3|$ of size at most $M$, for $M$ smaller than $\sqrt D$, using a smooth weight $Φ(x_3/M)$. Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant $D$, and hence to geodesics in the hyperbolic plane. Under this correspondence, $x_3$ is small exactly when the geodesic passes close to the point $i$. We count these geodesics by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. Throughout, $θ=7/64$ is the Kim-Sarnak exponent. For non-square $D=f^2D_0$, with $D_0$ a fundamental discriminant, the geodesics are closed. We obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(D^{\varepsilon}f^{1+θ}D_0^{2/3}M^{-1/2})$. The main inputs are the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao for cycle integrals, the cubic moment bounds of Young and of Andersen-Wu, and a Hecke relation which reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant $D_0$. For $D\equiv 5 \bmod 8$ this counts all solutions, and the range $M\ge D^{1/2-1/1332}$ of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to $M\ge D^{4/9+\varepsilon}$. For square $D=n^2$ the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to the single geodesic from $0$ to $\infty$. For every $n$ and both parities of $x_3$ we obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(n^{1+θ+\varepsilon}M^{-1/2})$, which is non-trivial for $M\ge n^{71/96+\varepsilon}$. This improves the range $n^{5/6+\varepsilon}$ of the elementary method and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High; Fable 5.2 in the final stage), an AI model developed by Anthropic.

papers.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carathéodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
papers.abstract: We study extension of additive measures when the range carries a prescribed separated Abelian net convergence. On a $σ$-complete, lattice-$σ$-continuous pseudo-D-lattice, we prove an uncontrolled modular extension theorem using finite-response reflection, closed countable summation and uniform closure. Completeness is imposed only on the limit-stable hull of the source values. No topology, lattice order or positive control is required in its range. Modular interval identities, an order-null separation argument and two uniform transfer arguments construct the extension before establishing its normality. A separate relative lifting theorem combines this modular construction with a nonmodular Sasaki argument. Its cone conditions are verified for positive lattice-group values, lattice-normed groups, products and limit-stable subgroups. These verifications give explicit positive, dominated lattice-normed and topological corollaries. Uniqueness holds among all sigma-additive extensions to the generated domain. Sion's inner and outer nets exist in the original convergence and recover the extension there. For Boolean domains we retain the stronger identification with the full regulated splitting class and the finite-variation and finite-semivariation results.

papers.title: Self-intersecting sections of polar actions on simply connected manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct a polar action of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ on a closed simply connected $11$-manifold with a compact three-dimensional section that is not injectively immersed. The section is injective over the regular part and has two distinct local branches along a singular stratum. All isotropy groups are connected, and all orbits are simply connected. This gives a negative answer to the injectivity question raised by Grove and Ziller.

papers.title: Fully Deterministic Shallow Neural Networks with Localized Activations: Construction and Optimal Sobolev Approximation
papers.abstract: We construct fully deterministic finite-dimensional spaces for Sobolev approximation using shallow neural networks with a localized activation $σ$, either Gaussian or tanh-difference. For a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, and a prescribed regularity index $s>0$, the approximation space at frequency resolution $M$ is\[ V_M^Ω=\operatorname{span}\left\{ σ\!\left(\frac{ω_i\cdot x-b_{j,M}}{\varepsilon_M}\right): 1\le i\le J_M,\quad 1\le j\le K_{i,M} \right\}. \]All parameters are prescribed explicitly and independently of the target function. The offset cutoff depends on the direction and the domain, with an exterior margin tending to zero. The feature count satisfies $N_M=\sum_{i=1}^{J_M}K_{i,M}\asymp M^d$. For sufficiently large $M$, we construct a bounded linear operator $\mathcal A_M^Ω:H^s(Ω)\to V_M^Ω$ that achieves the optimal approximation rate \[ \|u-\mathcal A_M^Ωu\|_{H^m(Ω)} \le C N_M^{-(s-m)/d}\|u\|_{H^s(Ω)} \] for every $u\in H^s(Ω)$ and every integer $0\le m<s$. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions illustrate the approximation behavior in $L^2$ and $H^1$.

papers.title: A Wasserstein Trust-Region Method for Smooth Potential-Interaction Energies
papers.abstract: Finding low-energy particle configurations and approximating probability distributions both lead to minimizing potential-interaction energies in Wasserstein space. Second-order information can speed up minimizing these possibly nonconvex energies, but a quadratic model is accurate only near the current measure. We introduce a Wasserstein trust-region (WTR) method for smooth, possibly nonconvex energies of this type. Each iteration transports the current measure $ρ$ along a displacement field $s$, producing $(\mathrm{Id}+s)_\#ρ$. The field approximately minimizes a quadratic model built from the second variation of the energy, subject to $\|s\|_{L^2(ρ)}\leΔ$, using a truncated conjugate-gradient method. The ratio of actual to predicted decrease determines step acceptance and updates the trust-region radius. Under a lower energy bound and globally bounded Hessians of the potential and interaction kernel, we prove that the objective is nonincreasing, the Wasserstein-gradient norms converge to zero, and an $\varepsilon$-stationary iterate is reached within $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations, rejected ones included. If the potential is quadratically coercive, every weak accumulation point is stationary. For empirical measures, WTR is an ordinary trust-region method in the particle positions, and its complexity bound does not depend on the number of particles provided the initial energy exceeds its infimum by a bounded amount. For $2048$ and $4096$ particles with Gaussian pair repulsion in a two-dimensional harmonic trap, WTR reaches the gradient tolerance $2\times10^{-4}$ a median $1.40$ times faster than L-BFGS. For equal-weight integration rules on two non-Gaussian targets, WTR reaches an integration error of $10^{-4}$ about $1.8$ times faster than L-BFGS and $1.3$ times faster than a Krylov trust-region solver.

papers.title: Spectral Erdős--Gallai Theorems for the \(\mathcal A_α\)-Tensor of the \(s\)-Clique Hypergraph
papers.abstract: The generalized Erdős--Gallai theorem determines the maximum number of $s$-cliques in an $n$-vertex graph with no matching of $t$ edges. We study its spectral analogue for the $\mathcal A_α$-tensor of the $s$-uniform clique hypergraph. For $n\geq2t-1$, $3\leq s\leq2t-1$, and $0\leqα\leq1$, we determine the maximum $α$-$s$-clique spectral radius among $n$-vertex graphs with no matching of $t$ edges, and characterize all extremal graphs. When $t<s\leq 2t-1$, the unique extremal graph up to isomorphism is a $(2t-1)$-clique with isolated vertices. When $3\leq s\leq t$, the extremal graphs are selected from this graph and the join of a $(t-1)$-clique with an independent set. We give the exact order at which the join becomes extremal and determine when both graphs attain the maximum.

papers.title: Optimal convergence rates in homogenization of Monge-Ampère equations with periodic measures
papers.abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates in periodic homogenization of Monge--Ampère equations, allowing the microscopic measure to be singular or degenerate. Let $μ$ be a nonnegative $\mathbb Z^n$-periodic Borel measure with $μ(\mathbb T^n)=1$, and set $μ_\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon^nμ(E/\varepsilon)$. On a bounded convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, let $u^\varepsilon$ and $u$ be the convex solutions of \[ \det D^2u^\varepsilon=F(x,x/\varepsilon)\,μ_\varepsilon,\qquad\det D^2u=\overline{F}(x) \] with the same Dirichlet data, where the coefficient $F$ is bounded, uniformly positive, and periodic in its second variable, and $\overline F(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}F(x,y)\,dμ(y)$. For $m=0,1$ and $0<α\leq1$, we prove \[ \|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\leq C\varepsilon^{m+α},\qquad \forall\,0<\varepsilon\leq1, \] provided that $u\in C^{m+2,α}(\overlineΩ)$ and $F(\cdot,y)\in C^{m,α}(\overlineΩ)$ uniformly in $y$. These exponents are optimal in their respective regularity scales, and the constant $C$ is independent of the distribution of the microscopic measure. In particular, the estimates include the optimal quadratic rate for general periodic measures. Our proof of the lower-order estimate ($m=0$) relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for periodic correctors. For the higher-order estimate ($m=1$), we introduce a constrained Monge--Ampère problem that produces convex approximations with prescribed cell averages. This construction captures the cancellation in the third-order corrector expansion without uniform Hessian bounds for the correctors.

papers.title: Quillen's finiteness conjecture for the cotangent complex in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Building on work of Turner, we propose a proof in positive characteristic of Quillen's conjecture on finiteness properties of the cotangent complex for homomorphisms between noetherian rings of possibly infinite flat dimension.

papers.title: Contraction-Based Model Predictive Control using Bilinear Koopman Realizations with Proportional Error Bounds
papers.abstract: Data-driven model predictive control based on Koopman operator theory is a promising approach for constrained control of nonlinear systems with unknown dynamics. This paper proposes a robust model predictive control framework for such systems using bilinear Koopman realizations with state- and input-dependent proportional approximation-error bounds that vanish at the target equilibrium. Since prediction in lifted coordinates with a finite-dimensional Koopman realization need not remain on the manifold of valid lifted states, multi-step prediction may leave the region where one-step error certificates apply. We avoid this difficulty by reprojecting each predicted lifted state onto the original state coordinates and lifting it again, yielding an error-aware discrete-time control-affine predictor in the original state space without assuming invariance of the Koopman dictionary. For this predictor, we develop a homothetic tube construction based on a discrete-time robust control contraction metric whose radius explicitly accounts for the proportional approximation error bounds. The tube tightening handles arbitrary continuously differentiable nonlinear constraints, and the resulting model predictive control problem includes terminal ingredients and a tube-radius penalty that exploits the vanishing uncertainty near the target. We prove robust satisfaction of the original nonlinear constraints, recursive feasibility, and exponential stability of the sampled true closed-loop system with high probability over the training data without requiring a globally optimal solution to the model predictive control problem. Numerical examples, including nonlinear obstacle-avoidance constraints, demonstrate robust stabilization and higher performance of the proposed approach compared to existing Koopman-based model predictive control methods in terms of smaller closed-loop cost and flexibility.

papers.title: Fixed point properties for random groups in the density model with $d > \frac{1}{4}$
papers.abstract: We prove that random groups in Gromov's density model have Kazhdan's property~\((T)\) asymptotically almost surely (a.a.s.) at every density \(d>\frac14\). Together with Ashcroft's theorem for \(d<\frac14\), this establishes \(\frac14\) as the sharp threshold and settles the long-standing problem of determining the threshold for property $(T)$ in the density model. More generally, for every fixed number of generators \(n\ge2\) and density \(d\in(\frac14,1)\), there exists \(C_{n,d}>0\) such that, a.a.s., every affine isometric action on a real \(L^p\)-space has a fixed point simultaneously for all \[ 1\le p\le C_{n,d}\sqrt{\frac{l}{\log l}}, \] where \(l\) is the relator length. In particular, \(\frac14\) is also the threshold for each fixed \(L^p\) fixed point property, \(1\le p<\infty\). We also establish a simultaneous fixed point theorem for a large class of uniformly smooth real Banach spaces with a common power-type convexity bound and a suitable common bound on their uniform curvature moduli. We further prove that, for each fixed real Banach space in a class that, to the best of our knowledge, contains all currently known examples of super-reflexive Banach spaces, random groups at density $d>1/4$ a.a.s.\ have the fixed point property for affine isometric actions. The proof combines a fixed point criterion based on harmonic cocycles with spectral estimates for random bipartite multigraphs arising from decompositions of relators into four consecutive subwords. All asymptotic conclusions hold as \(\RelLen\to\infty\) through all positive integers.

papers.title: The smallest square tileable by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles
papers.abstract: Croft, Falconer and Guy (Unsolved Problems in Geometry, Problem C5) exhibit a tiling of the 27 x 27 square by eight pairwise incomparable integer rectangles and remark that it is not known whether 27 is the smallest side length of a square that can be tiled by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles, no restriction being placed on the number of tiles. Knuth has since stated, in a 2019 draft of a section of The Art of Computer Programming, that 27 is indeed the smallest. We give a complete, independently reproducible proof: for every integer n <= 26 and every k >= 2, the n x n square admits no tiling by k pairwise incomparable integer rectangles. The proof combines two structural reductions with an exhaustive search over the 167538 surviving candidate tile sets, carried out by two independently written programs. The same search shows that at least eight tiles are needed at n = 27 and that the tile set of Croft, Falconer and Guy is the only one that tiles this square; it does so in exactly two arrangements up to symmetry. We also give explicit eight-tile tilings of the n x n square for every n >= 27, and seven-tile tilings for every n >= 34. With the classical lower bounds (every tiling of a rectangle by two or more pairwise incomparable rectangles uses at least seven, and no square of integer side less than 34 can be tiled by seven pairwise incomparable integer rectangles), this determines the least number of tiles for every square: there is no tiling for n <= 26, eight tiles are needed for 27 <= n <= 33, and seven for n >= 34. The complete software, build instructions and output logs are included as ancillary files.

papers.title: A complete characterization of sequential testability and change detectability in i.i.d. models
papers.abstract: We give qualitative and quantitative necessary and sufficient conditions for sequential testing and change detection in an i.i.d. composite problem. A level-\(α\) test with power one against every alternative exists if and only if the alternatives are separated from the null by a countable family of finite-block events. Equivalent conditions use randomized tests, bounded scores, e-processes, reduced-filtration test supermartingales, and a countable cover with positive finite-block weak-$*$ convex-hull separation. The construction gives pointwise expected sample size \(O_Q(\log(1/α))\). Quantitatively, one e-process attains the intrinsic pointwise growth rate \(Γ(Q)\) at every alternative if and only if a countable family of bounded block bets recovers these rates. The same condition characterizes simultaneous attainment of the sharp expected-sample-size coefficient \(1/Γ(Q)\); arbitrary attainable lower rate profiles admit an analogous characterization. Total-variation separability of the alternatives suffices for recovery. Weak lower semicontinuity of the KL projection, in particular weak compactness of the null, also identifies \(Γ(Q)\) with \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathrm{KL}(Q\|P)\). The qualitative and quantitative conditions also characterize change detectability under fixed-time false-alarm bounds \(\Prob_{P^\infty}(T_γ\le n)\le n/γ\), together with ordinary ARL control. Whenever countable rate recovery holds, for any \(η>0\) one calibrated e-detector has robust Lorden delay asymptotic to \((\logγ)/Γ(Q)\) at finite positive rates, while satisfying the stronger optional-horizon inequality and placing every null ARL in \([γ,(1+η)γ+1]\). Examples exhibit a strict cost of simultaneous optimality and show that ordinary ARL alone supports neither characterization, even with finite, tightly calibrated null means.

papers.title: Derivation of a linearly elastic elliptic membrane shell theory in the framework of magnetoelasticity
papers.abstract: Starting from a three-dimensional model of linearized magnetoelasticity, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of a thin shell as its thickness approaches zero. Our analysis focuses on a family of linearly elastic elliptic membrane shells. Using $Γ$-convergence, we rigorously derive a two-dimensional linear magnetoelastic shell model and establish its relationship to the original three-dimensional model in terms of the convergence of minimizers.

papers.title: Sturm--Liouville-Type Parity and Oscillation of a Cubic Spline Eigenbasis
papers.abstract: We study the eigen-structure of the kernel matrix arising from cubic smoothing splines on equally spaced knots. Using matrix-theoretic methods, we show that its positive eigenvalues are simple, that the associated eigenvectors alternate between even and odd, and that the eigenvector for the $k$th largest positive eigenvalue has exactly $k+1$ sign changes. Building on established results on oscillatory and centrosymmetric matrices, we provide a more explicit proof of the known oscillation property of the eigenvectors and establish their alternating parity. We then verify, by a separate argument, that both properties extend to the associated continuous cubic spline eigenfunctions, showing that the resulting spline basis exhibits both an alternating parity structure and an oscillation pattern analogous to that of classical Sturm--Liouville eigenfunctions.

papers.title: Polynomial permutation stability, soficity, and universal polynomial groups
papers.abstract: We introduce polynomial permutation stability for maps between groups, extending ordinary permutation stability from homomorphisms to polynomial maps defined by iterated finite differences. We show that a group $G$ is polynomially permutation stable in degree $s$ if and only if its universal polynomial group $\operatorname{Pol}_s(G)$ is permutation stable. While every finite group is polynomially permutation stable in degree two, we prove that the cyclic group of order six is not stable in degree three. More precisely, we construct a finite-index direct-product subgroup of $\operatorname{Pol}_3(C_6)$ to which an instability theorem of Ioana applies. We also show that polynomial sofic approximations characterize the usual class of sofic groups. In degree two, we obtain a split exact sequence relating $\operatorname{Pol}_2(G)$ to a restricted wreath product, with applications to soficity and property $(T)$. A quotient-transfer principle yields infinite, finitely presented, nonperfect groups that are polynomially permutation stable in every degree. Finally, we obtain nonamenability and largeness results for higher-degree universal polynomial groups of finite groups.

papers.title: Exact Algebraic Computation of Learning Coefficients for Two-Dimensional Singular Models
papers.abstract: Classical information criteria such as the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) rely on regularity assumptions that break down for singular models, leading to incorrect model selection in settings such as deep learning. The Widely Applicable Bayesian Information Criterion (WBIC) relies on local learning coefficients $λ$, which in the analytic case coincides with local Real Log Canonical Thresholds (RLCT) of the Kullback-Leibler divergence of the model, to capture correct marginal likelihood asymptotics. Exact computation of the learning coefficients has been limited to special cases, and only sampling-based estimation methods are generally applicable. We present the first deterministic algorithm that computes local RLCTs exactly for any two-dimensional model whose Kullback-Leibler distance is contact equivalent to a polynomial, derive a bound on its complexity, and demonstrate its effectiveness for a broad class of models, with applications including polynomial neural networks. Beyond providing ground truth to calibrate sampling-based estimators, exact computation reveals algebraic structure in learning coefficients that sampling cannot and out-speeds it in the shallow regime.

papers.title: Entrywise Positivity Preservers on Green Matrices
papers.abstract: We classify entrywise functions preserving positive semidefiniteness on Green matrices with positive parameters. For each fixed \(n\ge2\), PSD preservation is equivalent to \(f\) being nondecreasing and \((f(tr^{i+j}))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) being PSD for all \(t>0,r>1\). For \(f\in C^{2n-2}\), this is equivalent to \(f'\ge0\) and positive semidefiniteness of \(((t\,d/dt)^{i+j}f(t))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) at every positive \(t\). These fixed-order classes strictly decrease with \(n\); their intersection consists exactly of \(f(t)=\int_{[0,\infty)}t^α\,dμ(α)\), where \(μ\) is a finite positive measure and the integral is finite for every \(t>0\). At each fixed order, entrywise Loewner monotonicity is equivalent to \(f\in C^1\) and \(f'\) belonging to the corresponding PSD preserver class. In all orders, monotonicity itself implies smoothness. Nonnegative minors of orders one and two on every strict three-by-three Green input already force \(f\equiv0\) or \(f(t)=ct^α\), with \(c>0\) and \(α\ge0\). They give TN output in every order; the nonzero members also preserve PSD Green structure. We also classify PSD, TN, and Loewner-monotone extensions to the closure allowing zero entries. No regularity is assumed except in the differential criterion.

papers.title: Learning Forced Multibody Dynamics on Lie Groups
papers.abstract: We introduce an architecture for learning the dynamics of forced mechanical systems evolving on Lie groups, based on discrete forced Euler-Lagrange equations. The proposed method, termed Lie Group Discrete Forced Euler-Lagrange Neural Network (LieDFLNN), learns mechanical dynamics directly from discrete configuration observations, without requiring velocity measurements. This formulation allows the simultaneous identification of unknown mechanical properties and forcing terms, while ensuring that the predicted configurations remain on the underlying Lie group. We develop explicit formulations for rigid body dynamics on $SO(3)$ and $SE(3)$, extend the framework to interacting multibody systems, and introduce a method for learning unknown control forces when the Lagrangian is known. Finally, we evaluate the method through numerical experiments involving rigid body dynamics, nonlinear external forces, controlled systems, and real-world human motion capture data. The numerical results confirm the advantages of incorporating Lie group geometry and discrete variational structure into data-driven modeling of forced mechanical systems.

papers.title: Shifted-Binomial Coordinates of Dilated Binomial Polynomials: Multinomial Decimation and Arithmetic Structure
papers.abstract: For integers $m\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, let $d=m+r-1$ and consider the unique expansion \[ \binom{mn}{d}=\sum_{k=1}^{d+1}T_{m,r,k}\binom{n+k-1}{d}. \] By a standard multisection of a rational generating function, the coordinates are a residue-class subsequence of multinomial coefficients: \[ T_{m,r,k}=[x^{mk-1}](1+x+\cdots+x^{m-1})^{m+r}. \] From this representation we obtain the exact support, a counting interpretation by words by drops (Theorem~\ref{thm:drops}), a reflection criterion (the nonzero row is palindromic precisely when $r\equiv2\pmod m$), and log-concavity, hence unimodality, of the nonzero row. An integer-valued polynomial argument gives the universal divisor $m/\gcd(m,r-1)$ of each row, and a prime-adic computation of the fixed divisor of $\binom{mX}{d}$ gives the exact greatest common divisor of each row, a sharpness criterion, and a family of rows in which the universal divisor is arbitrarily far from sharp. We also obtain the row sum $m^{m+r-1}$, a Catalan-number specialization, and explicit coefficient arrays for $m=2,3,4,5$. The methods are finite differences, multisection of rational generating functions, and fixed divisors of integer-valued polynomials.

papers.title: A few remarks on the Baez-Duarte Criterion
papers.abstract: We study exponentially damped Möbius approximants in $\mathscr H=L^2([1,\infty),dt/t^{-2})$. With \[ γ_n(t)=\left\lfloor\frac tn\right\rfloor -\frac{\lfloor t\rfloor}{n},\qquad f(u)(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}μ(n)e^{-nu}γ_n(t),\] we compute the relevant scalar products, characterize the Möbius coefficients as the unique coefficients giving pointwise convergence to the constant function, and prove $\langle1 \mid f(u)\rangle\to1$. Vasyunin's formula expresses $F(e^{-u})=\|f(u)\|_2^2$ as an arithmetic cotangent sum. In the final section we give a criterion that would help in the analysis of asymptotics of $F(x)$ as $x\uparrow 1$.

papers.title: Group action-stabilizer graph of group actions of a group on a set
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce the group action-stabilizer graph $GAS(G)$ of a group $G$ on a set $X$. Its vertex set is the collection of all non-trivial group actions of $G$ on $X$, and two vertices $φ$ and $ψ$ are adjacent if and only if the normal subgroups $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^φ$ and $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^ψ$ of $G$ intersect non-trivially, where $G_x^φ$ and $G_x^ψ$ are the stabilizers of $x$ with respect to the actions $φ$ and $ψ$, respectively. We show that $GAS(G)$ is obtained from the intersection graph of those normal subgroups of $G$ that occur as kernels of actions on $X$ by replacing each vertex by a clique of twin vertices, and we characterize a special subgraph $gas(G)$ of $GAS(G)$ in which the vertex set contains the actions $φ$ of $G$ on $X$ such that the kernels $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^φ$ are distinct. We determine the number of group actions within some specific groups and find certain conditions under which $GAS(G)$ is equal to $gas(G)$. We also show that, for a finite nilpotent group $G$ with at least two prime divisors, $gas(G)$ is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^3p_2$, and its complement is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^2p_2^2$.

papers.title: Penalized hyperviscous Navier-Stokes flows: well-posedness, incompressible limit and sharp decay
papers.abstract: We study a three-dimensional Navier--Stokes system obtained by Temam's penalty method in the presence of a biharmonic viscosity: the pressure and the divergence constraint are replaced by the term $-\varepsilon^{-1}\nabla\,div\,u$, and the convection term is written in skew-symmetric form. We prove global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and global regularity for data of arbitrary size in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, with bounds uniform in $\varepsilon$ and in time. For data in $L^1\cap L^2$, the energy decays like $t^{-3/2}$, with a constant independent of $\varepsilon$; for data in $L^1\cap H^2$, the first two derivatives decay at the corresponding heat rates. We identify the leading asymptotic profile and show that $t^{3/2}\|u(t)\|_{L^2}^2\toγ_\varepsilon(8πν)^{-3/2}|m_\infty|^2$, where $m_\infty$ is an asymptotic momentum and the explicit factor $γ_\varepsilon\in(\frac23,1)$ measures the energy removed by the penalization. Consequently, the decay rates are optimal in $L^1\cap H^2$ under an explicit non-degeneracy condition. Finally, as $\varepsilon\to0$, the solutions converge globally in time to those of the incompressible hyperviscous Navier--Stokes equations at the rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, up to an explicit initial layer, and $-\varepsilon^{-1}div\,u$ converges to the pressure.

papers.title: Harmonic weights in inverse central binomial series
papers.abstract: We study how the partial fraction coefficients of an inverse central binomial series change when the harmonic weight $H_{pn}$ is replaced by $H_{qn}$. For positive integers $p<q$, every coefficient increases. As the index $k$ grows, the increase tends to $2\log(q/p)$ uniformly over all angles $0<φ\leπ$, even when the angle approaches either endpoint. The increase is above the limit at every odd index and below it at every even index. We give the first correction, of order $k^{-2/q}$ for $q>2$ and of order $k^{-2}$ for $(p,q)=(1,2)$. For the normalized transforms, subtracting $c$ times the first from the second gives a Stieltjes function exactly when $c\le1$. We also determine which real dilations $0<p<q$ satisfy the same sign law. For $p\ge1$ it holds exactly when $q\ge2$.
