Distinguishing availability from documented reading and use, the study shows that delayed recognition coexisted with early international circulation and a dispersed readership across scientific traditions.

papers.title: A unipotent witness: vanishing orders of word maps on SU(2) and lengths in the lower central series
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$, $k\ge2$ and $1\ne w\inγ_k(F_n)$, the $k$-th term of the lower central series of the free group of rank $n$. We prove that a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$ has at least $2k$ syllables, so $w$ has word length at least $2k$; the previous linear bound, due to Malestein and Putman, is $k$. For $1\ne w\in[F_n,F_n]$ we also prove that the word map of $w$ on $SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$ vanishes at the identity to order at most $T/2$, where $T$ is the number of syllables of a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$, with equality for $[x_1,x_2]$ and for a word with six syllables. Both proofs evaluate $w$ at unipotent matrices $I+tN_i$, with $N_i$ nilpotent of rank one, and compare the degree of the trace of the resulting matrix $M(t)\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z}[t])$ with the order of vanishing of $M(t)-I$ at $t=0$.

papers.title: Topology-Preserving Hodge--Laplacian Diffusion on Manifolds with Boundary
papers.abstract: Overview: We study deterministic and stochastic Hodge--Laplacian diffusion of differential forms on a fixed smooth compact Riemannian manifold with boundary. Absolute and relative boundary conditions select harmonic spaces representing ordinary and relative cohomology. We investigate the preservation properties of these diffusion processes, their compatible cellular discretizations, and their implications for reverse diffusion models. Numerical experiments on an annulus and a solid torus illustrate the theoretical results. Mathematical Significance: Using the de Rham complex and its constant-sheaf interpretation, we distinguish preservation of harmonic coordinates from preservation of a cohomology class. We establish that deterministic heat flow preserves the harmonic projection and exponentially damps its orthogonal complement. For additive stochastic forcing, we prove that pathwise harmonic preservation is equivalent to the absence of harmonic noise. Exact forcing preserves closedness and the initial cohomology class for closed initial data, whereas harmonic-projected forcing need not preserve closedness. We further show that compatible cellular discretizations retain these properties, with an algebraic extension to fixed weighted cellular sheaves. Separating invariant preservation from time-step stability and covariance accuracy, we derive bounds on leakage arising from approximate harmonic projectors. AI Relevance: We develop a finite-dimensional conditional score formulation that confines reverse diffusion to a prescribed harmonic component or, for closed data, a fixed cohomology class. This provides a mathematically grounded framework for incorporating topological constraints into diffusion-based generative AI models on manifolds.

papers.title: Triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes
papers.abstract: We study fractional triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes, unifying the settings of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions and the high-dimensional Dirac problem for Steiner triple systems. We prove that every sufficiently large two-dimensional simplicial complex with minimum degree at least $(1-d_1)n$ and maximum missing codegree at most $d_2n$ admits a fractional triangle decomposition, provided $d_1/0.21+d_2/0.27\leq 1$. As an immediate consequence, we prove the asymptotic form of Lee's high-dimensional Dirac conjecture: every sufficiently large admissible $3$-uniform hypergraph with minimum codegree at least $(3/4+\varepsilon)n$ contains a Steiner triple system. We also provide constructions establishing lower bounds on this fractional decomposition threshold problem.

papers.title: Norm-attaining operators on renormings of $c_0$
papers.abstract: We study norm-attaining operators on three renormings of $c_0$: Read's space $\Read$, its smooth renorming $\sRead$, and Martín's space $\X$. We prove that, for every Banach space $F$ and every $Z\in\{\Read,\sRead\}$, norm-attaining finite-rank operators are dense in $\K(Z,F)$. Consequently, $\NA(Z,F)$ is dense in $\Lin(Z,F)$ whenever $F$ is reflexive. More generally, we establish that the compact Hilbertian smoothing construction of Debs, Godefroy and Saint-Raymond \cite{DGS} preserves the density of norm-attaining operators for all finite-dimensional ranges. We also extend a second-order criterion of Kadets, López-Pérez, Martín and Werner \cite{KLMWfr} from rank two to arbitrary ranks $k\geq 2$ for operators into $\ell_2^k$, and prove that the same smoothing preserves the existence and non-existence of such operators. We further investigate the possibilities and limitations of renorming techniques for excluding rank-two norm-attaining operators through analytical and geometrical approaches, including constructions that preserve the set of norm-attaining functionals. For Martín's space $\X$, we prove that, for every Banach space $F$ and every integer $1\leq k\leq\dim F$, there exists a rank $k$ norm-attaining operator from $\X$ into $F$, answering a question of Martín \cite{Mar}. We also show that, for every nonzero Banach space $F$, $\K(\X,F)$ contains a norm-dense linear subspace whose nonzero elements fail to attain their norms.

papers.title: Enumerative Chromatic Choosability of Complete Multipartite Graphs with Small Partite Sets
papers.abstract: Chromatic choosability is a notion of fundamental importance in list coloring. A graph is chromatic-choosable when its chromatic number is equal to its list chromatic number. In their 1979 paper on list coloring, Erdős, Rubin, and Taylor showed that complete $m$-partite graphs with every partite set of size 2, denoted by $K_{2*m}$, are chromatic-choosable. In 1990, Kostochka and Sidorenko introduced the list color function of a graph $G$, denoted by $P_{\ell}(G,m)$, which is the list analogue of the chromatic polynomial of $G$, $P(G,m)$. A graph $G$ is enumeratively chromatic-choosable when $P_{\ell}(G,m) = P(G,m)$ whenever $m \in \mathbb{N}$. In this paper, we explore the question as to whether $K_{2*m}$ satisfies this stronger property. We establish a recursive lower bound on $P_{\ell}(K_{2*m},m)$ and prove that $K_{2*3}$ and $K_{2*4}$ are weakly enumeratively chromatic-choosable, meaning that equality holds at the chromatic number. We also develop a general lower bound for the list color function of certain joins with complete graphs and use it to prove that $K_p\vee K_{2*5}$ is weakly enumeratively chromatic-choosable whenever $p\geq 15$, and that $K_p\vee K_{2,2,3}$ is weakly enumeratively chromatic-choosable whenever $p\geq 3$. These results provide progress toward a weaker form of a conjecture of Allred and Mudrock concerning the enumerative chromatic choosability of complete graph joins.

papers.title: Kleinian groups with tunnel number one
papers.abstract: We give a structural theory for the holonomy groups of hyperbolic links with tunnel number 1 in arbitrary 3-manifolds. This is a first step towards understanding the canonical triangulations of such links, as it generalises the combinatorial structure theory of two-bridge link groups that is an input to the Sakuma--Weeks triangulation.

papers.title: Computability of states and non-computability of traces
papers.abstract: We study computable presentations of the state space and trace space of computably presented C*-algebras. We show that the state space has a computably compact presentation with respect to which the evaluation of states is a computable map. As an application of having computable states, we obtain a computable version of the GNS construction. We show that the trace space does not share these computational properties. Specifically, we give an example of a computable presentation of a simple AF algebra for which the trace space has no computably compact presentation with respect to which evaluation is computable. As a consequence, we demonstrate that the Elliott invariant of a computably presentable classifiable C*-algebra is not always presentable in a way that makes all key features of the invariant computable.

papers.title: Sharp Estimates for Jacobi Heat Kernels on a Ball and on a Simplex in the Full Range of Parameters
papers.abstract: We establish genuinely sharp heat-kernel estimates for orthogonal expansions on the Euclidean unit ball and on the unit simplex throughout their natural parameter ranges. For the ball weight $W_μ(x)=(1-\|x\|^2)^{μ-1/2}$, we extend the known estimate from the range $μ\geq0$ to every $μ>-1/2$. For the simplex, we prove the corresponding estimate for every $κ\in(-1/2,\infty)^{d+1}$. The estimates retain exactly the form known in the classical ranges. The proof is based on analytic continuation of the classical product and reduction formulas. Below the integrability threshold, the ball formula decomposes into an endpoint term and a derivative correction, while the simplex formula produces endpoint and mixed-derivative terms indexed by the negative coordinates. In the lowest simplex parameter range we use the auxiliary even ultraspherical kernel introduced by Nowak, Sjögren, and Szarek.

papers.title: Bivariant $K$-theory for bornological algebras
papers.abstract:
We construct a presentable, stable \(\infty\)-category \( KK\), and exhibit it as the target of the universal functor from the category of bornological algebras into cocomplete, stable \(\infty\)-categories, preserving filtered colimits, and satisfying smooth homotopy invariance, excision, and stabilisation with respect to Schatten-class or smooth compact operators. We also construct a bivariant \(K\)-theory \(
KK\) for suitably nuclear bornological algebras, and show that it is a right Bousfield localisation of \( KK\). The category \(
KK\) is symmetric monoidal and admits a bivariant Chern character to local cyclic homology. The categories \(
KK\) and \( KK\) corepresent Cortiñas and Thom's diffeotopy \(K\)-theory. We use the Chern character to show that up to a suitable Schatten-class stabilisation, the complexified Chern character from the diffeotopy \(K\)-theory (resp. \(K\)-homology) of a smooth manifold to the compactly supported cohomology (resp. locally finite homology) of the manifold is an isomorphism.

papers.title: Nehari type characterizations of the mountain pass level on cones
papers.abstract: We relate the mountain pass level of a functional to its infimum over the part of the Nehari set formed by local maximizers of the fiber maps. {Unlike in the classical setting where every fiber map has a unique global maximizer,} the fiber maps need not all have a maximizer: working on each path-connected component of the cone of directions where they do, we show that the two levels coincide, for merely continuous functionals and without any compactness assumption. We also introduce a notion of mountain pass geometry with respect to a cone, which may hold when the classical one fails. {This geometry includes the zero-level case when a suitable separating set exists.} Under the Palais--Smale condition, each component carries a critical point at its own mountain pass level. Applications include indefinite and concave-convex problems with sign-changing weights, the affine $p$-Laplacian, nonlocal problems, and a problem related to the Fučík spectrum.

papers.title: On the mode stability of a self-similar blow-up of Yang--Mills heat flow in five dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the spectral stability properties of an explicitly known self-similar blowup profile to the Yang-Mills heat flow on $\mathbb R^5\times SO(5)$ often referred to as the Weinkove solution. We prove that this solution is mode stable in a dynamically evolving DeTurck gauge. To arrive at that result, we first reduce the problem to countably many vector-valued Schrödinger operators on the half line. We then proceed by proving uniform estimates for all but finitely many of said operators. The spectra of the remaining operators are studied individually by means of GGMT bounds or by comparison arguments. Two of these operators are distinguished as they have negative eigenvalues originating from symmetries. Among these two there is a scalar operator, previously analyzed by Donninger and Schörkhuber, and an operator acting on a three-dimensional vector bundle. The latter operator's matrix structure prohibits a straightforward supersymmetric removal. To circumvent this, we transform the equation to a Schrödinger operator with drift terms to simplify the structure of the eigenfunction. We then develop tools to study such operators and conclude that said operator has no second negative eigenvalue.

papers.title: Skew-Symmetric Factor Models
papers.abstract: The paper introduces and analyzes a factor model for (real) skew-symmetric data, which arise naturally in directed flows and in pairwise comparisons used for rankings. Working within a signal-plus-noise framework, we analyze spectral inference and establish a BBP-type phase transition in signal strength. Under Gaussian noise, we derive joint eigenvalue fluctuation limits. Above the separation threshold, the estimated signal strength is asymptotically normal whenever the population strength has multiplicity one. For a general multiplicity $k$, the joint limiting fluctuations of the corresponding sample eigenvalues above the threshold are given by the eigenvalues of a scaled $k\times k$ Gaussian unitary ensemble matrix. The skew-symmetric structure induces paired eigenspaces, and we characterize the canonical angles between the population and sample eigenspaces. Below the threshold, the corresponding largest sample eigenvalue converges to the edge of the semicircle law, with fluctuations governed by the Tracy--Widom $F_2$ distribution, in contrast to the $F_1$ law familiar from real symmetric models. The approach is illustrated through financial and demographic applications.

papers.title: A simple counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem for excited states
papers.abstract: For an even number of non-interacting fermions on the one-dimensional unit torus, a semi-explicit counterexample to the Hohenberg--Kohn theorem for excited states is exhibited. Indeed, for each $n = 2l$, it is shown that there exist constants $m \in (0, 1)$ and $\ell > 0$ such that an $n$-body system with the rescaled Lamé potential $v_*(x) = 2m \ell^2 \operatorname{sn}^2(\ell x; m)$ has a simple first excited energy and a first excited-state particle density which is constant on the torus. By translating this potential, we exhibit a non-trivial one-parameter family of potentials, all of which have a constant first excited-state density. As such, the potential-to-density map is not one-to-one in this setting. Under a spectral nonresonance assumption, we obtain the same nonuniqueness at a simple excited energy for odd $n \geq 3$. We also explore connections to the classification problem of elastica in the plane when $n = 2$, and outline some related questions of interest.

papers.title: The Möbius Homology Laplacian for Persistence Modules
papers.abstract: Persistent homology provides a framework for studying the evolution of topological features across filtered spaces. While persistence diagrams give discrete invariants that record the birth and death of homological features, they do not directly encode analytic or geometric structure associated to persistence modules. This paper develops a spectral framework for persistent homology by introducing and studying a Laplace operator on the Möbius chain complex, called the Möbius homology Laplacian. Möbius homology categorifies Möbius inversion for persistence modules by replacing integer-valued data with vector-space-valued chain complexes. By equipping these chain complexes with inner products, we define a Laplace operator on the Möbius chain complex whose kernel provides canonical cycle representatives for the associated Möbius homology space. We analyze the spectral properties of this operator in two primary settings: one-parameter persistence modules and birth-death modules arising from filtrations of simplicial complexes. For one-parameter modules, we completely characterize the eigenvalues of the degree-one Möbius homology Laplacian. For birth-death modules, we show that the trace and determinant of the degree-zero Möbius homology Laplacian reflect the combinatorial structure of the persistence diagram.

papers.title: Kinetic moment estimates and a one-sided Lyapunov barrier for the relativistic fermionic Michie-King equation
papers.abstract: We study the cutoff Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR), or relativistic fermionic Michie--King, equation of state along an equilibrium family with fixed Tolman--Klein invariants. Three kinetic moments give exact formulas for both the pressure-to-density ratio and the derivative of pressure. Cauchy--Schwarz yields a global relation between these two quantities. It implies vertical vector-field domination of the associated Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff system by the linear equation of state $P=ρc^2/\sqrt3$ in the physical wedge $0<y\leq3x$. We construct a filled, one-sided version of the Bors--Stańczy Lyapunov barrier and check every boundary. This controls all outward excursions, including those after a lower exit from a Lyapunov sublevel. For regular configurations the resulting explicit Lambert bound is $2Gm(r)/(rc^2)<0.6879212521$. Using the diagonal where this ratio has a stationary value sharpens the bound to $0.6734385929$. The argument is conditional on a regular TOV configuration and does not require a separate finite-radius existence theorem. We also identify and correct a logarithmic coefficient in the previously used explicit linear-comparator formula.

papers.title: Associative operators and their iterated lifts: classification and cocycle identities
papers.abstract: The inverse problem of an inhomogeneous functional equation asks for which right-hand sides the equation is solvable. For the Cauchy equation and for the quadratic equation a necessary condition is a cocycle identity, and the two identities have a common form. We take this form as a definition. An operator from functions of one variable to functions of two variables can be lifted to functions of several variables, one argument at a time. We call it associative when its two iterated lifts from one variable to three coincide, that is, when every function in its image satisfies the corresponding cocycle identity. Composition with an associative binary operation is the model case. The Cauchy difference, the d'Alembert operator and the Jordan-von Neumann operator are associative as well. We prove that all iterated lifts of the same length of an associative operator coincide. Over abelian groups we classify, under suitable hypotheses, the associative integer combinations of translations, embeddings and the evaluation at the origin. For a composition operator the cocycle identity characterises the image over monoids and over bands. Over an arbitrary semigroup we reduce this question to the injectivity of a canonical map.

papers.title: Fermat costs and path-dependent first-passage percolation
papers.abstract: We introduce a path-dependent and space-inhomogeneous first-passage percolation (FPP) model in the continuum. Inspired by Euclidean FPP, it is defined through a sample of points drawn from a common density function on a Riemannian manifold. In Euclidean FPP, the cost of each step in a discrete path is given by its length raised to the power $α>1$. In our model, the power $α$ increases as the path progresses, governed by a control mechanism. Consequently, the resulting percolation cost is not a distance. However, we prove a shape theorem showing that, as the number of points goes to infinity, the percolation costs converge to deterministic space-time integrals along curves in the manifold. This limit defines a quasi-distance with the property that traversing a curve from a high-density region towards a low-density one is generally cheaper than in the reverse direction; thus highlighting its potential use in machine learning applications.

papers.title: A filtered basis for Haiman ideals
papers.abstract: Given the polynomial ring $R=\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n, y_1, \dots, y_n]$, we consider the Haiman ideal $J(d)$ of polynomials that vanish to order $d$ on the diagonals. We define a rotational order on monomials and use it to construct a filtration on $J(d)$ and a bigraded, homogeneous, free $\mathbb{C}[\mathbf{y}]$-basis compatible with this filtration. This gives a new independent proof that $J(d)$ is free over $y$'s. We also discuss the connections between this filtration and triply-graded link homology.

papers.title: Low-slope Lefschetz fibrations with finitely presented fundamental groups
papers.abstract: We prove that for any finitely presented group $G$, there exists a genus-$3k (k\in \Z)$ Lefschetz fibration over the two-sphere having slope as close as desired to $2$ and the fundamental group of the total space is isomorphic to given group $G$. These are the first examples not satisfying the slope inequality with total spaces being non-simply connected. As a corollary, by taking fiber sum of these Lefschetz fibrations with trivial genus-$3k$ Lefschetz fibration over any genus-$h(>0)$ (positive genus) surfaces, we obtain Lefschetz fibrations having slope arbitrarily close to $2$ with different fundamental groups over any genus-$h$ surface.

papers.title: Recurrence formulas for Taylor expansions at CM points on genus-one and genus-two Shimura curves
papers.abstract: We establish a general differential equation relating the expansion of a weight-two eigenform $f$ on a Shimura curve to the Schwarzian derivative $\mathcal{R}$ associated with $f$. When the quotient $X/W$ has genus zero, we introduce a Hauptmodul $u$ and obtain a coupled system of differential equations involving $f$, $\mathcal{R}$, and $u$. Geometric information, including local constraints on the poles of $\mathcal{R}$, together with the initial coefficients of the expansion of $f$, determine all the parameters in the system. We apply this method to all twelve weight-two eigenforms on Shimura curves $X_0^N(1)$ of genus one or two, obtaining explicit recurrence formulas for their Taylor expansions at selected CM points, conditional on the numerically recognized initial coefficients. As an application, we use the coefficients obtained from the recurrence to compute the Shimura uniformization $Φ: \operatorname{Jac}(X)\to E$ to high precision and identify a large family of CM points on the associated elliptic curves $E$.

papers.title: Reduction types of curves in tame extensions
papers.abstract: Let $C/K$ be a curve of genus $g\geq 1$ over a discretely valued field $K$ with algebraically closed residue field. In this paper, we study the behaviour of the reduction type of $C$ under finite tame extensions. If $L/K$ is a tame extension of degree $n$, we give sufficient conditions on the reduction type $R$ of $C$ so that the reduction type of the base change $C_L$ is uniquely determined by $R$ and $n$. In particular, if $C$ has abelian and toric ranks zero, then $R$ satisfies these conditions. We also give an algorithm to compute the possibilities for the reduction type of $C_L$ given only $R$ and $n$. The main method involves studying harmonic covers of graphs with a cyclic action. As a result, we obtain a characterisation of tame curves with potentially good reduction in terms of their reduction type, and a new proof of a result by Liu-Lorenzini-Raynaud regarding the non-realisability of certain reduction types.

papers.title: Epidemic random model under vaccination regime and non-permanent immunity driven by time-changed Levy noise
papers.abstract: A random version of the Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Vaccinated (SIRV) epidemic model with non-permanent immunity and a population of non-constant size is studied. The compartments satisfy a system of differential equations in which the contact rate is a random coefficient, and the contact rate itself is driven by a stochastic differential equation with time-changed Levy noise. This noise is constructed from a conditional Brownian motion and a doubly stochastic Poisson random field, both governed by a stochastic clock. When the clock is independent of the Brownian and Poisson components, the two parts of the noise are a time-changed Brownian motion and a time-changed Poisson random measure. The equation for the contact rate decouples from the compartment equations and enters them as a random parameter, which allows the compartments to be treated pathwise. The existence, uniqueness, and positivity of the global solution are proven, and the basic reproduction number of the model is shown to be random. Furthermore, sufficient conditions for extinction and persistence in mean of the disease are derived. The conditions are expressed in terms of the parameters of the model and two long-run characteristics.

papers.title: Generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg and related inequalities for Grushin-type gradients
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for a generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality involving the Grushin-type gradient $
abla_G=(
abla_x,|x|^α
abla_y)$, where $α\geq0$, in arbitrary dimensions. When $α=0$, our results recover the classical Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequalities and extend the mixed radial and cylindrical weight inequalities of Li and Yan \cite{LY23} to arbitrary dimensions of the $y$ variables. Our approach combines a change of variables with approximation arguments to reduce the Grushin inequalities to Euclidean inequalities with mixed weights. We also characterize the admissible parameters in Hardy--Sobolev inequalities, including the endpoint cases $p=1$ and $q=p$, and derive multiplicative Sobolev and Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequalities. Finally, we establish a weighted Moser--Trudinger inequality on bounded domains and deduce exponential integrability for subcritical growth with arbitrary locally integrable cylindrical power weights. By letting $α=0$, our results also yield the corresponding inequalities for the Euclidean gradient.

papers.title: The minimax value of outcome feedback in budget-constrained adaptive sampling
papers.abstract: Whether adaptivity improves estimation is a classical question in sequential design and information-based complexity. In practice, adaptive data collection can use two different kinds of information: process data on whether each contact succeeded, and the observed outcomes themselves. How much each kind is worth in the worst case under a hard budget has not been settled. We study this question for estimating a common Bernoulli mean through channels with unknown response probabilities and known costs, where failed contacts are charged and the budget must hold on every sample path. We compare static designs, designs that adapt to response indicators only, and fully adaptive designs, each with an arbitrary estimator. Our main theorem shows that when the costs are invariant under a group of channel permutations acting transitively on the nuisance parameter, outcome-adaptive allocation has zero minimax value: response-adaptive and fully adaptive designs have the same minimax risk, given by a one-dimensional optimization and attained by an explicit least-favourable prior and equalizer rule. For two contacts we obtain a closed-form criterion for when response feedback strictly improves on every static design. An unequal-cost example with a computer-certified exact saddle shows that the same conclusion can hold without symmetry, even though no product prior is least favourable there. A correlated prior shows that outcome feedback can still reduce Bayes risk, so the equivalence is genuinely minimax. In this idealized setting, the results support responsive survey designs that adapt to paradata but not to outcomes.

papers.title: A Note on the Topos-Inadmissibility of Free Heyting Algebras
papers.abstract: Yiqi Xu and Linguan Ye have recently settled the long-standing open question about which Heyting algebras are topos-admissible, that is, occur as the truth values of some topos. They prove that free Heyting algebras with two or more generators are not topos admissible. Their proof has been simplified by Zoltan Kocsis and by Sam van Gool. Here I make some further simplifications, emphasising algebraic methods over Kripke semantics and in particular the use of Sierpiński cones of Heyting algebras.

papers.title: Hermitian connections and holonomy with parallel torsions
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g,J)$ be a connected Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n\geq2$, and let $\nabla$ be a Hermitian connection with nonzero parallel torsion. Assuming that its restricted holonomy acts irreducibly on $T^{1,0}M$, the author proved that the first Ricci curvature must vanish. In this paper we derive a Berger like complete list of its holonomy representations: the complexified adjoint representation of a compact simple Lie algebra, and the standard seven-dimensional complex representation of compact $\Gtwo$. Curvature of such a connection is proven to be parallel. Secondly, without irreducibility assumption, we derive an explicit local normal form for the metric whose Chern connection has parallel trosion, which includes holomorphic warpings and nontrivial holomorphic extensions of hyperkähler manifolds. For complete metrics with bounded Chern curvature, the characters associated with nontrivial global restricted-holonomy blocks vanish. Compact metrics admit an unwarped local form, are balanced, and have a unimodular vertical Lie algebra. On their universal covers, suitable Kähler factors split off and the remaining factor has vanishing first Chern Ricci form. A compact simply connected elliptic bundle over a K3 surface explains why this local classification does not give a global product classification. This extends the classification result of Zheng and author on Hermitian manifolds whose Chern connection is Ambrose-Singer. In particular, the analysis shows that if the metric is not Kähler its Chern curvature must satisfies $\Rm_{(\cdot), (\cdot)}X=0$ for some parallel nonzero vector $X\in T'M$. In appendix we include a by-product: On a compact complex homogenous space $M$ with finite fundamental group, any Hermitian metric whose Chern connection has parallel torsion, must be Kähler.

papers.title: The Thue-Morse route to chaos in the open quantum baker map
papers.abstract: We study the resonances of the quantum baker map opened by a window of width $w$ centred at $q_c$. For $q_c=1/2$ the survivor set of the classical doubling map with a hole goes from zero to positive topological entropy along the Thue-Morse route, and we find numerically, for $N$ up to $2^{25}$, that the resonance spectrum follows this route step by step, also where the entropy is zero. Below the threshold $w_c=4a^*-1$, with $a^*$ the Thue-Morse constant, the surviving cycles have periods $2^ν$ and their thresholds accumulate doubly exponentially. Each cycle gives, as isolated orbits do, a multiplet of resonances close to modulus $2^{-1/2}$, with phases set by its action. Since a cycle is resolved only if its period is shorter than about $\log_2 N$, twice the Ehrenfest time, about $\log_2\log_2 N$ steps are resolved, four at our largest sizes. Near $w_c$ the 16-cycle perturbs the 8-multiplet through a return path that classically opens only at $w_c$. Cutting a few sites of this path removes the perturbation. At $w_c$ the leading resonance jumps within one or two lattice sites, since a window one site wider than the threshold already has an entropy of order $1/\log_2 N$. One site or more above $w_c$ it lies between 0.93 and 1.00 times the value set by the topological pressure, with no free parameter. There the Walsh eigenvalue count grows with the fractal Weyl exponent, and the Fourier count with an exponent a few hundredths smaller at the sizes we reach.

papers.title: Adaptive Precision Incomplete Matrix Factorization
papers.abstract: Incomplete factorizations are widely used to precondition Krylov subspace methods for solving large sparse linear systems. Recent work has explored computing approximate factorizations in low precision, but using only one uniformly low precision limits the achievable accuracy and can degrade the quality of the preconditioner. We propose adaptive precision incomplete factorization algorithms in which we store each entry of the factors in a precision chosen according to its magnitude and a target accuracy. We present a rounding error analysis showing that the adaptive precision threshold-based incomplete LU and incomplete Cholesky factorizations achieve a backward error of the order of the target accuracy. We also discuss how to incorporate pivoting and scaling and how to perform the triangular solves with the adaptive precision factors. Finally, we explain how the approach applies to memory-limited incomplete Cholesky factorizations by using the magnitude of the largest dropped entry as the target accuracy. Numerical experiments on a wide range of matrices from the SuiteSparse collection show that adaptive precision can substantially reduce the storage required by the factors without degrading the quality of the preconditioner and improve the storage-weighted iteration count and overall storage required compared with uniform 64-, 32-, and 16-bit factorizations.

papers.title: Dense ideals in forcing extensions of Nairian models
papers.abstract: Complementing the work of Blue, Larson, and Sargsyan~\cite{NM,NM2}, we obtain forcing extensions of minimal Nairian models in which the Axiom of Choice and the Generalized Continuum Hypothesis hold. In these extensions, every uncountable regular cardinal $κ$ carries a precipitous, uniform, $κ$-dense ideal $\mathcal{I}_κ$. In fact, $\mathcal P(κ)/\mathcal{I}_κ$ is isomorphic to the regular open algebra of $\textrm{Col}(ω,κ)$. This extends Woodin's theorem on the existence of $ω_1$-dense ideals on $ω_1$ in forcing extensions of models of $Θ_{\rm reg}$ \cite[Section~2.3]{ASTWZ24}, where $Θ_{\rm reg}$ denotes the theory $\textrm{ZF}+\textrm{AD}_{\mathbb R}+\text{``$Θ$ is regular''}$. Moreover, our work places the consistency strength of the aforementioned theory on generic embeddings below a Woodin cardinal that is a limit of Woodin cardinals, and also complements the seminal work of Eskew and Hayut~\cite{EH24}.

papers.title: The index from a super-point
papers.abstract: We extend the algebro-geometric construction of filtered graded rings that encode both the Higgs branch and the Macdonald index of 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories to theories whose Schur sector contains fermionic generators. The rings are then $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded-commutative, and the index is reproduced by the Hilbert series of a generalized arc space, whose defining ideal may contain relations among the generators and their derivatives. We study the free $\mathcal{N}=2$ vector multiplet, $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills with gauge algebras $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, and the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ SCFT. For the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, the ideal is the sum of the Jacobian ideals of a single superpotential and of its two supersymmetry variations. For $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills, the ideal is similarly the sum of the Jacobian ideals of the components of a single $\mathcal{N}=4$ superfield, which is a singlet of the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ flavor symmetry for gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and a triplet for $\mathfrak{su}(3)$. The associated VOA for the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ theory is given by the Feigin--Feigin--Tipunin $\mathcal{A}(6)$ algebra. The arc space of Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of $\mathcal{A}(6)$ does not reproduce the vacuum character, and therefore $\mathcal{A}(6)$ is not classically free. Supplementing Zhu's $C_2$-algebra by three relations in the first jet ring, the generalized arc space reproduces the Macdonald index of $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ up to, at least, order $q^{51}$.

papers.title: A proof of the weighted Böttcher-Wenzel inequality conjectured by Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński
papers.abstract: For a positive definite matrix $ω$ with two smallest eigenvalues $λ_1\leλ_2$ and the weighted Frobenius norm $\|X\|_ω^2=\mathrm{Tr}(X^*Xω)$, Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński conjectured that $\|[A,B]\|_ω^2\le\frac{λ_1+λ_2}{λ_1λ_2}\|A\|_ω^2\|B\|_ω^2$ for all complex matrices $A,B$. We prove this inequality for real and for complex matrices of every size, by a short computer-free argument, and we determine the cases of equality. In fact $\|XZY-YZX\|_2\le\|Z\|_{(2),2}\|X\|_2\|Y\|_2$ for all complex matrices of compatible sizes, where $\|Z\|_{(2),2}$ is the Ky Fan $(2),2$ norm (the $\ell^2$ norm of the two largest singular values), and the constant is attained unless $X$ and $Y$ are $1\times1$ matrices; the conjecture is the case $Z=ω^{-1/2}$. The best constant is the square of a unitarily invariant norm of $Z$, which is convex, so it suffices to treat weights whose $n-1$ largest eigenvalues coincide. For these, an inequality for one matrix and a pair of unit vectors, written in bases adapted to the pair of unit vectors, reduces the conjecture to the positive semidefiniteness of an explicit $4\times4$ Hermitian matrix depending on a $2\times2$ matrix $B$ in a convex set defined by two weighted operator-norm bounds, and an explicit determinant identity writes its determinant as a sum of products of factors that are visibly nonnegative; the phases of the entries of $B$ enter only through $|\det B|^2$, so the real case is literally a special case. As a second theorem we prove, for every weight, a strengthening of the conjecture that is equivalent to the inequality for one matrix and all pairs of unit vectors; its best constant is again a convex function of $ω^{-1/2}$, and the same argument applies. We also read the inequality as a sharp bound for inner derivations on the GNS space of a faithful state.

papers.title: Rollout Scheduling for Chaotic Neural ODEs: Coverage Gains, Computational Cost, and Predictive Accuracy
papers.abstract: Training Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs) on chaotic systems is difficult because small changes in model parameters can lead to rapidly growing differences in predictions. A rollout is a trajectory predicted by the model. Choosing its length from a single global Lyapunov time overlooks differences in local instability. We study rollout scheduling for training on one contiguous rollout per sampled state, asking whether adapting its length to local instability improves prediction. We find the schedule that uses the most trajectory data under an instability budget, a limit on how much instability any one rollout may accumulate. Under stated assumptions, we bound the resulting coverage gain and the coverage lost when the instability estimates are in error. Numerical checks illustrate the theory. Training experiments on Lorenz-63, Lorenz-96, and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky compare adaptive and constant schedules at the same instability budgets and maximum rollout lengths. The budgets are computed from the true system's finite-time Lyapunov exponents. Across the tested settings, adaptive schedules increase trajectory coverage at additional computational cost, without showing a consistent improvement in prediction accuracy. On Lorenz-63, limiting adaptive rollouts to the horizon used to estimate instability improves prediction at the larger budgets. On Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, most configurations provide useful short-time predictions, while all tested long rollouts eventually fail. These findings show why coverage, prediction accuracy, and long-time behavior need separate evaluation, and why instability estimates should be checked over the windows used in training.

papers.title: Leavitt path algebras, growth series, Thompson groups
papers.abstract: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Martín Barquero, Martín González, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.

papers.title: Generalized Fundamental Theorem of Calculus on a Regular Time Scale
papers.abstract: The main objectives of this paper can be summarized as, giving a fundamental theorem on a regular time scale as well as illustrating that applications are possible on a homogeneous time scale.

papers.title: Correspondence between orbit equivalences and exact symplectomorphisms for Anosov flows
papers.abstract: We show that for a closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, two Anosov flows are orbital equivalent if and only if the corresponding Anosov Liouville structures are exact symplectomorphic.

papers.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous étale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $Ω_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{ét}}(k)$, where $Ω_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor. In this note, using the Dwyer-Greenlees equivalence between $\ell$-completed objects and $\ell$-torsion objects, we prove that $Ω_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{ét}}(k)$, and consequently, based on Kahn's early work, the Tate conjecture at positive characteristics.

papers.title: Density Regularity from Derivative Growth of Cauchy-Type Integrals
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between the behavior of the derivative of a Cauchy-type integral near the curve of integration and the regularity of its density. We consider Jordan curves and Jordan arcs composed of finitely many regular $C^1$ arcs meeting at nondegenerate angles. For a Cauchy-type integral with continuous density, we establish an inverse estimate: if the growth of its derivative off the curve is controlled by a continuous integrable function of the distance to the curve that is nonincreasing near zero, then the modulus of continuity of the density at scale $h$ is bounded by the integral of this majorant over $(0,h)$. As a consequence, we prove that power-law decay of the derivative as the curve is approached forces the density to be constant. For Jordan curves, combining the inverse and direct estimates yields a criterion for Hölder continuity of the density in terms of the growth of the derivative of the integral. We then apply this criterion to characterize the Hölder regularity of analytic functions in bounded Jordan domains whose boundaries satisfy the same geometric assumptions. The proof relies on uniformly transverse shifts of local subarcs and a symmetric jump formula.

papers.title: Sharp Simultaneous Asymptotic Expansions for Sample-Mean Operators from Natural Exponential Families
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of positive linear operators constructed from sample means of natural exponential families parametrized by their means. We show that the variance function $V$ determines the entire hierarchy of cumulants, central moments, and coefficient differential operators $A_r[V]$ governing the asymptotic expansions. The cumulants satisfy the recursion $κ_{j+1}=Vκ_j'$, whereas the central moments are expressed in terms of partial Bell polynomials. Quantitative expansions of arbitrary order, uniform on compact subsets of the mean domain, are obtained. We also establish simultaneous expansions for the derivatives $(L_nf)^{(\ell)}$, with an explicit remainder estimate in terms of the modulus of continuity of the highest derivative. We prove that $C^{2N+\ell}$-smoothness is sufficient for the expansion of the derivative of order $\ell$ up to and including the term of order $n^{-N}$. The Gauss-Weierstrass operators show that, within the scale of spaces $C^m$, this smoothness threshold cannot generally be lowered and that the order of the modulus-of-continuity term is optimal. The general framework is applied to the Bernstein, Szász-Mirakjan, Baskakov, Post-Widder, and Gauss-Weierstrass operators.

papers.title: Geometric foundations of mesoscopic nucleation theory: commutativity of kinetic and probabilistic reduction for the Dean-Kawasaki equation
papers.abstract: The reduction of a stochastic field equation to a few degrees of freedom is a central problem in many areas of physics, applied mathematics and engineering. In this work we present two routes for the dimensional reduction of conservative stochastic partial differential equations of Dean-Kawasaki type. To our knowledge, such reductions have always been carried out at the level of the trajectories, i.e. on Dean's equation, and never at the level of the probability distribution, i.e. on Kawasaki's equation. The first route starts from the parametrisation of the density introduced by Lutsko [J. F. Lutsko, J. Chem. Phys. 136, 034509 (2012)], who imposed it on the field equation and obtained stochastic equations for the order parameters by integrating against a suitable weight. The second route, which reduces Kawasaki's equation, is new. This route averages the functional forward Kolmogorov equation over the fast transverse degrees of freedom, using Fermi tubular coordinates around the manifold. Since the equations of Dean and Kawasaki are formally equivalent, one would expect both reductions to be equivalent as well. We show that this is not the case. In particular, we prove that the two reduced generators coincide if and only if the noise-induced drift corrections arising along each route, which we call anomalies, are equal, and that this condition fails in general. For noise regularised over a correlation length $δ$ on a spherical domain, the mismatch diverges as $δ^{-1}$ for the ideal gas and, under a closure of the transverse dynamics, as $δ^{-3}$ for a fluid with a local excess free energy, the latter order being set by the closure. Finally, we show that, under the same closure, regularity hypotheses and the normalisation $\varepsilon^2 = N^{-1}$, the two reduced theories differ after a time $t$ by at most $O(t/nδ^3)$, where $n$ is the mean number density.

papers.title: Measure-class classification of achievable Cantorvals
papers.abstract: An achievable Cantorval is a Cantorval that is the set of subsums of a convergent series of positive terms. We construct an explicit achievable Cantorval whose boundary has Lebesgue measure at least $2\prod_{j\ge 1}(1-2^{-j})=0.5775\ldots$. This answers a question of Gł{ą}b and Prus-Wi{ś}niowski and gives a counterexample to the conjecture of Nowakowski and Prus-Wi{ś}niowski that every achievable Cantorval is standard. The example is generated by a hybrid series of Pratsiovytyi, Vynnyshyn and Vynnyshyn. The lower bound comes from an isolated-digit criterion, which produces a Cantor subset of the boundary whose measure is an explicit infinite product; after rescaling, the boundary measure can be made arbitrarily close to $1$. We also prove that the boundary of every achievement set is either Lebesgue null or has positive measure near each of its points. Consequently, up to homeomorphisms that preserve Lebesgue null sets in both directions, there are exactly two achievable Cantorvals, distinguished by whether the boundary is null. For boundaries of positive measure, the homeomorphism can be chosen so that it changes the normalized boundary measure of every Borel set by a factor arbitrarily close to $1$. For general Cantorvals we classify the case of a relatively clopen boundary support and show that further invariants appear beyond this case. Finally, the null-set preserving self-homeomorphisms of a Cantorval always form a meager subgroup of its homeomorphism group. This subgroup is dense exactly when the support of Lebesgue measure on the boundary is empty or the whole boundary; in particular, it is dense for every achievable Cantorval.

papers.title: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II
papers.abstract: We prove optimal non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in 3D within the class of axially symmetric swirl-free flows. More precisely, we construct two solutions $u_1,u_2$ that have the same initial data $u_1(0)=u_2(0)$, are smooth for every positive time, satisfy the energy identity, and satisfy \[ u_1,u_2\in C_tH_x^α\cap L_t^2H_x^{α+1}\,\,\text{ for every }\,\,0\leqα<1/2,\qquad u_1,u_2\in L_t^\infty L_x^{3,\infty}\cap L_t^{2,\infty}L_x^\infty. \] Thus non-uniqueness holds in optimal Sobolev spaces and critical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin weak spaces, even in a symmetry class where smooth solutions are globally regular. The proof relies on a computer-assisted construction of a linearly unstable forward self-similar solution, starting from the numerical profiles identified in our preceding paper (arXiv:2606.07501). We combine explicit asymptotic expansions and global residual estimates with weak coercivity inequalities stabilized by finitely many functionals. Approximate solutions of auxiliary linear equations yield quantitative inverse bounds, allowing us to correct both the stationary profile and its unstable eigenpair by contraction arguments. The instability and localization theorem proved in arXiv:2606.07501 then produces the non-unique solutions.

papers.title: Hölder continuity of meromorphic functions and equisingularity
papers.abstract: For a complex analytic variety and an exponent between zero and one, we study the sheaf of meromorphic functions that are locally Hölder continuous with that exponent for the outer metric. It sits between the structure sheaves of the seminormalization and of the Lipschitz saturation of Pham and Teissier. We prove that these sheaves are coherent and that only finitely many of them are distinct, the exponents at which they change being rational numbers governed by the Rees valuations of the ideal of a certain diagonal. Each exponent defines a Hölder saturation of the variety. We show that a variety whose Hölder saturation is smooth for some exponent larger than one third is itself smooth and that one third is sharp. For reduced curve germs we compute the Hölder saturations from the characteristic exponents of the branches and give explicit thresholds, in terms of classical invariants, at which they become the seminormalization, the Lipschitz saturation, or a curve of the same multiplicity. We prove that homeomorphic curves are bi-Hölder homeomorphic for some positive exponent, whereas bi-Hölder homeomorphisms with exponent close enough to one preserve the multiplicity. We then introduce the relative Hölder saturation of a family and prove that it specializes to the saturations of the fibers over a dense Zariski-open subset of the base. This leads to two notions of equisingularity for families of complex analytic varieties, Hölder equisingularity, defined by a bi-Hölder trivialization, and the stronger Hölder equisaturation, defined by the triviality of the relative saturation. For families of reduced curve germs we show that they interpolate between topological, Whitney and Lipschitz equisingularity, with explicit exponents depending only on the invariants of the special fiber.

papers.title: Localization of weakly integral objects in braided fusion categories
papers.abstract: An object $X$ of a braided fusion category is called weakly integral if $\mathrm{FPdim}(X)^2$ is an integer. We prove that every nonzero weakly integral object admits a localization, that is, a Yang-Baxter operator $R$ on a finite-dimensional vector space $W$ such that, for every $n$, the algebra homomorphisms from the group algebra of the braid group $B_n$ to $\mathrm{End}(W^{\otimes n})$ and to $\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})$, defined by $R$ and by the braiding, have the same kernel. The operator $R$ can be chosen unitary when the braided fusion category is unitary. This proves the 'if' direction of a conjecture of Rowell and Wang, motivated by topological quantum computation, which states that a simple object admits a localization if and only if it is weakly integral. For a simple weakly integral object of a unitary braided fusion category, the operator $R$ that we construct has an enhancement in the sense of Turaev, and the resulting knot invariant is the Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant of knots colored by $X$.

papers.title: Convergence of a finite element Chorin projection method for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We analyze a fully discrete finite element projection method for the stochastic incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and multiplicative noise. We show solvability and uniform moment estimates for the intermediate and the corrected velocity approximations under the assumption that the initial data is square-integrable and divergence free, and that the deterministic forcing term is bounded in $L^{q}(0,T;H^{-1}(D))$ for a sufficiently large $q$. Under standard stability and approximation assumptions on the finite element spaces and a coupling condition on the spatial and temporal discretization parameters, we prove convergence of a subsequence to a martingale solution of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations. The analysis combines the complementary spatial and temporal estimates of the predicted and the corrected velocity approximations and uses the numerical dissipation to identify their common limit. We establish tightness of the piecewise constant temporal interpolations of the velocity field approximations using Aldous' criterion combined with the uniform discrete moment estimates. The convergence result holds in two and three space dimensions as it does not rely on any additional regularity of the limiting martingale solution beyond the one naturally available from the energy inequality. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the scheme in numerical experiments in two space dimensions for smooth and vortex sheet initial data.

papers.title: A proof of the polygonal Faber--Krahn inequality
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every integer $n\ge3$, the regular $n$-gon uniquely minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, up to congruence, among simple polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides. We also obtain the optimal linear correction when fewer than $n$ sides are present. The proof combines a partition into convex cells with a mixed boundary comparison. Among convex polygons of fixed area and fixed sum of base angles less than $π$, the isosceles triangle minimizes the first eigenvalue with Dirichlet conditions on the base and Neumann conditions elsewhere. A comparison of Fourier transforms of conformal area densities proves this inequality and the corresponding upper bounds for inverse spectral moments of integer order at least two. We prove strict log-convexity of an interpolation of the eigenvalues of regular polygons of unit area for real parameters at least four. We then derive sharp hexagonal bounds for periodic convex polygonal tilings and asymptotic bounds for convex polygonal partitions of a fixed convex polygon, with an explicit correction for boundary junctions.

papers.title: All stable Schoen--Wolfson cones are minimizing
papers.abstract: In the late nineties, R.~Schoen and J.~Wolfson studied the problem of minimizing the area among Lagrangian surfaces in a Riemannian symplectic $4$-manifold. In their parametric approach, they showed that minimizers are smoothly branched-immersed away from a discrete set of points, where there exists a nonflat tangent cone minimizing the area among Lagrangian disk competitors. They also classified the stable singular cones into a family $C_{p,p+1}$ indexed by a positive integer $p$, but left open the question of which of them are globally minimizing. We settle this question by showing that for each $p \geq 1$, $C_{p,p+1} \cap B_1$ minimizes the area among Lagrangian disks spanning its boundary with degree one.

papers.title: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
papers.abstract: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time. The complexity of deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible for every fixed $k\geq 3$ has been a long-standing open problem. We prove that deciding whether a tournament is 3-inducible is NP-complete and then leverage this result to show that deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible is NP-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. Our results imply that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs.

papers.title: Differential Transmutations and First-Passage Expansions for Monomial Brownian Boundaries
papers.abstract: Let $P_t=\exp(t\partial_x^2/2)$ be the heat semigroup and let $F(t)=ρt^p$, where $p\ge2$ is an integer. Previous transported-zero theory associates with this boundary a constant-flux solution annihilated by a polynomial-coefficient differential operator of order $2p-1$. We show that the same differential structure contains the complete formal perturbation expansion of the Brownian first-passage density to $F$. For $N=2p-1$ we construct graded spatial operators \[ \mathcal A_r^{(p)}x^n= \frac{(-1)^r}{r!} \frac{\prod_{j=0}^{pr-1}(n+2j+1)} {\prod_{j=1}^{Nr}(n+j)}x^{n+Nr} \] and prove the Laplace conjugacy \[ \mathscr L\mathcal A_r^{(p)}\mathscr L^{-1} =\frac{(-1)^r}{r!}k^r \left(-\frac1k\frac{d}{dk}\right)^{pr}. \] Consequently, the inverse spatial transmutation applied to a reflected Dirac mass generates, coefficient by coefficient, the unique formal solution of the exponential-martingale transform equation for first passage. The cubic case is developed explicitly and checked algebraically through fifth order. We also explain how this differential construction and the independently developed Wright--Volterra generalized-image construction represent the same first-passage law in different coordinates. The present result is formal at all orders; convergence of the resulting perturbation series is left as a separate analytic problem.

papers.title: Yau's pinching problem and vanishing of Betti numbers
papers.abstract: We prove that a closed connected Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq4$, satisfying $\sec>\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$ at every point has vanishing real cohomology in degrees $1,..., n-1$. It is consequently a rational homology sphere if $n$ is odd or the manifold is orientable. Complex projective space shows that the coefficient is optimal and that the strict inequality is necessary in every even dimension. The required estimate for the Weitzenböck curvature term is established by integrating restricted Ricci operators over orthonormal frames and combining complementary degrees using Hodge duality. This also allows us to replace sectional curvature pinching by intermediate Ricci curvature bounds. For a nonflat metric, the weak Yau inequality, $\sec\geq\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$, gives the same cohomology vanishing unless the manifold is isometric, up to scaling, to a quotient of complex projective space with its Fubini-Study metric. This also holds using the second intermediate Ricci curvature in place of sectional curvature. More generally, a nonzero Betti number in the range controlled by an intermediate Ricci bound forces local symmetry. We also derive sharp Hodge eigenvalue estimates and a scalar spectral vanishing criterion.

papers.title: Weighted sum commuting maps with the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ denote the algebra of all $n\times n$ complex matrices, where $n\geq2$, and let $Δ_{f,g}$ be the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform associated with nonnegative continuous functions $f,g$ on $[0,\infty)$ satisfying $f(t)g(t)=t$ for all $t\geq0$. In this paper, we characterize all surjective maps $Φ:\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C}) \to\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfying\[Φ(Δ_{f,g}(αA+βB))=Δ_{f,g}(αΦ(A)+βΦ(B))\]for all $A,B\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$, where $α,β$ are fixed nonzero real numbers. Without assuming additivity or linearity, we prove that when $f$ is nonconstant, $Φ$ must be of the form $Φ(A)=cUAU^*$ or $Φ(A)=cU\overline{A}U^*$ for all $A$, where $U$ is a fixed unitary matrix, $\overline{A}$ denotes the entrywise complex conjugate of $A$, and $c$ is a nonzero complex scalar. Moreover, we completely determine the possible values of $|c|$, which form either $\{1\}$, $q^{\mathbb{Z}}$ for some $q>1$, or $(0,\infty)$. When $f$ is constant, we show that $Φ(A)=S(A)+D$ for all $A$, where $S$ is a surjective $\mathbb{Q}(α,β)$-linear map and $D\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfies $(α+β-1)D=0$.

papers.title: Minkowski Correlation Functions (MCF): Long-range, robust shape descriptors for point patterns
papers.abstract: A morphometric analysis of point patterns using Minkowski functionals is short-sighted, whereas correlation functions do not provide robust, i.e., additive shape descriptors. To combine the advantages of both standard techniques and to overcome their weaknesses, we introduce ring-based Minkowski correlation functions (MCFs) as robust and sensitive descriptors of disordered point patterns. By assigning to each point a spherical shell and quantifying the resulting two-phase morphology via Minkowski functionals, MCFs capture structural information across multiple length scales, remain sensitive at radii where conventional disk-based Minkowski functionals have saturated, and implicitly encode higher-order correlations beyond the pair correlation and structure factor. We present an exact and efficient algorithm for planar patterns extending the established disk-based morphological approach to long ranges. Applications across scales -- active colloids (Quincke rollers), longleaf pine trees, and the Hubble Ultra Deep Field -- demonstrate clear and systematic deviations from homogeneous Poisson references, with distinct responses of covered area, boundary length, and Euler characteristic. The approach combines short computation times, robustness to noise, and straightforward edge handling with clear interpretability as low-dimensional functions of the outer ring radius.

papers.title: Freedom is all you need
papers.abstract: The functional calculus allows for the rigorous analysis of functions of matrices or even operators. The free functional calculus gives the natural class of functions over any category. We initiate the representation theory for taking a generic free functional calculus to the classical nc functional calculus going back to Taylor, Voiculescu and many others, with an eye towards learning of categories. The functional calculus on direct sum closed and locally similarity (i.e. change of coordinates) invariant domains inherits the niceties of complex analysis and large-scale parallel networks, such as automatic analyticity, free universal monodromy, which gives a hypothetical explanation for beneficial overfitting.

papers.title: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
papers.abstract: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.

papers.title: Intervals of limit points for $B_α$-spectral radii
papers.abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let \[ B_α(G)=αA(G)+(1-α)L(G)=(1-α)D(G)+(2α-1)A(G),\qquad 0\leq α\leq 1. \] We study the limit points of the spectral radii of these matrices. Put $a_α=1-α$, $b_α=|2α-1|$, and $w_α=a_α+b_α$. We prove that, for every $α\neq 1/2$ and every integer $d\geq 3$, the interval \[ \left[a_αd+2b_α\sqrt{d-1},\,w_αd\right] \] consists entirely of $B_α$-limit points. All these points are realized by connected bipartite graphs of maximum degree at most $d$. We extend the induced-subgraph interpolation of Alon and Wei from $A$ to $aD+bA$, and obtain a unified proof using bipartite Ramanujan graphs. Consecutive intervals overlap for large $d$; hence the set of $B_α$-limit points contains a half-line for every $α\neq 1/2$. At $α=1/2$, one has $B_{1/2}=D/2$, and the set of spectral radii is discrete. Combining uniform edge subdivisions with generalized Bethe decorations, we improve the Laplacian and signless Laplacian half-line to $[29/5,\infty)$, verified by an exact rational certificate. We also treat two complementary tree constructions. For the starlike trees $T_{1,m,m}$, the limiting $B_α$-spectral radius is the unique solution above the path threshold of an explicit unsquared equation. More generally, letting selected arms of a starlike tree tend to infinity produces ordered limit points with tree realizations. Finally, we give the exact affine relations among $B_α$, the $A_β$-matrix, and the deformed Laplacian. These identify which tree and caterpillar results are reparametrizations of earlier work. The interval theorem also yields half-lines of $A_β$-limit points for every $0\leβ<1$, and of deformed-Laplacian limit points for every nonzero deformation parameter.

papers.title: Star Triangulations
papers.abstract: We study full triangulations of planar point configurations consisting of $n$ points in convex position and one point in the interior, assuming that no three points are collinear (star configurations). Our main contribution is a classification of the star configurations up to combinatorial equivalence. We show that there are $2^{n-1}-n$ equivalence classes, by establishing a bijection between a star configuration and a particular Young diagram. By transforming each such Young diagram to a binary sequence, we manage to also give a combinatorial description of the orbits of these star configurations under the dihedral group action, encoding each such orbit through a black-and-white bracelet. For each star configuration, we derive an explicit formula for the number of its full triangulations, expressed in terms of Catalan numbers and the parts of the associated Young diagram. Additionally we derive a formula of these full triangulations expressed only in terms of Catalan numbers and the bead structure of the associated bracelet. Finally, we let the points move freely under the restriction that they stay in a star configuration and show that there exist $\binom{2n-3}{n-3}$ topologically distinct full triangulations.

papers.title: Ehrhard-Type inequalities for radial measures
papers.abstract: We study Ehrhard-type inequalities for convex sets under rotationally invariant probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge2$, described by a radial density profile $\varphi$. We give sufficient conditions on the profile that apply to Gaussian and multivariate Student measures, including the Cauchy measure, and to a family of mixtures of two Student measures. We also prove necessary conditions on the profile and its tails. Together, these conditions determine the exact parameter range for this mixture family and characterize the rotationally invariant stable measures satisfying the inequality.

papers.title: The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids
papers.abstract: We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$. While this might appear to follow from the edge-expansion properties established by Anari, Liu, Gharan and Vinzant (STOC'19), we show that this inutition is false by constructing a graph $G$ with edge-expansion at least $1$ for which sampling two random vertices does \emph{not} give a constant-factor approximation to its diameter. We turn to finding $k\geq 2$ maximally-diverse bases of a matroid, the $k$ (max--min) diversity problem. When $k=2$, the problem is solvable via matroid intersection. However, for $k\geq 3$ no polynomial-time approximation or hardness is known, even for diverse spanning trees. We show that sampling $k\geq 3$ bases provides a tight $Θ(\log k)$ approximation. We then combine structural insights about the local density of $\mathcal{G}(M)$ with classical LP-rounding techniques to obtain a polynomial-time $1/6$-approximation algorithm for the $k$-diversity problem in arbitrary matroids, the first constant-factor polynomial-time approximation for max--min diversity on any matroid. A key ingredient for our result is the \emph{Farthest Matroid Basis} problem: given a collection of bases, find a new basis as far as possible from all of them. We give a polynomial-time $1/3$-approximation algorithm for this, which is our main algorithmic primitive for $k$ max--min diversity. We also show it is $W[1]$-hard when parameterized by the optimal distance. We also improve the $1/6$-approximation for $k$-diversity, for partition matroids and graphic matroids of constant arboricity.

papers.title: A Coats-Based Formulation for Multiphase Reactive Transport Accounting for Aqueous Phase Disappearance
papers.abstract: As part of the energy transition, underground hydrogen (H2) storage in porous media has emerged as an alternative solution for large-scale energy storage to salt caverns. Assessing the feasibility of such systems and ensuring their operation requires accurate modeling of the geochemical processes that may alter the composition of the stored gas. This results in a highly nonlinear coupled system of partial differential equations, ordinary differential equations, and algebraic constraints, calling for robust and specialized numerical strategies. In this work, we adopt a Globally Implicit Approach (GIA), as sequential solution algorithms are known to introduce splitting errors due to the decoupling of flow and geochemical processes. In addition, most splitting-based methods implicitly assume the persistent presence of the liquid phase, an assumption that may be violated during gas injection or withdrawal owing to aqueous phase vaporization and mineral precipitation in the vicinity of wells. We extend Coats' formulation to multiphase reactive transport with a rigorous and fully implicit management of aqueous phase disappearance and reappearance. The proposed approach introduces new molar concentration unknowns for basis species that track the re-appearance of the aqueous phase and guarantee the nonsingularity of the Jacobian matrix. Additionally, the appearance of the liquid phase is managed using a multiphase flash calculation algorithm. The proposed algorithm is validated against the CO2 storage benchmark problems. Finally, the approach is applied to an underground H2 storage in an aquifer under cyclic injection and withdrawal conditions.

papers.title: Optimal High-Dimensional Martingale CLTs over Rectangles
papers.abstract: We prove Gaussian approximation bounds over rectangles for high-dimensional martingale sums, with lower bounds showing optimality up to powers of $\log n$. The results cover bounded increments, conditional and marginal sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential tails, and uniform $q$th-moment bounds on the largest absolute coordinate for $2<q\le3$. The predictable quadratic variation $Q$ may be random; the comparison Gaussian has deterministic covariance $Σ=\mathbb{E}Q$. We assume $Σ_{jj}=1$ and $\max_j\sum_k|Σ_{jk}|^s\le M$ for fixed $s>0$ and $M\ge1$, allowing $Σ$ to be singular, and quantify the error due to $Q-Σ$. Conditional tail bounds yield the same dimension threshold as boundedness, whereas marginal tail bounds give smaller thresholds. We also establish necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform convergence in all these classes; under the uniform moment assumption, the criterion holds for every fixed $q>2$. When $Q=I_d$, the bounded and marginal light-tail rates have no additional factors in $\log n$ if $\log(ed)\ge\{\log(en)\}^2$; the same holds for the finite-moment rates with $2<q\le3$ in every dimension, for all sufficiently large $n$.

papers.title: A quasi-tree expansion of the Homfly polynomial
papers.abstract: The Homfly polynomial is one of the best-studied invariants of oriented links. Here, building on work of Jaeger and others, we present a new method of computing it. Terms in the expansion are algebraically simple and they are indexed by certain quasi-trees of the Seifert graph of an (almost) arbitrary link diagram. The quasi-trees, in turn, depend on a single basepoint along the link but no more auxiliary data. This allows us to streamline the proofs of some old results and to find new ones as well, such as an upper bound on the total degree in terms of directed joins of the Seifert graph.

papers.title: The Thurston algorithm for general entire maps on the complex plane: Existence and uniqueness
papers.abstract: We prove that a marked topological entire Thurston map $(f,A)$ of stable parabolic type is Thurston equivalent relative to $A$ to a postsingularly finite entire function if and only if it has no Levy cycle relative to $A\cup\{\infty\}$. Here $A$ is a finite forward-invariant set containing the postsingular set. In the realizable case, the entire function is unique up to complex affine conjugacy, and every orbit of the Thurston pullback converges to its fixed point. We establish a Wolff--Denjoy type estimate for nonexpanding self-maps $T$ of the Teichmüller space of any connected orientable surface of finite type without boundary. If $T$ has an unbounded orbit, there are a nonzero measured foliation $G$ and a constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}_{T^k x}(G)\le C\operatorname{Ext}_x(G)$ for every $x$ and $k\ge0$. For a fixed-point-free transcendental Thurston pullback, this supplies the foliation used in the existence proof. A central tool is a fixed finite measure obtained as the total-variation limit of renormalized pushforward measures transported back along a Teichmüller ray. It allows us to select a cylinder at a late time and compare the mass of the same marked region at different times. If $G$ has a cylinder, a four-point extremal-length estimate and the Thurston matrix force a Levy cycle. Otherwise, in the absence of a Levy cycle, cluster rescaling shows that cylinders of large modulus carry almost all the fixed measure at all late times. Following a cylinder of definite mass until its modulus decreases gives a contradiction. We compare this geometric argument with the proofs for real entire maps and exponential maps.

papers.title: Sharp Last-Iterate Bounds for the Stochastic subGradient Method
papers.abstract: We determine the worst-case expected optimization error of the last iterate of constant-stepsize projected Stochastic subGradient Method on convex Lipschitz objectives. The upper and lower bounds match up to universal constants for every stepsize, horizon, dimension, and conditional noise moment of order $p\in[1,\infty]$. With bounded noise and a fixed positive bound on the initial distance to a minimizer, the best constant stepsize gives worst-case error after $n$ iterates of order $1/\sqrt n$ on the line and $\sqrt{\log n/(n\log\log n)}$ in every fixed dimension at least two.

papers.title: Large orbits of $p$-groups on conjugacy classes of arbitrary finite groups
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a $p$-group that acts faithfully and coprimely on a finite group $H$. In a previous paper it was shown that if $H$ is solvable, then there exists a conjugacy class $c$ of $H$ whose stabilizer in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$, and that this bound is best possible. In this paper we remove the hypothesis that $H$ is solvable. As a consequence, there always exists an irreducible character of $H$ whose inertia group in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$. The proof depends on the classification of finite simple groups. Its main new ingredient is a result on quasiprimitive linear actions of $p$-nilpotent groups which shows that the elements acting as field automorphisms can be ignored when one looks for vectors with small stabilizers. We also present a new family of examples, with nonsolvable $H$, in which the bound is attained.

papers.title: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus. There are several consequences of these results. In particular, we prove that the empirical spectral distribution of the density operator converges almost surely to a rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law. We also prove that this ensemble can be written as a sum of asymptotically free random density operators, leading to an alternative proof of the convergence of the spectral distribution. Finally, we compute the asymptotic expansion of the average entanglement entropy.

papers.title: Submanifolds, restriction of differential operators and Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket
papers.abstract: In this article, we present new formulas for restricting the Hodge operator, the codifferential and the Hodge Laplacian to a submanifold. These formulas are concise, thanks to the use of tools for differential forms (Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket and generalized interior product). They also facilitate explicit calculations for practical applications.

papers.title: Representations of spectral systems over finite distributive lattices
