papers.title: A Game-Theoretic Characterization of Feedback Capability for Fully Coupled Vector-Valued Nonparametric Systems
papers.abstract: We study feedback stabilization for the discrete-time system $x_{t+1}=f(x_t)+u_t+w_{t+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unknown $f$ and arbitrary bounded disturbances. For scalar plants, the sharp feedback capability threshold under generalized Lipschitz uncertainty is $\frac{3}{2}+\sqrt{2}$. We treat fully coupled vector-valued systems, where scalar order and interval recursion are unavailable and coupling precludes a coordinatewise reduction. We introduce a response-history escape game whose adversarial objective requires a finite envelope and an unbounded state radius. Borel determinacy, invariance under a change of finite initial history, and slope monotonicity define a game value $Γ_d$. One causal feedback law stabilizes every plant in the uncertainty class against every bounded disturbance sequence whenever $L<Γ_d$. At every $L\geΓ_d$, each causal feedback law and each initial state admit a globally $Γ_d$-Lipschitz plant whose state norms tend to infinity with zero disturbances. Thus stabilization is possible exactly below the critical value. We also prove $Γ_d=1+(\log d)/(2d)+O((\log\log d)/d)$, with explicit coefficients in bounds on both sides of the remainder. Explicit finite-dimensional bounds give $Γ_d>1$ in every dimension and $Γ_2\ge 7/5$. A nearest-neighbor law achieves the planar guarantee. The values are nonincreasing in dimension, and comparison with the scalar theory yields $Γ_1=\frac{3}{2}+\sqrt{2}$.

papers.title: A congruence obstruction to Roman's bound for Zarankiewicz numbers
papers.abstract: Let z(m,n;s,t) be the largest number of ones in an m x n zero-one matrix with no s x t all-ones submatrix. Roman's 1975 inequality gives a general upper bound for s >= 3, with improvements known in special parameter ranges. We show it is not attained on much of the range just below the design threshold T = (t-1)C(m,s)/(s+1). For n = T-c with 1 <= c <= sT/(s+2), Roman's bound equals the counting bound. Viewing columns as sets of row indices (points), attainment forces all but at most one column to have cardinality s+1 or s+2. These two sizes contribute multiples of d = gcd(s,C(s+1,2)) to the coverage count at each point. At each point, the unused coverage is congruent to mu modulo d, with a correction for the possible exceptional column. With r = c mod s and sigma(r) a slack depending only on s, the bound drops by at least one whenever 1 <= sigma(r) < d and m*mu != s*sigma(r), or mu != 0 and m*mu > s*sigma(r). The first needs s odd and is confined to one residue class; the second covers the whole interval when mu != 0 and m is sufficiently large. For s = 4, t = 2, m = 28 all 2730 values of n are covered. For odd s, when c = (s+1)/2 and an s-(m,s+1,t-1) design exists we obtain the exact value z = (s+1)(T-c). We also locate the obstruction relative to linear programming: the refined program of Davies, Gill and Horsley (2026) still attains the Roman vertex on an explicit family of such parameters.

papers.title: Real morsifications via the trace map
papers.abstract: We prove that every reduced real plane curve singularity admits a real morsification. This settles a question of A'Campo and Gusein-Zade, later stated as conjectures by Leviant--Shustin and by Fomin--Pylyavskyy--Shustin--Thurston. In particular we overcome the main obstruction that remained posed by conjugate pairs of nonreal branches. Our new main ingredient is a construction that produces the divide from a nodal smoothing of two normalization disks. This is what we call the trace map. For real branches, it recovers Gusein-Zade's construction using Chebyshev polynomials. For pairs of complex conjugate branches with distinct tangents, the construction gives an explicit formula for the divide in terms of the Puiseux data. The general method consists in a delicate combination of the trace map with A'Campo's translations and contractions to produce divides and real morsifications for all reduced real plane curve singularities.

papers.title: Classification of some $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-quadratic fusion categories of rank 6
papers.abstract: A fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ is said to be $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-quadratic if the group $G(\mathcal{C})$ of invertible objects is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, and the remaining simple objects form an orbit under the action of $G(\mathcal{C})$. In this paper, we give a partial classification of spherical $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-quadratic fusion categories of rank six. More precisely, we show that its Grothendieck ring $\mathcal{K}_0(\mathcal{C})$ must be one of nine fusion rings if the fusion rule multiplicities are less than $20$, and the categorifications of five of them are previously known. We prove that one of the last four fusion rings can be realized as de-equivariantization of a near-group fusion category of type $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}+8$.

papers.title: At least seven modes in a heteroscedastic three-component bivariate Gaussian mixture
papers.abstract: A Gaussian mixture density can have more modes than components. It has been conjectured that the maximum number of modes of a $d$-variate $k$-component Gaussian mixture density is $\binom{d+k-1}{d}$, which equals six for $(d,k)=(2,3)$. We construct an explicit family of equally weighted heteroscedastic three-component bivariate Gaussian mixture densities with at least seven distinct nondegenerate modes, showing that this conjectured upper bound fails for $(d,k)=(2,3)$. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first counterexample to the conjecture across all pairs $(d,k)$.

papers.title: Fundamental group schemes of globally F-regular varieties
papers.abstract: Let X be a globally F-regular projective variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We show that the Nori fundamental group scheme of its regular locus is finite and linearly reductive. Finiteness is the counterpart of theorems of Xu and Braun on the fundamental group of the smooth locus of a complex log Fano variety. The key input is that if a cover of a splinter is a torsor in codimension one and induces an isomorphism on global functions, then its structure group is linearly reductive. We then show that towers of such covers stabilize, both over globally $F$-regular varieties and, in mixed characteristic, over the globally $+$-regular schemes considered by Cai-Lee-Ma-Schwede-Tucker.

papers.title: A Coarse-Geometric Interpretation of Holt's One-End Theorem
papers.abstract: Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element. Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, almost invariant color classes are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then show, via a separate argument for all slowly oscillating functions, that for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---Protasov's stronger conclusion holds: the full corona is a singleton.

papers.title: Positive definite matrices and involutions: the manners of their infinite cousins
papers.abstract: Matrices and involutions in/on the algebras $B(\mathbb{R})$ and $B(\mathbb{C})$ of real (resp., complex) row- and column-finite $ω\timesω$ matrices are studied. It is proved that any positive definite $\mathbb{R}$-algebra involution on $B(\mathbb{R})$ (resp., any positive definite conjugate-linear involution on $B(\mathbb{C})$) is given by conjugating the transpose involution (resp., the conjugate-transpose involution) with a positive definite matrix from the algebra in question. All positive definite matrices in these algebras have Cholesky factorizations within the algebra. Examples are constructed to show that such positive definite matrices need not have any eigenvalues for their canonical action on column-finite column vectors, and they need not have any square roots in $B(\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: A New Look at the Classical Estimation Problem
papers.abstract: Bahadur's \emph{Lectures on the Theory of Estimation} develop the classical theory of point estimation inside the geometry of Hilbert space, and they record with unusual honesty where the theory strains: the locally best unbiased estimate depends on the parameter, a two-point parameter space yields an estimate Bahadur calls absurd, the odds in binomial sampling have no unbiased estimate, and the virtues of maximum likelihood remain heuristics. We present a subset of the lectures in Bahadur's notation and, at each strain, make one small modification: for each sample point, an estimate $τ$ becomes a function on the parameter space rather than a point in it. The result is the continuum of null hypotheses that Fisher, in 1955, identified with the theory of estimation; we call this \emph{generalized estimation}, and $τ$ a generalized estimator. Bahadur's own definition of an estimate, square-integrable at every distribution in the family, already supplies the domain. The payoffs are tracked lecture by lecture: estimators that exist at boundary samples where point estimates do not; an elementary lemma showing that no pointwise criterion admits a uniformly optimal estimator, which explains why admissibility, minimaxity, Bayes averaging and unbiasedness arose; assessment by information, $Λ(τ)$, with the score attaining the Fisher information bound uniformly by a three-line argument; Cramér--Rao attainment and sufficiency recovered as equality cases of that bound; and the maximum likelihood heuristics converted into exact statements about the score. Nothing classical is overturned; the classical apparatus is explained by Fisher's characterization of estimation as a continuum of significance tests.

papers.title: A major origin of quantumness
papers.abstract: A system property is considered to be elementary, when any further refined specification is impossible. Any two elementary properties of a classical system mutually exclude each other. However, this does not hold anymore for a quantum system, where mutual exclusivity becomes a special relation. This orthogonality relation becomes our first axiom. It is sufficient to define states in an abstract setting and we then introduce two simple, but far-reaching further basic axioms for the states, which mimic the quantum mechanical correspondence between the pure states and the rank-one projections. All examples that we can identify origin from operator algebras or certain Jordan algebras and require the Gleason theorem. The identification of further cases is an unresolved challenge. If some exist, they might result in promising new mathematical models for an extended quantum theory. The non-existence would mean that our extremely basic postulates bring us unexpectedly close to common quantum theory. In any case, the distinction between inequality and mutual exclusivity of elementary system properties appears to be a major origin of quantumness. Our basic approach does not encompass the non-atomic von Neumann algebras of type II and III, which play a crucial role in quantum field theory, and we present a modification of the axioms to include them.

papers.title: Continuous solutions of the complex Kac--Bernstein functional equation on the integers and the real numbers
papers.abstract: In this paper, the continuous solutions of the complex Kac--Bernstein functional equation \[ f_1 ( u + v ) f_2 ( u - v ) f_1 ( u' + v' ) f_2 ( u' - v' ) = f_1 ( u + v' ) f_2 ( u - v' ) f_1 ( u' + v ) f_2 ( u' - v ) \] are classified for $ \mathbb{ Z } $ and $ \mathbb{ R } $. By using this classification for $ \mathbb{ Z } $, we consider a generalization of the Kac--Bernstein theorem on the one-dimensional torus $ \mathbb{ T } $ by Baryshnikov--Eisenberg--Stadje from probability Borel measures to complex Borel measures. Similarly, the original Kac--Bernstein theorem on $ \mathbb{ R } $ is generalized from probability Borel measures to complex Borel measures.

papers.title: Regularity and Decay for Navier-Slip Fluid-Structure Interaction in Exterior Domains
papers.abstract: We study the linearized motion of a spherical rigid body immersed in an incompressible viscous fluid occupying the whole space, under Navier slip boundary conditions with friction. While semigroup regularity and decay estimates are well understood for the no-slip case, such results have been limited to bounded domains in the slip setting. By exploiting the geometric regularity of the sphere, we establish strong $L^q$-regularity, bounded analyticity, and sharp $ L^q-L^r$ estimates for the corresponding fluid-structure operator. These results would provide a foundation for constructing strong $W^{2,1}_q$ solutions and Kato-type solutions to the corresponding nonlinear system.

papers.title: Non-orbit 3-representation-finite symmetric algebras
papers.abstract: We construct two $3$-representation-finite symmetric algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero that are not orbit algebras of repetitive categories. This answers a question of Darpö and Iyama in the negative.

papers.title: Matroid Contention Resolution with Concentration
papers.abstract: Contention resolution schemes (CRS) are widely used for rounding fractional solutions subject to combinatorial constraints. Their guarantees are typically in expectation. Such guarantees alone do not ensure that covering constraints hold, limiting the applicability to problems with covering requirements. We prove lower-tail concentration bounds for the random-order CRS of Adamczyk and Włodarczyk (AW) under the intersection of $k$ matroid constraints. For every linear function with coefficients in $[0,1]$,the output attains nearly the fractional value divided by $k+1$ with failure probability exponentially small in this benchmark,independently of the ground-set size. We extend this bound to normalized monotone submodular functions: the fractional value is given by the multilinear extension, and the concentration bound accounts for the largest singleton value. These guarantees apply to both objectives and covering requirements. Our analysis bounds the fractional value lost in each update and applies a general gain--loss concentration theorem whose bounds are independent of the number of updates. We apply these bounds to obtain new approximation guarantees for matroid intersection coloring and for monotone submodular maximization under matroid, packing, and covering constraints.

papers.title: A unified perspective of Gaussian process approximation for differential equations
papers.abstract: The use of Gaussian processes for approximating differential equations has expanded rapidly, leading to a growing, diverse, and fragmented body of numerical methods. We present a unified Bayesian perspective that places these techniques within a common probabilistic framework, based on a derivative matching interpretation for incorporating differential equation constraints into likelihood. This unified perspective supports both parameter estimation and solution approximation, and shows how a range of existing methods can be understood within it. This work aims to consolidate current developments and provide a foundation for future research.

papers.title: Long-time behaviour of dynamical systems driven by bounded mixing noises
papers.abstract: We study the mixing properties of discrete-time and continuous-time dissipative dynamical systems driven by bounded mixing random forces. The continuous-time systems are reduced to discrete-time random dynamical systems generated by time-one maps, so that the main analysis is carried out in the discrete setting. We introduce a class of mixing random forcings whose regular conditional distributions with respect to the past satisfy natural regularity, recurrence, and non-degeneracy assumptions, extending the framework previously developed for more restrictive classes of processes in a paper by Kuksin-Shirikyan in GAFA (2025). Under a linearised controllability assumptions on the system, we prove exponential mixing in the total variation metric for finite-dimensional phase spaces. We then establish an infinite-dimensional counterpart yielding exponential mixing in the dual-Lipschitz metric under suitable amendments of restrictions on the system and the random forcing. Our approach is based on lifting the dynamics to an appropriate Markov process on an infinite-dimensional history space and applying a Doeblin coupling argument through the method of Kantorovich functional. As applications, we derive exponential mixing for a broad class of ordinary differential equations driven by mixing random processes with bounded continuous trajectories. As an application of our result to PDEs we discuss the randomly perturbed primitive equations of atmospheric dynamics.

papers.title: Oddomorphisms, Split-Off Minors, and the Strong Roberson Conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that the existence of an oddomorphism from a graph $F$ to a graph $G$ does not imply that $G$ is a minor of $F$. This answers a question posed by Roberson (2026) and shows that the CFI graphs cannot be used to prove the Strong Roberson Conjecture. Additionally, we introduce the concept of a split-off minor and show that the existence of an oddomorphism from $F$ to $G$ implies that $G$ is a split-off minor of $F$. Consequently, every class that is closed under taking split-off minors and disjoint unions is homomorphism distinguishing closed. The split-off minor relation is the first minor-like structural relation shown to have this property, marking a meaningful advancement in our understanding of the interaction between structural graph containment and homomorphism indistinguishability relations.

papers.title: Thresholds for the Frankl-Wang $3/7$ conjecture on maximum-degree ratios
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}\subset\binom{[n]}{k}$ be an intersecting family, $Δ(\mathcal{F})=\max_{x\in[n]}|\{F\in\mathcal{F}:x\in F\}|$, and $\varrho(\mathcal{F})=Δ(\mathcal{F})/|\mathcal{F}|$. Frankl and Wang conjectured that if $n>100k$ and $|\mathcal{F}|>\binom{n-3}{k-3}$, then $\varrho(\mathcal{F})\ge 3/7$; the constant $3/7$ is sharp because of the Fano-plane construction. In this note we obtain three results. First, we show that no linear threshold $n>Ck$ can be sufficient: using a truncated Fano-plane construction we exhibit, for every constant $C$ and all large $k$, an intersecting family with $n>Ck$, $|\mathcal{F}|>\binom{n-3}{k-3}$, yet $\varrho(\mathcal{F})<3/7$. In particular, the original condition $n>100k$ does not guarantee the conclusion. Second, for $k=3$ we prove that $\varrho(\mathcal{F})\ge 3/7$ holds for every nonempty intersecting $3$-uniform family; the proof is nontrivial and does not rely on any assumption on $n$ or $|\mathcal{F}|$. Third, using the classical pseudo-sunflower bound $|\mathcal{F}|\le t^k$ (for families containing no pseudo-sunflower of size $t+1$), we obtain a completely explicit polynomial threshold for all $k\ge4$: if $n>(k-3)(7k^4+k)+3$ and $|\mathcal{F}|>\binom{n-3}{k-3}$, then $\varrho(\mathcal{F})\ge 3/7$. In particular, the simplified bound $n>7k^5$ is sufficient for every $k\ge4$.

papers.title: Feigin-Semikhatov duality at the critical level
papers.abstract: The Feigin-Semikhatov duality asserts that the Heisenberg cosets of the subregular $W$-algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ at level $k$ and the one of the principal $W$-superalgebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n|1}$ at level $\ell$ coincide when the levels satisfy the Feigin-Frenkel relation $(k+n)(\ell+n-1)=1$. A similar duality holds between the subregular $W$-algebra of $\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}$ and the principal $W$-superalgebra of $\mathfrak{osp}_{2|2n}$. We study these dualities in the critical/large level limit. We describe the centerless subregular $W$-algebra at the critical level as an orbifold of the large level limit of the principal $W$-superalgebra times a lattice VOA. Our construction yields a functor between certain categories of the two involved vertex algebras. We show that in this set-up one in fact gets block-wise equivalences of categories. Studying the principal block of the large level limit of the principal $W$-superalgebra then gives us the structure of the principal blocks of the subregular $W$-algebras in the category of weight modules (which is much larger than the more common category of lower bounded modules).

papers.title: Generalized Nikulin surfaces and irreducible symplectic fourfolds
papers.abstract: A Nikulin surface is the minimal resolution of the quotient of a $K3$ surface $S$ by a symplectic involution $ι_S$. Equivalently, it is the $2$-dimensional component of the fixed locus of the involution induced by $ι_S$ on the Hilbert scheme $S^{[2]}$. We study $K3$ surfaces $F$ that are the $2$-dimensional component of the fixed locus of a symplectic involution $ι$ on hyper-Kähler manifolds $X$ of $K3^{[2]}$-type; we call them generalized Nikulin surfaces. We show that a projective $K3$ surface is a generalized Nikulin surface if and only if its Néron-Severi lattice contains primitively the lattice $E_7(-2)$. Moreover, we show that the transcendental lattices $T_F$ and $T_{\widetilde{X/ ι}}$, where $\widetilde{X/ ι}$ is the terminalization of the quotient $X/ι$, are Hodge isometric. Finally, we describe projective models of generalized Nikulin surfaces of small degrees.

papers.title: Minkowskian open/closed conformal field theory possibly without vacuum: the Cardy case
papers.abstract: For any conformal net, not necessarily rational, we construct the associated Cardy-type conformal field theory on the Minkowski spacetimes $(\mathbb R/2π\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb R$ for closed strings and $[0,π]\times\mathbb R$ for open strings within the framework of algebraic quantum field theory. In addition to verifying some of their basic properties, we prove three forms of Haag duality for multi-double-cones and boundary intervals, interpreted respectively as the Minkowskian versions of modular invariance, the Cardy consistency condition, and the Morita equivalence of boundary field algebras.

papers.title: Random coloured digraphs defined by a Markov logic network
papers.abstract: A Markov Logic Network (MLN) $M$ is a probabilistic relational model used in Statistical Relational Artificial Intelligence for defining a probability distribution $P_D^M$ on the set $W_D$ of possible worlds with domain $D$ for an arbitrary finite domain $D$. An MLN consists of first-order formulas, which we call soft constraints, with associated weights which are nonnegative real numbers. The behaviour of the probability distribution, including the effect of the weights, on different domain sizes is poorly understood. We approach the problem in a systematic way by studying sequences $(P_n^M(ψ) : n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots)$ where $ψ$ is a first-order sentence and $P_n^M(ψ)$ is the probability that $ψ$ holds in $W_D$ where $D = [n] := \{1, \ldots, n\}$. We consider a first-order language that can express a property $P(x)$ and relation $R(x, y)$ and show that all of the following cases can be realized for an MLN $M$ such that each of its soft constraints is a boolean combination of $P(x)$, $P(y)$ and $R(x, y)$ in which both $x$ and $y$ appears: For every first-order sentence $ψ$, $P_n^M(ψ)$ converges to 0 or 1 as $n\to\infty$. For every first-order sentence $ψ$, $P_n^M(ψ)$ converges as $n\to\infty$ but not necessarily to 0 or 1. There is a first-order sentence $ψ$ such that $P_n^M(ψ)$ does not converge as $n\to\infty$. In fact, all three cases can be realized even after fixing the soft constraints and, for any $\varepsilon > 0$, by varying their weights by less than $\varepsilon$. We also show that, given any MLN as described above, we can efficiently determine which case it belongs to by inspecting the MLN. Then we show that if the weights are scaled by $1/n$ then we end up in case~(1) no matter how the weights are chosen.

papers.title: The ratio spectrum of Lagrange constants under linear fractional transformations
papers.abstract: In this note we solve a problem posed by Lagarias and Shallit concerning Lagrange constants under linear fractional transformations $Mx=\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}$. For an integer matrix $M$ with nonzero determinant and relatively prime entries, define the ratio spectrum \begin{equation*} \mathcal{V}(M)=\left\{\frac{k(Mx)}{k(x)}:x\in\mathrm{Bad}\right\}, \end{equation*} where $k(x)$ denotes the Lagrange constant of the irrational number $x$ and $\mathrm{Bad}$ is the set of badly approximable numbers. Lagarias and Shallit proved that \begin{equation*} \mathcal{V}(M)\subseteq\left[\frac{1}{|\det M|},|\det M|\right], \end{equation*} and asked for the determination of $\mathcal{V}(M)$. We prove that \begin{equation*} \mathcal{V}(M)=\left[\frac{1}{|\det M|},|\det M|\right]. \end{equation*}

papers.title: A Projection-Free Algorithm for Variational Inequalities in Hilbert Spaces with Strong Convergence
papers.abstract: We study variational inequalities governed by a point-to-set maximal monotone operator in a real Hilbert space and constrained by a convex inequality \(C=\{x\in\Hi:c(x)\le0\}\), where the defining function \(c\) is continuous and not necessarily differentiable. The proposed method uses only projections onto intersections of half-spaces and avoids the metric projection onto \(C\). Feasibility is handled by subgradient cuts and, when a trial operator point is infeasible, by a Slater correction based on a fixed strictly feasible point. The variational inequality is represented by Minty-type separating half-spaces generated at feasible graph points of the operator, and a Haugazeau half-space is added to obtain best-approximation convergence. Under a Slater-corrected feasible-separation condition, together with explicit exact, approximate and finite-candidate oracle realisations, the whole sequence converges strongly to \(P_{S^*}(x^0)\), the projection of the initial point onto the solution set. We also derive best-iterate \(O(N^{-1/2})\) residual estimates for the step residual, feasibility violation and Minty gap. The analysis is stated directly for point-to-set maximal monotone operators, while the concrete oracle realisations include finite-dimensional single-valued models. We record the consequences of strong monotonicity in the point-to-set setting and provide numerical comparisons on nonsmooth and large-scale constraints, including maxima of convex quadratics, a discretised optimal-control problem, mixed-norm sparse recovery, a Cournot--Nash capacity equilibrium, and a genuine point-to-set \(\ell_1\)-subdifferential example.

papers.title: Low-Rank Acceleration of the Operator Fourier Transform
papers.abstract: We develop a numerical algorithm for the efficient solution or approximation of solutions to the Helmholtz equation on a structured grid in two dimensions. We make use of the Operator Fourier Transform (OFT) and a low-rank cross approximation scheme (Cross-DEIM) to decompose the problem into an integral over a pseudo-time of solutions to the Schrödinger equation. The OFT is a framework for solving operator equations like fractional Laplacian equations or the Helmholtz equation, when the latter is written as a product of two paraxial operators. The main computational cost in the OFT is the solution to the Schrödinger equation, especially when the dimension or mesh resolution is high. In this work, we alleviate this cost by utilizing a low-rank method. Such methods aim to beat the curse of dimensionality when low-rank structures are present in the solution. For a problem with a constant coefficient we show that the resulting solver converges at second order in the pseudo-time step and reaches the accuracy of the direct solution of the discretized linear system, which is limited by the second-order finite-difference discretization in space, while keeping the solution in low-rank form. The ranks of the accumulated solution change little as the grid is refined, which suggests a cost per time step that grows nearly linearly with the number of grid points in each direction.

papers.title: Cheeger-type inequalities for the second largest spectral gap from $1$ of the normalized Laplacian
papers.abstract: We study the second largest spectral gap from $1$ of the normalized Laplacian of a graph, a quantity that appears in the literature in connection with random walks, expander graphs, and Ramanujan graphs. We relate it to the classical Cheeger and dual Cheeger constants, and we introduce a new Cheeger-type constant admitting a probabilistic interpretation in terms of two-step random walks. For this constant, we establish sharp inequalities analogous to the classical Cheeger inequalities.

papers.title: Optimal constants of smoothing estimates for quantum harmonic oscillators
papers.abstract: We study optimal constants and extremizers of smoothing estimates for quantum harmonic oscillators. In particular, we establish harmonic oscillator analogues of free particle results due to Simon (1992), Bez and Sugimoto (2015), and Bez et al. (2015).

papers.title: Geometric Properties of positive solutions of Lane-Emden problems on convex domains of $§^2$
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions of the Dirichlet problem $-Δu = u^p$ in a uniformly convex domain $Ω\subset §^2$, $u= 0$ on $\partialΩ.$ For $p=1$, we assume that the right-hand side is replaced by $λ_1 u$, where $λ_1$ is the first eigenvalue of $-Δ$ on $Ω$ with zero Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that for $0 \leq p < 1$ the unique positive solution $u$ is such that $u^{\frac{1-p}{2}}$ is strictly concave in $Ω$, while for $1 < p \leq 3$ every positive solution $u$ which belongs to the connected component of the least-energy branch of solutions issued from $p=1$ is such that $u^{\frac{1-p}{2}}$ is strictly convex in $Ω$.

papers.title: Lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimension of expressible sets
papers.abstract: We obtain positive lower bounds on the Hausdorff dimension of sets of real numbers given by expressions of the form $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{a_n b_n}$, where $b_n$ satisfies some growth condition and $a_n$ lies in some set, possibly depending on $n$. As a consequence of our results, some of the irrational numbers arising from Erdős' celebrated construction from 1976 are not Liouville numbers.

papers.title: Merge Trees of Length-Filtered Lattice Knot Spaces
papers.abstract: We study length-filtered BFACF graphs of self-avoiding polygons in the simple cubic lattice, emphasizing the birth and merging of connected components and the minimax length required to connect prescribed states. For the published shortest-layer censuses of $4_1$ and $6_3$, we compute BFACF merge trees: the former has four components at length 30 merging at 32, while the latter has twelve components at 40, two at 42, and one at 44. Completeness for the entire minimal layer is conditional on the published populations exhausting it (and on 40 being minimal for $6_3$). For one trefoil chirality, we certify six selected nonminimal components born at length 26, with merge heights 28 or 30 relative to the minimal branch. We characterize eventual connectivity of capped BFACF graphs in terms of bounded birth levels of strong local-minimum components. An explicit 64-edge Hamiltonian lattice unknot has no neutral or shortening BFACF move, and a verified BFACF path gives exact merge height 66 with the square. Our main new construction is a block substitution: every vertex of an arbitrary lattice polygon $Q$ is replaced by a $5\times5\times5$ Hamiltonian block with face-centred ports. For every knot type $K$ and every lattice polygon $Q$ of type $K$ with $m$ edges, this gives a BFACF-frozen polygon of the same oriented knot type and length $125m$. Consequently every knot type, of either chirality, has infinitely many nonminimal strong local-minimum births and lattice Gordian representatives, and its capped BFACF graphs are not eventually connected. Explicit coordinate data and independent BFACF local-move verifiers accompany the constructions. Unbounded minimax excess and analogous barriers in continuous ropelength-filtered knot spaces remain open.

papers.title: Self-similarity and diffusive limits for linear kinetic equations: a Wild sum approach
papers.abstract: We prove that linear collisional kinetic equations in the whole space without confinement mechanism display a long-time self-similar behaviour. This drastically improves the recently known results (decay estimates) about the solutions in such a context, providing the first result regarding this self-similar behaviour. As a consequence, we also establish a uniform-in-time convergence of the suitably rescaled solutions to their diffusion limit, which is also new. The class of equations considered includes some BGK type equations, some kinetic nonlocal Fokker--Planck-type equations and some kinetic (possibly fractional) Fokker--Planck equations, for which we are able to write explicitly solutions through a Wild sum (or Dyson series) or we can manage some accurate computations on the Fourier side.

papers.title: Higher Rank-Support Weights and $(q,m)$-Polymatroids
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to develop a $(q,m)$-polymatroidal approach to higher supports and higher rank-weight enumerators of Delsarte rank-metric codes. In this framework, we establish rank-metric analogs of several fundamental results known for matroids and linear codes. We describe minimal higher supports in terms of cocircuits of suitable truncations of the associated $(q,m)$-polymatroid, and obtain a polymatroidal interpretation of generalized minimum rank weights and their Singleton-type bound. We also prove that the associated $(q,m)$-polymatroid and the higher support distributions determine each other. On the enumerative side, we establish a Greene-type identity relating higher rank-weight enumerators to the rank generating function, and conversely show that the full sequence of higher rank-weight enumerators determines this function. As the main application, we prove MacWilliams-type identities for higher rank-weight enumerators by first deriving a duality formula for higher weight polynomials of $(q,m)$-polymatroids and then applying it to a rank-metric code and its dual.

papers.title: Moduli of semistable Lie algebroid connections and twisted Higgs bundles
papers.abstract: We study integrable Lie algebroid connections and twisted Higgs fields on vector bundles and principal bundles over smooth projective families of complex curves. Under suitable hypotheses, we construct quasi-projective moduli spaces of semistable principal bundles equipped with these structures and prove that their formation commutes with arbitrary base change. We also characterize algebraically integrable transitive Lie algebroids on smooth irreducible complex varieties as Atiyah algebroids of principal bundles whose gauge groupoids are representable by separated schemes of finite type. Further results concern the local freeness of twisted Higgs sheaves and neutral Tannakian descriptions of the associated categories.

papers.title: A Volume of Fluid Immersed Boundary Method for Industrial Polymer Mixing
papers.abstract: Free-surface numerical simulation of polymer mixing processes requires handling rotating solid boundaries of complex shapes as well as kinematic viscosity ratios between polymer melt and air up to $10^8$. We present a finite volume method that couples a Volume of Fluid (VOF) interface-capturing scheme with a non-conforming immersed boundary (IB) method, so that moving screws are represented on a fixed mesh without remeshing. In standard segregated VOF solvers, part of the viscous stress is treated explicitly, which can lead to instabilities and severe time-step restrictions at such viscosity ratios. To address this limitation, we integrate into the VOF-IB framework a block-coupled (BC) scheme in which the full viscous stress, including its transposed-gradient part, is treated implicitly. The method is implemented in the finite volume library OpenFOAM. On a three-dimensional injection-molding test case with a generalized Newtonian melt, segregated solvers either diverge or produce spurious air-phase velocities at the time steps allowed by the block-coupled solver, which instead yields a physical solution and reduces the computing time by a factor of about 2.7 with respect to the fastest segregated run that remains physical. On the finer grid, the IB solution agrees with the conforming-mesh solution within 2% in velocity and 0.5% in pressure drop. The BC-VOF-IB solver is then applied to single- and twin-screw extruders under fully and partially filled conditions, capturing the filling dynamics and the resulting pressure build-up along the screw, demonstrating the applicability of the method to industrial geometries. The current formulation is isothermal; its extension to non-isothermal flows, required for quantitative prediction of melt temperature and viscous heating, is the subject of ongoing work.

papers.title: Shape theory for condensed anima
papers.abstract: We give different perspectives on the notion of shape for condensed anima. We prove that it recovers more classical notions of shape not only for all locally compact Hausdorff but also locally contractible spaces. These recovering statements imply and extend comparison results on sheaf and condensed cohomology by Clausen-Scholze and Haine. Another homotopy-theoretical direction for condensed anima are their condensed homotopy groups. Connected to this, we give a description of the underlying topological group functor on condensed groups via quasi-topological groups.

papers.title: The Endogeneity of Miscalibration: Impossibility and Escape in Scored Reporting
papers.abstract: An agent's probability report is paid for twice: by a strictly proper scoring rule, which rewards accuracy, and by an approval rule for the decision it triggers. An approval rule that is not affine is known to defeat truthful reporting. We show the conflict is built in: whenever perfect screening is attainable, the welfare-maximizing approval rule is never affine. The distortion is predictable: there is a reserve report at which pretending to be the marginal type costs exactly what approval is worth. Approving every report at or above the reserve sorts agents as if their beliefs were observed, under every strictly proper score and for any belief distribution. So does a continuous rule with one corner; under strict feasibility no continuously differentiable rule does. The binding constraint is steepness, not smoothness: a slope-capped rule sorts perfectly if and only if the cap reaches the critical slope, the steepest chord of the pretending cost up to the reserve; below it the welfare loss is cubic in the shortfall. For the Brier, log and power scores, and whenever the pretending cost is convex up to the reserve, the critical slope has a closed form. The instances are AI-agent oversight and marketplace operation.

papers.title: Thresholds for Tic-Tac-Toe on Finite Affine Spaces
papers.abstract: We study the strong positional game in which two players alternately claim points of $\F_q^m$ and the first to complete an affine $n$-subspace wins. We distinguish the first winning dimension $τ(n,q)$ from the eventual winning threshold $T(n,q)$, without assuming monotonicity in $m$. Affine Ramsey theory proves finiteness, while the Erdős-Selfridge criterion and explicit geometric strategies give lower bounds. In the binary case, a quantitative form of the classical quotient argument yields $T(n,2)\le2^{n-1}+n$, with a corresponding bound for any number of colors. A plane-counting recursion gives further multicolor and extremal estimates. We prove $τ(2,2)=T(2,2)=4$ and show that every $31$-point subset of $\F_2^6$ contains an affine $3$-subspace. This gives an elementary proof of the known equality $\AR_2(3;2)=6$ and implies $τ(3,2)=T(3,2)\in\{5,6\}$. Previously known planar outcomes are recovered within the same framework.

papers.title: Modeling sequential cognitive states via population level cortical dynamics
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a mathematical framework for cyclic and sequential patterns of brain activity, combining heteroclinic dynamics with discrete neural-field models. Under explicit structural and positivity assumptions on the prescribed activity patterns, we show that the resulting spatially discrete neural-field system supports neither heteroclinic cycles nor nonconstant periodic orbits. Heteroclinic dynamics, on the other hand, arise in Lotka--Volterra-type systems, but these equations do not directly correspond to neuronal processes. To bridge these descriptions, we use a $C^1$ version of the Universal Approximation Theorem to approximate a target vector field by a neural network interpretable as a high-dimensional Amari-type neural-field system. Each periodic solution of the reduced dynamics admits a unique periodic realization at the population level with the same minimal period. For three-dimensional heteroclinic targets, we establish sufficient conditions ensuring that the approximating vector field admits a unique hyperbolic attracting periodic orbit in a trapping channel surrounding the original heteroclinic cycle. As a proof of concept, we apply this construction to a Lotka--Volterra-type target phenomenologically representing sequential network activations associated with focused-attention meditation.

papers.title: Gradient Regularized Newton Boosting Trees with Global Convergence
papers.abstract: Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDTs) dominate tabular machine learning, with modern implementations like XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost being based on Newton boosting: a second-order descent step in the space of decision trees. Despite its empirical success, the global convergence of Newton boosting is poorly understood compared to first-order boosting. In this paper, we introduce Restricted Newton Descent, a framework for convex optimization with Newton's method on Hilbert spaces with inexact iterates, based on the concepts of cosine angle and weak gradient edge. Within this framework, we recover Newton boosting with GBDTs and classical finite-dimensional theory as special cases. We first prove that vanilla Newton boosting achieves a linear rate of convergence for smooth, strongly convex losses that satisfy a Hessian-dominance condition. To handle general convex losses with Lipschitz Hessians, we extend a recent gradient regularized Newton scheme to the restricted weak learner setting, establishing the first global $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{k^2})$ convergence rate for second-order GBDTs. This scheme minimally modifies the classical algorithm by introducing an adaptive $\ell_2$-regularization term proportional to the square root of the gradient norm at each iteration. In numerical experiments, we show that this scheme converges while vanilla Newton boosting may diverge.

papers.title: Benders Cut Filtering for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Robustness Scenarios and Topology Switching
papers.abstract: Many large-scale optimization problems decompose into a master problem and scenario subproblems. Benders decomposition exploits this structure by iteratively solving the subproblems and adding constraints, called Benders cuts, to the master problem. We study Benders cut filtering: given a set of Benders cuts produced in one iteration, which subset should be added to the master problem? Adding all generated cuts can cause rapid master problem growth, whereas retaining fewer cuts may require more Benders iterations. To our knowledge, few prior works have studied this question for Benders cuts. Classical cut filtering techniques require modification because Benders cuts enforce constraints omitted from the master problem, whereas conventional cutting planes are optional inequalities that strengthen the relaxation. We propose violation-based filtering, diversity-based filtering via k-medoids clustering on cosine distances, and a hybrid that selects a most-violated cut per cluster. We compare these strategies with no filtering, random filtering, and our adaptation of SCIP's hybrid cut selector on an affine potential-based flow problem with topology switching and robustness scenarios. On instances solved by all configurations, our hybrid approach reduces the shifted geometric mean solve time by about 45% compared to no filtering, and by 39% compared to our adaptation of SCIP's hybrid cut selector. While violation-based filtering achieves a similar runtime, the hybrid approach requires about 17% fewer callback rounds. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of Benders cut filtering on this problem class and motivate evaluation in other domains.

papers.title: The maximum Cox complexity of a Fano-type variety and the Mukai conjecture
papers.abstract: We define an intrinsic invariant $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(\cdot)$, the maximum Cox complexity, of Fano-type varieties $X$. We prove $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)\in\mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}$ and $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)=0$ if and only if $X$ is toric. We then apply this invariant to the Mukai conjecture, which characterises powers of projective spaces among smooth Fano varieties in terms of $\dim(X)$, the Picard number $ρ(X)$, and the Fano index $i(X)$. All klt Fano varieties $X$ canonically embed into a projective toric variety $Z$ via their Cox ring. When $Z$ is smooth, we call $X$ ambiently smooth. We prove the Mukai conjecture for ambiently smooth Fano varieties by establishing the stronger inequality: $\dim(X)+ρ(X)-i(X)ρ(X)\geqγ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)\geq 0$. Notably, 45% of the deformation families of smooth Fano threefolds have an ambiently smooth member. For a Fano-type variety $X$, the invariant $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)$ is defined using coefficient sums of anticanonical divisors supported on the divisors corresponding to minimal homogeneous generators of the Cox ring. Our proof proceeds by reducing the Cox ring to positive characteristic, using strong F-regularity to obtain the coefficients of an anticanonical divisor, and the F-pure threshold to establish the nonnegativity of $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)$.

papers.title: Inference for Linear Systems with Unknown Coefficients
papers.abstract: This paper considers the problem of testing whether there exists a solution satisfying known linear constraints to a linear system of equations. Importantly and in contrast to some prior work, we allow all parameters in the system of equations, including the slope coefficients, to be unknown. For this reason, we describe the linear system as having unknown (as opposed to known) coefficients. This hypothesis testing problem arises naturally when constructing confidence sets for possibly partially identified parameters in the analysis of nonparametric instrumental variables models, treatment effect models, and random coefficient models, among other settings. We begin our analysis by providing a novel characterization of the set of coefficient pairs for which the linear system is feasible. Leveraging this characterization, we develop a testing procedure based on sample splitting. We establish its validity under weak and interpretable conditions on the linear system. An important feature of these conditions is that they permit the dimensionality of the problem to grow rapidly with the sample size. A further attractive property of our test is that it does not require simulation to compute suitable critical values. We illustrate the practical relevance of our theoretical results in a simulation study.

papers.title: Root laminations of arbitrary degree
papers.abstract: This paper studies the space of degree $d>1$ invariant q-laminations, i.e., geodesic laminations invariant under the $d$-tupling map of the circle and associated with equivalence relations. Our main construction associates a q-lamination with any degree $d$ critical portrait \emph{in a canonical way}. Even though somewhat technical, this is the initial step in the program of classification of all degree $d$ invariant q-laminations.

papers.title: Rational relative sectional category
papers.abstract: We develop an algebraic model for the relative sectional category of a continuous map in rational homotopy theory using commutative differential graded algebras (CDGAs). Our main result establishes that for formal maps, the rational relative sectional category can be computed purely from cohomology, using ideal nilpotency. We also show that this equality may fail in general topological settings. Applying this framework, we obtain purely algebraic characterizations for the rational Lusternik-Schnirelmann category and the rational higher topological complexity of a map. Finally, we provide an algebraic description of the rational homotopic distance between formal maps.

papers.title: Learning Curves and Prediction Persistence to Under-Regularization of Spectral Algorithms in Large Dimensions
papers.abstract: We study how prediction risk changes as regularization is reduced for spectral algorithms when the sample size $n$ and dimension $d$ satisfy $n\asymp d^γ$ for fixed $γ>0$. For inner-product kernels on the sphere, under a source condition with smoothness $s\geq0$ and a signal nondegeneracy condition, we characterize the conditional excess risk up to constant factors at each fixed admissible scale $λ\asymp d^{-u}$, $u>0$, and at interpolation. The resulting risk orders describe the effects of source smoothness, filter qualification, and transitions between spectral blocks. They identify when the conditional excess risk retains the minimax risk order as regularization is weakened from an optimal scale to interpolation, and when an interval before interpolation exhibits a polynomially larger risk. We also compare the kernel risk with a population sequence risk for the same spectral filter, using a deterministic regularization scale bounded below by order $n^{-1}$. Finally, for noninteger $γ$, we extend the risk characterization for kernel ridge regression to kernels on general domains under spectral scaling, hyper-contractivity, and tail diagonal concentration conditions, together with the source and signal conditions.

papers.title: Infinite graphs with finite metric dimension
papers.abstract: We study the metric dimension (strong and weak) of connected infinite graphs. In particular, our main interest is characterizing infinite graphs with finite dimension. Our main results: (1) graphs with more than one end have infinite strong dimension; (2) for locally finite graphs with a finite number of cycles, the weak dimension is finite if and only if the graph has finitely many vertices of degree at least three, and the strong dimension is finite if and only if the graph has one end and finitely many vertices of degree at least three.

papers.title: An Adaptive Log-Laguerre Spectral Method for the Radial Dirac Equation: Resolving Asymptotic Decay and Core Singularities in Atomic Calculations
papers.abstract: The high-precision solution of the radial Dirac equation is fundamental to relativistic quantum chemistry, essential for reliable pseudopotential generation and all-electron electronic structure methods. Capturing both the non-polynomial singularities at the origin and the state-dependent asymptotic decay on semi-infinite domains presents a significant computational challenge. In this work, we propose the Adaptive Log-Laguerre Spectral Method (ALLSM), a novel coupled spectral-element solver that seamlessly integrates three advanced mathematical methodologies into a unified framework. Specifically, Generalized Log-Orthogonal Functions (GLOFs) are deployed in the near-core region to intrinsically approximate complex $r^s$ singular behaviors without requiring prior knowledge of the exact analytical exponent $s$. Concurrently, an adaptive Laguerre spectral method is employed to dynamically capture diverse exponential tails on $[0, \infty)$, avoiding artificial domain truncation. To structurally guarantee spectral purity across this bipartite basis, the framework rigorously incorporates the Inverse Dirac Operator Method (IDOM), effectively eliminating variational collapse and spurious states. Validated across diverse physical regimes, including Coulomb, finite-nucleus, and screened potentials, the proposed solver restores exponential convergence and consistently achieves relative accuracies of $10^{-10}$. This work provides a robust, pollution-free computational kernel for atomic structure calculations, establishing a highly reliable numerical standard for complex molecular simulations.

papers.title: Geometric bounds for Steklov and weighted Neumann eigenvalues on Euclidean domains
papers.abstract: We obtain sharp upper bounds for the first two nonzero Steklov eigenvalues among bounded domains in Euclidean spaces of dimension $d \geq 7$ under a natural normalization involving volume and boundary measure. These bounds are derived from a characterization of optimal domains and weights for the first two nonzero weighted Neumann eigenvalues. In dimensions $3 \leq d \leq 6$, we obtain upper bounds that are not sharp. We further establish strict upper bounds with sharp constants for all higher Steklov eigenvalues on simply connected planar domains with continuous boundary and finite boundary length. Beyond the second nonzero eigenvalue, these bounds were previously known only for smooth planar domains.

papers.title: Elephant Random Walks on Coverings of Dipole Graphs
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we introduce and analyze elephant random walks (ERWs) on bipartite periodic lattices arising as coverings of dipole graphs. We focus on lattices whose admissible step directions in the two parts of the bipartition are negatives of each other and disjoint. On such graphs, we define an ERW in which each step is chosen by referring to the entire history of the walk. The ERW on the hexagonal lattice is a prototypical example of our model. The definition and asymptotic analysis of such ERWs are not straightforward because both depend strongly on the underlying geometric structure. Our analysis is based on a combination of the Pólya-type urn techniques and the martingale approach, two standard methods for analyzing ERWs. We find that the counting process of the ERW forms a Pólya-type urn with two-periodic generating matrices. By analyzing such urn models, we show the strong law of large numbers for the counting process. Combining the result for the counting process with the martingale approach, we derive the strong laws of large numbers with non-standard normalizations and central limit theorems for the position process of the ERW in the diffusive and critical regimes, as well as almost sure and $L^2$ scaling limits in the superdiffusive regime.

papers.title: Low regularity potentials in heterogeneous Cahn--Hilliard functionals
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the prototypical model of liquid-liquid phase separation, the Cahn-Hilliard functional, in a highly irregular setting. Specifically, we analyze potentials with low regularity vanishing on space-dependent wells. Under remarkably weak hypotheses, we establish a robust compactness result. Strengthening the regularity of the wells and of the growth of the potential close to the wells only slightly, we completely characterize the asymptotic behavior of the associated family of functionals through a $Γ$-convergence analysis. As a notable technical result, we prove the existence of geodesics for a degenerate metric and establish a uniform bound on their Euclidean length.

papers.title: The Value of Information in Resource-Constrained Pricing
papers.abstract: Dynamic pricing with resource constraints requires balancing exploration of unknown demand patterns against exploitation of known information to maximize revenue. We develop algorithms for this problem across different information regimes. Products share perishable resources, and the firm posts prices and observes the realized requests, which may exceed the remaining capacity. In the full-information setting, a residual-correction policy that solves the fluid problem once attains $O(\log T)$ regret with bounded prices and arbitrary-rank resource matrices. In the no-information setting, deterministic exploration followed by a certainty-equivalent policy attains $O(\sqrt T)$ regret when the limiting fluid solution is nondegenerate. In the informed-price setting, given an initial price-demand estimate, a feedback controller learns the implementing prices without estimating the slope matrix if the slope matrix is symmetric, a set containing it is known in advance, the informed price is aligned with the resource constraints, and an inverse-image condition holds. A selector chooses between the informed-price algorithm and the no-information algorithm from historical data. Its regret bound includes observation error, misalignment, inventory exits, and periods on the fixed price. We further show how offline surrogate models reduce the regret of the learning policy through variance reduction, even when misspecified. The bound includes calibration and screen failures, and the regret is reduced for all sufficiently large horizons. We finally demonstrate the empirical performances of our policies through complete numerical experiments.

papers.title: Stabilization of highly nonlinear hybrid stochastic differential delay equations by periodically intermittent feedback controls based on discrete time observations with asynchronous switching
papers.abstract: This paper extends the stabilization analysis of highly nonlinear time delay systems to the case where periodic intermittent control, discrete time observation, and sampling-induced asynchronous mode switching coexist, and establishes corresponding moment estimates and exponential stability criteria. To overcome the difficulties emerged due to intermittent control and discrete time observations with asynchronous switching, we introduce a discontinuous Lyapunov function and account for the effect of the discontinuities of the intermittent control function at switching instants, thereby establishing the moment exponential stability of the controlled system. Finally, an example is presented to interpret the conclusion.

papers.title: Power-Law Spectrum of the Random Feature Model
papers.abstract: Scaling laws for neural networks, in which the loss decays as a power-law in the number of parameters, data, and compute, depend fundamentally on the spectral structure of the data covariance, with power-law eigenvalue decay appearing ubiquitously in vision and language tasks. A central question is whether this spectral structure is preserved or destroyed when data passes through the basic building block of a neural network: a random linear projection followed by a nonlinear activation. We study this question for the random feature model: given data $x \sim N(0,H )\in \mathbb{R}^v$ where $H$ has $α$-power-law spectrum ($λ_j( H ) \asymp j^{-α}$, $α> 1$), a Gaussian sketch matrix $W \in \mathbb{R}^{v\times d}$, and an entrywise polynomial $f$ of degree $p$, we characterize the eigenvalues of the population random-feature covariance $\mathbb{E}_{ x }[\frac{1}{d}f(. W ^\top x )^{\otimes 2}]$. We prove matching upper and lower bounds: for all $1 \leq j \leq c_1 d \log^{-(p+1)}(d)$, the $j$-th eigenvalue is of order $\left(\log^{p-1}(j+1)/j\right)^α$. For $ c_1 d \log^{-(p+1)}(d)\leq j\leq d$, the $j$-th eigenvalue is of order $j^{-α}$ up to a polylog factor. That is, the power-law exponent $α$ is inherited exactly from the input covariance, modified only by a logarithmic correction that depends on the degree $p$ of the activation. The proof combines a dyadic head-tail decomposition with Wick chaos expansions for higher-order monomials and random matrix concentration inequalities; a Gaussian integration-by-parts argument then extends the result from monomials to polynomials

papers.title: Oort's conjecture on automorphisms of generic supersingular abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We prove Oort's conjecture that generically on the supersingular locus of the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of genus g and in characteristic p, the automorphism group of the universal principally polarized abelian variety consists only of $\pm 1$, unless g=2, 3 or 4 and p=2. On the way, we provide an explicit description of the a=1-locus in the Rapoport-Zink space of principally polarized supersingular p-divisible groups of any dimension g. We also prove analogous results for generic automorphism groups on moduli spaces of supersingular p-divisible groups with and without polarization.

papers.title: Weighted boundedness for the maximal operator associated with matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the boundedness on $L^p(w)$ of the maximal operator $M_{A^{-1}}$, defined by $M_{A^{-1}}f(x)=Mf(A^{-1}x)$, that is, the maximal of Hardy-Littlewood composed with a invertible matrix $A$. We present two different results of boundedness and provide a characterization for a particular case of matrices. The main novelty lies in examples illustrating the difference between the class of weights with a matrix, $\mathcal{A}_{A,p}$, and the classical Muckenhoupt weight class, $\mathcal{A}_{p}$. Finally, we extend these results to the fractional framework, considering the fractional maximal operator $M_{α, A^{-1}}$.

papers.title: A Constructive Proof of the Four-Color Theorem
papers.abstract: This paper presents a path to proving the Four-Color Theorem that differs from the traditional "reducible configuration" method. By introducing concepts such as "outer boundary," "primitive set," "Property A," "knot," "valid pair group," and the operation of "adding an n-point region on an interval," we construct a framework for gradually coloring any given planar graph. The core of this framework consists of three theorems, which ensure that after sequentially adding specific regions on an outer boundary satisfying Property A, the new outer boundary still satisfies Property A, ultimately allowing the entire given graph to be colored with four colors. This method avoids computer enumeration and provides a more constructive proof perspective.

papers.title: A type theory for invertibility in weak $ω$-categories
papers.abstract: We present a conservative extension ICaTT of the dependent type theory Catt for weak $ω$-categories with a type witnessing coinductive invertibility of cells. This extension allows for a concise description of the ``walking equivalence'' as a context, and of a set of maps characterising $ω$-equifibrations as substitutions. We provide an implementation of our theory, which we use to formalise basic properties of invertible cells. These properties allow us to give semantics of ICaTT in marked weak $ω$-categories, building a fibrant marked $ω$-category out of every model of ICaTT.

papers.title: On the Coupled Cluster Doubles Truncation Variety of Four Electrons
papers.abstract: We extend recent algebro-geometric results for coupled cluster theory of quantum many-body systems to the truncation varieties arising from the doubles approximation (CCD), focusing on the first genuinely nonlinear doubles regime of four electrons. Since this doubles truncation variety does not coincide with previously studied varieties, we initiate a systematic investigation of its basic algebro-geometric invariants. We show that for $4$ electrons in $n \geq 13$ orbitals, the CCD truncation variety is not a complete intersection, and we present numerical and symbolic evidence that for the remaining cases it is a complete intersection defined by $\binom{n-4}{4}$ quadrics. Using representation-theoretic arguments, we uncover a Pfaffian structure governing the quadratic relations that define the truncation variety for any $n$, and show that an exact tensor product factorization holds in the distinguished limit of disconnected doubles. We connect these structural results to the computation of the beryllium insertion into molecular hydrogen ({Be$\cdots$H$_2$ $\to$ H--Be--H}), a small but computationally challenging bond formation process where multiconfigurational effects become pronounced.

papers.title: D-ripALM: A Tuning-friendly Decentralized Relative-Type Inexact Proximal Augmented Lagrangian Method
papers.abstract: This paper proposes D-ripALM, a Decentralized relative-type inexact proximal Augmented Lagrangian Method for consensus convex optimization over multi-agent networks. D-ripALM adopts a double-loop distributed optimization framework that accommodates a wide range of inner solvers, enabling efficient treatment of both smooth and nonsmooth objectives. D-ripALM employs a relative-type error criterion to regulate the switching between inner and outer iterations, replacing a prescribed absolute tolerance sequence with a single relative tolerance parameter. Moreover, we establish rigorous convergence guarantees for D-ripALM under general convexity assumptions, without requiring smoothness or strong convexity conditions commonly imposed in the distributed optimization literature. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that a restarted variant of D-ripALM achieves competitive computational efficiency and solution accuracy relative to representative decentralized algorithms.

papers.title: Convergence Rate of the Last Iterate of Stochastic Proximal Algorithms
papers.abstract: We analyze two classical algorithms for solving additively composite convex optimization problems where the objective is the sum of a smooth term and a nonsmooth regularizer. The first algorithm is the proximal stochastic gradient method for a single regularizer; the second is the randomized incremental proximal method, which uses the proximal operator of a randomly selected function when the regularizer is given as the sum of many nonsmooth functions. We focus on relaxing the bounded variance assumption that is common, yet stringent, for getting last iterate convergence rates. We prove the $\widetilde{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ rate of convergence for the last iterate of both algorithms under componentwise convexity and smoothness, which is optimal up to log terms. Our results apply directly to graph-guided regularizers that arise in multi-task and federated learning, where the regularizer decomposes as a sum over edges of a collaboration graph.

papers.title: A nonvanishing criterion and families of counterexamples to the motivic Peterson conjecture
papers.abstract: The motivic Peterson conjecture asks whether the numerical condition forcing classical polynomial indecomposables to vanish has the same consequence in motivic cohomology. Kameko disproved this assertion by constructing a family of non-hit monomials. To determine all linear relations among the projected classes of these monomials, we compute the image of the motivic hit subspace under a projection onto their span: it consists precisely of the combinations whose coefficients sum to zero. Explicit Bockstein preimages establish the reverse inclusion, showing that no further linear relations hold and yielding a nonvanishing criterion. A binary calculation then produces infinitely many counterexamples for each fixed difference of at least three between the number of variables and the exterior degree.

papers.title: Composition operators on weighted Bergman spaces of the polydisc
papers.abstract: We study composition operators between weighted Bergman spaces of the polydisc induced by smooth symbols. We prove a general result of continuity which only involves the behaviour of the symbol on the polytorus. We deduce from this several consequences about the automatic continuity of the induced operator. We study in depth the case of the tridisc and exhibit several examples showing that a characterization of continuity using only derivatives seems impossible.

papers.title: A hierarchical splitting approach for N-split differential equations
papers.abstract: We propose a hierarchical splitting approach that constructs splitting methods for N-split differential equations by iteratively applying splitting methods for two-split systems along a splitting tree. Since assigning methods of order p to all nodes of the tree yields a hierarchical splitting method of order p, the order theory for two-split systems carries over to any number of partitions. We derive explicit formulas for the leading-order error terms, investigate self-adjointness, and show that state-of-the-art composition approaches are contained in the resulting class as special cases. Augmenting the approach with multiple time stepping yields a framework at the intersection of geometric numerical integration and multirate integration, for which we characterize the computational order of a multirate integrator and introduce a reweighting of the multirate factors that reduces computational overhead, but can lead to an order reduction when applied within composition techniques. We further discuss principles for designing splitting trees, with particular attention to separable Hamiltonian systems and port-Hamiltonian systems. Numerical experiments for both classes demonstrate that the hierarchical splitting approach yields efficient methods for N-split systems. We find that the approach is particularly efficient when commutator-based splitting methods become available and the partitions evolve on distinct time scales.

papers.title: Succinct Strict Pair Certificates for Reduced Groebner Bases
papers.abstract: We classify verification of supplied strict critical-pair witnesses for Groebner bases in a graph model with shared polynomial and exponent computations. Over the rationals, unrestricted verification in two variables is polynomial-time many-one equivalent to identity testing for powerful skew circuits over the integers. The reverse reduction uses a fixed two-element reduced Groebner basis and preserves the formal monomial bound on every witness it constructs. The forward reduction gives a one-sided-error randomized polynomial-time verifier without a support bound. We also prove matching bounds on certificate length for explicit families. For a bivariate family indexed by $k$, literal shifts require $Θ(k^2)$ bits, shared exponent computations require $Θ(k)$ bits, and an expanded certificate requires $Ω(k2^k)$ bits. For a multivariate family with $K=\sum_i k_i$, the bounds are $Θ(nK+\sum_i k_i^2)$ for full shift vectors and $Θ(K\log_2(n+1)+\sum_i k_i^2)$ for sparse shift labels.

papers.title: Combined effects of evaporation, sedimentation and solute crystallization on the dynamics of aerosol size distributions on multiple length and time scales
papers.abstract: We investigate three aspects of aerosol-mediated air-borne viral infection mechanisms on different length and time scales. First, we address the evolution of the size distribution of a non-interacting ensemble of droplets that are subject to evaporation and sedimentation using a sharp droplet-air interface model. From the exact solution of the evolution equation we derive the viral load in the air and show that it depends sensitively on the relative humidity. Secondly, from Molecular Dynamics simulations we extract the molecular reflection coefficient of single water molecules from the air-water interface. This parameter determines the water condensation and evaporation rate at a liquid droplet surface and therefore the evaporation rate of aqueous droplets. We find the reflection of water to be negligible at room temperature but to rise significantly at elevated temperatures and for grazing incidence angles. Thirdly, we derive a thermodynamically consistent three-dimensional diffuse-interface model for solute-containing droplets that is formulated as a three-phase Cahn-Hilliard/Allen-Cahn system. By numerically solving the coupled system of equations, we explore representative scenarios that show that this model reproduces and generalizes features of the sharp-interface model. These interconnected studies on the dynamics of aerosol droplet evaporation are relevant in order to quantitatively assess the airborne infection risk under varying environmental conditions.

papers.title: Arboreal Networks and Ultrametrics
papers.abstract: Ultrametrics are an important class of distances used in applications such as phylogenetics, clustering and classification theory. Ultrametrics are essentially distances that can be represented by an edge-weighted rooted tree so that all of the distances in the tree from the root to any leaf of the tree are equal. In this paper, we introduce a generalization of ultrametrics called arboreal ultrametrics which have applications in phylogenetics and also arise in the theory of distance-hereditary graphs. These are partial distances, that is distances that are not necessarily defined for every pair of elements in the groundset, that can be represented by an ultrametric arboreal network, that is, an edge-weighted rooted network whose underlying graph is a tree. As with ultrametrics all of the distances in the ultrametric arboreal network from any root to any leaf below it are are equal but, in contrast, the network may have more than one root. In our two main results we characterize when a partial distance is an arboreal ultrametric as well as proving that, somewhat surprisingly, given any unrooted edge-weighted phylogenetic tree there is a necessarily unique way to insert roots into this tree so as to obtain an arboreal ultrametric.

papers.title: Learning Multinomial Logits in $O(n \log n)$ time
papers.abstract: A Multinomial Logit (MNL) model is composed of a finite universe of items $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, each assigned a positive weight. A query specifies an admissible subset---called a slate---and the model chooses one item from that slate with probability proportional to its weight. This query model is also known as the Plackett--Luce model or conditional sampling oracle in the literature. Although MNLs have been studied extensively, a basic computational question remains open: given query access to slates, how efficiently can we learn weights so that, for every slate, the induced choice distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the ground truth? This question is central to MNL learning and has direct implications for modern recommender system interfaces. We provide both adaptive and non-adaptive algorithms for this task. Our first adaptive algorithm makes $O(\frac{n\log n}{\varepsilon^2})$ queries and learns every choice distribution in total variation distance $\varepsilon$. We also provide a second adaptive algorithm that with $O(\frac{n \log n}{\varepsilon^3})$ queries provides a stronger guarantee: each choice distribution is approximated to a multiplicative $1\pm\varepsilon$ error (except for subsets of mass smaller than $\varepsilon$). We complement these algorithms with lower bounds of $Ω(\frac{n\log n}{\varepsilon^2})$ for total variation distance and $Ω(\frac{n \log n}{\varepsilon^3})$ for the multiplicative error guarantee, showing the optimality of our adaptive algorithms. Our non-adaptive algorithm makes $O\left(\frac{n^{2}}{\varepsilon^{3}}\log n \log\frac{n}{\varepsilon}\right)$ queries to obtain guarantees under the multiplicative error notion. We complement this result with an $Ω(\frac{n^2 \log n}{\varepsilon^2})$ lower bound for any non-adaptive algorithm, showing that our algorithm is almost tight in $n$ (within a $\log n$ factor).

papers.title: Data-driven Reduction of Transfer Operators for Particle Clustering Dynamics
papers.abstract: We develop an operator-based framework to coarse-grain interacting particle systems that exhibit clustering dynamics. Starting from the particle-based transfer operator, we first construct a sequence of reduced representations: the operator is projected onto concentrations and then further reduced by representing the concentration dynamics on a geometric low-dimensional manifold and an adapted finite-state discretization. The resulting coarse-grained transfer operator is finally estimated from dynamical simulation data by inferring the transition probabilities between the Markov states. Applied to systems with multichromatic and Morse interaction potentials, the reduced model reproduces key features of the clustering process, including transitions between cluster configurations and the emergence of metastable states. Spectral analysis and transition-path analysis of the estimated operator reveal implied time scales and dominant transition pathways, providing an interpretable and efficient description of particle-clustering dynamics.

papers.title: Variational estimates for discrete spherical averages: $\ell^p$-boundedness and related arithmetic obstructions
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate variational inequalities for the family of discrete spherical averages. We establish $\ell^p$-boundedness of the $r$-variation operators for $1<p<\infty$ and $r>2$ along sufficiently sparse sequences of factorial radii. Moreover, we also study arithmetic obstructions to these variational estimates and construct counterexamples to show that such boundedness properties for the corresponding variational operators cannot hold for lacunary sequences of radii.

papers.title: Efficient Inference for Inverse Reinforcement Learning and Dynamic Discrete Choice Models
papers.abstract: In many sequential decision-making problems, researchers observe actions but not the rewards that drive behavior, yet wish to evaluate counterfactual policies. Flexible inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) methods accommodate rich reward representations but typically lack valid inference, whereas classical dynamic discrete choice (DDC) methods provide inference under restrictive parametric structure. We develop a semiparametric framework for debiased inverse reinforcement learning in maximum-entropy IRL and Gumbel-shock DDC models. We show that the log behavior policy acts as a pseudo-reward, identifying policy-value differences without point identifying the reward and, under a normalization, yielding a point-identified reward representative. This reduces inference on reward-dependent estimands to inference on smooth functionals of the behavior policy and transition kernel. We establish pathwise differentiability and characterize efficient influence functions through reward and transition Riesz representers, with the transition component obtainable from existing observed-reward off-policy evaluation theory. For normalized rewards, we derive an explicit transformation of these representers that accounts for the normalization constraint. We construct automatic debiased machine-learning estimators that permit flexible nuisance estimation while attaining $\sqrt{n}$-consistency, asymptotic normality, and semiparametric efficiency. We illustrate the theory through efficient inference for fixed-policy values under pseudo-rewards and normalized rewards, and for counterfactual values when the agent reoptimizes over a restricted action set.

papers.title: Computations with diagonal simplicial tensor modules
