papers.abstract: For each vertex order $π$ of a finite simple graph on at least two vertices, insert an isolated vertex between successive vertices. In the resulting adjacency matrix $A$, deleting row $i$ and column $i$ gives a principal submatrix $A_i$. The alternating sum of the $A_i$ is the simplicial boundary of $A$ and has full rank over $\mathbb F_2$ exactly when $π$ traces a Hamiltonian path. Each Hamiltonian path gives two full-rank orders. We tabulate boundary rank distributions over all vertex orders of the Petersen, $4\times4$ rook, and Shrikhande graphs. Full-rank counts distinguish the cospectral rook and Shrikhande graphs. For each finite graph, vertex and edge tensors in a three-axis diagonal simplicial tensor module generate a simplicial submodule whose normalized chains form the graph's incidence complex and compute its homology. Let $X$ be a diagonal simplicial tensor module on $k\ge1$ axes over a nonzero unital commutative ring. We give coordinate bases for its horn kernels and normalized chains. A horn has a unique filler exactly when its degree exceeds $k$. For a shape in $X$ of simplicial dimension $n$ (shortest axis length $n+1$), the simplicial module $X$ is an $n$-hypergroupoid exactly when $k\le n$. We prove analogous bounds for horn filling in a dendroidal module on rooted trees. Over a field, we construct a rational map from the space of hypermatrices of fixed shape and degree to a product of Grassmannians. The reduced closure of its image is rational and, over $\mathbb C$, is isomorphic to a Schubert variety. Python code for this paper's examples and rank tables is at https://github.com/flengyel/SimplicialTensors.

papers.title: Infinitely many positive normalized solutions for Schrödinger equations with nonlinear point defects on noncompact metric graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the multiplicity of positive normalized solutions for the following Schrödinger equation with nonlinear point defects on a general metric graph $\G=(\V,\E)$, possibly with infinitely many edges \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u'' = λu & \text{on every } \e \in \E, \\ \int_\G \abs{u}^2\, dx = μ& \\ \displaystyle \sum_{\e \succ \vv} u'_\e(\vv) = -\abs{u(\vv)}^{p-2}u(\vv) & \text{at every } \vv \in \V_0, \\ \displaystyle \sum_{\e \succ \vv} u'_\e(\vv) = 0 & \text{at every } \vv \in \V \setminus \V_0, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $p>2$, $\G$ is connected, $\V_0 \subset \V$ is nonempty, $μ>0$ is a given constant, $λ$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplie. For $p\neq4$, every fixed nonempty finite set $W\subset\V_0$ gives at least $2^{\#W}-1$ distinct positive normalized solutions, for every sufficiently small mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$ and for every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $2<p<4$. When $\V_0$ is finite and $\G$ is noncompact with the bottom of the Kirchhoff Laplacian spectrum equal to zero, we prove that there are exactly $2^{\#\V_0}-1$ positive solutions at every sufficiently small mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$, and at every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $2<p<4$ and $|\overline B_r(o)|=O(r^{4/p})$ as $r\to+\infty$ for a fixed $o\in\G$. If infinitely many defect vertices $\vv \in \V_0$ have uniformly bounded degree, we also obtain infinitely many positive solutions that are pairwise inequivalent under the automorphisms of $\G$ preserving $\V_0$, for every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $2<p<4$ and for every prescribed mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$. In the $L^2$-critical ($p=4$) case, under local conditions near the selected defect vertices, analogous results hold for masses slightly below $kq^2/2$, where $k$ is the number of these vertices and $q$ is their common degree.

papers.title: Linear independence of values of Dirichlet $L$ functions
papers.abstract: For any Dirichlet character $χ$ with conductor $N$, we give a lower bound of order $\sqrt{s/\log(s)}$ on the dimension of the $\mathbb{Q}(e^{2iπ/\varphi(N)})$-vector space spanned by the values of its $L$-function at integers $2\leq i\leq s$ of the parity opposite to that of $χ$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. This generalizes a 2026 result of Fischler, which corresponds to principal characters. To this end, we construct linear combinations of these values of $L$-functions using a refined version of Siegel's lemma, and apply to them a linear independence criterion that generalizes Fischler's. To verify a crucial hypothesis of this criterion, we rely on a ``Shidlovskii's lemma".

papers.title: Variational analysis of determinantal varieties
papers.abstract: Determinantal varieties---the sets of bounded-rank matrices or tensors---have attracted growing interest in low-rank optimization. The tangent cone to low-rank sets is widely studied and underpins a range of geometric methods. The second-order geometry, which encodes curvature information, is more intricate. In this work, we develop a unified framework to derive explicit formulas for both first- and second-order tangent sets to various low-rank sets, including low-rank matrices, tensors, symmetric matrices, and positive semidefinite matrices. The framework also accommodates the intersection of a low-rank set and another set satisfying some assumptions, thereby yielding a tangent intersection rule. Through the lens of tangent sets, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition under which a nonsmooth problem and its smooth parameterization share equivalent second-order stationary points. As applications, we exploit tangent sets to characterize optimality conditions for low-rank optimization and prove that verifying second-order optimality is NP-hard. Moreover, for low-rank semidefinite programs, the Burer--Monteiro parameterization maps fourth-order stationary points of the parameterized problem to second-order stationary points of the original problem. In a separate line of analysis, we investigate variational geometry of the graph of the normal cone to matrix varieties, deriving the explicit Bouligand tangent cone, Fréchet and Mordukhovich normal cones to the graph. These results are further applied to develop optimality conditions for low-rank bilevel programs.

papers.title: Equi-integrable approximation of Sobolev mappings between manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that limits of sequences of smooth maps between compact Riemannian manifolds with equi-integrable $W^{1, p}$-Sobolev energy can always be strongly approximated by smooth maps, giving a counterpart of Hang's density result in $W^{1, 1}$ for the Sobolev space $W^{1, p}$ with integer $p \ge 2$. Our result extends to higher-order Sobolev spaces and is straightforward in fractional Sobolev spaces. We also provide a proof based on the weak continuity of Jacobians in the cases where the cohomological criterion of Bethuel, Demengel, Colon and Hélein applies.

papers.title: Adjusting SPRT for an Asymptotically Efficient Procedure with Finite Number of Applications of Less Effective Treatment
papers.abstract: We propose an adaptive Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) with a finite expected number of allocations to the less effective treatment. In the classical SPRT framework, patients are assigned to the two competing treatments one-by-one until a stopping criterion, based on breaching the boundary values which are pre-determined using the Type-I and Type-II error probabilities, is met. This controls the errors at the cost of ethical efficiency as the exposure to the less effective treatment is large. For testing two simple hypotheses, our proposed procedure employs a likelihood ratio-driven adaptive allocation rule, dynamically concentrating sampling effort on the superior population while preserving asymptotic efficiency (in terms of average sample number) comparable to the classical SPRT. We show that at each step, the allocated observations remain independent despite the data-dependent allocation, prove that the expected number of allocations to the inferior treatment remains finite, with an explicit upper bound, and derive a closed-form approximation to it. Extensive simulation studies and data-calibrated case studies substantiate the theoretical results, evincing a significant reduction in inferior allocations compared to the classical SPRT. The proposed design thus offers a balanced method between statistical precision and ethical responsibility, aligning inferential reliability with patient safety.

papers.title: A convenient category of locales
papers.abstract: The notion of Kan extendable subcategories was initially introduced to define the category of compactly generated fibrewise topological spaces over a T1 base space and to establish its cartesian closure. In this paper, we show that the same framework can likewise be applied to define the category of compactly generated strongly Hausdorff locales and to prove that it, too, is cartesian closed

papers.title: Attractors of sequences coding $β$-integers
papers.abstract: In this paper, we describe minimal string attractors of prefixes of simple Parry sequences. These sequences form a coding of distances between consecutive $β$-integers in numeration systems with a real base $β$. Simple Parry sequences have been recently studied from this point of view and attractors of prefixes have been described. However, the authors themselves had doubts about their minimality and conjectured that attractors of alphabet size should be sufficient. We confirm their conjecture. Moreover, we provide minimal attractors of prefixes of some particular form of binary non-simple Parry sequences.

papers.title: $m$-Positivity and Regularisation
papers.abstract: Starting from the notion of $m$-plurisubharmonic function introduced recently by Dieu and studied, in particular, by Harvey and Lawson, we consider $m$-(semi-)positive $(1,\,1)$-currents and Hermitian holomorphic line bundles on complex Hermitian manifolds and prove two kinds of results: vanishing theorems and $L^2$-estimates for the $\bar\partial$-equation in the context of $C^\infty$ $m$-positive Hermitian fibre metrics; global and local regularisation theorems for $m$-semi-positive $(1,\,1)$-currents whose proofs involve the use of viscosity subsolutions for a certain Monge-Ampère-type equation and the associated Dirichlet problem. The results of the latter type require techniques of a substantially different nature from those of the classical $m=1$ case and have already been applied in subsequent joint work of the present authors and in further work of the second-named author with K. Broder.

papers.title: Survival of the fittest Cox model: Pivotal variable selection for time-to-event data
papers.abstract: We revisit Cox's proportional hazards model to improve variable selection in survival analysis. A square-root transformation of the partial likelihood renders the selection of the regularization parameter asymptotically pivotal: the baseline hazard and the censoring rate cancel exactly, and the way censoring is spread over time only enters through a bounded correction of order $1/\log n$. Using martingale residuals, we compute this penalty level by Monte Carlo without reordering the design matrix. The resulting criterion borrows from information criteria such as BIC and from penalized regression methods such as the lasso, taking the best of both. On simulated and real data, our method substantially improves upon state-of-the-art approaches used daily.

papers.title: Don't Look Back in Anger: Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Optimization with Nonstationary Data
papers.abstract: We study data-driven decision problems where historical observations are generated by a time-evolving distribution whose change over time is bounded in Wasserstein distance. We address this nonstationarity using a distributionally robust optimization model with an ambiguity set that is a Wasserstein ball centered at a weighted empirical distribution, thereby allowing for the time decay of past data in a way which accounts for the drift of the data-generating distribution. Our main technical contribution is a concentration bound for weighted empirical distributions that explicitly captures both the effective sample size (i.e., the equivalent number of equally weighted observations) and the distributional drift. Using our concentration bound, we select observation weights that optimally balance the effective sample size against the distributional drift of the data-generating process, taking into account the order of the Wasserstein ball. We also consider simple weighting schemes, and find that across a wide range of problem settings, a triangular weighting scheme is an effective choice that outperforms the classical weighting schemes of time windowing and simple exponential smoothing. Numerical experiments on a multi-item newsvendor problem illustrate the benefits of our approach.

papers.title: Extensions of Robbins-Siegmund Theorem with Applications in Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: The Robbins-Siegmund theorem establishes the convergence of stochastic processes that are almost supermartingales and is one of the most commonly used approaches for analyzing stochastic iterative algorithms in stochastic approximation and reinforcement learning (RL). However, its original form has a significant limitation as it requires the zero-order term to be summable. In many important RL applications, this summable condition, however, cannot be met. This limitation motivates us to extend the Robbins-Siegmund theorem for almost supermartingales where the zero-order term is not summable, but only square-summable. In particular, we introduce a novel and mild assumption on the increments of the stochastic processes. This together with the square-summable condition enables an almost sure convergence to a bounded set. Additionally, we further provide almost sure convergence rates, high probability concentration bounds, and $L^p$ convergence rates. We then apply the new results to stochastic approximation and RL. Notably, we obtain the first almost sure convergence rate, the first high probability concentration bound, and the first $L^p$ convergence rate for $Q$-learning with linear function approximation.

papers.title: A FISTA-type Riemannian Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method
papers.abstract: We study accelerated proximal gradient methods for minimizing the sum of a smooth and a nonsmooth function on Riemannian manifolds. Accelerated convergence rates under geodesic convexity have not been established for some existing methods, and global geodesic convexity may fail or be difficult to verify. We develop a Riemannian accelerated proximal gradient method that combines tangent-space proximal steps with momentum updates based on parallel transport and the exponential map. Under geodesic $μ$-strong convexity ($μ\geqslant0$) of the smooth term and pullback $ρ$-convexity ($ρ\in\mathbb{R}$) of the nonsmooth term, we establish accelerated convergence rates for the objective gap: an $\mathcal{O}(k^{-2})$ rate when $μ-ρ\geqslant0$ and a linear rate when $μ-ρ>0$, where $k$ is the iteration count. The rates depend on sectional curvature bounds and the diameter of a prescribed region assumed to contain the iterates. For nonconvex objectives or unknown problem parameters, we further consider an adaptive restart variant with proximal gradient safeguards. If the initial sublevel set is compact, we prove that every accumulation point of the safeguard reference sequence is stationary and that an $\varepsilon$-stationary point is obtained within $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations for any tolerance $\varepsilon>0$. Both methods also apply to smooth objectives. In this setting, the basic method yields a single Riemannian accelerated gradient scheme for geodesically convex and geodesically $μ$-strongly convex problems. Its iteration and parameter recurrence extend continuously to $μ=0$, and a single analysis establishes accelerated rates in both cases. Numerical experiments on nonsmooth composite and smooth problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Optimal phase change for a generalized Grover's algorithm
papers.abstract: We study the generalized Grover's algorithm with an arbitrary amplitude vector to find the optimal phase change for maximizing the gain in probability for the target of each iteration. In the classic setting of Grover's algorithm with a real initial amplitude vector, we find that a phase change of $π$ stays optimal until the probability of observing the target is quite close to 1. We provide a formula for identifying this cut-off point based on the size of the data set. When the amplitude is truly complex, we find that the optimal phase change depends non-trivially on the complexity of the amplitude vector. We provide an optimization formula to identify the required optimal phase change.

papers.title: Property B: A Baumgartner-style Property that Applies to Preservation of $\aleph_1$ and $\aleph_2$ under Iterations with Supports of Size $\aleph_1$
papers.abstract: We prove a theorem on iterated forcing that can be used for preservation of $\aleph_2$ and $\aleph_1$ in the usual iterations along an ordinal, with supports of size $\aleph_1$ of forcings that have amalgamation properties similar to those present in the perfect set forcing. The work is modelled after Baumgartner's Axiom A and his proof that iterations with countable support of the same preserve $\aleph_1$. In honour of James E. Baumgartner, the property introduced here is called Property B$(κ)$. The known additional difficulties when forcing at cardinals higher than $\aleph_1$ make for a less general theorem and a more complex theorem on the iteration, which is not an iteration theorem in the classical sense. The results extend to other cardinals $κ$ such that $κ^{<κ}=κ$, in place of $\aleph_1$. We give examples of individual forcings that have Property B$(κ)$ and their products. In particular, we introduce a correct version of the generalised perfect set forcing, which we call Perfect Set Forcing with Respect to a Filter. We give its basic properties and show that for the right kind of filter $\mathcal F$ this kind of forcing is iterable with supports of size $\leκ$. Our further work has extended some of the results from the paper to iterations along any well-founded partial order.

papers.title: A case of the dijoin conjecture on inverting oriented graphs
papers.abstract: For an oriented graph $D$, the inversion of $X\subseteq V(D)$ in $D$ is the graph obtained by reversing the orientation of all arcs with both ends in $X$. The inversion number $\mathrm{inv}(D)$ is the minimum number of inversions needed to obtain an acyclic oriented graph. We show that the dijoin conjecture of Bang-Jensen, da Silva and Havet, that $\mathrm{inv}(D_1\rightarrow D_2)=\mathrm{inv}(D_1)+\mathrm{inv}(D_2)$, is true in the case where $\mathrm{inv}(D_1)=2$ and $\mathrm{inv}(D_2)$ is even. We also characterise the cases $\mathrm{inv}(D_1)=2$ and $\mathrm{inv}(D_2)$ odd, for which the conjecture does and does not hold. We then go on to show a similar result for n-joins, in doing so we prove a conjecture of Alon, Powierski, Savery, Scott and Wilmer. Our proofs build on the idea of tournament minimum rank, introduced by Behague, Johnston, Morrison and Ogden.

papers.title: Weighted Kernel Functions on Planar Domains
papers.abstract: We study the variation of weighted Szegő and Garabedian kernels on planar domains with respect to the weight and establish a Ramadanov-type convergence theorem. As a consequence, we obtain detailed information on the behaviour of the zeros of the weighted Szegő and Garabedian kernels for weights close to the constant function $1$ on the boundary. We also study the weighted Ahlfors map and strengthen known results concerning its boundary behaviour. Explicit examples of the weighted kernels are presented for certain classes of weights. We strengthen Nehari's construction of the weighted Szegő and Garabedian kernels by showing that the meromorphic function associated with the weight can be chosen holomorphic. We further identify his auxiliary kernels with reproducing kernels of finite-codimensional Hardy subspaces, and derive further representation formulas and consequences. Finally, we discuss the weighted Carathéodory metric, and describe relations between the weighted Szegő and Garabedian kernels with certain classical kernel functions.

papers.title: A marking graph for finite-type Artin groups
papers.abstract: Clean markings on surfaces were a key component in Masur and Minsky's hierarchy machinery, which proved to be a powerful tool in the study of mapping class groups. We construct a marking graph for irreducible finite-type Artin groups which is quasi-isometric to the group modulo its center, i.e., an element of $A_Γ/Z(A_Γ)$ is determined up to finite error by its action on one of our markings. To construct this graph, we construct suitable collections of transverse parabolic subgroups which extend the maximal simplices of the complex of irreducible parabolic subgroups to analogues of clean markings, and we define natural analogues of elementary moves.

papers.title: Unimodality and Cluster Algebras from Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the rank polynomial of the lattice of order ideals of a loop fence poset is unimodal. This poset arises as the poset of join-irreducibles in the lattice of good matchings of loop graphs associated with notched arcs. Equivalently, such polynomials can be obtained by evaluating all coefficient variables in an F-polynomial at a single variable q. We also conclude that the rank polynomial of any tagged arc, whether plain or notched, is not only unimodal but also satisfies a symmetry condition known as almost interlacing. Furthermore, when the lamination consists of a single curve, the cluster expansion-evaluated by setting all cluster variables to 1 and all coefficient variables to q-is also unimodal. We conjecture that polynomials in this case are log-concave.

papers.title: Abstract Formulation of Mean-Field Models and Propagation of Chaos
papers.abstract: We formulate a unified abstract framework for mean-field particle systems and their macroscopic limits from the perspective of differential equations and functional analysis. Combining semigroup theory with optimal transport, we study measure-valued evolutions directly through their generators, allowing different classes of mean-field models to be treated within a common structure. Specifically, the framework involves (1) formulating mean-field models abstractly using semigroups and generators; (2) establishing well-posedness of the corresponding nonlinear mean-field evolution equations in a class of solutions stable under approximation; and (3) proving quantitative propagation of chaos for the associated $N$-particle systems. The central tool is the transport derivative, which measures the infinitesimal variation of transport costs between Markov evolutions. We establish transport-stability criteria expressed through local generator inequalities and show how these criteria underpin both nonlinear well-posedness and particle approximation. When the generator's dependence on the law is controlled by averaged Hilbert-valued features, we obtain an $O(N^{-1})$ sampling contribution to the quadratic Wasserstein estimate through a variance argument. As an application, we obtain quantitative propagation of chaos for Lévy-type mean-field systems with state- and law-dependent drift, diffusion, and jump kernels under intrinsic transport conditions. The admissible jump kernels extend beyond those generated by multiplicative Lévy noise, demonstrating the scope of the abstract framework.

papers.title: Irreducible representations of pointed Hopf algebras of type $A_2$
papers.abstract: We classify the irreducible representations of a family of finite-dimensional pointed liftings $H_λ$ of the Nichols algebra associated with the diagram $A_2$ with parameter $q=-1$. We show that these algebras have infinite representation type and construct an indecomposable $H_λ$-module of dimension $n$ for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Finally, we study a semisimple category $\underline{\operatorname{Rep}} H_λ$ arising as a quotient of $\operatorname{Rep} H_λ$.

papers.title: Embedding lattices of quasivarieties of periodic groups into lattices of additively idempotent semiring varieties: An algebraic proof
papers.abstract: A general result by Jackson (Flat algebras and the translation of universal Horn logic to equational logic, J. Symb. Log. 73(1) (2008) 90--128) implies that the lattice of all quasivarieties of groups of exponent dividing $n$ embeds into the lattice $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$ of all varieties of additively idempotent semirings whose multiplicative semigroups are unions of groups of exponent dividing $n$; the image of this embedding is an interval in $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$. We provide a new, direct, and purely algebraic proof of these facts and present a new identity basis for the top variety of the interval. In addition, we obtain new information about the lattice $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$, demonstrating that the properties of the lattice for $n\ge 3$ differ drastically from those previously known when $n=1$ or $2$.

papers.title: A nonsmooth extension of the Brezzi-Rappaz-Raviart approximation theorem via metric regularity techniques and applications to nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: We generalize the Brezzi-Rappaz-Raviart approximation theorem, which allows to obtain existence and a priori error estimates for approximations of solutions to some nonlinear partial differential equations. Our contribution lies in the fact that we typically allow for nonlinearities having merely Lipschitz regularity, while previous results required some form of differentiability. This is achieved by making use of the theory of metrically regular mappings, developed in the context of variational analysis. We apply this generalization to derive quasi-optimal error estimates for finite element approximations to solutions of viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations and second order mean field game systems.

papers.title: Uniform Hypercontractivity and Log-Sobolev Inequality and Applications for Non-equilibrium Kinetic System
papers.abstract: In this paper, we derive exponential ergodicity in relative entropy for general kinetic SDEs under a partially dissipative condition. It covers non-equilibrium situations where the forces are not of gradient type and the invariant measure does not have an explicit density, extending previous results set in the equilibrium case. The key argument is to establish the hypercontractivity of the associated semigroup, which follows from its hyperboundedness and its $L^2$-exponential ergodicity. Moreover, we obtain exponential ergodicity in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance by combining Talagrand's inequality with a log-Harnack inequality. These results are further extended to the McKean-Vlasov setting and to the associated mean-field interacting particle systems under a suitable smallness condition on the distribution dependence. In the latter case, the convergence rates are uniform in the number of particles and we also establish the hypercontractivity and log-Sobolev inequality uniform in the number of particles using a new approach based on Girsanov's transform and hypercontractivity.

papers.title: An inverse problem for semilinear elliptic equations with generalized Kerr-type nonlinearities
papers.abstract: We study the inverse problem of reconstructing the convex hull of unknown inclusions in semilinear elliptic equations with nonanalytic nonlinearities, by extending Ikehata's enclosure method to accommodate such nonlinear effects. To overcome the lack of the higher-order differentiability required for the Taylor-based construction, we construct an approximate solution based on the linearized equation through a first-iteration approximation. Under suitable structural conditions on the nonlinearity, we establish a reconstruction result for the convex hull of the inclusion. The method applies to a broad class of generalized Kerr-type nonlinearities that need not be analytic, without requiring an explicit formula for the nonlinear term. We also address the numerical challenges arising from the exponential decay of the CGO test data and show how they limit the accuracy of an implementation in double-precision arithmetic.

papers.title: Convergence of adaptive boundary element methods driven by functional a posteriori error estimates
papers.abstract: The recent work [Kurz et al., Numer. Math., 147 (2021)] proposed functional a posteriori error estimates for boundary element methods (BEMs) together with a related adaptive mesh-refinement strategy. Unlike most a posteriori BEM error estimators, the proposed functional error estimators cover Galerkin as well as collocation BEM and, more importantly, do not control the error in the integral density on the boundary, but the error of the potential approximation in the domain, which is of greater relevance in practice. The estimates rely on the numerical solution of auxiliary problems on auxiliary strip domains along the boundary, where the strips are affected by the adaptive mesh-refinement and hence vary. For Galerkin BEM, we prove that the proposed adaptive mesh-refinement algorithm yields convergence of the potential error to zero. Due to the structural difference to residual-based estimators, the proof requires new ideas.

papers.title: A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme for Lévy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Drifts
papers.abstract: We present an explicit numerical approximation scheme, denoted by $\{X^n\}$, for the effective simulation of solutions $X$ to a multivariate stochastic differential equation (SDE) with a superlinearly growing $κ$-dissipative drift, where $κ>1$, driven by a multiplicative heavy-tailed Lévy process that has a finite $p$-th moment, with $p>0$. We show that the strong $L^{p_X}$-convergence $\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbf E \|X^n_t-X_t\|^{p_X}=\mathcal O (h_n^γ)$ holds for any $p_X\in (0,p+κ-1)$, which is exactly the range where the $p_X$-moment of the solution is known to be finite. Additionally, for any $p_X\in (0,p)$ we establish strong uniform convergence: $\mathbf E\sup_{t\in[0,T]} \|X^n_t-X_t\|^{p_X}=\mathcal{O} ( h_n^δ )$. In both cases we determine the convergence rates $γ$ and $δ$. In the special case of SDEs driven solely by a Brownian motion, our numerical scheme preserves super-exponential moments of the solution. The scheme $\{X^n\}$ is realized as a combination of a well-known Euler method with a Lie-Trotter type splitting technique.

papers.title: The Cesàro Value Iteration
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider undiscouted infinite-horizon optimal control for deterministic systems with an uncountable state and input space. We specifically address the case when the classic value iteration does not converge. For such systems, we use the Ces`aro mean to define the infinite-horizon optimal control problem and the corresponding infinite-horizon value function. Moreover, for this value function, we introduce the Cesàro value iteration and prove its convergence for the special case of systems with periodic optimal operating behavior. For this instance, we also show that the Cesàro value function recovers the undiscounted infinite-horizon optimal cost, if the latter is well-defined.

papers.title: Veech groups of covers of the Chamanara surface
papers.abstract: We study finite abelian covers of the Chamanara surface, an example of a finite-area infinite translation surface with interesting dynamics and a large Veech group. Specifically, the Veech group of the Chamanara surface is a virtually free group on two generators. We characterize when finite abelian covers have large Veech groups themselves, namely when their Veech group has finite index in that of the Chamanara surface. For degree-2 covers, we provide a detailed analysis of these finite-index Veech groups. As an application, we prove that every free group arises as the projective Veech group of a finite-area infinite translation surface.

papers.title: Persistent Stiefel-Whitney Classes of Tangent Bundles
papers.abstract: Stiefel--Whitney classes are invariants of the tangent bundle of a smooth manifold, represented as cohomology classes of the base manifold. These classes are essential in obstruction theory, embedding problems, and cobordism theory. In this work, we propose a concrete algorithm to compute persistent cohomology classes representing these characteristic classes. Given a point cloud, we construct a Čech or alpha filtration and apply the Wu formula using the cup product and Steenrod squares. The algorithm runs in polynomial time in the number of simplices without estimating tangent spaces or constructing a classifying map. Under suitable hypotheses on the filtration, the resulting classes represent those of a closed smooth manifold even when the filtration contains additional wedge summands on whose reduced cohomology all positive Steenrod squares vanish. For sufficiently large samples drawn independently and uniformly from the manifold, recovery holds with high probability over an interval of scales. We present experiments on triangulated four-manifolds and on point clouds from image patches and a molecular conformation space.

papers.title: Further Generalization of Ramanujan Sums with Regular A-Functions
papers.abstract: In the study of Ramanujan sums, the so-called regular $A$-function is a set-valued multiplicative function that tracks certain subsets of the divisor sets of natural numbers. McCarthy provided a generalization of the Ramanujan sum using these regular $A$-function based arithmetic convolutions. This approach has recently attracted considerable interest from several researchers. In this paper, we extend McCarthy's generalization by introducing two regular $A$-functions corresponding to both parameters in the Ramanujan sum. Our generalization exhibits several properties of the Ramanujan sums. Using the regular $A$-function, We also generalize the greatest common divisor (GCD) function and the Von Sterneck formula. Our introduction of two regular $A$-functions into these expressions enables us to explore a novel perspective on the connection between these expressions and the order relation between the two regular $A$-functions. In particular, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions for orthogonality and Dedekind-Hölder's identity (i.e., Ramanujan sum = Von Sterneck function) to hold. Our primary motivation for the proposed generalization is Ramanujan expansions of arithmetic functions based on arbitrary regular $A$-functions. These expansions of arbitrary $A$-functions discussed here are new in the literature.

papers.title: Settling the no-$(k+1)$-in-line problem when $k$ is not small
papers.abstract: What is the maximum number of points that can be selected from an $n\times n$ square lattice so that no $k+1$ of them are collinear? This was asked more than $100$ years ago for $k=2$ and it remained wide open ever since. In this paper, we prove the exact answer is $kn$, provided that $ n\ge k\ge C\log n$ for an absolute constant $C<20$. The proof relies on carefully constructed block-uniform random bipartite graphs and concentration inequalities.

papers.title: Jordan-Hölder property for shifted quantum affine algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that finite length representations of shifted quantum affine algebras in category $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are stable by fusion product. This implies that in the topological Grothendieck ring $K_0(\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}})$ the Grothendieck group of finite length representations forms a non-topological subring. We also conjecture this subring is isomorphic to the cluster algebra discovered in arXiv:2401.04616. In the course of our proofs, we establish that any simple representation in category $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ descends to a truncation, for certain truncation parameters as conjectured in arXiv:2010.06996 in terms of Langlands dual $q$-characters.

papers.title: Hardy operators: In the footsteps of Brown, Halmos, and Shields
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the two classical Hardy operators $\mathcal{H}_{1}$ on $L^2(0, 1)$ and $\mathcal{H}_{\infty}$ on $L^2(0, \infty)$ initially studied by Brown, Halmos and Shields. Particular emphasis is given to the construction of explicit cyclic and $*$-cyclic vectors in conjunction with a characterization of their invariant and reducing subspaces. We also provide a complete description of the frame vectors for $I - \mathcal{H}_{1}^{*}$.

papers.title: Itô formula for planarly branched rough paths
papers.abstract: The Itô formula is a cornerstone of stochastic calculus, providing a fundamental change-of-variables formula for stochastic processes. In rough path theory, Itô formulas have been proved for rough paths with roughness $\frac{1}{3}< α\leq \frac{1}{2}$ and branched rough paths with roughness $0< α\leq 1$. Planarly branched rough paths provide a natural framework for studying rough differential equations on homogeneous spaces, extending the theory of branched rough paths through the Munthe-Kaas-Wright Hopf algebra. In the present paper, we prove the Itô formula for planarly branched rough paths with roughness $\frac{1}{4}< α\leq \frac{1}{2}$.

papers.title: On finiteness of fiber space structures of klt Calabi-Yau pairs in dimension 3
papers.abstract: We prove that for a fixed klt Calabi-Yau pair $(X,Δ)$ of dimension $3$, the set of fiber space structures of $X$ is finite up to $Aut(X,Δ)$.

papers.title: Refined Strichartz Estimates for sub-Laplacians in Heisenberg and $H$-type groups
papers.abstract: We obtain refined Strichartz estimates for the sub-Riemannian Schrödinger equation on $H$-type Carnot groups using Fourier restriction techniques. In particular, we extend the previously known Strichartz estimates previously obtained for the Heisenberg group also to non radial initial data. The same arguments permits to obtain refined Strichartz estimates for the wave equation on $H$-type groups. Our proof is based on estimates for the spectral projectors for sub-Laplacians and reinterprets Strichartz estimates as Fourier restriction theorems for nilpotent groups in the context of trace-class operator valued measures.

papers.title: A hypergeometric transformation formula of Ramanujan, its validity range and implications
papers.abstract: We extend the validity range of a hypergeometric transformation formula of Ramanujan proved by Berndt, Bhargava and Garvan [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 347, 4163 (1995)] and study its implications. Relations to special values of complete elliptic integrals of the first kind in singular value theory are established. Consequently, we derive several closed-form evaluations of hypergeometric functions $_2F_1$ with different sets of parameters and arguments. Connections with other hypergeometric transformations and some recent results are discussed.

papers.title: A polyptych of multi-centered deformation spaces
papers.abstract: Extending Verdier's deformation space to the normal cone of a closed subscheme and Rost's double deformation space of a pair of nested closed subschemes, we introduce a notion of deformation spaces attached to chains of immersions of arbitrary lengths $n$. One main result, which builds on the formalism of multi-centered dilatations of schemes, is the existence of so-called panelization isomorphisms, which produce under suitable regularity conditions several canonical isomorphisms between a given deformation space of length $n$ and some deformation spaces of smaller lengths. Having these panelization isomorphisms also allows to give geometric descriptions of the strata -- certain restrictions of special interest -- of deformation spaces.

papers.title: Almost Sure Convergence Rates and Concentration of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning with Markovian Noise
papers.abstract: This paper establishes, to our knowledge, the first almost sure convergence rate and the first maximal concentration bound with sub-Weibull tails for general contractive stochastic approximation algorithms with Markovian noise. As a corollary, we also obtain convergence rates in $L^p$. Key to our successes is a novel discretization of the mean ODE of stochastic approximation algorithms using intervals with diminishing (instead of constant) length. Applications yield the first almost sure convergence rate for $Q$-learning without count-based learning rates and the first maximal concentration bound for off-policy temporal difference learning, both with Markovian samples.

papers.title: The one-shot problem: Solution to an open question of finite-fuel singular control with discretionary stopping
papers.abstract: We resolve a long-standing open question posed by Karatzas, Ocone, Wang, and Zervos (Stochastics, 2000) on finite-fuel singular stochastic control with discretionary stopping. Our approach introduces a novel "one-shot" solution technique, based on reduction to an auxiliary optimal stopping problem. We prove that, despite the convexity of the objective function, the waiting region of the optimal strategy need not be connected. Furthermore, we identify a qualitative transition in the optimal policy: even with arbitrarily small positive fuel, the solution can differ from the zero-fuel (pure optimal stopping) limit. These results reveal a fundamental non-robustness in such control problems, showing that zero-fuel models need not approximate behaviour under small but positive fuel constraints.

papers.title: Slow Mixing of Quantum Gibbs Samplers
papers.abstract: Preparing thermal (Gibbs) states is a common task in physics and computer science. Recent algorithms mimic cooling via system-bath coupling, where the cost is determined by mixing time, akin to classical Metropolis-like algorithms. However, few methods exist to demonstrate slow mixing in quantum systems, unlike the well-established classical tools for systems like the Ising model and constraint satisfaction problems. We present a quantum generalization of these tools through a generic bottleneck lemma that implies slow mixing in quantum systems. This lemma focuses on quantum measures of distance, analogous to the classical Hamming distance but rooted in uniquely quantum principles and quantified either through Bohr spectrum jumps or operator locality. Using our bottleneck lemma, we establish unconditional lower bounds on the mixing times of Gibbs samplers for several families of Hamiltonians at low temperatures. For classical Hamiltonians with mixing time lower bounds $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[Ω(n^α)]$, we prove that quantum Gibbs samplers also have $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[Ω(n^α)]$. This applies to models like random $K$-SAT instances and spin glasses. For stabilizer Hamiltonians, we provide a concise proof of exponential lower bounds $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[Ω(n)]$ on mixing times of good $n$-qubit stabilizer codes at low constant temperature. Finally, we consider constant-degree classical Hamiltonians and show how to lift classical slow mixing results in the presence of a transverse field using Poisson Feynman-Kac techniques. We show generic results for models with linear free energy barriers, and we demonstrate that our techniques extend to models with sublinear free energy barriers by proving $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[n^{1/2-o(1)}]$ for the ferromagnetic 2D transverse field Ising model.

papers.title: Regularity of the Semigroup of Regular Probability Measures on Locally Compact Hausdorff Topological Groups in which every element is of finite order
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group in which every element is of finite order, and let $P(\mathcal{G})$ denote the class of all regular probability measures on $\mathcal{G}$. In this note, it is observed that a characterization of algebraically regular elements in certain subsemigroups of $P(\mathcal{G})$ (Theorem~4.1 \cite{MNN}) for compact $\mathcal{G}$ remains true for locally compact $\mathcal{G}$. The results presented rely very much on Wendel's support theorem and the theory of doubly stochastic matrices (\cite{PLC} \cite{WEN}). A more general situation in which the assumption that every element is of finite order is not satisfied is also considered and illustrated with an example. This short article is a followup of \cite{MNN}.In addition,the random walk on an infinite discrete group associated with the generalised inverse of a probability measure is also studied.The last section is devoted to Fourier transform techniques to study the same problem using Bochner-type theorem in harmonic analysis.

papers.title: Fast Mixed-Precision Real Evaluation
papers.abstract: Evaluating real numbers to high precision is important in computational science, numerical computing, and in hardware and software design. Efficient algorithms exist for computing arithmetic operations and common elementary functions, but composing these primitives into larger expressions remains a challenge. The typical expression-evaluation algorithm computes all primitives in the expression to a uniform precision, doubling that precision until a sufficiently-accurate result is achieved. This is wasteful: usually only a few operations really need to be performed at high precision, and the bulk of the expression could be computed at a much lower, faster precision. However, no rigorous algorithm currently exists to compute these non-uniform precision assignments, nor to leverage non-uniform precision to reduce the number of primitive computations needed to evaluate an expression. We propose a new algorithm for deriving such rigorous precision assignments and reducing the number of primitive computations needed. This algorithm can leverage results computed at lower precisions to analytically determine a precision for each primitive that will result in a sufficiently-accurate evaluation. It can also use information from constant subexpressions, movability flags, and repeat flags to skip the computation of certain primitives, further reducing the time to evaluate real expressions. Our implementation, Reval, achieves an average speed-up of 3.97x compared to the widely-used Sollya tool, with the speed-up increasing to 9.26x on the most difficult inputs. A detailed evaluation shows that this speed-up results from both assigning lower precisions to the majority of primitives and from computing fewer primitives overall.

papers.title: Generic local identifiability for ODE inverse problems from discrete observations
papers.abstract: We study local parameter identification from finitely many measurements of an analytic output along a single ODE trajectory. At a fixed initial state and parameter, the time derivatives of the output sensitivity define a decreasing sequence of parameter kernels. If the sequence reaches zero, any prescribed pattern of distinct positive sampling times gives full parameter rank after a sufficiently small common rescaling, provided the number of times is at least the number of strict kernel drops. The orders of these drops determine the asymptotic orders of all singular values of the sampled Jacobian. We also give a sharp worst-case bound on the number of freely chosen observation times needed for the sampled Jacobian to have full column rank. At a generic point, the maximum parameter rank determines how many local parameter coordinates can vary without changing the observations. A quantitative inverse estimate bounds the error of every estimate in the certified neighborhood that fits the data at least as well as the true parameter. For a \(d\)-dimensional homogeneous linear system with known initial state and \(d\) equally spaced positive-time full-state observations, cyclicity for the sampled propagator is equivalent to local identifiability of the generator. In this case, one additional exact full-state sample at a time incommensurate with the grid spacing gives global recovery.

papers.title: An analogue of Reed's conjecture for digraphs
papers.abstract: Reed in 1998 conjectured that every graph $G$ satisfies $χ(G) \leq \lceil \frac{Δ(G)+1+ω(G)}{2} \rceil$. As a partial result, he proved the existence of $\varepsilon > 0$ for which every graph $G$ satisfies $χ(G) \leq \lceil (1-\varepsilon)(Δ(G)+1)+\varepsilonω(G) \rceil$. We propose an analogue conjecture for digraphs. Given a digraph $D$, we denote by $\vecχ(D)$ the dichromatic number of $D$, which is the minimum number of colours needed to partition $D$ into acyclic induced subdigraphs. We let $\overleftrightarrowω(D)$ denote the size of the largest biclique (a set of vertices inducing a complete digraph) of $D$ and $\tildeΔ(D) = \max_{v\in V(D)} \sqrt{d^+(v) \cdot d^-(v)}$. We conjecture that every digraph $D$ satisfies $\vecχ(D) \leq \lceil \frac{\tildeΔ(D)+1+\overleftrightarrowω(D)}{2} \rceil$, which if true implies Reed's conjecture. As a partial result, we prove the existence of $\varepsilon >0$ for which every digraph $D$ satisfies $\vecχ(D) \leq \lceil (1-\varepsilon)(\tildeΔ(D)+1)+\varepsilon\overleftrightarrowω(D) \rceil$. This implies both Reed's result and an independent result of Harutyunyan and Mohar for oriented graphs. To obtain this upper bound on $\vecχ$, we prove that every digraph $D$ with $\overleftrightarrowω(D) > \frac{2}{3}(Δ_{\max}(D)+1)$, where $Δ_{\max}(D) = \max_{v\in V(D)} \max(d^+(v),d^-(v))$, admits an acyclic set of vertices intersecting each biclique of $D$, which generalises a result of King. We finally give a short proof that every oriented graph $D$ with underlying graph $G$ satisfies $\vecχ(D) \leq \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \tildeΔ(D) + 2$ and $\vecχ(D) \leq \frac{1}{3}Δ(G)+2$, improving on results of Golowich and Steiner, respectively.

papers.title: Finite-difference least square methods for solving Hamilton-Jacobi equations using neural networks
papers.abstract: We present a simple algorithm to approximate the viscosity solution of Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) equations by means of an artificial deep neural network. The algorithm uses a stochastic gradient descent-based method to minimize the least square principle defined by a monotone, consistent numerical scheme. We analyze the least square principle's critical points and derive conditions that guarantee that any critical point approximates the sought viscosity solution. The use of a deep artificial neural network on a finite difference scheme lifts the restriction of conventional finite difference methods that rely on computing functions on a fixed grid. This feature makes it possible to solve HJ equations posed in higher dimensions where conventional methods are infeasible. We demonstrate the efficacy of our algorithm through numerical studies on various canonical HJ equations across different dimensions, showcasing its potential and versatility.

papers.title: On the cone conjecture for pairs of large Kodaira dimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, by running the minimal model program and considering the anti-canonical fibration, we prove the Morrison-Kawamata cone conjecture for klt Calabi-Yau pairs $(X,Δ)$ such that the Iitaka dimension $κ(X,-K_X)$ is at least $\dim X - 2$.

papers.title: Univalent approximation by Fourier series of step functions
papers.abstract: We prove that univalent harmonic mappings can be approximated by univalent Fourier series of step functions.

papers.title: F-signature functions of diagonal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a diagonal hypersurface in $A_p=\mathbb{F}_p[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]$. We study the behavior of the function $φ_{f,p}({a}/{p^e})=p^{-ne}\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}\big(A_p/(x_1^{p^e},\dots,x_n^{p^e},f^a)\big)$ which encodes information about the F-threshold, the Hilbert-Kunz, and the F-signature functions. We prove that when $p$ goes to infinity $φ_{f,p}$ converges to a piecewise polynomial function $φ_f$ and the left and right derivatives of $φ_{f,p}$ converge to $φ'_f$. We use this fact to prove the existence of the limit F-signature and limit Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity for diagonal hypersurfaces. When $f$ is a Fermat hypersurface, we investigate the shape of the F-signature function of $f$ and provide an explicit formula for the limit F-signature and, in some cases, also for the F-signature for fixed $p$. This allows us to answer negatively to a question of Watanabe and Yoshida.

papers.title: Quotients of Leavitt path algebras over commutative rings by graded ideals
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be a graph and $R$ a unital commutative ring. We study quotients of the Leavitt path algebra $L_R(E)$ by graded ideals which, unlike in the case of field coefficients, need not be basic. Using the saturated functions of Rigby and van den Hove, we introduce $I$-basic graded ideals, where $I$ is an ideal of $R$, and we prove that, for an arbitrary graph $E$, the quotient of $L_R(E)$ by an $I$-basic graded ideal is isomorphic to the Leavitt path algebra of a quotient graph of $E$ with coefficients in $R/I$. More precisely, for every graded ideal there is a canonical epimorphism from such an algebra onto the quotient, and it is an isomorphism if and only if the graded ideal is $I$-basic. This extends a result of Larki for basic graded ideals. We also introduce graded ideal functions, defined on the vertices of $E$ and on the pairs $(H,v)$ formed by a hereditary saturated set $H$ and a breaking vertex $v$ of $H$, and we show that they form a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of graded ideals of $L_R(E)$. As an application, for a finite graph $E$ in which no cycle has an exit, we describe the quotient of $L_R(E)$ by any graded ideal as a direct sum, indexed by the sinks and the cycles of $E$, of Leavitt path algebras over quotient rings of $R$, namely matrix algebras over quotient rings of $R$ and of $R[x,x^{-1}]$. Finally, examples on the infinite binary tree and Toeplitz graph show that the hypothesis on the finiteness and cycles cannot be removed.

papers.title: An almost effective proof of the class number 1 problem for imaginary quadratic fields via Frobenius--Rabinowitsch
papers.abstract: Let $D \neq 1$ be a square-free integer, and let $K = {\mathbb Q}(\sqrt D)$ be the corresponding quadratic field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ lying over an odd rational prime that splits in $K/\mathbb Q$. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition in terms of a binary quadratic form for $\mathcal{P}$ to be a principal ideal. Then, when $K$ is imaginary with $D\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ and $|D|>16$, we use this result to prove $K$ has class number 1 only if $D=1-4p$ where $p$, $4p-1$, and $4p+3$ are prime. Finally, combining this condition with results on the representation of integers by the sum of three squares, the theorem of Frobenius and Rabinowitsch, and a theorem of Tatuzawa we provide a proof, up to at most one possible additional field, of the well-known theorem on imaginary quadratic fields with class number 1. If Dirichlet $L$-functions have no zeros in the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s)>11/12$, then the possible additional field of our result does not exist.

papers.title: Odd Fredholm modules over differential graded algebras: Chern character and spectral flow
papers.abstract: Let $Ω$ be a locally convex differential graded algebra. For $q \in \mathbb{N}_0$ we construct the Chern character of $\vartheta$-summable $\mathcal{C}_q$-Fredholm modules over $Ω$, an entire cyclic cocycle which extends the JLO cocycle to the differential graded setting. For $q = 0$ it is the Chern character of even $\vartheta$-summable Fredholm modules over $Ω$ due to Güneysu and Ludewig; for $q = 1$ it yields a Chern character for odd $\vartheta$-summable Fredholm modules over $Ω$, which reduces to Getzler's odd Chern character for $Ω$ trivially graded with trivial differential. We prove that this cocycle is Chen normalized and invariant under homotopies. Moreover, we generalize the constructions by Cacciatori and Güneysu to arbitrary $Ω$ and $g \in \mathrm{GL}_m(Ω^0)$ to get an odd chain $\mathrm{Ch}(g)$ and prove the following odd index theorem: the pairing of the odd Chern character with $\mathrm{Ch}(g)$ may be written as an explicit integral formula which equals $\sqrtπ$ times the spectral flow from $Q$ to $\mathbf{c}(g)^{-1} Q \mathbf{c}(g)$ whenever $\mathbf{c}(g)$ is unitary. For odd-dimensional spin manifolds (where $\mathbf{c}$ is Clifford multiplication) this supplies the cochain side of the loop space approach to the odd-index theorem.

papers.title: Nisnevich equivalences of local essentially smooth open pairs
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove a Nisnevich local equivalence \begin{equation*} X/(X-Z)\simeq X^\prime/(X^\prime-Z^\prime) \end{equation*} for essentially smooth local schemes $X$ and $X^\prime$ of the same dimension over a base scheme $B$, and arbitrary isomorphic closed subschemes $Z$ and $Z^\prime$, with immediate applications in motivic homotopy theory.

papers.title: Freeness conditions for intermediate $C^*$-algebras of crossed products
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a separable $C^*$-algebra, let $Γ$ be a discrete countable group, let $α: Γ\to \text{Aut}(B)$ be an action, and let $A$ be an invariant subalgebra. We find certain freeness conditions which guarantee that any intermediate $C^*$-algebra $A \rtimes_{α,r} Γ\subseteq C \subseteq B \rtimes_{α,r} Γ$ is a crossed product of an intermediate invariant subalgebra $A \subseteq C_0 \subseteq B$ by $Γ$. Those are used to generalize related results by Suzuki.

papers.title: Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for $321$-avoiding Kazhdan-Lusztig varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity of 321-avoiding Kazhdan--Lusztig varieties can be computed combinatorially in terms of $K$-theoretic skew excited Young diagrams. We present an algorithm which gives a lower bound for this regularity and describe a setting in which this algorithm provides precise regularity computations. This algorithm specializes to compute the regularity of all two-sided mixed ladder determinantal varieties.

papers.title: Categorical concentration
papers.abstract: Given a torus action on a compact space $X$, a fundamental result of Borel and Atiyah-Segal asserts that the equivariant cohomology of $X$ is concentrated in the fixed locus $X^T$, up to inverting enough Chern classes. For algebraic varieties and stacks over an arbitrary field, we prove an analogous concentration statement for equivariant derived categories of sheaves. On the localized categories, restriction to the fixed locus coincides with Braden's hyperbolic localization, and as an application we obtain torus localization for the Donaldson-Thomas perverse sheaves of (-1)-shifted symplectic spaces. Concentration holds more generally for actions of affine algebraic groups, and for abstract six functor formalisms (e.g. motivic sheaves). For $μ_\ell$-actions, it recovers Treumann's sheaf-theoretic Smith theory. We also prove a categorification of the virtual localization formula for torus actions.

papers.title: Notes on modules of finite injective dimension
papers.abstract: Motivated by Bass' conjecture, we study finitely generated modules of finite injective dimension and the additional constraints they impose on the ambient ring. Beyond ensuring the Cohen--Macaulay property, the presence of such modules enforces further conditions on the ring, including reducedness, normality, being an integral domain, and various singularity conditions such as complete intersection, Gorenstein, and beyond. This continues to detect non-singularity as well. We also address the reflexivity (and also torsionlessness) of modules with finite injective dimension and show that this forces the ring to be quasi-normal. In the same vein, we investigate the injective dimension of tensor products and endomorphism rings. Finally, we study the behavior of R when high syzygies of ksurject onto a non-zero R-module of finite injective dimension.

papers.title: Stratification de Hesselink rationnelle et contribution unipotente à la formule des traces en caractéristique p>0
papers.abstract: For a field $F$ and a connected reductive group $G$ defined over $F$, we develop a theory of Kempf-Rousseau-Hesselink unipotent $F$-strata in $G(F)$ that should allow us to attack open problems in positive characteristic. As an application, we use this theory to establish an expansion (preliminary to the fine expansion) of the unipotent contribution to the trace formula over a global field of characteristic $p>0$. The unipotent $F$-strata play here the role of the unipotent geometric orbits in Arthur's work over a number field. The expansion in terms of products of local distributions is not discussed here; it will be the subject of further work.

papers.title: The homotopy types of $Sp(n)$-gauge groups over $S^{4m}$
papers.abstract: Let $m$ and $n$ be two positive integers such that $m < n$. Denote by $P_{n,k}$ the principal $Sp(n)$-bundle over $S^{4m}$ and $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$ be the gauge group of $P_{n,k}$ classified by $k\varepsilon'$, where $\varepsilon'$ is a generator of $π_{4m}(B(Sp(n)))\cong\mathbb{Z}$. In this article, we will partially classify the homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$ by giving a lower bound for the number of homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$. Also, in special cases $Sp(3)$-gauge groups over $S^8$ and $Sp(4)$-gauge groups over $S^{12}$ we give an upper bound for the number of homotopy types of these gauge groups.

papers.title: Global-in-time L p -- L q estimates for solutions of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation
papers.abstract: In this work, we prove an optimal global-in-time $L^p \to L^q$ estimate for solutions to the Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation with short range potential in dimension three. Our result shows that the decay rate as t $\rightarrow$ +$\infty$ is the same as the heat equation in x-variables and the divergence rate as t $\rightarrow$ 0 + is related to the sub-ellipticity with loss of 1/3 derivatives of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator.

papers.title: Nonabelian mirrors and Gromov-Witten invariants
papers.abstract: We propose quantum differential equations (QDEs) for periods of nonabelian mirror theories and develop an algorithm for constructing them directly from the mirrors. We verify the proposal by recovering known quantum differential equations of Grassmannians and Picard-Fuchs equations of Calabi-Yau complete intersections in Grassmannians. Our algorithm applies to a broad class of nonabelian GLSMs and yields new examples of quantum differential equations for several Fano varieties. The associated cohomology-valued generating functions can be extracted directly from these equations. Using them, we compute instanton numbers of both complete-intersection and non-complete-intersection Calabi-Yau manifolds, including the Pfaffian and Gulliksen--Negård Calabi-Yau threefolds. The resulting instanton numbers agree with all previously known computations, while the generating functions obtained for the non-complete-intersection examples are new.

papers.title: Lofty Models of Peano Arithmetic
papers.abstract: If M is a nonstandard model of Peano Arithmetic, then M is lofty iff M has a simple elementary extension that is recursively saturated. This had previously been known for countable M.

papers.title: An Open Petri Net Implementation of Gene Regulatory Networks
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are a central object of systems biology, and many formalisms have been used to model them, among them Petri nets. Ordinary Petri nets, however, provide no built-in way to assemble a large network from smaller, separately specified pieces. Open Petri nets, in the sense of Baez and Master, supply exactly this: an open Petri net is a Petri net with designated boundary places, and open Petri nets are composed by gluing boundaries together (a pushout), giving a symmetric monoidal double category Open(Petri). In this paper we (i) state precisely the standard encoding of activation, inhibition and degradation as Petri net transitions; (ii) distinguish the classical "Petri nets are monoids" view of Meseguer and Montanari, which describes how processes inside one net compose, from the open Petri net view, which describes how nets compose; (iii) show, with a worked example, how a GRN can be cut into open Petri net modules along shared genes and recovered exactly by composition, together with simple rules that make such a decomposition correct; and (iv) use the compositional rate-equation semantics of Baez and Pollard to show that the mass-action dynamics of the composite network are obtained by gluing the dynamics of its modules, linking Petri net models of GRNs to their ordinary differential equation counterparts. We close by discussing what the reachability semantics does and does not give for GRN modules, and the limitations of the approach.

papers.title: On Herman's Positive Entropy Conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that any area-preserving $C^r$-diffeomorphism of a two-dimensional surface displaying an elliptic fixed point can be $C^r$-perturbed to one exhibiting a chaotic island whose metric entropy is positive, for every $1\le r\le \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Herman stating that the identity map of the disk can be $C^\infty$-perturbed to a conservative diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy. This implies also that the Chirikov standard map for large and small parameter values can be $C^\infty$-approximated by a conservative diffeomorphisms displaying a positive metric entropy (a weak version of Sinai's positive metric entropy conjecture). Finally, this sheds light onto a Herman's question on the density of $C^r$-conservative diffeomorphisms displaying a positive metric entropy: we show the existence of a dense set formed by conservative diffeomorphism which either are weakly stable (so, conjecturally, uniformly hyperbolic) or display a chaotic island of positive metric entropy.

papers.title: Unitarizability of weight modules over noncommutative Kleinian fiber products
papers.abstract: Noncommutative Kleinian fiber products $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ are $\ast$-algebras attached to $(m,n)$-periodic higher spin six-vertex configurations $\mathscr{L}$. Examples include quotients of the enveloping algebra of the affine Lie algebra $A_1^{(1)}$ and of a finite W-algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_4$. We determine which simple integral weight $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$-modules carry an invariant inner product and which of them are unitarizable, and we compute the signature of the form. All three answers are read off from the vertex configuration: the signature of a module is a count of faces in a two-coloring of an eight-vertex configuration canonically attached to $\mathscr{L}$. The main tool is a one-parameter family $Δ_ξ$ of representations of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ by difference operators on sections of a line bundle over the face lattice. These representations carry an explicit indefinite invariant inner product, and together they contain every simple integral weight module. Along the way we show that the Casimir element of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ is unitary.

papers.title: Residue Automata Modulo $3^k$, Syracuse Random Variables, and Terminal-Branch Bias in Collatz Trajectories
papers.abstract: We study the residues modulo $3^k$ visited by trajectories of the accelerated Collatz map $T(n)=n/2$ ($n$ even), $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ ($n$ odd), starting from the six ``recurrent forms'' $9n+r$, $r\in\{1,2,4,5,7,8\}$. (i)~We give the exact transition automaton on these forms and its extension to every modulus $3^k$, and prove that for integers drawn from a complete residue system modulo $2^j3^k$ the first $j$ residues modulo $3^k$ form \emph{exactly} a Markov chain; its stationary law is Tao's Syracuse random variable, so the form $9n+8$ receives the fraction $22/63$ of all visits. (ii)~We determine the spectrum of this chain completely: its characteristic polynomial is $(x-1)\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}\bigl(x^{2\cdot 3^i}-4^{-3^i}\bigr)$, so every non-trivial eigenvalue has modulus exactly $\tfrac12$ for every $k$. We prove that the mixing time lies between $k\log_2\frac32$ and $2k+O(\sqrt{k})$, show that the stationary mass of the class $-1 \bmod 3^k$ is at least $\tfrac43 2^{-k}$, and present numerical evidence for a cutoff at $k\log_2 3$. (iii)~We explain the strong bias observed in the residue class of the first power of~$2$ met by a trajectory: this class is determined by the last odd term $q_k=(4^k-1)/3$ through $k \bmod 3$; three of the six classes contain only powers of~$2$, a fourth has $O(\log^2N)$ elements up to $N$, and the remaining two are unions of predecessor sets of the $q_k$. Computations for $n\le 4\times10^{9}$ give the frequencies $0.9761$ and $0.0239$. (iv)~We formulate an \emph{octave law}---the expected number of orbit points in $[y,2y)$ lying in a class $r \bmod 3^k$ tends to $\frac{2\log 2}{\log(4/3)}$ times the Syracuse probability of $r$---and support it by exhaustive and Monte Carlo computation.

papers.title: Fishburn Numbers Count Homogeneous Games
papers.abstract: We prove a new combinatorial interpretation for Fishburn numbers, in that they count the number of homogeneous games; specifically homogeneous games without dummy players, which we show extends to homogeneous games via the partial sums of Fishburn numbers. In doing so, we settle two conjectures commented in the OEIS A189359 entry, and finish off by providing some immediate consequences on homogeneous game counts; including an asymptotic formula and congruences.

papers.title: Every friend of 10 has at least eleven distinct prime factors
papers.abstract: A friend of $10$ is a positive integer $N\neq 10$ such that $σ(N)/N=σ(10)/10=9/5$. Whether one exists is an open problem. Thackeray proved that a friend of $10$ has at least $10$ distinct prime factors. We describe a computer-assisted proof that it has at least $11$. The proof is an exhaustive search over sets of primes, carried out by a recursive certifier written in PARI/GP, which extends the open-source project caioross/solitary10. The new ingredients are a split of ``almost tight'' nodes that avoids enumerating the smallest unknown prime, a treatment of nodes with three or more unknown primes by a saturation dichotomy, a counting rule for unfactored cofactors of cyclotomic values, and the correction of a soundness gap in the earlier closure rule. The certification run for $ω=10$ visited $157{,}210{,}962$ nodes in $11.4$ hours on $12$ threads. As a consequence, a friend of $10$ would be larger than $10^{38}$.

papers.title: Local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of the least possible dimensions
papers.abstract: In \cite{Ma} we have observed the example of local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over a 12 dimensional ramified regular local ring. In this paper we construct examples of local cohomology modules with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of two different ring dimensions. The result of this paper is very much dependent on the result (\cite{SS}, Theorem 2.6).

papers.title: Local connectivity of Julia sets of Newton maps of trigonometric and hyperbolic functions
papers.abstract: We study the Newton maps of $\sin z$, $\cos z$, $\sinh z$, and $\cosh z$, each of which is transcendental meromorphic and has infinitely many unbounded immediate attracting basins. We first verify directly that, for the cosine Newton map $N_{\cos}(z) = z + \cot z$, the half-planes $\{\pm \operatorname{Im} z > M\}$ are repelling petals at infinity for every $M \ge 2$. These explicit petals allow us to apply the tame-basin criterion of Barański, Fagella, Jarque, and Karpińska and obtain local connectivity of the spherical boundary of each immediate basin of $N_{\cos}$. We also show that the Newton map of $Ae^{λz} + Be^{-λz}$, where $ABλ\neq 0$, is affinely conjugate to the sine Newton map $N_{\sin}(z) = z - \tan z$. The published local-connectivity theorem for $J(N_{\sin})$ therefore applies to this entire family, including the cosine and the two hyperbolic Newton maps. We describe the invariant lines and basin geometry of the four maps and illustrate the corresponding dynamical planes numerically.

papers.title: Proof Checking Continuous Reachability
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a proof format and proof checker for certifying reachability computations of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with polynomial vector fields. Establishing a proof checking framework for certifying ODE reachability is similar to the checking of UNSAT proofs for propositional satisfiability solving, but it is even more important due to the challenges inherent in dealing with ODEs, and even more challenging due to the numerical nature of ODE reachability algorithms. The proofs are expressed in differential dynamic logic (dL), and can be independently verified with symbolic theorem provers for dL (e.g. KeYmaeraX). Such proofs are naturally generated by reachability algorithms based on Taylor models, a popular technique to obtain rigorous bounds on approximations of ODEs. This paper proves the completeness of such proofs - if an approximation was correctly computed by some (possibly untrusted) reachability algorithm via Taylor models, then a corresponding proof in dL can be automatically generated and checked to be correct in dL's proof calculus. A dedicated proof checker is implemented in Lean4 for improved performance, which is capable of formally verifying benchmarks in the ARCH competition.

papers.title: Kernel Regression using Persistence Diagrams
papers.abstract: Persistence diagrams are widely used in topological data analysis to summarize topological and geometric structure in data. We study nonparametric regression where inputs are persistence diagrams and outputs are real-valued. Using kernel-based local averaging estimators defined directly over diagram space with Wasserstein distance, we establish consistency and derive bounds on the rate of convergence under suitable assumptions in the $L^2$-theory. We also present computational experiments that demonstrate strong performance of the proposed estimator, particularly in low data regimes.

papers.title: Large Gaps Between Piatetski-Shapiro Primes
papers.abstract: A Piatetski-Shapiro prime is a prime number that can be written as $\lfloor m^c \rfloor$ for some positive integer $m$ and non-integer $c>1$. Li and Pan showed the results for small gaps between consecutive Piatetski-Shapiro primes for $1<c<9/8$. On the other hand, Deshouillers, Drmota, and Müllner showed the large gaps between Piatetski-Shapiro primes although they did not mention it explicitly whenever there are infinitely many Piatetski-Shapiro primes with exponent $c$ using binomial expansion. In this article, we use a different method from theirs, and we obtain the explicit exponent that appears in their paper.

papers.title: Pointwise Minmax Representations for Total Variation Denoising on Graphs
papers.abstract: Total variation denoising (TVD) is a fundamental method in image denoising, signal processing, and nonparametric regression. We establish exact pointwise minmax/maxmin representations for TVD on arbitrary finite graphs, extending recent one-dimensional results. Under squared loss, fitted values are expressed through corrected local averages over nested connected vertex sets. The correction is a signed boundary count: edges leaving the inner set contribute +1 if they remain within the outer set and -1 otherwise. To the best of our knowledge, this representation is new even for two-dimensional TVD. We show that Brunk's classical minmax formulas for isotonic regression on every finite directed acyclic graph arise as special cases of our graph TVD representation. The exact reduction proceeds through asymmetric TVD and nearly isotonic regression, which coincides with isotonic regression above a finite penalty threshold. We further extend the representations to arbitrary finite separable convex losses, assuming coercivity of the full objective, but without requiring differentiability or strict convexity. For nonunique solutions, the possible fitted values at each coordinate form a compact interval. Its lower and upper endpoints admit maxmin and minmax representations, respectively, through scalar local optimization problems and are attained simultaneously at all coordinates by two extremal solutions. This yields exact representations for quantile TVD on arbitrary graphs and unifies TVD, nearly isotonic regression, and isotonic regression within a single pointwise framework for general separable convex losses.

papers.title: Exceptional zeros for $\mathrm{GSp}(4) \times \mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Yoshida lifts
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to study an exceptional zero phenomenon for the $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $\mathrm{GSp}_4\times\mathrm{GL}_2$ in the critical regions (F) and (D). We construct improved $p$-adic $L$-functions by replacing the $p$-depleted Eisenstein family with its $p$-ordinary counterpart. Under a local compatibility hypothesis at the ramified places and classical control for the families, we show that their poles detect exactly the Yoshida lifts whose smaller constituent is dual to the $\mathrm{GL}_2$ representation. The proof compares their residues with distinguished automorphic periods, extending the coherent period formula to the case where one modular form has weight zero. An explicit Euler-factor identity relates each improved function to the usual $p$-adic $L$-function. At these Yoshida points, the vanishing factor cancels the pole, and the resulting value is expressed through the distinguished period and the logarithmic derivative of the ordinary elliptic root. We also discuss the expected factorization along Yoshida families into Hida--Rankin $p$-adic $L$-functions.

papers.title: Preservation of big diagonal for automorphisms of Hilbert schemes
papers.abstract: If $X$ is a smooth projective surface that is not K3 or abelian surface, we show that any automorphism of the Hilbert scheme of points $X^{[n]}$ preserves the big diagonal. This generalizes several previous works, and gives a complete description of automorphisms of $X^{[n]}$ when $X$ is not K3 or abelian surface. We also obtain a Torelli-type theorem: a smooth projective surface $X$ can be recovered from $X^{[n]}$ unless $X$ is a K3 surface. Further, for each integer $n\geq 2$, we construct automorphisms of $A^{[n]}$ not preserving the big diagonal for an abelian surface $A$.

papers.title: Moduli of continuity preserved by the Hilbert Transform
papers.abstract: It has long been known that the Hilbert transform preserves certain moduli of continuity such as Hölder continuity. In~\cite{GS01}, M. Goldstein and W. Schlag provided a criterion, based on two simple conditions, for a modulus of continuity to be preserved under the Hilbert transform. These conditions are not satisfied by the weak-Hölder and the log-Hölder moduli of continuity. More recently, A. Avila, Y. Last, M. Shamis and Q. Zhou proved in~\cite{ALSZ21} that for compactly supported $t$-log-Hölder continuous functions ($t>1$) their Hilbert transforms are at least $(t-1)$-log-Hölder continuous. A similar result holds for weak-Hölder continuous functions. In this note we extend these results to a class of continuous functions satisfying a couple of mild integrability conditions.

papers.title: DS3M: Deep structured state space models for nonlinear system identification on modern hardware
papers.abstract: Neural state-space identification learns dynamical models from measured inputs and outputs. SUBNET combines this task with an encoder that estimates initial states from short measurement histories.
