Its continuous-time version requires many successive neural-network evaluations during numerical integration, resulting in slow training speed which is a major limitation for practical use cases. We propose deep structured state space models (DS3M), which combine compact nonlinear dynamical components in parallel and in series. Custom GPU kernels implemented with Triton reduce the launch and memory overhead of their sequential evaluation. We explain this construction, describe a port-Hamiltonian variant, and present various benchmark comparisons of accuracy and training time.

papers.title: On the non-extendibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs $\{n,2n\}$ with $n = 2k^2 \pm k$
papers.abstract: We study a class of Diophantine problems arising from triangular analogues of classical Diophantine tuples. A set of positive integers is called a triangular $D(n)$-tuple if the product of any two distinct elements, increased by $n$, is a triangular number. In this paper, we investigate the extensibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs of the form $\{n,2n\}$, where $n = 2k^2 + \varepsilon k$, with $k$ an odd positive integer and $\varepsilon \in \{-1,1\}$ such that $4k + \varepsilon$ is prime. We prove that for all $(k,\varepsilon)$ in a finite explicitly determined set, the pair $\{n,2n\}$ cannot be extended to a triangular $D(n)$-quadruple. The obtained results give further evidence for a general non-extensibility phenomenon, which we formulate as a conjecture.

papers.title: Integer Programming Strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box Problem
papers.abstract: We present a selection of Integer Programming (IP) strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box problem, which asks for the longest induced path in the $d$-dimensional hypercube. Current records are based on sophisticated, exhaustive searches, with optimality proven only for instances up to dimension 8, motivating our study of IP formulations. We address symmetries and potential strengthenings. With the smallest open instance having as few as 512 binary decision variables, the proposed IPs offer a challenging and intriguing combinatorial problem. In addition, we extend the problem to higher-dimensional grid graphs and provide solutions for unexplored and unsolved instances.

papers.title: Algebraic independence of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms via period interpretations
papers.abstract: Based on Hartl's de Rham-crystalline comparison isomorphism, we formulate a notion of André's $v$-adic periods for a class of Anderson $\mathbb{F}_q[z]$-motives with respect to a degree-one finite place $v$ of a rational function field over a finite field, following Ancona-Frăţilă's formulation of $p$-adic periods. The formulation naturally produces deformation series of the resulting periods and Frobenius difference equations satisfied by these series. We then explain how the formulation brings the resulting $v$-adic periods within the scope of Chen's $v$-adic ABP criterion and of difference Galois theory, and gives us a strategy to study the transcendence degrees of $v$-adic periods through their deformation series. We show that certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms can be expressed in terms of André's $v$-adic periods. Applying the strategy to these examples, we obtain algebraic independence results for certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms; more precisely, the transcendence degree of the field generated by a suitable collection of special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms is one less than the transcendence degree of the field generated by the corresponding special values of $\infty$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms together with the Carlitz period.

papers.title: Nilpotent skew-symmetric tridiagonal Bohemian matrices: a proof of Corless's conjecture
papers.abstract: Corless studied the skew-symmetric tridiagonal matrices $T_m(u)$ with superdiagonal $u \in \{1, i\}^{m-1}$. He showed that $T_m(u)$ can be nilpotent only if $m = 2^K - 1$ and that the $2^{K-1}$ vectors $u$ obtained from the empty vector by repeated application of $u \mapsto (u, 1, i, \rev u)$ and $u \mapsto (u, i, 1, \rev u)$ give nilpotent matrices, and he conjectured that there are no others. We prove this conjecture. Reducing the characteristic polynomial modulo $4$ gives a necessary condition for nilpotency that is linear over $\F$. For $m > 1$ it forces $u = (v, 1, i, \rev v)$ or $u = (v, i, 1, \rev v)$, and an identity implicit in Corless's proof then reduces the problem to $v$. Since $T_m(u)$ is diagonally similar to a finite section of the Feinberg--Zee hopping matrix, the theorem also determines the nilpotent tridiagonal sign matrices. We further show that the $(1,1)$ entry of the resolvent of a nilpotent $T_m(u)$ is $λ^{-1} \pm λ^{-3} \pm λ^{-7} \pm \dots \pm λ^{-(2^K - 1)}$, with signs that determine $u$. The proof of the main theorem has been formalised in Lean~4.

papers.title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function II
papers.abstract: We apply the elementary arithmetic argument of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689) to binomial coefficients, and obtain upper and lower bounds for Sylvester's denumerant function for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ that sharpen those of Agnarsson. The lower bound is a sum of binomial coefficients; it holds along the multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ without assuming that a solution exists, and it is greater than the polynomial lower bound of the first paper. In the upper bound the shift of Agnarsson's binomial coefficient is reduced.

papers.title: A fast iterative solver for lopsided Sylvester matrix equations
papers.abstract: A generalization of the factored alternating direction implicit algorithm is introduced that makes use of type $(p, q)$ Zolotarev rational functions to apply unequal numbers of left and right shifts. Convergence properties of the algorithm are discussed, as well as a method for computing shift parameters. Several applications are highlighted where the generalized method is useful, including in the solving of a collection of shifted linear systems, for discretizations that involve left and right operators that are not equally amenable to inversion, and for Sylvester matrix equations with differently-sized, differently-structured, or differently-conditioned coefficient matrices.

papers.title: A note on Turán densities of daisies and hypergraph products
papers.abstract: The Turán density of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ is defined as $π(\mathcal{H})=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})/\binom{n}{r}$, where $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal H)$ denotes the largest number of edges in an $\mathcal H$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $r\geq s\geq2$ and $t\geq s$, an $(r,s,t)$-daisy $\mathcal D_r(s,t)$ is the $r$-uniform hypergraph consisting of all unions of a fixed $(r-s)$-set with the $s$-subsets of a disjoint $t$-set. We show that for every fixed $s\geq3$, \[ \lim_{r\rightarrow\infty}π(\mathcal D_r(s,t))=1-O_s(t^{-(s-1)}) \] as $t\rightarrow\infty$. This bound is best possible up to the implicit constant by a classical result of de Caen, and it answers, in a stronger form, a question of Ellis, Ivan and Leader, who asked for the case $s=3$. Moreover, we show a related result for matroid basis hypergraphs. We also consider Turán densities of hypergraph products, of which daisies are a special case. The product of two hypergraphs on disjoint vertex sets consists of all unions of an edge of the first with an edge of the second. For the product $\mathcal H^d$ of $d$ disjoint copies of a fixed $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ that is not $r$-partite, we show that $1-π(\mathcal H^d) \rightarrow 0$ exponentially fast as $d\rightarrow\infty$, and we determine the exponential rate in terms of the minimum number of edges in a homomorphic image of $\mathcal H$. This answers a question of Bollobás, Leader and Malvenuto up to a polynomial factor in $d$, and we further address a related question of theirs for products of two different hypergraphs.

papers.title: Interior and global $W^{2,1}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that for $3\leq k\leq n-1$, continuous $k$-convex solutions of the $k$-Hessian equation with density bounded above and below by positive constants belong to $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$. This regularity holds globally on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex domains when both the boundary and the boundary values are of class $C^{1,1}$.

papers.title: The upper copula capacity
papers.abstract: Many problems in statistics, combinatorics, econometrics, and other fields are expressible in terms of the upper probability of all copulas. We formally study this capacity, which we call the upper copula capacity, as a mathematical object. In particular, we examine the capacity of given sets and integration with respect to this capacity. For two-dimensional convex sets, the upper copula capacity equals the smaller of the two coordinate projection lengths. We also give an exact formula for the capacity of lower-tail events for positively weighted sums in any dimension and characterize when the upper Choquet integral equals the supremum of expectations over all copulas. Various problems in different fields can be formulated via the upper-copula capacity, and we discuss how known and new results connect to offer new perspectives on these problems.

papers.title: The 1d Stochastic Dirac Operator
papers.abstract: We introduce a random Dirac operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R}^2)$ that we call $1d$ Stochastic Dirac Operator and which is indexed by two parameters $κ_0,κ$. In two companion articles, we show that this operator arises generically as the small disorder limit of one-dimensional random Schrödinger operators, thus revealing a universal behavior. In the present paper, we provide a detailed construction of this singular operator, and investigate its spectral properties. In particular, we show that its spectrum is either absolutely continuous when $κ= 0$, or pure point when $κ>0$. In the latter case, we show that the shape of the eigenfunctions is given by the exponential of a two sided Brownian motion with drift, in connection with a result of Rifkind and Virág. Finally, we establish a delicate convergence result of the sequence of eigenvalues / eigenfunctions from the finite-volume operator to the infinite-volume one.

papers.title: Steinness and Complete Expanding Kähler-Ricci Solitons
papers.abstract: We prove that complete expanding Kähler-Ricci solitons with complete soliton fields characterize Steinness of relatively compact domains in Stein manifolds, and hence pseudoconvexity of bounded domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We construct canonical, instantaneously complete Kähler-Ricci flows from positive closed $(1,1)$-currents with global plurisubharmonic potentials and vanishing Lelong numbers. Nonzero currents homogeneous under a complete real holomorphic flow yield nontrivial expanders with prescribed soliton fields. We obtain a product criterion and uniformization results for balls and finite-type domains in complex surfaces. If $D$ is a relatively compact Stein domain in a reduced pure-dimensional Stein space of dimension at least two and $\operatorname{Sing} D$ is finite and nonempty, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Reg} D)$ is compact, excluding nontrivial expanders with complete soliton fields.

papers.title: The Bolker condition and overdetermined FBI transforms
papers.abstract: We study real analytic canonical relations satisfying the Bolker condition and show that, in the FBI representation, they can be described by phases of overdetermined FBI transforms. As an application, we give a simplified proof of an analytic regularity result for generalized Radon transforms due to Mazzucchelli-Salo-Tzou.

papers.title: The geometry and classification of positive frames
papers.abstract: We investigate the geometric and operator-theoretic structure of positive frames and their duals in finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, with particular emphasis on positive linear dependence, redundancy, and convex geometry. Building on the classical theory of positive spanning sets, we characterize equivalence classes of positive frames through the kernels of their synthesis operators and obtain parametrizations in terms of the relative interior of a standard simplex and suitable subsets of Grassmannians. We establish that every redundant frame admits a positive dual, regardless of whether the original frame is positive, and provide an explicit construction through a rank-one perturbation of the canonical dual. Furthermore, we investigate the affine and topological structure of positive dual frames, proving their relative openness in the space of all duals and the absence of extreme points. We characterize dual frames satisfying prescribed positive relations and derive criteria for the existence of positive-basis duals. We also examine semi-positive frames and their boundary behavior, together with connections between positive spanning, balancedness, and finite group representations. Finally, we study the convex geometry of nonnegative relation spaces and establish a directional characterization of positive-spanning robustness under arbitrary vector erasures. These results provide a unified geometric framework for understanding positive frames, their dual systems, and the role of redundancy in constrained reconstruction.

papers.title: On generalizations of the Cohen structure theorem
papers.abstract: The Cohen structure theorem is an important tool in commutative algebra and algebraic geometry. Recent work of Caviglia, Goswami, and Mesiti addresses the related question of which unital rings admit a maximal ideal for which the natural projection admits a section; for such rings, they prove a structure theorem in terms of semidirect products of rings. In this paper, we extract the underlying mechanism of their structure theorem to address when unital rings admit a nonzero proper ideal whose associated projection map has this property. We also address other settings involving ideals with conditions which are determined by ring theoretic properties of the corresponding quotient.

papers.title: Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the homology of symplectic groups with Steinberg module coefficients forms a comodule algebra over the homology of general linear groups with Steinberg module coefficients. We prove a freeness-type result for comodule algebras. We deduce new lower bounds for the high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups of number rings and their congruence subgroups.

papers.title: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in genera four and five, and of mixed Tate subquotients of $H_c^{2g}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ associated with shuffle algebras and multiple zeta values in every genus.

papers.title: The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121
papers.abstract: We prove that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(121)$ of the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of level 121, of genus 511, has exactly seven rational points, all of them CM. This is the level 121 case of a conjecture of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and with their theorem it determines the 11-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The Jacobian has rank equal to the genus. At $p = 17$ and $43$ one Hecke block of the Mordell-Weil group has logarithm divisible by $p^2$ but $p$-adic height of valuation one, and a comparison of valuations in the quadratic Chabauty identity then shows that each CM point is the only rational point in its residue disc, with no computation of the local height at $p$, no basis of the Mordell-Weil group and no equations for the curve. The inputs come from expansions of differentials at CM points and from a formula we prove for intersection numbers of CM divisors of coprime fundamental discriminants under Hecke operators on $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(\ell^e)$ (Theorem 1.3).

papers.title: Iterative constructions of semifields 2-dimensional over a nucleus
papers.abstract: The construction of finite semifields dates back to Dickson's work in 1906. To the best of our knowledge, only two iterative constructions were previously known: those of Hiramine, Matsumoto and Oyama in 1987, and of Kantor and Williams in 2004. The latter yields, for suitable even orders, superpolynomially many pairwise non-isotopic semifields. In this paper, we use skew-polynomial rings to give a new iterative construction of finite semifields. This construction produces large families of pairwise non-isotopic semifields, each of which is $2$-dimensional over one of its nuclei. In particular, we show that this construction method yields semifields not contained in any family of semifields known so far.

papers.title: On a critical nonlinear Schrödinger system with $K$-wise interaction: the cooperative case
papers.abstract: We study least energy fully non-trivial solutions of a nonlinear Schrödinger system with $K\ge3$ components and $K$-wise interaction, in the Sobolev critical regime. We consider bounded domains with Brezis--Nirenberg-type assumptions, and the associated homogeneous problem in $\mathbb R^N$. For every positive coupling, we prove the existence of a nonnegative ground state and identify a strictly positive threshold separating semi-trivial ground states from fully non-trivial ones. When the linear coefficients coincide, a finite-dimensional reduction gives an exact formula for the ground state energy and a characterization of all nonnegative ground states. In particular, above the threshold all ground states are synchronized; for sufficiently strong cooperation, their amplitude vector is unique and has an explicit asymptotic behavior. We also establish existence results for positive synchronized solutions beyond the ground state regime. For sufficiently weak cooperation, we obtain least energy positive solutions in the critical ternary case $N=K=3$, by minimizing on the component-wise Nehari set and ruling out critical concentration. The analysis includes the endpoint interaction exponent $q=1$, where the energy functional is not differentiable.

papers.title: An Explicit Three-Dimensional Dispersing Billiard with Finite Horizon
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit three-dimensional periodic Lorentz gas whose quotient by the period lattice \(2\Z^3\) has 38 spherical scatterers with rational centers and four rational radii. The scatterers are strictly separated, so the associated dispersing billiard has no corners or cusps. We prove finite horizon by establishing a common blocking margin for every rational direction. A projected-lattice estimate for the face-centered cubic core leaves nine exceptional directions, handled by a finite line-space covering certificate. Simultaneous rational approximation transfers this margin to every direction and yields an explicit upper horizon bound. All finite calculations use exact arithmetic, with verification data and algorithms included. The positive separation and blocking margins also ensure stability under sufficiently small independent perturbations of the centers and radii.

papers.title: Formally Verified Semidefinite Programming
papers.abstract: We present a formally verified Rust implementation of a first-order semidefinite programming solver, a nontrivial piece of numerical software. We wrote the solver by hand and then directed Claude to generate the entire verification in Verus, an automated theorem prover for Rust programs. We discuss the algorithm underlying the solver, its implementation in Rust, and our pragmatic approach to proving it correct in Verus.

papers.title: Convexity is overrated: Shortest paths on 4-polytopes are hard to compute
papers.abstract: We prove that computing geodesic distance on the boundary of a rational convex $4$-polytope is NP-hard. We then construct rational $4$-polytopes with two rational points joined by exponentially many shortest paths of equal rational length, disproving several conjectures along the way. For the same problem, we also prove SQRTSUM-hardness under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. By a separate argument, we show that the square of the geodesic distance between distinct rational boundary points of a rational convex polytope is a totally positive multiquadratic number.

papers.title: The low-degree sample complexity of clustering Gaussian mixtures with more groups than dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the computational limits of clustering $n$ observations drawn from a mixture of $K$ isotropic Gaussian distributions in $\mathbb R^d$, when the number $K$ of groups is much larger than the dimension $d$. In this regime, distance-based and spectral procedures require a squared separation $Δ^2$ of order $\sqrt d$. In contrast, tensor-based procedures cluster at a polylogarithmic separation but need a sample size that is a large polynomial of $dK$, and the low-degree lower bounds known for random centers only show that $n$ must exceed $dK^2$. Focusing on normally distributed centers, we characterize the minimal separation for clustering with low-degree polynomials in the regime $K>d$, through a low-degree lower bound and a matching upper bound, up to subpolynomial factors. In particular, for $K=d^{p/2}$ with $p> 2$ a real number, we show that a sample size of the order of $K^3 d^{(\lceil p\rceil-p)/2}$ is required to recover the clustering with subpolynomial separation, and that it suffices when $p$ is not an integer.

papers.title: On the ring of bounded functions on the character variety
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ denote the character variety associated to the group $(o_L, +)$, where $o_L$ is the ring of integers in a finite extension $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$. $\mathfrak{X}$ is a rigid analytic variety parametrizing locally $L$-analytic characters. Let $Λ_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)$ denote the global sections bounded by $1$. In this paper we prove that $Λ_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)= o_L[[o_L]]$, answering the question posed in [AB24].

papers.title: Small-Gain Analysis of Robust Event-Triggered Extremum Seeking for Scalar Maps
papers.abstract: We study a sample-and-hold implementation of gradient extremum seeking for a scalar quadratic map in which the control signal is refreshed only when an event occurs. The event generator acts on the demodulated gradient signal as it is actually measured, rather than on its averaged version, and contains a strictly positive offset, following the small-gain philosophy for robust event-triggered control. Rather than invoking averaging theorems, we work directly with the exact dynamics of the parameter estimation error. In the scalar setting, the demodulated gradient has an explicit sinusoidal structure, which is exploited through a change of variables that absorbs the zero-mean oscillatory perturbation, together with a quadratic Lyapunov function and the persistence of excitation of the probing signal. For a sufficiently fast dither, the estimation error is shown to decay exponentially to a residual neighborhood of the origin whose size is quantified by the dither amplitude and frequency, and by the relative threshold and the offset of the event generator. All constants, including the input-to-state stability gain of the extremum seeking loop, the admissible dither frequency and the positive lower bound on the time between two consecutive events, are given in closed form, so that Zeno behavior is excluded. A simulation example illustrates the results.

papers.title: Self-adjoint skew quartics, symplectic monodromy, and zeta functions
papers.abstract: For an odd prime power $P$, let $A_H(P)$ be the number of $a\in\F_{P^H}$ for which the self-adjoint skew quartic $t^4+t^3+at^2+t+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{P^H}[t;σ]$, with $σ(c)=c^P$. We determine $A_H(3)$ for every $H\ge1$ and prove that its minimal constant-coefficient recurrence has order $24$. Local ramification gives the degrees of the Steinberg and regular cuspidal Frobenius polynomials. Duality and finitely many exact counts determine both polynomials. For $P=p^f$ with $p\nmid f$, we construct an explicit genus-$P(P+1)/2$ flag curve whose zeta numerator is the Steinberg Frobenius polynomial. At $P=3$ this identifies the degree-$12$ factor computed above with the zeta numerator of a genus-$6$ curve. For general $P$ the flag curve and the regular cuspidal factors give a rational expression for the counting series. We evaluate the linear coefficients of the two factors by an elliptic-curve point count and express their quadratic coefficients through a single finite-field character sum.

papers.title: Optimal Robust Community Detection
papers.abstract: We study community detection in the sparse two-community stochastic block model when an adversary may corrupt a small constant fraction of the edges of the observed graph. For every choice of parameters above the Kesten-Stigum threshold and every $\varepsilon > 0$, we give a nearly-linear-time algorithm which estimates the communities with accuracy within $\varepsilon$ of the information-theoretically optimal accuracy, while tolerating a small constant fraction of adversarially corrupted edges. Previously, efficient algorithms with optimal accuracy were known only in the absence of corruptions, while robust algorithms either achieved only weak recovery or approached optimal accuracy only in the limit of large signal-to-noise ratio. Our algorithm is simple: approximate the second eigenvector of the nonbacktracking matrix, using a semidefinite program to cope with the corruptions, and use it to initialize belief propagation. Along the way, we show that in the absence of corruptions, belief propagation initialized at this eigenvector achieves optimal accuracy, resolving an open problem of Zdeborová in the two-community case. The proof of this fact is short and independent of our robustness results--its key ingredient is a local characterization of the second eigenvector of the nonbacktracking matrix in terms of constant-depth nonbacktracking walks.

papers.title: Robust BUG dynamical low-rank integrators based on the Euler-Maruyama method for stochastic differential equations. Part I: a closed-moment approach
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce Euler-Maruyama-based Basis-Update & Galerkin (EM-BUG) dynamical low-rank integrators for stochastic differential equations (SDEs). These integrators extend the standard BUG integrator to the Euler-Maruyama scheme by incorporating diffusion directions into the augmented physical basis and exploiting the second moment to update the physical basis independently of the new Brownian increments. This construction avoids the inversion of the reduced second-moment matrix and allows us to derive convergence estimates that are robust with respect to small eigenvalues. We establish preservation of positive semidefiniteness, exactness with respect to Euler-Maruyama at full rank, and second-moment stability. Strong and weak convergence estimates show that the time-discretization accuracy of the underlying Euler-Maruyama scheme is preserved up to the low-rank approximation error. We also derive Monte Carlo error estimates recovering the standard sampling rate up to the time-discretization and low-rank approximation errors. Numerical experiments on linear SDEs with additive and multiplicative noise support these theoretical results and demonstrate accuracy comparable to the standard BUG integrator.

papers.title: An α-potential linear approximation for LQ differential games
papers.abstract: Feedback Nash equilibria of infinite-horizon linear-quadratic (LQ) differential games are characterized by coupled algebraic Riccati equations (cAREs), whose numerical solution generally relies on iterative algorithms and can be highly sensitive to their initialization. Motivated by the $α$-potential-game framework, this letter proposes an $α$-potential linear approximation for constructing a systematic, game-dependent initialization. For an N-player LQ game, a reference potential game is constructed. Its equilibrium requires solving only one standard algebraic Riccati equation. The original cAREs are subsequently linearized around this reference solution, yielding a coupled linear system whose solution provides player-specific corrections and hence an approximate feedback Nash equilibrium. The resulting approximation is used to initialize three standard cARE solvers. Numerical experiments on $10^4$ randomly generated two-player games show that the proposed initialization reduces the mean number of iterations. Further experiments for $N=2,\ldots,13$ show that the reduction in iteration count persists as the number of players increases.

papers.title: A refinement of Szemerédi's distinct-distance bound for points in general position
papers.abstract: We prove that every collinear triple free set of $n\ge4$ points in the Euclidean plane determines at least $\lfloor n/3\rfloor+1$ distinct distances. This refines the classical bound $\lceil(n-1)/3\rceil$ of Szemerédi that is based on counting isosceles triangles. The refinement is based on treating the diameters separately: they only appear on the convex hull, so for them, we can use the planar diameter theorem and Altman's theorem on distances in convex polygons.

papers.title: Accelerating Diffusion Maps on a Quantum Computer: Spectral Filtering and Galerkin PDE Solvers
papers.abstract: Diffusion maps generalize principal component analysis (PCA) to nonlinear manifolds, enabling spectral dimensionality reduction, geometric data analysis, and elliptic PDE approximation on point clouds. For large datasets of size $N$, however, classical matrix operations incur prohibitive $\operatorname{poly}(N)$ scaling, even when extracting low-dimensional spectral features or targeted scalar observables. We introduce a quantum algorithmic framework that bypasses explicit graph-Laplacian assembly by exploiting the symmetric factorization $G = A^T A$ directly at the block-encoding level. Combining Gaussian moment dilation, Laplace-weighted linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT), we implement spectral filters of $A$ to estimate heat-semigroup overlaps, regularized inverse queries, and energy responses, as well as to prepare spectral Galerkin solution states. A common-state construction further allows the block-encoding queries to be used across multiple scalar observables. Under polylogarithmic-cost block-encoding access to $A$ and state-preparation oracles, our heat-overlap algorithm achieves $O(\operatorname{polylog} N)$ gate complexity at fixed normalized precision, confidence, and spectral scale. Ideal statevector simulations validate our discrete circuit constructions, while a matched approximate-counting benchmark demonstrates the quadratic precision advantage of coherent amplitude estimation for energy readout.

papers.title: Detection and Recovery of Core--Periphery Structure in Random Geometric Graphs
papers.abstract: Core--periphery (CP) structure, characterized by a dense core of interconnected nodes linked to sparsely connected peripheral nodes, is a prevalent feature of many real-world networks. We propose a core--periphery random geometric graph (CP-RGG) model in which vertices are independently and uniformly distributed on the unit cube \([0,1]^m\), and each vertex is designated as a core node with probability \(p_n\). Two vertices are connected if their Euclidean distance falls below a type-dependent threshold, governed by three distinct radii for core--core, core--periphery, and periphery--periphery pairs. We investigate the information-theoretic limits for both the detection and recovery of the core in the CP-RGG. For detection in the non-degenerate regime, we prove that the total variation distance between the CP-RGG and a null RGG without CP structure converges to one if and only if the expected number of core nodes tends to infinity. For recovery, we demonstrate that almost exact recovery is achievable if and only if the expected degree tends to infinity. Finally, we establish limits for exact recovery. In the one-dimensional sparse regime (\(m=1\)), we obtain a sharp threshold when the core--core and core--periphery radii coincide. For \(m\ge2\), when the core has polynomial size and the core--periphery radius exceeds twice the periphery--periphery radius, we prove that the exact recovery threshold is sharp up to constant factors, scaling on the order of \(\log n\).

papers.title: New lower bounds for six small hypergraph Ramsey numbers
papers.abstract: Let $R(k,l;t)$ denote the least $n$ such that every colouring of the $t$-subsets of an $n$-set with two colours has $k$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the first colour, or $l$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the second. We give explicit colourings proving $R(4,5;3)\ge 38$, $R(4,6;3)\ge 71$, $R(5,5;3)\ge 99$, $R(5,6;4)\ge 201$, $R(6,6;4)\ge 601$ and $R(6,6;5)\ge 84$. The first three improve the bounds 35, 63 and 88 listed in Radziszowski's dynamic survey. The last three improve the listed bounds 67, 133 and 72, and for the two 4-uniform numbers also the values 159 and 317 of a recent data deposit. The colourings of 3-subsets are invariant under groups of affine maps $x\mapsto ax+b$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n$, for $n=37$, 69 and 97, in the last two cases with one further fixed point. Those of 4-subsets live on the projective line over $\mathbb{F}_q$, for $q=199$ and $q=599$, and are invariant under $\mathrm{PSL}(2,q)$ or $\mathrm{PGL}(2,q)$, so each is given by a table of $q$ entries. For 5-subsets we show that, for every prime $q\ge 5$, invariance under $\mathrm{PGL}(2,q)$ forces six points all of whose 5-subsets have the same colour; our colouring is invariant under all affine maps of $\mathbb{Z}_{83}$. By known constructions the bounds give $R(5,5,5;3)\ge 9605$ and $R_k(5;3)\ge 98^{2^{k-2}}+1$, and $R(6,7;4)\ge 2001$, $R(7,7;4)\ge 12001$ and $R(8,8;4)\ge 588001$. The colourings, and programs that verify them, accompany the paper as ancillary files.

papers.title: Labeled Chip-Firing on Ordered Directed Graphs
papers.abstract: We study labeled chip-firing on rooted directed graphs where for each vertex $v$, the children of $v$ are linearly ordered. When a vertex fires, the selected chips are sent to its children in increasing order. We show that homomorphisms preserving these child choices transport legal firing sequences. We then consider the directed lattice $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$ and ask which chips can reach a given vertex. We give a recurrence for the smallest reachable label when sufficiently many chips are present and show that consecutive pairing attains this minimum. Finally, we determine the largest reachable label by symmetry and prove that the reachable labels form an interval when the number of initial chips is sufficiently large.

papers.title: The Scaled Dirichlet Distribution: Lauricella Representations and Estimation
papers.abstract: We derive explicit expressions for the mixed moments of the scaled Dirichlet distribution in terms of the Lauricella hypergeometric function of type $D$. The relationship with Carlson's multivariate $R$-function is stated, and the convergence conditions required for the series derivation are made explicit. The general expressions yield means, second moments and covariances, with Gauss and Appell hypergeometric representations in the bivariate and trivariate cases. Method-of-moments and maximum-likelihood formulations are presented, together with simulation summaries and an illustrative comparison of scaled Dirichlet and ordinary Dirichlet fits to compositional futures-return data.

papers.title: A Modified Quasi-Newton Method for Unconstrained Optimization with Nonpositive Curvature Detection and Structured Complexity
papers.abstract: We consider the convergence, worst-case complexity, and implementation of R2N, a modified quasi-Newton method for large-scale unconstrained smooth optimization. At each iteration, we compute a step that approximately minimizes the sum of a quadratic model of the objective with an adaptive quadratic regularization, and that results in sufficient decrease. The objective is only assumed to be $C^1$, although second derivatives may be used if they are available. The implementation features a broad range of step-computation strategies, from sparse factorization to matrix-free Krylov methods, that satisfy global convergence requirements. When detected, directions of nonpositive curvature are exploited. Our analysis allows unbounded model Hessians, provided they satisfy a mild growth condition. We derive a worst-case evaluation complexity bound that separates the progress made along positive- and nonpositive-curvature directions. By forcing the regularization parameter to vanish near isolated local minimizers, we obtain superlinear local convergence. The implementation specializes naturally to nonlinear least-squares problems. We provide a modular Julia implementation, and use it in a numerical study on the CUTEst test set that assesses the treatment of nonpositive curvature, the subproblem solver, the update of the regularization parameter, and direct versus iterative subproblem solves. An Armijo-Goldstein line search along nonpositive-curvature directions, MINRES-QLP as subproblem solver, and a regularization parameter driven to zero near a solution form our recommended configuration. With exact second derivatives, R2N is competitive with a trust-region method, solving slightly more problems with fewer objective and gradient evaluations. With convex models, the trust-region method performs as well or better.

papers.title: A Generalized Lefschetz Degree with applications to Fixed Point Theory
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a class of spaces, named Lefschetz admissible, where the identity maps on compacts can be approximated by certain maps with values in Lefschetz spaces in a suitable sense. For maps defined on these spaces, we introduce a generalized Lefschetz degree obtained as the set of accumulation points of usual Lefschetz degrees for the approximant maps in a certain compactification. We show that when the degree is nonempty, fixed point results hold. We consider both the situation of spaces embedded in topological vector spaces (TVSs) as global and as neighborhood retracts. As two consequences, we obtain a generalization of a fixed point result due to Browder, and a no-retraction criterion for compact subsets of locally convex TVSs.

papers.title: Antipodal Parity and Second-Chaos Regge Curvature on Random Hyperplane Arrangements
papers.abstract: Limit theorems are proved for the signed Regge curvature of independent oriented hyperplanes in Euclidean space under the piecewise-flat metric induced by unit linear ramps on their positive half-spaces. Provided each hyperplane law is invariant under orientation reversal, the curvature has zero mean and zero first Hoeffding component at every finite sample size. In particular, it is uncorrelated with all square-integrable unoriented functionals. For isotropic Gaussian normals on bounded windows, the rescaled curvature is approximated in mean square by a degenerate U-statistic and converges to a second-chaos series diagonalised on odd spherical harmonics. In the plane, the global cone-angle deficit admits a closed-form limit law universal up to scale under finite fourth moments.

papers.title: Algebraically elliptic resolutions in a family of determinantal quartic threefolds
papers.abstract: We construct a family of determinantal irrational quartic threefolds in $\mathbf{P}^4$ for which the blow-up of the sixteen nodes and two distinguished small projective resolutions are algebraically elliptic in the sense of Gromov.

papers.title: Rank and Rel in Strata of Abelian Differentials
papers.abstract: We prove that every invariant subvariety M in a genus g stratum H(k_1,...,k_n) of Abelian differentials satisfies rank(M) <= rel(M) + 1 + sum_i (k_i - 1). In particular, every invariant subvariety with rel zero in a principal stratum is a Teichmüller curve. Combined with work of Eskin, Filip and Wright, this implies that each principal stratum contains only finitely many nonarithmetic Teichmüller curves. If rank(M) < g, we also show that rank(M) + rel(M) <= g - 1 + n/2.

papers.title: A Density Bound for Muñiz's List Reversal
papers.abstract: Muñiz described the problem of reversing a list of positive integers under the following rules: given a list of distinct positive integers, at each step, one can combine two adjacent entries into their sum or break an entry into two entries with the same sum, under the constraints that after each step the list must contain distinct entries no larger than the original largest entry. The question of what lists are and are not reversible under these rules is studied and an asymptotic upper bound on the density of an irreversible list is established.

papers.title: Compact Slack-Free Penalty Functions for Inequality Constraints in Higher-Order Unconstrained Binary Optimization
papers.abstract: Inequality constraints in higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO) are commonly handled using slack variables or by enumerating infeasible assignments, which respectively enlarge the search space or produce penalties whose size grows with the number of forbidden values. We construct exact slack-free penalty functions for upper- and lower-bound constraints on binary-encoded integers. Each function is constructed hierarchically from the threshold bits through a recursive addition-and-multiplication rule, and its correctness for arbitrary bit widths and representable thresholds is proved by mathematical induction. Equivalent explicit finite sum-product representations are also derived, enabling direct analysis of product-term count and polynomial degree. Interval constraints are obtained by adding the lower- and upper-bound penalties, while exclusion constraints are obtained by multiplying them. Compared with the trivial enumerative construction, the proposed method reduces the worst-case product-term count from linear to logarithmic in the representable range. Except at one non-vacuous boundary threshold for each bound, it also reduces both product-term count and degree. The resulting single-bound penalties have minimum positive value 1 and maximum value at most the bit width, which may simplify penalty-weight selection. The same construction also extends exactly to fixed-scale fractional variables through appropriate scaling of the integer thresholds.

papers.title: Flatness and Tightness in Hypertopes
papers.abstract: A hypertope is a thin, residually connected incidence geometry. For each pair of types $\{i,j\}$, the residues of that type must be polygons, and if all residues of that type are the same type of polygon, then we can record this information in a diagram $D$. Given such a diagram, we prove a lower bound on the number of chambers of a hypertope with that diagram. A hypertope that achieves this bound is called \emph{tight}. We prove that a hypertope is tight if and only if its diagram $D$ is a forest and, for every pair of types $\{i,j\}$ that is not an edge of $D$, every $i$-element is incident to every $j$-element. This generalizes a previously known result about abstract polytopes. Finally, we describe a combinatorial method and an algebraic method for constructing tight hypertopes.

papers.title: When Is an OIRI-Algebra a Banach Lattice? Structure Theorems and Counterexamples
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the exact conditions under which a relatively uniformly complete semiprime $f$-algebra whose order ideals are ring ideals (an OIRI-algebra) admits a norm turning it into a Banach lattice or an AM-space. While recent literature claimed that this equivalence holds automatically in the presence of a weak order unit, we construct a concrete counterexample within a relatively uniformly complete vector lattice showing that this assertion fails in general. By analyzing the canonical embedding $ψ:A\rightarrow Orth(A)$, we prove that the equivalence between being an OIRI-algebra, admitting an AM-space or Banach lattice norm and satisfying $Orth(A)=$ $Stab(A)$ $=Z(A$) holds under the assumption that $ψ\left( A\right) $ is relatively uniformly closed in $Orth(A)$ (alongside a characterization via finite elements in the unitization $A^{\sharp}$). We also deduce immediate consequences for unital $f$-algebras and generalize our main theorem to non-semiprime $f$-algebras via the quotient modulo the nilpotent radical $N(A)$.

papers.title: The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
papers.abstract: We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. We consider laws under which, conditionally on the metric map, the decoration follows a statistical physics model such as the Ising model or the Gaussian free field: the values at the vertices interact through a quadratic Hamiltonian and, given these values, the decoration along each edge is a Brownian bridge. Working with 4-regular maps with a boundary (the duals of quadrangulations with a boundary), we define a Markov property that allows explorations to stop in the middle of an edge. We show that, under mild regularity assumptions, the rerooting-invariant families of laws satisfying this Markov property are exactly the Boltzmann decorated metric maps. We also prove a strong Markov property and show that the random submaps inducing a Markovian decomposition are exactly the stopping maps for a suitable filtration. Finally, we obtain analogous results for classical decorated planar maps.

papers.title: The Partial Trace Functor on Soergel Bimodules in Type $\mathbb{B}$
papers.abstract: We write down some observations about the partial trace functor between the categories of Soergel bimodules of type $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$ and $\mathbb{B}_n$ for future reference. In particular, we observe that, like in type $\mathbb{A}$, the partial trace sends Soergel bimodules to a semi-infinite $q$-graded sum of Soergel bimodules.

papers.title: Globally $F$-regular varieties are rationally chain connected
papers.abstract: We prove that projective globally $F$-regular varieties are rationally chain connected. We deduce this from a study of the positivity of their tangent bundles and their purely inseparable covers. Although some globally $F$-regular varieties admit non-vanishing pluridifferential forms, we show that each admits a unique purely inseparable crepant cover that does not have this pathology. These covers carry very free curves, which can be degenerated to chains of rational curves through general pairs of points.

papers.title: Functional Estimation under Local Differential Privacy: General Lower Bounds and Applications to Entropy and Power Sums
papers.abstract: We study the estimation of functionals of discrete distributions under local differential privacy (LDP). Even for well-studied examples like Shannon entropy and power sums, the existing bounds left open how the minimax risk scales with the alphabet size, the sample size, and the privacy parameter. To understand these dependences, we establish two general minimax lower bounds for the broader class of additive functionals. The first lower bound links the difficulty of estimating a functional to how well it can be approximated by polynomials of a given degree. The second complements the first by capturing how sensitive the functional is to small changes in the underlying distribution. To illustrate the effectiveness of these two bounds, we apply them to the estimation of Shannon entropy and power sums. In both cases, they close the existing polynomial gaps and, perhaps surprisingly, show that simple plug-in type estimators already achieve the optimal polynomial rates.

papers.title: Decomposition of trilinear forme
papers.abstract: In this work, we are interested in the decomposition of trilinear forms. We associate this decomposition with the decomposition into irreducible subspaces of the group algebra associated with the symmetric group. We have a correspondence between a ternary form and a symmetric trilinear form, in the same way that we have the correspondence between a quadratic form and a symmetric quadratic form. We are then interested in the decomposition of ternary forms into a sum of cubes of linear forms and as an application we find the Tartaglia formulae on the expression of the roots of equations of degree 3.

papers.title: Monomial singularities of maps in low codimension and their deformations
papers.abstract: We study complex analytic map germs whose coordinate functions are monomials up to a change of coordinates. Motivated by recent normal form results of Rodrigues Hernandes and Ruas for $\mathcal{A}$-finite monomial maps in the range $p\ge 2n$, we address the remaining gap $p<2n$, solving an open problem posed in their work in the range $n<p<2n$. Our main results show that a monomial map germ $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^p,0)$ with $p < 2n$ and $(n,p) \neq (1,1)$ is $\mathcal{A}$-finite if and only if it is $\mathcal{A}$-equivalent to an $\mathcal{A}$-stable germ. For $n = p = 1$ we also obtain the family of simple singularities of type $A_k$. Finally, we construct new families of $\mathcal{A}$-finite (generally non-monomial) map germs starting from monomial ones.

papers.title: On the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem for $\mathbb Z_n^3$
papers.abstract: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)$ is the least positive integer $t$ such that every sequence of $t$ elements of $\mathbb Z_n^r$ contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero. In this paper, we prove that $$\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^3)=9n+o(n)$$ for odd $n$. For every fixed $r\ge 4$, we also show that $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)\le\bigl(\binom{2r-1}{r}+1\bigr)n+o_r(n).$ Our approach combines Alon--Dubiner-type spectral expansion, Zakharov's convex-geometric framework, and restricted-sum ideas developed by Han and Ren.

papers.title: A census of alternating tangles
papers.abstract: We give a census of the roughly 10 billion prime, connected, alternating tangles with at most 14 crossings. Along the way, we prove analogs of the Tait conjectures for alternating tangles and observe that aspects of the geometry of alternating tangles are reflected in their diagrams, as is the case with links.

papers.title: The Clifford Hierarchy from Clifford Stabilizers in 2D
papers.abstract: The Bravyi-König theorem limits the constant-depth logical gates of 2D topological Pauli stabilizer codes to be in the Clifford group. Known qubit codes with Clifford stabilizers exceed it by only one level of the Clifford hierarchy, and this was conjectured to hold generally. We show that this bound can be completely bypassed, and that topological codes with Clifford stabilizers in 2D can realize transversal logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy. We present two explicit constructions of codes based on copies of the quantum doubles of $D_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$, with $k$ logical qubits and a logical $C^{k-1}Z$ gate, which is at level $k$ of the Clifford hierarchy. The physical circuits realizing the gates consist only of physical $Z$ or $CZ$ gates. The main new ingredient comes from the logical encoding, which depends crucially on non-Abelian group multiplication.

papers.title: Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models
papers.abstract: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them. This sequence returns the quiver to its original form while transforming the J- and E-terms. We explain the relation between quiver-invariant triality and the orbifold reduction of quiver-invariant brane tilings.

papers.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
papers.abstract: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way. The sample compression conjecture of Floyd and Warmuth (1995) asserts that every binary concept class of VC dimension $d$ admits a sample compression scheme of size $O(d)$; a weaker conjecture asks only for size polynomial in $d$. Both have remained open: the first bound depending only on $d$, due to Moran and Yehudayoff (2016), is exponential in $d$. We prove the weaker conjecture by constructing a sample compression scheme of size $O(d^2 \log^2 d)$.

papers.title: Geometry, Local Minimax Risk, and the Limits of Sample Average Approximation in Linear Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We study how the local geometry of a linear stochastic optimization problem determines its statistical difficulty, measured by expected decision regret. The optimal local rate is governed by how fast the support function of the feasible set grows away from its linearization at the true mean; depending on the instance, it can be $n^{-1/2}$, $n^{-1}$, $n^{-2}$, or a non-power rate, and sample average approximation (SAA) attains these rates in a Gaussian mean model. At smooth instances, SAA also attains the classical sharp local minimax constant. We then allow the data distribution to vary in a Kullback--Leibler (KL) ball of radius proportional to $1/n$ around a reference distribution $P$. The exact local minimax limit of this benchmark, which may depend on $P$, coincides with that of a Gaussian model whose local parameter set is the covariance ellipsoid of $P$. A simple coordinatewise truncated SAA rule, which does not use $P$, attains the minimax rate, and at smooth instances its constant matches the minimax constant as the neighborhood radius grows. Ordinary SAA, in contrast, can have strictly suboptimal worst-case expected regret when the local rate is fast relative to the tails of $P$, because rare tail events then dominate the expectation. The results delineate when SAA is sharply optimal, rate-optimal, or statistically suboptimal, and quantify the local price of distributional robustness.

papers.title: Mateability of Fuchsian lattices with polynomials, and failure of algebraicity
papers.abstract: We prove that all Fuchsian lattices, with the possible exceptions of those associated with compact orbifolds of type (0,3) and (1,1), can be mated with complex polynomials, providing the first examples of such combinations beyond genus-zero orbifolds. We also present the first construction of matings between simply degenerate Kleinian groups and polynomial maps. These matings are realized as holomorphic, though not necessarily algebraic, correspondences, demonstrating that Fatou's vision of unifying Kleinian group actions and polynomial dynamics can be fulfilled in the wider setting of transcendental correspondences. We achieve this by generalizing the orbit equivalence mating framework introduced in our earlier work. Specifically, we use pinching and acceleration techniques to construct a new class of piecewise Möbius covering maps of the circle that are orbit equivalent to Fuchsian groups. By mating these circle coverings with polynomials, we construct degenerate polynomial-like maps whose analytic continuations yield the desired correspondences. The quality of this orbit equivalence plays a crucial role in the mating description, as well as in governing whether the resulting correspondences are algebraic.

papers.title: There is no binary linear $[65,9,29]$ code
papers.abstract: We prove that no binary linear $[65,9,\geqslant29]$ code exists, equivalently, that no even binary linear $[66,9,\geqslant30]$ code exists. Together with known constructions, this determines $d_2(65,9)=28$, $n_2(9,29)=66$, and $n_2(9,30)=67$. A residual-code bound and a known construction also give $d_2(122,10)=56$. To prove nonexistence, we associate with a hypothetical even code a quadratic function derived from half the codeword weight modulo $2$. Its polar form determines the fourth derivative of a Boolean function of degree at most four. Character sums, weight moments, and the exclusion of weight-$42$ codewords give upper bounds on the support of this function in seven cases. Restrictions to nondegenerate affine subspaces exclude six cases. In the remaining case, equality would force four distinct coordinate functionals to be identically $1$ on an affine seven-space, although at most two can have this property. The argument uses published minimum-length results for binary linear codes of dimensions eight and nine.

papers.title: Variance-Adaptive Upper Confidence Bounds for Multi-Armed Bandits with Kaplan--Meier Survival Estimation
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic multi-armed bandit problem in which the reward associated with each arm is the survival probability at a pre-specified time horizon, and the observed outcome is a right-censored time-to-event variable. Standard bandit algorithms face delayed and partial observations in this setting. Prior adaptations for the Kaplan--Meier (KM) estimator rely on Hoeffding-type bounds that ignore the inherent heteroscedasticity of continuous survival processes. To bridge this gap, we propose KM-UCB, a variance-adaptive policy that unites continuous-time survival analysis with discrete sequential decision-making. By leveraging martingale theory and continuous influence functions, we derive a fixed-cohort empirical Bernstein bound parameterized by Greenwood's variance formula. For realtime allocation, we retain the Greenwood index and use a survival bound from completed records to review the recommended arm. Under catch-up reporting, the policy has logarithmic expected regret with an arm-specific variance term in the exploration bound. We evaluate the original policy in a dual-layer delayed simulation and a retrospective replay of breast cancer trial data, and evaluate the correction in a separate paired simulation.

papers.title: Low Moments, Small Balls and Star Discrepancy
papers.abstract: Let $D_P$ be the discrepancy function of a configuration $P$ of $N$ points in the $d$-dimensional unit cube, and let $\|D_P\|_q$ be its $L^q$ discrepancy. We prove that for all fixed $d\ge2$ and $0<q\le1$ the $L^q$ discrepancy of every configuration of $N\ge2$ points is at least $c_{d,q}(\log N)^{(d-1)/2}$ with a constant $c_{d,q}>0$. This bound is sharp; together with the classical results for $q>1$, it determines the minimal order of the $L^q$ discrepancy for every $0<q<\infty$ in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for $q=1$ it answers Chen's problem on the sharp lower bound for the $L^1$ discrepancy in dimension $d\ge3$. We prove the small ball inequality for Haar functions in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$ and for arbitrary real coefficients with the conjectured power of $n$, up to a polylogarithmic factor; here $2^{-n}$ is the smallest volume of the dyadic boxes involved. The method also extends to a class of piecewise polynomial mother functions. For the $L^\infty$ discrepancy $\|D_P\|_\infty=ND^*(P)$, where $D^*(P)$ is the star discrepancy, we prove the conjectured lower bound $c(\log N)^{3/2}$ in dimension three, and the lower bound $(\log N)^{d/2}$ up to a power of $\log\log N$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge4$. Finally, we construct $N$-point sets whose $L^\infty$ discrepancy is $O_d((\log N)^{d-1-1/16})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$; this disproves the conjectured optimality of the order $(\log N)^{d-1}$ of the classical constructions.

papers.title: On the refined Kaneko--Zagier conjecture
papers.abstract: We extend our results on Zhao's conjectural basis to finite multiple zeta values modulo arbitrary prime powers and to the corresponding completed algebra. As a consequence, the refined Kaneko--Zagier conjecture, which gives a precise description of relations modulo arbitrary prime powers in terms of ordinary multiple zeta values, follows from the dimension and direct-sum conjectures for ordinary and finite multiple zeta values. We also prove Rosen's lifting conjecture under the dimension conjecture for finite multiple zeta values. The proofs use confluence relations and $p$-adic associators and do not use motivic theory.

papers.title: A Weinstein manifold without any spherical Fukaya category
papers.abstract: We show that, after attaching a subcritical handle to $T^*\bP^2$ to obtain a manifold $M$, the integral wrapped Floer endomorphism algebra of a cotangent fibre admits no spherical refinement for any choice of brane structure; this obstructs the existence of any wrapped Fukaya category for $M$ over the sphere spectrum. We further discuss some features of the resulting Weinstein eight-manifold $M$, which is homotopy equivalent to $S^4$.

papers.title: Unique determination of ellipsoids by their intrinsic volumes
papers.abstract: We prove that ellipsoids in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge 2$, are uniquely determined by their intrinsic volumes up to congruence, resolving the conjecture posed by Gusakova and Zaporozhets in 2017.

papers.title: The Holomorphic Reduction of Pseudoconvex Homogeneous Manifolds
papers.abstract: Suppose $G$ is a connected complex Lie group and $H$ is a closed complex subgroup. Then there exists a closed complex subgroup $J$ of $G$ containing $H$ such that the fibration $π:G/H \to G/J$ is the holomorphic reduction of $G/H$, i.e., $G/J$ is holomorphically separable and ${\mathcal O}(G/H) \cong π^*{\mathcal O}(G/J)$. In this paper we prove that if $G/H$ is pseudoconvex, i.e., if $G/H$ admits a continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion function, then $G/J$ is Stein and $J/H$ has no non-constant holomorphic functions.

papers.title: Shadowing Property for Linear Operators on Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: This note is dedicated to the study of the shadowing property for (bounded linear) operators on Banach spaces. We combine the spectral characterization of the shadowing property, recently established by Dragičević and Pituk, with tools from local spectral theory, to obtain new results and simpler proofs of known results on shadowing for operators. We also prove that the shadowing property always implies the average shadowing property and the asymptotic average shadowing property for invertible operators on Banach spaces. Furthermore, we investigate the shadowing property for some specific classes of operators, such as weighted composition operators and adjoints of multiplication operators on certain spaces of holomorphic functions.

papers.title: A Geometric Calderón Problem for Differential Forms
papers.abstract: We establish boundary determination and global partial-data uniqueness for Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential $p$-forms. We derive an explicit recursion for its full symbol and determine the full boundary jet of the metric, modulo conformal gauge in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$. For $p\geq1$, partial data determine metrics that are analytic in the interior and near the measured boundary subset, up to isometry or conformal equivalence. The global uniqueness relies on a new projection-kernel embedding that detects the unobserved boundary through rank loss and small eigenvalues. We also establish global partial-data uniqueness for smooth metrics with harmonic curvature, using elliptic-transport unique continuation and, in the critical dimension, conformal-geodesic coordinates. A Weyl nondegeneracy condition further upgrades conformal equivalence to isometry.

papers.title: Gauss--Bonnet theorem for o-minimal surfaces with isolated singularities
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between topology and curvature of surfaces definable in an o-minimal structure. Our main result is a Gauss--Bonnet-type formula for closed (not necessarily compact) definable surfaces with finitely many singular points, expressing the Euler characteristic in terms of the total Gaussian curvature, the local densities at the singular points, and the density at infinity. As consequences, we obtain an inequality for definable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities and, for complex algebraic curves, a formula and an inequality relating the Euler characteristic, the total curvature, the multiplicities at the singular points and the degree.

papers.title: Pair Siegel-Veech constants for branched covers of tori and Veech surfaces
papers.abstract: For a locus $\mathcal{E}$ of branched covers of tori satisfying a monodromy assumption, we show there exists an explicit constant $c_A(\mathcal{E})$ so that the number of pairs of saddle connections on surfaces in $\mathcal{E}$ of length at most $R$ and cross product at most $A$ grows like $c_A(\mathcal{E})R^2$ for every Diophantine surface in $\mathcal{E}$; this constant is moreover piecewise linear in $A$. In particular, this covers the case of billiards on rectangles with a barrier. Similar pointwise results are shown for Veech surfaces. The proof uses work of Margulis-Mohammadi on the quantitative inhomogeneous Oppenheim conjecture.

papers.title: The Ceresa Cycle on $X_0^+(p)$
papers.abstract: We consider the curve $X_0^+(p)$ with prime $p$, which is the quotient of the modular curve $X_0(p)$ by the Fricke involution. We describe how one can explicitly calculate the shadow of a Hecke operator on $X_0^+(p)$, which is a rational divisor on $X_0^+(p)$ whose nonvanishing is an obstruction to the Ceresa cycle of $X_0^+(p)$ being torsion in the Chow group of the Jacobian of $X_0^+(p)$. We also provide an implementation of this procedure in PARI/GP and SageMath and use this on all primes below 5000.

papers.title: The limits of inertia bounds on graph powers
papers.abstract: We investigate the tightness of inertia and inertia-type bounds related to graph powers. This class of graphs appears in several contexts, such as the theory of distance-regular graphs, quantum information theory and coding theory. They are a priori not covered by previous separation constructions involving locally sparse graphs, see Kwan and Wigderson (2024), or Alon's pseudorandom graphs, see Elphick, Tang and Zhang (2025). Instead, we apply the latter's lower bound for complements of pseudorandom graphs to random graphs and random Cayley graph constructions, whose graph-power structure is ensured by additive combinatorial arguments. From this we are able to conclude that also for graph powers there can be a large gap between inertia bounds and the actual independence number. For the inertia-type bound, which is based on polynomials, we achieve even larger separation by considering sequences of graphs whose spectrum converges to a continuous distribution. Our methods draw from several areas of mathematics, ranging from additive combinatorics and probabilistic methods, to character sums over finite fields and arithmetic geometry.

papers.title: Topological Properties of Cones with Small Entropy
papers.abstract: We show that regular hypercones in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with small entropy have simple topology. As a result, the link of the given cone is topologically an $(n-1)-$sphere. Moreover, the space of all links whose associated cones have entropy close to 1 can be retracted onto the space of equatorial spheres, which is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^n$.

papers.title: Divisibility of Character Values of Wreath Products of Symmetric Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group whose character table is integer-valued, and let $K$ be any fixed positive integer. We prove that almost every entry of the character table of the wreath product $G\wr S_N$ is divisible by $K$ as $N\to\infty$.

papers.title: Non-intrusive modal decomposition of transport-dominated data
papers.abstract: We derive a non-intrusive modal decomposition method for positive transport-dominated datasets. We derive our method by generalizing an optimization-centric formulation of the Proper Orthogonal Decomposition. We propose two principles as a basis for this generalization. The first is that the Wasserstein distance is a more effective measure of the approximation error for transport-dominated problems, and the second is that the smoothness of the low-dimensional trajectories must be taken into account during the reconstruction. The framework is sufficiently flexible that domain-expert knowledge, in the form of inequality constraints, can be easily included. These features are demonstrated on synthetic problems and on data from a wildland fire simulation. Our method is based on the Shifted POD, which models the data as the sum of modes undergoing different coordinate transformations, but unlike the bulk of Shifted POD literature we do not assume that the correct transformation parameters are known. For a fixed number of modes, we observe a reduction of the reconstruction error of up to $43\%$ with respect to the Shifted POD baseline, despite the fact that the baseline assumes a-priori knowledge of the coordinate transformation parameters and the proposed method does not.

papers.title: Uniqueness of coexistence states in diffusive predator-prey models, at the occasion of the 100th anniversary of the first publication of V. Volterra on the predator-prey system
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes the existence and uniqueness of coexistence states for a generalized class of diffusive Lotka--Volterra predator-prey models involving spatial heterogeneities and mixed boundary conditions of non-classical type. Its main findings are the following: (a) after characterizing the existence of coexistence states, the uniqueness of the coexistence state is established, in a multidimensional context, near the curves of change of stability of the semi-trivial positive solutions of the model, (b) the one-dimensional uniqueness theorem of López-Gómez and Pardo [65,67] is sharpened up to cover the case of mixed boundary conditions of nonclassical type, (c) the multidimensional uniqueness theorem of [66] is substantially generalized up to deal with variable coefficients, and it is complemented with the global attractivity of the unique coexistence state, which excludes any Hopf bifurcation, (d) assuming Neumann boundary conditions and constant coefficients, we can sharpen, very substantially, the pioneering results of Leung [46] establishing the the constant coexistence state is the unique coexistence state of the model. In this setting, we can also prove that the constant coexistence state is a global attractor with respect to the positive solutions of the associated parabolic problem, and that it is non-degenerate, even for general differential operators, not necessarily self-adjoint. \par As this paper is a personal homage to Volterra [92] at the centenary of the publication of his foundational paper on the predator-prey model, based on the field data of D'Ancona [4], this paper begins with a review of the first scientific works in population dynamics of Vito Volterra and Umberto D'Ancona.

papers.title: Invariant solitons of the inverse mean curvature flow in the sphere and in hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: We study hypersurfaces of the sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ and of hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, $n\ge 3$, that move under the inverse mean curvature flow by a one-parameter group of isometries. No closed hypersurface has this property, and a soliton with constant mean curvature is an open subset of a horosphere. For the rotation hypersurfaces of do Carmo and Dajczer, of spherical, hyperbolic and parabolic type, the soliton equation reduces to a single ordinary differential equation, which we analyse in every dimension. In $\mathbb{H}^n$ the horosphere appears at the critical speed $λ=1$ and separates entire bowls from solitons that end at a singular $(n-2)$-sphere; each class has exactly one horospherical end, and it is the threshold between ends asymptotic to totally geodesic hypersurfaces and ends at a singular orbit. At an axis of codimension two we obtain a complete trichotomy, which changes at the speed $λ=2(n-1)$ from logarithmic spirals to cuspidal edges. In $\mathbb{S}^n$ no rotational soliton through the axis is complete, and the radius of its singular sphere satisfies $\fracπ{2}-r_+=\frac{K_n}λ\left(1-2(n-1)^2λ^{-2}\logλ\right)+O(λ^{-3})$, with $K_n=\sqrtπ\,Γ(\frac{n+1}{2})/Γ(\frac{n}{2})$. For $n=3$, the commuting pairs of Killing fields give two further classes, helicoidal and Hopf-invariant surfaces; the latter are the rotators of the inverse curve shortening flow on the round two-sphere.

papers.title: Two almost sure upper bounds for sums of random multiplicative functions
papers.abstract: Let $f,g$ be a squarefree and extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions, respectively. We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, almost surely $$\big|\sum_{n \le x}\frac{f(n)}{\sqrt{n}}\big| \ll (\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}, \qquad \big|\sum_{n\le x}g(n)\big|\ll\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}.$$ We also show that almost surely, there exist arbitrarily large values of $x$ such that $\sum_{n \le x}\frac{f(n)}{\sqrt{n}} \gg (\log\log x)^{1/4+o(1)}$. We follow Caich and Durkan and Pearce-Crump by using a version of the Azuma--Hoeffding inequality for martingale difference sequences.

papers.title: On the Vertex Growth Rate of Integer Partition Polytopes and Their Non-Vertex Structure
papers.abstract: The Hardy-Ramanujan formula states that the asymptotic growth of the number of integer partitions of $n$ is $\exp(Θ(\sqrt{n}\,))$. We prove that the number of vertices of the integer partition polytope is bounded by $\exp\left(\mathcal{O}(\ln^2 n)\right)$. This implies that all partitions of $n$ can be generated from a negligible subset of vertex partitions using convex combinations. We also present new computational data on the structure of non-vertex partitions, which cause the huge gap between the number of vertices and the total number of partitions.

papers.title: List packing for graphs with small arboricity
papers.abstract: We prove that every graph $G$ whose edge set is the union of $r$ forests has list packing number at most $2^r$. This means that for all $k\ge 2^r$ and every list-assignment $L$ with lists of size $k$, the graph $G$ admits $k$ disjoint proper $L$-colourings. While for large $r$ this bound is far from optimal, for $r\in\{1,2\}$ it is sharp. As a direct corollary of the case $r=2$, we obtain that every triangle-free planar graph has list packing number at most $4$, thus improving upon a result of Dvořák, Masařík, Musílek and Pangrác and providing the optimal answer to a question of Dvořák, Postle and Norin on (weighted) $ε$-flexibility of such graphs. As a corollary of the case $r=3$, we obtain a short alternative proof that every $K_5$-minor-free (and hence every planar) graph has list-packing number at most $8$, matching the state of the art. All results above also hold for the stronger notion of correspondence packing.

papers.title: On least energy solutions for a critical nonlinear Schrödinger system with $K$-wise interaction: the competitive case
papers.abstract: We study least energy fully non-trivial solutions of a nonlinear Schrödinger system with Sobolev critical nonlinearities and repulsive interaction involving all the components at the same time. Under the scalar Brezis-Nirenberg assumptions on the linear coefficients, we prove existence of least energy fully non-trivial solutions on smooth bounded domains for every negative coupling in dimensions \(N=5,6\). For \(N=3,4\), due to the lack of $L^2$-integrability of the Aubin-Talenti bubbles, the same conclusion holds under additional sufficient assumptions, and in particular we provide an explicit condition on the domain and coefficients. We also investigate the strong competition limit, and characterize fully non-trivial limiting profiles as minimizers of a partially segregated variational problem. A preliminary study of independent interest concerns the whole-space problem. For general admissible \(K\), we determine the component-wise Nehari infimum and prove that it is not attained, even in the radial class. Finally, when the linear coefficients coincide, we establish a sharp criterion for the existence of positive synchronized solutions in terms of the strength of the competition.

papers.title: Whitehead doubles and the failure of the AJ conjecture
papers.abstract: For marked Whitehead doubles of torus knots with coprime parameters $2\le r<s$, the AJ conjecture fails for both clasp signs, both companion chiralities, and every integer twist. The zero-framed signed unreduced colored Jones sequence has a nonzero rationally saturated annihilator. Every nonzero primitive representative specializes nontrivially at $t=-1$ with the meridian variable $M$ independent. With $L$ the longitude variable, the specialization contains the irreducible quadratic $E=L^2-(M^4-4M^2+1)L+M^4$ for the negative clasp and $M^4E(M^{-1},L)$ for the positive clasp. The corresponding quadratic is coprime to the full classical $A$-polynomial, including $L-1$, over $\mathbb{Q}(M)[L^{\pm1}]$, so the discrepancy persists when each irreducible factor is counted once. The curve $E=0$ comes from the marked Whitehead link exterior with its axis cusp complete. For the displayed monic polynomial, $πm(E)$ is the unsigned volume of that two-cusped exterior. We use the actual Jones sequence to select a right divisor of the satellite transfer operator. Rational factor tests show that the quadratic survives in this divisor, and the two marked companion fillings exclude it as a component of the satellite boundary curve.

papers.title: Systole and kissing number of closed hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that if the genus of a closed hyperbolic surface $S$ is sufficiently large, then\[ \operatorname{sys}(S)\leq\frac{4}{3}\log(\operatorname{area}(S)). \] This proves a conjecture by Schmutz for large genus. The proof is based on quantitative counting estimates for closed geodesics derived from the Selberg trace formula. As a consequence, we also prove that for such surfaces, the kissing number of $S$ satisfies \[ \operatorname{Kiss}(S) \leq C\frac{\operatorname{area}(S)^{\frac{5}{3}}}{\log(\operatorname{area}(S))}, \] where $C>0$ is a constant.

papers.title: Inversion of Set-Valued Wiener Models
papers.abstract: A Wiener system consists of a linear system followed by a nonlinear system. This paper addresses the problem of recovering a vector in a Hilbert space from the outputs of multiple Wiener systems.
