This notion is important, e.g., in insurance pricing as it ensures no cross-subsidization between different price cohorts. In this paper, we show that boosting trees can be used to test necessary conditions for strong calibration and auto-calibration, respectively. The practical relevance of our approach is supported by a numerical example, in which the proposed tests achieve high empirical power.

papers.title: On vacuum static foliations
papers.abstract: We study the compact vacuum static foliation, a Riemannian foliation which generalizes the compact vacuum static space. In particular, we investigate the relations between the tautness of a compact vacuum static foliation and the bound of transverse curvatures.

papers.title: On the dynamics of composition operators: supercyclicity, odometers and translations
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical properties of composition operators acting on Banach spaces of measurable functions. In particular, we study in some detail the composition operators induced by odometers, which allows us to give a variety of new examples and counter-examples. We also get general statements about supercyclicity and frequent hypercyclicity of composition operators on $L\_p$-spaces.

papers.title: Fourier--Galerkin Methods for Subwavelength Resonances in two-dimensional Acoustic Metamaterials
papers.abstract: We present a Fourier--Galerkin asymptotic framework for the analysis and computation of subwavelength resonances in two-dimensional scattering problems in finite domains. Starting from the boundary integral formulation, we apply a Fourier--Galerkin discretization to derive an explicit finite-dimensional effective matrix whose kernel characterizes the resonant frequencies. In the subwavelength regime, we obtain asymptotic expansions of this matrix in terms of $ω$ and the material contrast, identifying the leading-order operators and their kernel structure. This reduction transforms the resonance problem into a low-dimensional nonlinear eigenvalue problem, avoiding large-scale discretizations and global root-search procedures. The entries of the effective matrix are explicitly computable and admit fast evaluation using FFT-based quadrature. The resulting approach provides an efficient and robust computational framework for resonances in general smooth geometries.

papers.title: A new upwind DG scheme for a Cahn-Hilliard-Darcy model of tumor growth
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop a new numerical scheme for a Cahn-Hilliard-Darcy model that describes tumor growth in a fluid-saturated porous medium. First, we derive a physically consistent model from the general framework proposed in [35] that guarantees mass conservation and pointwise bounds on the phase-field and nutrient variables, with a decreasing energy law. The resulting model couples the evolution of tumor cells via a Cahn-Hilliard equation with a diffusion equation for the nutrients through chemotactic interactions and extends the model in [1] by introducing the effect of a surrounding fluid described by Darcy's law. Subsequently, we propose a fully discrete scheme that combines an upwind discontinuous Galerkin method in space and a convex splitting strategy in time, which inherits the fundamental properties of the continuous model: mass conservation, pointwise bounds and a discrete energy law that mimics the one of the continuous model up to some residual terms. Our theoretical analysis is accompanied by numerical experiments that demonstrate the robustness of the proposed scheme and show the influence of the surrounding fluid on the tumor evolution.

papers.title: From Multirelations to Meet-Relations: A Relational Duality for Semilattices with Adjunctions
papers.abstract: We develop a relational duality for semilattices with adjunctions (SLatas) based on binary meet-relations. First, we introduce the category of MoS-spaces and establish a dual equivalence with modal semilattices. Then, by means of A-relations, we define the category RelSP and prove a dual equivalence between SLata and RelSP. To compare this framework with the multirelational semantics previously developed for SLatas, we introduce the notion of normal mS-space and show that, under this condition, the multirelational structure can be canonically recovered from a meet-relation, and conversely. As a consequence, we prove that the categories RelSP and SLataSp are isomorphic.

papers.title: Complex deformations of the circle: Group cohomology and Virasoro uniformization
papers.abstract: We approach the question of complexification of the diffeomorphism group of the circle by considering real-analytic maps from the circle into the punctured complex plane with winding number +1. Such complex deformations form an infinite-dimensional manifold with partially defined inversion and composition operations, smooth in the sense of Frölicher structures, and with Lie algebra relations at the identity given by the Witt algebra. We compute their second group cohomology with real coefficients. It is generated by two cocycles: One cocycle extending the Bott-Thurston cocycle related to the Gelf'and-Fuks cocycle of the Virasoro algebra, and another Euler class cocycle combining mean rotation and conformal radius. Complex deformations act naturally on the (infinite-dimensional) Segal moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces with enumerated and analytically parametrized boundary components, equipping them with smooth Frölicher structures. We prove a Virasoro uniformization theorem: The tangent spaces of the Segal moduli spaces are spanned by vector fields induced by the Witt algebra. Finally, we relate the actions of complex deformations to Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates and Schiffer variation on finite-dimensional moduli spaces of bordered hyperbolic surfaces with one marked point on each boundary component.

papers.title: MIST: Reliable Streaming Decision Trees for Online Class-Incremental Learning via McDiarmid Bound
papers.abstract: Streaming decision trees are natural candidates for open-world continual learning, as they perform local updates, enjoy bounded memory, and static decision boundaries. Despite these, they still fail in online class-incremental learning due to two coupled miscalibrations: (i) their split criterion grows unreliable as the class count K expands, and (ii) the absence of knowledge transfer at split time. Both failures share a common root: the range of Information Gain intrinsically scales with log2 K. Consequently, any Hoeffding-style confidence radius derived from it must inevitably grow with the class count, making a K-independent split criterion structurally impossible, taking away the potential benefits of applying streaming decision trees to continual learning. To fix this issue, we present MIST (McDiarmid Incremental Streaming Tree), which resolves both failures through three integrated components: (i) a tight, K-independent McDiarmid confidence radius for Gini splitting that acts as a structural regulariser; (ii) a Bayesian inheritance protocol that projects parent statistics to child nodes via truncated-Gaussian moments, with variance reduction guarantees strongest precisely when splitting is most conservative; and (iii) per-leaf KLL quantile sketches that support both continuous threshold evaluation and geometry-adaptive leaf prediction from a single data structure. On standard and stress-test tabular streams, MIST is competitive with global parametric methods on near-Gaussian benchmarks and uniquely robust on non-Gaussian geometry where SOTA benchmarks collapse.

papers.title: Algorithms for Computing Set Tolerances: Theory, Computational Analysis and Applications
papers.abstract: The regular set tolerance is an important term in sensitivity analysis. For combinatorial sum problems, e.g., the Traveling Salesman Problem, Shortest Path Problem and Minimum Spanning Tree Problem, it determines how much the sum of the costs of the elements of a set can be increased while ensuring that all current optimal solutions remain optimal. The regular set lower tolerance determines how much the sum of the costs of the elements of a set can be decreased while ensuring that the objective value of the optimal solution is not changed. We investigate general methods for computing regular (upper and lower) set tolerances in combinatorial sum problems. For the upper tolerance, we present a linear programming approach, and for the lower tolerances, three linear programming approaches, where the last two are novel and lead to recursive procedures for computation of the lower tolerances of all subsets of the given ground set. We give new upper bounds for set lower tolerances. For both upper and lower tolerances, we give an exact formula for sets of cardinality 2 and 3. Furthermore, we computationally compare and analyze our introduced tolerance LPs. Finally, we consider the computation of tolerances for the Minimum Spanning Tree Problem, give a formula for single tolerances, a lower bound for regular set upper tolerances and an exact formula for regular set lower tolerances.

papers.title: Signature Approach for Contextual Bandits with Nonlinear and Path-dependent Rewards: Regret Bound and Statistical Inference
papers.abstract: We study contextual bandits with nonlinear and path-dependent rewards through a novel signature-transform-based approach. Leveraging the universal nonlinearity property of signatures, we approximate continuous path-dependent reward functionals by linear functionals in the signature space. This representation enables the use of efficient linear contextual bandit methods while preserving expressive sequential structure. Building on this framework, we propose \texttt{DisSigUCB}, a signature-based disjoint upper confidence bound (UCB) algorithm. Under boundedness and non-degeneracy assumptions, we establish a high-probability regret bound of order \(\tilde\mathcal{O}\bigl(d_{\text{Sig}} \sqrt{KT} + \ varepsilon_N T \sqrt{d_\Sig}\bigr)\) with \(K\) being the number of actions, \(d_{\text{Sig}} \) the signature feature dimension, and \(\varepsilon_N\) the finite-depth approximation error. We further introduce $ζ$-\texttt{DisSigUCB}, a randomized variant that ensures persistent exploration for statistical inference. Under additional margin and long-run design conditions, we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the action-specific ridge estimators. Both the synthetic experiments and the numerical studies on temperature sensor monitoring, sleep-stage classification, and hospital nurse staffing demonstrate the effectiveness of \texttt{DisSigUCB} over linear and kernelized contextual bandit baselines in nonlinear and path-dependent settings.

papers.title: Hecke monoids, their homomorphisms and parabolicity
papers.abstract: One of the motivations of this work was the rather mysterious commutative submonoid of parabolic elements in any Hecke monoid of finite type, discovered by the first author and D. Kazhdan. To understand it, we introduce the class of (weakly) parabolic homomorphisms, which map parabolic elements to parabolic elements. The most prominent ones are those we call parabolic projections. We prove that products of parabolic elements can be described explicitly in terms of these remarkable homomorphisms. We also use them to find all pairs of commuting idempotents in Hecke monoids and prove that the number of such pairs in finite types miraculously depends only on the rank and satisfies a Fibonacci-like recurrence. We also introduce the class of locally injective homomorphisms. As a major step towards the classification of injective homomorphisms, we find all locally injective connected homomorphisms between Hecke monoids of types A, B and D and identify, albeit conjecturally, the injective ones. As a surprising byproduct of our study of parabolic and injective homomorphisms, we describe all homomorphisms between Hecke monoids. This gives hope that the classification of injective ones is achievable.

papers.title: Computer-Assisted Proofs in Dynamical Systems: A Case Study of a Heteroclinic Orbit in the Shimizu--Morioka System
papers.abstract: The radii polynomial approach is an a posteriori validation method based on the contraction of a quasi-Newton operator. We apply this strategy to give a computer-assisted proof of a transverse heteroclinic orbit in the Shimizu--Morioka system, validating the equilibria and eigenpairs, the local invariant manifolds via the parameterization method, and the connecting orbit via a boundary-value problem. For each subproblem we present a four-step procedure: $(i)$ zero-finding formulation, $(ii)$ approximate zero, $(iii)$ approximate inverse, and $(iv)$ bound estimates. More broadly, this highlights the unifying structure behind the a posteriori validation method. Alongside the analysis, we include code snippets implemented in Julia using the RadiiPolynomial library.

papers.title: Polynomials from tilings of rectangles
papers.abstract: We study tilings of rectangular boards using unit squares together with a single type of big tile shaped as a Ferrers diagram. We derive generating functions for these tilings, prove real-rootedness and interlacing properties of associated independence polynomials, and establish connections with several sequences in the OEIS. Our results touch on tilings involving L-shaped polyominoes, fault-free tilings, and cylindric variants. For rectangular tiles of shape $(k,k)$, we prove real-rootedness and interlacing in the range $d\leq k$.

papers.title: Supercriticality of the SIRS on random networks
papers.abstract: We analyze the supercritical regime of the SIRS process (Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Susceptible) on random graphs and Galton-Watson trees. Our results provide a three-part characterization of this process: first, we prove that even on finite sparse graphs, the epidemic can survive for an exponentially long time. On heavy-tailed networks with power-law-like exponents, we show that this holds for the entire range of parameters. Notably, while contemporary works establish a stretched exponential survival time for power-law networks, our approach provides the optimal bound of order $e^{Θ(n)}$ via a different approach. Finally, for infinite trees, we establish sufficient conditions for strong survival, proving that the root is re-infected infinitely often even for light-tailed degree distributions like the Poisson distribution.

papers.title: Noise-induced enhancement of regime lifetimes -- A data-driven approach using deterministic trajectories
papers.abstract: We investigate the lifetime of dynamical regimes under the impact of noise motivated by low-dimensional models of the atmosphere. One may expect that the inclusion of noise tends to make the system leave prescribed regions of the state space faster. However, for relevant systems with complexities ranging from phenomenological toy models to reduced models of atmospheric dynamics, this intuition has proven misleading. As long as the noise is sufficiently small, the noisy system stays in regimes of interest on average longer than its deterministic counterpart, an effect we call ``stochastic inertia''. This phenomenon has been observed through extensive numerical simulations for different noise levels. We propose a numerical technique for testing the occurrence of stochastic inertia, constructing, for any fixed noise level, a Markov chain on the set of points given by a sufficiently long trajectory of the system without noise. The method is shown to correctly predict the presence of stochastic inertia in simple systems, and its utility is demonstrated on a paradigm model of atmospheric dynamics.

papers.title: Galois lines for a canonical curve of genus 4, III: non-cyclic Galois lines
papers.abstract: Let $C \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ be a canonical curve of genus $4$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero. For a line $l \subset \mathbb{P}^3$, we consider the projection $π_l: C \to \mathbb{P}^1$ from $l$ and the induced extension of function fields $π_l^*: k(\mathbb{P}^1)\hookrightarrow k(C)$. A line $l$ is called an \emph{$S_3$-line} (resp. a \emph{$K_4$-line}) if the extension $k(C)/π_l^*(k(\mathbb{P}^1))$ is Galois and its Galois group is isomorphic to the symmetric group $S_3$ on three letters (resp. the Klein four-group $K_4$). We prove that the number of $S_3$-lines (resp.\ $K_4$-lines) is at most $10$ (resp.\ $15$).

papers.title: Subword enumeration up to stack-sorting equivalence
papers.abstract: Defant and Kravitz introduced generalizations of West's stack-sorting map $s$ from permutations to finite words. This raises questions as to how such generalizations could be applied in the field of combinatorics on words. The Defant-Kravitz generalizations of $s$ depend on how repeated occurrences of the same character within a word may be repositioned, according to their $\textsf{tortoise}$ and $\textsf{hare}$ operations. As demonstrated in this paper, these operations provide a natural way of extending abelian complexity functions for infinite sequences, in a way that gives light to structural properties associated with infinite words. We apply these new ideas to two famous infinite words: the paperfolding word and the Thue-Morse word. In the case of the Thue-Morse word, we discover an interesting connection to the previous work of several authors, such as de Luca and Varricchio, on the ``special'' factors of the Thue-Morse word. This may be seen as providing a basis for a new and interdisciplinary area linking the combinatorics about the stack-sorting of permutations with the field of combinatorics on words.

papers.title: Increasing arc-connectivity by bounded- and fixed-size inversions
papers.abstract: For a digraph $D$ and some $X \subseteq V(D)$, the inversion of $X$ is the operation of flipping all arcs both of whose endvertices are in $X$. We initiate the study of establishing arc-connectivity properties by applying inversions of bounded or fixed size. For fixed-size inversions, the feasibility problem is interesting. For all integers $p \geq 2$ and $k \geq 1$, we give a characterization of the digraphs that can be made $k$-arc-strong by applying inversions of size exactly $p$, provided they are sufficiently large. For bounded-size inversions, the feasibility problem is easy, so we focus on minimising the number of inversions. We prove that for all integers $p\geq 3$ and $k \geq 1$ and any $ε>0$, there exists a polynomial-time $(4k-2+ε)$-approximation algorithm for computing the minimum number of inversions of size at most $p$ that make a given digraph $k$-arc-strong. This is in stark contrast to other results on inversion optimization problems. On the other hand, we show that for any $p\geq 3$ and $k \geq 1$ the problem is NP-hard, and, moreover, APX-hard. As a result on parameterized complexity, we show that for any $k \geq 2$, it is $W[1]$-hard with respect to $p$ to decide whether a given digraph can be made $k$-arc-strong by applying a single inversion of size at most $p$. We also prove that for a given multidigraph, it is $W[1]$-hard with respect to $\ell$ to decide whether it can be made 2-arc-strong by applying $\ell$ inversions of size 2.

papers.title: On Word Representations and Embeddings in Complex Matrices
papers.abstract: Embeddings of word structures into matrix semigroups provide a natural bridge between combinatorics on words and linear algebra. However, low-dimensional matrix semigroups impose strong structural restrictions on possible embeddings. Certain finitely generated groups admit faithful representations in SL(2, C) and other similar matrix groups. On the other hand, it is known that the product of two free semigroups on two generators cannot be embedded into the 2x2 complex matrices. In this paper we study embeddings of word structures into low-dimensional matrix semigroups over the complex numbers and develop new techniques for constructing word representations of the Euclidean Bianchi groups. These representations provide a symbolic framework and a natural first step towards analysing fundamental decision problems in 2x2 matrix semigroups.

papers.title: Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, I. Main Results
papers.abstract: In this paper, we combine techniques from functional analysis and spectral theory to obtain semiclassical Weyl laws and extensions of Connes' integration formula for a large class of spectral triples. These results generalize and simplify recent work of McDonald--Sukochev--Zanin: all regularity assumptions and dimension restrictions are removed, and their Tauberian condition is replaced by a weaker spectral condition, Condition~(W), which holds in far greater generality. We also establish Tauberian criteria for Condition~(W) involving zeta functions and heat traces, as sought by Alain Connes. The results are illustrated on bounded Euclidean domains, closed Riemannian manifolds, the Steklov problem, and quantum tori. In the latter setting they resolve a conjecture of Edward McDonald and the author. This is the first part of a two-part work. The proofs of the main technical results are given in Part II.

papers.title: Logarithmically Coupled p-Laplacian Systems: From Discrete Ground States to Rigidity and Critical Continuous Limits
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of logarithmically coupled p-Laplacian systems on locally finite graphs and on \(\mathbb{R}^N\) for the critical case \(p = N > 4\). The coupling poses two challenges: the energy functional is ill-defined on the natural Sobolev space, and loss of the \(L^\infty\)-embedding prevents standard control of logarithmic terms. To resolve this non-separable logarithmic singularity, we develop an \textbf{exponent calibration technique} that converts logarithmic terms into strictly lower-order power estimates. The technique plays an essential role in two critical steps: the existence proof for the regularised problem and the uniform boundedness of regularised ground states that restores compactness. Thus, we prove solvability of the original ill-posed continuous critical equation. In the discrete setting, we identify five new intrinsic structures, including an exact constrained Hessian factorisation and a scalar rigidity index. We complete a discrete--continuous double loop, providing a unified variational framework for logarithmically coupled systems.

papers.title: A Partially Parabolic Damage-Driven Inflammation Model: Threshold Dynamics and Linear Spreading
papers.abstract: We study a partially parabolic reaction--diffusion--chemotaxis model of damage--inflammation feedback motivated by Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The model couples functional and damaged tissue with effective macrophage activity and a damage-induced inflammatory signal. The invariant tissue simplex bounds the damage source and, together with parabolic estimates, yields global well-posedness and dissipativity in every spatial dimension covered by the regularity assumptions, for arbitrary chemotactic sensitivity. A dimensionless feedback threshold separates resolution to a damage-free dystrophin-deficient state from the existence of a positive damage equilibrium in the spatially homogeneous system. On bounded connected domains, we prove resolution at and below the threshold and, above it, uniform componentwise persistence with spatially uniform lower bounds for initial data with at least one nonzero active component. We derive a candidate linear spreading speed for localized damage and establish a nonlinear upper spreading bound in the absence of chemotaxis. Numerical front speeds agree closely with the linear prediction in the simulations.

papers.title: Prime Density, Kolmogorov Quotients and Homeomorphisms between Macías Spaces of Integral Domains
papers.abstract: For an integral domain $R$ that is not a field, the Macías space $M(R)$ is the topological space whose underlying set $R^0=R\setminus\{0\}$ is endowed with the topology generated by the basis $\{σ_k^0:k\in R^0\}$, where $σ_k^0=\{x\in R^0:\langle x\rangle+\langle k\rangle=R\}$. We characterize the openness of the unit group in $M(R)$ via semiprimitivity and, for Dedekind domains and unique factorization domains (UFDs), relate semiprimitivity and the infinitude of prime elements to the density of irreducible and prime elements. We identify the Kolmogorov quotient of $M(R)$ with a space of sets of maximal ideals and reduce the homeomorphism problem to these quotients and the cardinalities of the fibers of the quotient maps; in particular, local domains of equal cardinality have homeomorphic Macías spaces. For Dedekind domains, we solve this problem in terms of the cardinalities of their unit groups and relations among the ideal classes of their maximal ideals, thereby answering the homeomorphism problem of Macías (2024) for countable semiprimitive ones. When the class groups are torsion, as they are for principal ideal domains, the cardinalities of the unit groups and of the sets of maximal ideals suffice. For UFDs, we characterize homeomorphic Macías spaces via comaximality with prime elements and, under an additional hypothesis, obtain a solution analogous to that for Dedekind domains. We solve the problem for several classes of polynomial rings over discrete valuation rings, UFDs and fields. Finally, we characterize additive homeomorphisms between Macías spaces of certain domains of characteristic zero via ring isomorphisms, partially answering a problem of Macías and Ortiz (2025).

papers.title: Induced replication and the assessment of models
papers.abstract: The paper is a first attempt at a foundation of inference for the assessment of semiparametric and other high-dimensional models, seeking reconciliation with the low-dimensional Fisherian foundations by replacing out-of-sample prediction error as a criterion for semiparametric model assessment by a type of within-sample prediction error. We highlight the possibility, in some contexts, of avoiding the usual semiparametric considerations, including estimation of unparametrised nuisance components and the associated difficulties of tuning-parameter choice that blur the distinction between estimation and model assessment. A key aspect of the work is the inducement of replication under the postulated model, the route to which being context-specific but based on structural properties of the model. The ideas are isolated through examples.

papers.title: The Bollobás--Nikiforov inequality for complete multipartite graphs, with remarks on the $K_4$-free case
papers.abstract: Bollobás and Nikiforov conjectured that every graph $G \neq K_n$ with $m$ edges and clique number $ω$ satisfies $λ_1^2(G) + λ_2^2(G) \leq 2(1 - 1/ω)m$, where $λ_1(G) \geq λ_2(G)$ are the two largest adjacency eigenvalues. We give a short self-contained proof of the inequality for complete multipartite graphs, based on a quadratic-form identity which shows that $λ_2 \leq 0$, and we determine the equality cases in this class. We show that equality in the conjecture is attained by a wider family than the Turán graphs, namely by disjoint unions of two complete bipartite graphs, or of two balanced complete $r$-partite graphs of possibly different orders. For $K_4$-free graphs we record the cases that follow from known results, with corrected attributions, and we give examples showing that three natural lines of attack fail: a Hoffman-type eigenvalue bound for graphs with large independence number, a spectral stability statement for connected graphs, and Zykov symmetrization in an arbitrary direction.

papers.title: Kinetic Langevin Splitting Schemes for Constrained Sampling
papers.abstract: Constrained sampling, the task of generating samples from a distribution restricted to a convex set, is an important problem in computational statistics. In this paper, we propose new unadjusted sampling algorithms obtained by applying the symmetric BAOAB and ABOBA splittings, of the kinetic Langevin dynamics, to a penalized surrogate of the constrained target. This also includes their stochastic gradient versions. Since the Hessian of the penalized surrogate is discontinuous across the boundary of the constraint set, analyses relying on a Lipschitz Hessian do not apply. We therefore develop an analysis based only on strong convexity and smoothness, proving one-step Wasserstein contraction schemes, non-asymptotic Wasserstein bounds of both schemes and complexity bounds. The resulting complexities for the stochastic gradient versions improve substantially on traditional Euler-type discretizations. Numerical experiments verify our theory, which is tested on a toy problem and Bayesian constrained regression problem. Overall, the splitting schemes demonstrate stability at step sizes several times larger than Euler-type methods, require five to seventeen times fewer gradient evaluations for a given accuracy.

papers.title: Towards sparse optimization over convex loops: Equivalence of Square Root Velocity distance and Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao
papers.abstract: The Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) distance on $S^{2}$ has recently been shown to coincide with a classical elastic distance between $S^{2}$-immersions in the theory of Riemannian shape analysis. While this correspondence holds in dimension $2$, the analogous statement fails in general on $S^{1}$ and, in the case of convex curves, it cannot be derived from existing two-dimensional arguments. In this paper, we establish that for convex absolutely continuous immersions of $S^{1}$ in the plane, the shape distance induced by the square root velocity transformation (SRVT) is indeed equivalent to the WFR distance acting on their associated length measures. The proof exploits a monotonicity principle for optimal transport on the universal cover of the circle, which in turn guarantees the existence of an optimal reparametrization achieving the SRVT infimum and enables a one-dimensional unbalanced optimal transport reformulation. Motivated by this equivalence, we further investigate the role of sparsity in shape optimization problems formulated in terms of length measures and regularized by the WFR distance. We study linear optimization over the corresponding balls, for which we prove a finiteness result when the reference measure is discrete, and propose a convex, positively one-homogeneous regularizer suitable for conditional gradient algorithms.

papers.title: A multiscale discrete-to-continuum framework for structured population models
papers.abstract: Mathematical models of biological populations commonly use discrete structure classes to capture trait variation among individuals (e.g. age, size, phenotype, intracellular state). Upscaling these discrete models into continuum descriptions can improve analytical tractability and scalability of numerical solutions. Common upscaling approaches based solely on Taylor expansions may, however, introduce ambiguities in truncation order, uniform validity and boundary conditions. To address this, here we introduce a discrete multiscale framework to systematically derive continuum approximations of structured population models. Using the method of multiple scales and matched asymptotic expansions applied to discrete systems, we identify regions of structure space for which a continuum representation is appropriate and derive the corresponding partial differential equations. The leading-order dynamics are given by an advection equation in the bulk domain and advection-diffusion processes in small inner layers about wavefronts. We further derive discrete boundary layer descriptions for regions where the discrete model cannot be approximated by a continuum description. Finally, we demonstrate the method on a simple lipid-structured model for early atherosclerosis and verify consistency between the discrete and continuum descriptions. The multiscale framework we present can be applied to other heterogeneous systems with discrete structure in order to obtain appropriate upscaled dynamics with asymptotically consistent boundary conditions.

papers.title: Convergence Rate of a Functional Learning Method for Conditional Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We consider a stochastic optimization problem involving two random variables: a context variable $X$ and a dependent variable $Y$. The objective is to minimize the expected value of a nonlinear loss functional applied to the conditional expectation $\mathbb{E}[f(X, Y,β) \mid X]$, where $f$ is a nonlinear function and $β$ represents the decision variables. We focus on the practically important setting in which direct sampling from the conditional distribution of $Y \mid X$ is infeasible, and only a stream of i.i.d. observation pairs $\{(X^k, Y^k)\}_{k=0,1,2,\ldots}$ is available. In our approach, the conditional expectation is approximated within a prespecified parametric function class. We analyze a simultaneous learning-and-optimization algorithm that jointly estimates the conditional expectation and optimizes the outer objective. Using a specially designed measure of non-optimality, combining the squared norm of the objective function's gradient and the mean square error of the auxiliary parametric model, we establish that the method achieves a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}\big(1/\sqrt{N}\big)$, where $N$ denotes the number of observed pairs. The rate holds in expectation when the auxiliary model is linear in its parameters, which includes linear architectures with bounded features, and in probability for general smooth models.

papers.title: Introduction to Dieudonné modules and supersingular abelian varieties revisited
papers.abstract: In this Note we present an expository account for \dieu modules and revisit supersingular abelian varieties. We give a simple proof of the uniqueness of products of two or more supersingular elliptic curves (a theorem due to Deligne, Ogus and Shioda), and of Oort's theorem for superspecial abelian varieties.

papers.title: A Cheng-type Eigenvalue-Comparison Theorem for the Hodge Laplacian
papers.abstract: We consider the class of closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds with Ricci curvature and injectivity radius bounded below by uniform constants, and an upper bound on the diameter. We establish a uniform upper bound for the eigenvalues of the Hodge Laplacian acting on differential forms on Riemannian manifolds in this class, similar to the classical eigenvalue comparison theorem proved by Cheng for the Laplace-Beltrami operator acting on smooth functions. This extends earlier work of Dodziuk and Lott, which required sectional curvature bounds in addition to bounds on other geometric quantities. As an application, we obtain uniform eigenvalue estimates for the connection Laplacian acting on $1$-forms.

papers.title: Non-Runge Fatou-Bieberbach Domains in Stein Manifolds with the Density Property and Non-tame Families of Stein Structures
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Stein manifold with the density property. We present methods of constructing two kinds of non-Runge Fatou-Bieberbach domains in $X$, which by definition are proper open subsets of $X$ biholomorphic either to $\mathbb{C}^n$ with $n = \dim X$ or to $X$. For both kinds, we provide examples where our methods apply. The results are applied to give new examples of non-tame families of Stein structures on manifolds with non-trivial topology.

papers.title: Cohen-Macaulay squarefree powers of edge ideals of very well-covered graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with edge ideal $I(G)$. For $q\ge 1$, the $q$th squarefree power $I(G)^{[q]}$ is the Stanley-Reisner ideal of the $q$-matching-free complex $\mathsf{MF}^q(G)$, whose faces are the vertex sets containing no $q$ pairwise disjoint edges. We determine exactly which squarefree powers of the edge ideal of a very well-covered graph are Cohen-Macaulay: if $G$ has $2n$ vertices, then $R/I(G)^{[q]}$ is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if $q=n$, or $q=1$ and $G$ is Cohen-Macaulay, or $G=W(H)$ is a whisker graph and $q \le \left\lfloor \frac{\operatorname{girth}(H)}{2} \right\rfloor$. The answer is independent of the field. The proof rests on a rigidity theorem: among very well-covered graphs, only whisker graphs have a sequentially Cohen-Macaulay squarefree power strictly between the first and the last. For whisker graphs we show that $\mathsf{MF}^q(W(H))$ is vertex decomposable for $q \le \left\lceil \frac{\operatorname{girth}(H)}{2} \right\rceil$, and we express the depth and the regularity of every squarefree power through the homology of explicit auxiliary complexes. As a consequence we prove a conjecture of Das, Roy and Saha on the depth of squarefree powers of whisker cycles. Finally, for every graph with a perfect matching, we compute the top homology of $\mathsf{MF}^q(G)$ and determine when the regularity of $R/I(G)^{[q]}$ attains its maximal possible value.

papers.title: Torsion cycles on Fermat varieties
papers.abstract: A theorem of Manin and Drinfeld states that any divisor of degree $0$ on the cusps of a modular curve is torsion in the Jacobian. An elegant proof of this result was provided by Elkik using mixed Hodge theory. Rohrlich proved a generalization of this to Fermat curves. In this paper we reprove his results along the lines of the work of Elkik. We then use the same methods to generalize it to higher Chow cycles. We introduce a notion of `ambient decomposability' - essentially cycles coming from the ambient ${\mathbb P}^{n+1}$ and the base field - and show that higher Chow cycles determined by coordinate sections are necessarily of this type. This is a revised and accepted version of the earlier manuscript of the same name and is to appear in Indagationes Mathematicae. The results are stronger than the results in the earlier manuscript.

papers.title: Countability Properties of Weakly Compact Sets in Asymmetric Locally Convex Spaces
papers.abstract: A dual pair formulation for asymmetric locally convex spaces is introduced that strictly generalises the ordinary vector space setting. The concept of a polar topology carries over to the asymmetric case and some familiar results are reproduced or generalised such as the bipolar theorem and a Mackey-Arens type theorem. The implications of weak compactness and countability properties are studied and appear intimately connected to separation properties. An asymmetric analogue $C_a(K)$ of the well-known space $C_p(K)$ is introduced and the properties of (relatively) countably respectively sequentially) compact subspaces are investigated. In particular, it is shown that $C_a([0,1])$ is not angelic. However, for Hausdorff subspaces, the different compactness conditions are equivalent and imply the Fréchet-Urysohn property. Moreover, an analogue of the Eberlein-Šmulian theorem holds in asymmetrically normed spaces.

papers.title: Prefactorization algebras for the conformal Laplacian: Central charge and Hilbert Fock space
papers.abstract: Let $d \geq 2$. We consider the symmetric monoidal category of oriented Riemannian $d$-manifolds with conformal open embeddings. The prefactorization algebra associated with the conformal Laplacian defines a symmetric monoidal functor from this category to real vector spaces. For Euclidean domains $U\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, the value of this functor is identified, via the Green function, with the symmetric algebra on the topological dual of the space of harmonic functions. For $d \geq 3$ this identification is natural under all conformal transformations, while in dimension two, its failure of naturality is governed by a harmonic cocycle, which gives rise to the Virasoro central charge. For the unit disk, the resulting vector space carries an algebra structure over the operad of conformal disk embeddings and admits a canonical dense embedding into the Hilbert Fock space. In dimension two, this statement holds after restricting to a codimension-one subspace, as suggested by logarithmic CFT.

papers.title: Completing the classification of torsion over sextic fields for elliptic curves defined over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We complete the classification of torsion subgroups $E(K)_{\text{tors}}$ occurring for an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ over a sextic number field $K$. Previous work determined the complete set of possible groups up to one remaining case, namely $C_3 \oplus C_{18}$. We prove that this group does not occur.

papers.title: A Direct Translation from Abstract Cyclic Proofs to Inductive Proofs
papers.abstract: We identify the notion of a `well-organized' cyclic proof, show that any cyclic proof can be unfolded to a well-organized one, and present a constructive and relatively simple translation from well-organized cyclic proofs to ordinary well-founded proofs. We work with a general class of cyclic proof systems, and translate from such a system to an induced inductive proof system: a multi-sorted predicate logic that extends the cyclic system with a well-founded induction principle. This setting is broad enough to cover trace-based cyclic proofs and size-change terminating functions. Our unfolding technique is a refinement of earlier annotation-based approaches, and allows us to handle cyclic proofs where the underlying inductive sorts need not be linearly ordered.

papers.title: From Consensus-Based Optimization to Evolution Strategies: Proof of Global Convergence
papers.abstract: Consensus-based optimization (CBO) is a powerful and versatile zero-order multi-particle method designed to provably solve high-dimensional global optimization problems, including those that are genuinely nonconvex or nonsmooth. The method relies on a balance between stochastic exploration and contraction toward a consensus point, which is defined via the Laplace principle as a proxy for the global minimizer. In this paper, we introduce new CBO variants that address practical and theoretical limitations of the original formulation of this novel optimization methodology. First, we propose a model called $δ$-CBO}, which incorporates nonvanishing diffusion to prevent premature collapse to suboptimal states. We also develop a numerically stable implementation, the Consensus Freezing scheme, that remains robust even for arbitrarily large time steps by freezing the consensus point over time intervals. We connect these models through appropriate asymptotic limits. Furthermore, we derive from the Consensus Freezing scheme by suitable time rescaling and asymptotics a further algorithm, the Consensus Hopping scheme, which can be interpreted as a form of $(1,λ)$-Evolution Strategy. For all these schemes, we characterize for the first time the invariant measures and establish global convergence results, including exponential convergence rates.

papers.title: On the Order of Products of Coprime Elements in Finite Groups
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce the subgroups $D_m(G)$ and $D_{m,n}(G)$ for a group $G$ with finite exponent. We show that both subgroups are characteristic, that $D_{m,n}(G)$ is always nilpotent, and that their nilpotent structure provides a characterization of Frobenius group decompositions. Furthermore, we define the $E_{m,n}$-series, which extends this framework to the study of an important class of solvable groups of Fitting height at most $4$. In this sense, we say that a group is $E_{m,n}$-nilpotent if it possesses a finite, strictly increasing $E_{m,n}$-series, and we prove that the maximum length of such a series in an $E_{m,n}$-nilpotent group is 4.

papers.title: Wedge Sampling: Efficient Tensor Completion with Nearly-Linear Sample Complexity
papers.abstract: We introduce wedge sampling, a non-adaptive sampling scheme for recovering an order-$k$ low-rank tensor of side length $n$ from structured observations of its entries. The scheme samples pairs of entries in the same column of a tensor unfolding, forming length-two paths (wedges) in the associated bipartite sampling graph. The products of the paired entries supply the row correlations needed for spectral initialization in regimes where uniform sampling yields too few wedges. For fixed rank, incoherence, tensor order, and condition number, wedge sampling enables polynomial-time recovery with nearly linear sample complexity in $n$. The spectral initializer can be combined with existing refinement procedures using only an additional $\tilde O(n)$ uniformly sampled entries. Spectral refinement achieves weak recovery to any fixed relative Frobenius error. For symmetric third-order tensors with incoherent canonical polyadic factors, gradient descent achieves exact recovery in the noiseless setting, with error decreasing geometrically. The improvement over the $\tilde O(n^{k/2})$ sample complexity typical of efficient methods under uniform entry sampling shows how the conjectured computational barrier depends on the observation model. A key ingredient for the gradient descent analysis is a concentration bound for sparse random tensors in an incoherent spectral norm. We also give error bounds for both procedures under additive Gaussian noise and explicit signal-to-noise conditions. Beyond tensor completion, the same sampling scheme improves the sample complexity of one-sided matrix completion, where the goal is to recover the left singular subspace of a matrix with many more columns than rows.

papers.title: On cyclically covering subspaces of $\mathbb{F}^n_q$
papers.abstract: For a prime power $q$ and a positive integer $n$, let $h_q(n)$ be the largest codimension of a subspace of $\mathbb F_q^n$ whose cyclic shifts cover the whole space. Using invariant decompositions and trace pairings, we prove that $h_q(\ell^t)=0$ whenever $q>2$ is a primitive root modulo the odd prime power $\ell^t$. We also show that $h_q(2n)=0$ if and only if $h_q(n)=0$ when $q$ and $n$ are odd. Multiplicative-subgroup constructions yield further exact values, and we establish $h_3(11)=h_3(16)=1$. Finally, we prove $h_{q^m}(n)\leq h_q(n)$, so every zero value is preserved under field extension.

papers.title: Auslander correspondence for proper connective DG-algebras via extended module categories
papers.abstract: We establish a $d$-dimensional Auslander correspondence for $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebras via $d$-extended module categories. A $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebra $Γ$ is called Auslander if its $d$-extended module category is a $d$-Auslander extriangulated category. Our main theorem gives a one-to-one correspondence: for any $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebra $Λ$ whose $d$-extended module category has finitely many indecomposable objects, the endomorphism DG-algebra of an additive generator is Auslander, and conversely every Auslander $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebra arises in this way.

papers.title: Transitive Sets of Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares
papers.abstract: Write $n=\prod_{i=1}^u p_i^{a_i}$ for the prime factorization of $n$. We prove that a net of order $n$ admitting a point-transitive group of automorphisms preserving each parallel class has at most $\min_i(p_i^{a_i}+1)$ parallel classes. This extends Jungnickel's sharp bound for translation nets. Equivalently, the maximum number of jointly cell-transitive mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order $n$ is $\min_i(p_i^{a_i}-1)$. An explicit Latin square of order nine answers affirmatively Krotov and Potapov's question about the existence of an isotopically transitive, non-topolinear Latin square.

papers.title: On the Damped Euler-Monge-Ampere equations with Radial Symmetry: Critical Thresholds and Large-Time Behavior
papers.abstract: We investigate the global well-posedness and large-time dynamics of the pressureless Euler-Monge-Ampere (EMA) system with velocity damping in multidimensions, subject to radially symmetric initial data. We first establish the phenomenon of critical thresholds, where subcritical initial data maintain global regularity, and supercritical initial data lead to finite time singularity formation. We provide two methods for constructing these thresholds: a refined spectral dynamics approach based on Liu and Tadmor (2002 Commun. Math. Phy. 228 435-66) and a comparison principle based on Lyapunov functions introduced in Bhatnagar and Liu (2020 Math. Models Methods Appl. Sci. 30 891-916). A key finding of this work is that the inclusion of linear damping effectively removes the initial density lower bound previously required in the undamped case (Tadmor and Tan 2022 SIAM J. Math. Anal. 54 4277-96) in certain regimes, allowing for global regularity even in the presence of vacuum or arbitrarily low density. Furthermore, for subcritical initial data, we prove an exponential decay rate to the equilibrium state. Our results unify and extend existing theories for 1D Euler-Poisson system and undamped multidimensional EMA system with radial symmetry.

papers.title: Stability and Decay for the 2D Anisotropic Navier-Stokes Equations with Fractional Horizontal Dissipation on $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: The stability problem for the 2D Navier-Stokes equations with dissipation in only one direction on $\mathbb R^2$ is not fully understood. The model lies between the fully dissipative Navier-Stokes equations and the inviscid Euler equations. Fully dissipative Navier-Stokes solutions exhibit algebraic decay, whereas Euler solutions can develop growing vorticity gradients. We establish small-data global stability for $0\leq s<1$ under assumptions adapted to $s$, and derive decay estimates. Different techniques are developed to treat different ranges of fractional exponents: $0\leq s\leq \frac34$, $\frac34<s<\frac{11}{12}$, and $\frac{11}{12} \leq s <1$. For the final range, we combine polynomial vertical weights with partial Fourier kernel estimates for the pressure and faster decay in a mixed norm of the second velocity component.

papers.title: Fujita exponents on quantum Euclidean spaces
papers.abstract: We study the well-posedness of a non-linear heat equation with power nonlinearity with positive initial data on quantum Euclidean spaces. We prove a noncommutative analogue of the classical Fujita theorem by identifying the critical exponent separating finite-time blow-up from global existence for small initial data. Moreover, we establish a fundamental inequality in general semifinite von Neumann algebras that is of independent interest and plays a crucial role in the study of global existence and local well-posedness of solutions of nonlinear equations in noncommutative setting.

papers.title: Low-Dimensional Adaptation of Rectified Flow: A Diffusion and Stochastic Localization Perspective
papers.abstract: In recent years, Rectified flow (RF) has gained considerable popularity largely due to its generation efficiency and state-of-the-art performance. In this paper, we investigate how well RF automatically adapts to the intrinsic low dimensionality of the support of the target distribution to accelerate sampling. We show that, using a carefully designed end-point adapted time-discretization scheme and with sufficiently accurate drift estimates, the RF sampler enjoys an iteration complexity of order $O(k/\varepsilon)$ (up to log factors), where $\varepsilon$ is the precision in total variation distance and $k$ is the intrinsic dimension of the target distribution. In addition, we show that the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) procedure is equivalent to a stochastic version of RF by establishing a novel connection between these processes and stochastic localization. Building on this connection, we further design a stochastic RF sampler that also adapts to the low-dimensionality of the target distribution under mild requirements on the accuracy of the drift estimates, and also with a specific time schedule. We illustrate the efficacy of newly designed time-discretization schedules with simulations on the synthetic data and text-to-image (T2I) data experiments.

papers.title: Finite de Finetti for convex bodies and Polynomial Optimization
papers.abstract: We study polynomial optimization over convex bodies with separately affine objectives and local affine equality and inequality constraints. We construct a convergent hierarchy of conic relaxations with explicit finite-level error bounds of order $n^{-1/2}$ at level $n$, complemented by a constructive rounding scheme that produces feasible points. The relaxation bounds and rounded objective values bracket the optimum at the same rate. The analytic ingredient is a finite de Finetti representation theorem for arbitrary proper cones: bipartite marginals of symmetric extensions in maximal tensor products are $O(n^{-1/2})$-close, in base norm, to points of the minimal tensor product. Its proof combines a uniform, monogamy-type bound on a variational mutual information based on Frenkel's relative entropy with classical conditioning and informationally complete measurements. We apply the framework to the assemblage relaxation of two-player non-local games in general probabilistic theories. For polytopic state spaces, the hierarchy consists of linear programs, and experiments on the Clauser--Horne--Shimony--Holt (CHSH) game provide a numerical proof of concept for the outer approximations and feasible rounding procedure.

papers.title: Semifields and rank-metric codes from Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between Drinfeld modules and rank-metric codes, focusing on maximum rank distance codes arising from finite semifields. Our method constructs rank-metric codes from linear subspaces of endomorphisms of a Drinfeld module acting on torsion submodules. Using a duality between a Drinfeld module and its endomorphisms, we show that Sheekey's construction fits naturally into this framework, yielding a short conceptual proof of his main theorem. Next, to demonstrate the potential of our method, we construct, for every prime power $q$, new semifields of order $q^9$, which are distinguished from the known ones by their nuclear parameters. Finally, going beyond the Drinfeld module $φ_T=τ^n$ that underlies Sheekey's and related constructions, we obtain infinite families of semifield codes from Drinfeld modules with smaller endomorphism rings, and show that the corresponding semifields are cyclic semifields of Petit.

papers.title: Lagrangian slice disks with symplectomorphic exteriors
papers.abstract: By modifying a construction of Abe and Tange, we exhibit arbitrarily large families of Lagrangian slice disks with Weinstein deformation equivalent exteriors. This answers a Lagrangian version of a question of Hitt and Sumners. We raise other open questions related to Lagrangian slice disks and their exteriors.

papers.title: Affine Invariant Langevin Dynamics for rare-event sampling
papers.abstract: We introduce an affine invariant Langevin dynamics (ALDI) framework for the efficient estimation of rare events in nonlinear dynamical systems. Rare events are formulated as Bayesian inverse problems through a nonsmooth limit-state function whose zero level set characterises the event of interest. To overcome the nondifferentiability of this function, we propose a smooth approximation that preserves the failure set and yields a posterior distribution satisfying the small-noise limit. The resulting potential is sampled by ALDI, a (derivative-free) interacting particle system whose affine invariance allows it to adapt to the local anisotropy of the posterior. We demonstrate the performance of the method across a hierarchy of benchmarks, namely two low-dimensional examples (an algebraic problem with convex geometry and a dynamical problem of saddle-type instability) and a point-vortex model for atmospheric blockings. In all cases, ALDI concentrates near the relevant near-critical sets and provides accurate proposal distributions for self-normalised importance sampling. The framework is computationally robust, potentially gradient-free, and well-suited for complex forward models with strong geometric anisotropy. These results highlight ALDI as a promising tool for rare-event estimation in unstable regimes of dynamical systems.

papers.title: Formal contact-line regimes in the vanishing-slip limit of the thin-film equation
papers.abstract: We analyze the evolution of thin liquid droplets in the lubrication approximation with different slip conditions at the liquid-solid interface. Motivated by the classical no-slip paradox which states that the Navier-Stokes equations with a no-slip boundary condition require unphysical infinite dissipation during droplet spreading, we focus on the limit of vanishing slip. We show that in the no-slip limit three fundamentally different classes of limiting solutions are approached, each of them corresponding to a different scaling of the microscopic contact angle as the regularization parameter vanishes. These findings suggest that the thin-film equation with no slip supports a rich family of physically admissible solutions, provided one interprets the no-slip thin film equation as the asymptotic limit of models which regularized slip conditions. Even though the large apparent contact angles in some of these solutions seem incompatible with the lubrication approximation, a refined analysis shows that the underlying physical variables remain consistent with the assumptions for the lubrication approximation.

papers.title: Generative modeling of conditional probability distributions on the level-sets of collective variables
papers.abstract: Given a probability distribution $μ$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ represented by data, we study in this paper the generative modeling of the corresponding conditional probability distributions on the level-sets of a collective variable $ξ:\mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^k$, where $1 \le k<d$. We propose a general and efficient learning approach that can learn generative models on different level-sets of $ξ$ simultaneously. To improve the learning quality on level-sets in low-probability regions, we also propose a data enrichment strategy by utilizing data from enhanced sampling techniques. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed learning approach through concrete numerical examples. The proposed approach is potentially useful for the generative modeling of molecular systems in biophysics.

papers.title: Abelian approximations for bicrossed products
papers.abstract: We propose a general framework to interpret the cocycle bicrossed product of a matched pair $G \bowtie H = D$ of locally compact quantum group as a deformation quantization of an extension $V \to \mathcal{G} \to G$ with $V$ abelian. This construction requires the existence of a $G$-equivariant measure class isomorphism $η_H : H \to \hat V$, which we call an abelian approximation of $H$. In the smooth case, the extension $\mathcal{G}$ naturally becomes equipped with a Lie-Poisson structure. When both $G$ and $H$ admit abelian approximations, the duality of the bicrossed products provides a unitary operator $\mathcal{F} : \mathrm{L}^2(\mathcal{G}) \to \mathrm{L}^2(\mathcal{G}^*)$, the Poisson-Fourier transform, which implements the quantum duality principle of Drinfel'd. We discuss the construction of abelian approximations from Lie bialgebras and present several classes of examples.

papers.title: Linear dynamics of random products of weighted shifts
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to study the dynamics of random products of weighted shifts on a separable Fréchet sequence space. That is, given a measure-preserving dynamical system $(Ω, \mathcal{F}, μ, τ)$, a Fréchet sequence space $X$ with a basis $(e_n)_{n \geq 0}$, and a strongly measurable map $T : Ω\to \mathcal{B}(X)$ taking values in a finite set of weighted shifts on $X$, we study the dynamics of the sequence $(T(τ^{n-1}ω) \dotsm T(τω) T(ω))_{n \geq 1}$ for almost every $ω\in Ω$. After proving criteria to determine whether this sequence is universal, weakly mixing or mixing for almost every $ω\in Ω$, we study some examples on the spaces $X = \ell_p$, $X = c_0$ and $X = H(\mathbb{C})$ involving two shifts, first in the commuting case and then in the non-commuting one.

papers.title: Sampling Density for Gabor Phase Retrieval
papers.abstract: We study sampling density and geometry for Gaussian Gabor phase retrieval on the full space $L^2(\mathbb R)$. We classify the power lattices $a\mathbb Z^ν\times b\mathbb Z^ν$ that determine every function up to a global phase. For $0<ν<1$ with $ν\ne1/2$, uniqueness holds for every $a,b>0$, whereas it fails for every pair when $ν\ge1$. At the square root scale, uniqueness holds whenever $a^2/b^2$ is irrational. If $a^2=κp$ and $b^2=κq$ with coprime positive integers $p,q$, it holds precisely when $κ\le1$. The critical case follows from a sharp quadratic growth bound, classification of its equality case, and Fock integrability. For $1/2<ν<1$, we prove the stronger modulus-uniqueness statement for all entire functions of finite quadratic type using only first-quadrant samples. We also give uniqueness and nonuniqueness conditions for samples on two intersecting or three parallel lines, relating the sampling scale to the geometry of the lines. The lattice classification extends coordinatewise to Gaussian Gabor measurements on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$.

papers.title: Coupled Stochastic Multigrid Reconstruction for Blind Ptychography
papers.abstract: Blind ptychography enables quantitative imaging when both the specimen and illumination probe are unknown, but modern data sets call for reconstruction methods that can assimilate many diffraction patterns while resolving structure across spatial scales. We introduce a coupled stochastic multigrid framework that addresses these requirements within a unified optimization construction. Rather than appending multigrid correction to an existing stochastic algorithm, the framework begins with a common surrogate for the local object and probe updates and connects these updates to minibatch consensus and coarse-grid correction through a unified residual analysis. This analysis establishes local control of the geometric-mean coupling and characterizes its extension across a grid hierarchy. The fine-grid construction yields the geometric-mean regularized Ptychographical Iterative Engine (GM-rPIE), while the inclusion of multilevel corrections yields the geometric-mean Multilevel-Adaptive-Guided Ptychographic Iterative Engine (GM-MAGPIE). Across nine synthetic configurations spanning scan overlap and Poisson noise, GM-MAGPIE achieves the lowest final object error at the prescribed budgets, while either GM-rPIE or GM-MAGPIE achieves the lowest probe error. Reconstructions of experimental test-pattern and integrated-circuit data further demonstrate the framework's applicability to measured X-ray data.

papers.title: Borel Combinatorics of Schreier Graphs of $\mathbb{Z}$-actions
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the Borel combinatorics of Schreier graphs of $\mathbb{Z}$-actions with arbitrary finite generating sets. We focus mostly on the problem of computing the Borel chromatic numbers of the Schreier graphs on the free part of the shift space $2^\mathbb{Z}$ with a finite symmetric generating set $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}$. Our main results include some general lower and upper bounds, as well as the exact values in some special cases. These values are sometimes the same as the chromatic numbers of the distance graphs on $\mathbb{Z}$ given by $S$, and more often different from them.

papers.title: An Anchor-and-Propagate Scheme for Certified $O(n^2)$ Computation of Shapley Vectors in Cooperative Product Games
papers.abstract:
For a general cooperative game, the Shapley values of the players need not be related, but for cooperative product games they are closely linked; identifying and exploiting these relations is one purpose of this study. We consider a network of \(n\) devices that participate independently with probabilities \(p_1,\dots,p_n\), giving the plausibility game \(T(S)=1-\prod_{i\in S}(1-p_i)\), whose Shapley values are \(φ_i=p_i\int_0^1\prod_{j
e i}(1-p_jt)\,dt\). Since \(T=1-w\) for the product game \(w(S)=\prod_{i\in S}(1-p_i)\), the results transfer to product games with factors in \([0,1]\). Our main contribution is an \emph{anchor-and-propagate} scheme: once \(φ_1\) is computed exactly, the exact identities \(φ_i=c_iφ_1+p_i(p_i-p_1)B_i\) and \(φ_i=φ_1+(p_i-p_1)J_i\), with \(c_i=p_i/p_1\) and one-dimensional integrals \(B_i\le	frac12J_i\), give the remaining \(n-1\) values in \(O(n)\) total time with certified error bounds. For small \(S_i=\sum_{j
e1,i}p_j\) we use a truncated Bonferroni expansion of \(B_i\); for large \(S_i\), a new estimator with relative error \(O(m_i^2/S_i^2)\), \(m_i=\max_{j
e1,i}p_j\). The anchor is computed by Gauss--Legendre quadrature in \(O(n^2)\) operations or, without irrational nodes, exactly by polynomial expansion. The whole vector costs \(	frac32n^2+O(n)\) operations, about half the exact baseline and less than QuadraSHAP. For \(n=100\), the scheme uses \(1.8	imes10^4\) operations with errors below \(3.4	imes10^{-7}\), within a certified bound of \(2.1	imes10^{-6}\); permutation sampling (Castro et al.) needs \(4	imes10^7\) operations for an error of \(7.9	imes10^{-4}\), controlled only in probability. We also give an anchor-free closed-form approximation with an explicit error bound, and a self-contained derivation of Shapley's formula using combinatorial identities and the Beta function.

papers.title: Noncollapsing for Curvature Flows with Inhomogeneous Speeds
papers.abstract: We study closed, embedded hypersurfaces in Euclidean space evolving by fully nonlinear curvature flows, whose speed is given by a symmetric, monotone increasing, $1$-homogeneous, positive underlying speed function $F$ composed with a modulating function $Ψ$. Under the assumption that $F$ is convex or inverse-concave and that $Ψ$ satisfies the corresponding structural conditions, we establish exterior noncollapsing estimates for the flow. The main difficulty stems from the nonlinearity of the evolution equation satisfied in the viscosity sense by the exscribed curvature, whereas in previous works it is a solution to the linearized flow. Moreover, in the case where $F$ is inverse-concave, we adopt an argument different from that of Andrews and Langford to treat off-diagonal extrema.

papers.title: Small Prime Primitive Roots in Arithmetic Progressions
papers.abstract: Let $p>1$ be a large prime number, let $q=O(\log\log p)$ and let $1\leq a<q$ be a pair of relatively prime integers. It is proved that there is a prime primitive root $u\ll (\log p)(\log \log p)^5$ such that $u\equiv a\bmod q$ in the prime finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$.

papers.title: The extended horizontal linear complementarity problem: iterative methods and error analysis
papers.abstract: To the best of our knowledge, since the extended horizontal linear complementarity problem (EHLCP) was first introduced and studied by Kaneko in 1977, no iterative methods or error analysis have been developed for it due to the interdependence of its multiple unknowns in a 'chain-like' structure. This paper aims to address these gaps by: (1) proposing an equivalent fixed-point formulation of the EHLCP by using a variable transformation technique with the max-min function; (2) developing efficient iterative methods for solving the EHLCP based on this fixed-point form, along with their convergence analysis; (3) deriving global error bounds and computable estimates for the EHLCP. Several numerical examples from applications such as multicommodity market equilibrium and bilateral obstacle problems are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods and bounds.

papers.title: Synthetic Acceleration Preconditioners for Parametric Radiative Transfer Equations based on Trajectory-Aware Reduced-Order Models
papers.abstract: The parametric radiative transfer equation (RTE) arises in multi-query applications, such as design optimization, inverse problems, and uncertainty quantification, which require solving the RTE multiple times for various parameters. Classical synthetic acceleration (SA) preconditioners are typically derived from low-order approximations of the kinetic correction equation, such as the diffusion approximation in diffusion synthetic acceleration (DSA). Despite their widespread success, these methods rely on empirical physical assumptions and do not exploit low-rank structures across parameters of the parametric problem. To address this limitation, our previous work developed ROMSAD, a reduced-order model (ROM) enhanced SA preconditioner that incorporates low-rank structures across parameters and the original kinetic description of the correction equation. While ROMSAD improves overall efficiency compared with DSA, its efficiency decreases after the first iteration because the construction of the underlying ROM ignores the preconditioner-dependence of the residual trajectory, leading to a mismatch between the offline and online residual trajectories. To address this offline-online mismatch, we adapt multispace reduced basis preconditioning to parametric RTEs, developing a trajectory-aware ROM framework. Specifically, we sequentially construct iteration-dependent reduced bases to account for the dependence of residual trajectories on the ROM-based preconditioners applied in preceding iterations. We also formulate SA-based kinetic corrections tailored to matrix-free transport sweeps in RTE solvers to achieve efficient online solves. Numerical experiments demonstrate superior efficiency over DSA and ROMSAD. For a parametric lattice problem, the proposed preconditioners lead to convergence within only average 3.4 transport sweeps online.

papers.title: Rates of convergence for extremal spacings in Kakutani's random interval-splitting process
papers.abstract: Kakutani's random interval-splitting process iteratively divides, via a uniformly random splitting point, the largest sub-interval in a partition of the unit interval. The length of the longest sub-interval after $n$ steps, suitably centred and scaled, is known to satisfy a central limit theorem as $n \to \infty$. We provide a quantitative (Berry-Esseen) upper bound for the finite-$n$ approximation in the central limit theorem, with conjecturally optimal rates in $n$. We also prove convergence to an exponential distribution for the length of the smallest sub-interval, with quantitative bounds. The Kakutani process can be embedded in certain branching and fragmentation processes, and we translate our results into that context also. Our proof uses conditioning on an intermediate time, a conditional independence structure for statistics involving small sub-intervals, an Hermite-Edgeworth expansion, and moments estimates with quantitative error bounds.

papers.title: On models of affine arithmetic
papers.abstract: By affine arithmetic is meant the set of affine consequences of Peano arithmetic. This is a continuous theory which is studied in the framework of affine logic, a sublogic of continuous logic. Affine arithmetic is undecidable. Also, its models are generally lattice ordered and carry a nontrivial metric. Classical models are then characterized as those which are linearly ordered. In this paper, the affine variants of several classical results in Peano arithmetic are proved. In particular, an affine form of Gaifman's splitting theorem is proved.

papers.title: Exploration of vertical self-resonant bifurcations from Distant Retrograde Orbits (DROs) in the Earth-Moon Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP)
papers.abstract: This paper investigates vertical self-resonant bifurcations from the Distant Retrograde Orbit (DRO) family in the Earth-Moon circular restricted three-body problem. Using a predictor-corrector continuation algorithm, we identify fourteen vertical-critical DROs consisting of twelve higher-order periods of multiplicity from integer multiples of five to ten and two vertical pitchfork bifurcations. Their continuation generates twenty-five families of spatial symmetric periodic orbits. Beyond the computation of new periodic orbit families, the main contribution of this work is a systematic characterization of the resulting global bifurcation topology through symplectic invariants. To this end, we combine Floquet multiplier transitions at local bifurcations with Conley-Zehnder indices, Krein signatures and the Euler characteristic of the local Floer homology to develop a computational symplectic framework that systematically classifies the bifurcated families and provides a topological interpretation of their numerically established connections. The computations reveal a global bifurcation network generated by the DRO family, including bridge families that connect the DROs with Butterfly, planar prograde and P3DRO families, together with several families consisting of long-period multi-excursion orbits that approach collision with the Moon. The computations also identify spatial periodic orbits satisfying Earth-Moon resonances along several bifurcated families.

papers.title: Statistical stability for systems semi-conjugate to pre-piecewise \textit{convex or expanding} maps with countably many branches
papers.abstract: We investigate the statistical stability of a class of dynamical systems semi-conjugate to pre-piecewise \textit{convex or expanding} maps with countably many branches. These systems naturally arise in the study of transformations with unbounded derivatives, discontinuities, or infinite Markov partitions; features that pose significant challenges for stability analysis. Specifically, we consider one-parameter families of transformations $\{F_δ\}_{δ\in [0,1)}$ and their corresponding invariant measures $\{μ_δ\}$. We provide general conditions ensuring that the unperturbed measure $μ_0$ is statistically stable, meaning the map $δ\mapsto μ_δ$ is continuous at $δ= 0$ in the appropriate topology. Furthermore, we establish explicit quantitative estimates for the modulus of continuity of $μ_δ$ in terms of the perturbation parameter $δ$. Our results apply to a broad class of maps, including those semi-conjugate to classical examples such as the Gauss and Lüroth maps.

papers.title: Pretty good state transfer in Grover walks on abelian Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study pretty good state transfer (PGST) between vertex states in Grover walks on graphs. Using Chebyshev polynomials, we obtain a spectral and number-theoretic characterization for the occurrence of PGST on general graphs and on Cayley graphs over finite abelian groups. This approach yields complete classifications of hypercubes, the prisms $K_m\square K_2$, and unitary Cayley graphs. In particular, the hypercube $Q_d$ exhibits PGST if and only if $d$ is odd, $d\equiv2\pmod4$, or $d\equiv8\pmod{16}$, extending the known result for only prime $d$ (Chan and Zhan~\cite{pgst1}). We show that the independent-set blow-up $G[\overline K_2]$ exhibits PGST if discriminant eigenvalues of $G$ are reciprocals of nonzero integers. Using techniques from algebraic number theory, we obtain several infinite families of graphs exhibiting PGST, including examples with rationally dependent spectral angles not covered by earlier constructions based on linear independence over $\mathbb Q$.

papers.title: Base-extension Semantics for Intuitionistic Predicate Logic
papers.abstract: Sandqvist's base-extension semantics explains the logical constants of intuitionistic propositional logic by inference in bases: collections of rules over atomic sentences that record the inferential content of a state of affairs. We extend it to intuitionistic predicate logic, first- and second-order, reading the quantifiers substitutionally, and prove natural deduction sound and complete. Two ideas carry the extension. First, a rule of a base may require a premiss to be established for a fresh name, one about which neither the assumptions nor the base say anything. With such rules, Sandqvist's completeness proof extends to first-order logic, whether validity is taken over all bases or over finite ones. Second, the second-order quantifier ranges over the atomic predicates, and validity is support in comprehensive bases, where every expressible condition has a definitional proxy. This yields intuitionistic Henkin second-order logic with full comprehension, not full second-order semantics.

papers.title: On integral and $p$-adic Bost-Connes systems
papers.abstract: Using Borger and de Smit's theory of periodic Witt vectors, we construct integral models of Bost-Connes systems for general number fields, generalizing Connes, Consani and Marcolli's construction over $\mathbb Q$. As an application, for totally real number fields other than $\mathbb Q$, we construct $p$-adic Bost-Connes systems whose $p$-adic KMS states are described in terms of Deligne-Ribet's theory of $p$-adic $L$-functions, extending the work of Connes and Consani for $\mathbb Q$.

papers.title: Mixed local and nonlocal laplacian without standard critical exponent for Lane-Emden equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate a mixed elliptic equation involving both local and nonlocal Laplacian operators, with a power-type nonlinearity. Specifically, we consider a Lane--Emden type equation of the form \[ -Δu + (-Δ)^s u = u^p\quad\text{ in }\R^n, \] where the operator combines the classical Laplacian and the fractional Laplacian, \(s\in(0,1)\). We first observe, by a variational argument that works for any finite sum of fractional Laplacians of different orders, that positive radial solutions exist in the whole range \(\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}<p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}\), while in star-shaped bounded domains the threshold for existence is the local Sobolev exponent \(\frac{n+2}{n-2}\). Hence, for a sum of two diffusion operators without zero-order term, the classical duality between the critical exponent in \(\R^n\) and the one in star-shaped domains fails. Our main results describe the solutions near both thresholds. For \(n\ge6\) (or \(n=5\) and \(s>\frac14\)) and \(p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}\) close to \(\frac{n+2}{n-2}\), we construct by a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction radial solutions which concentrate at the origin with the profile of the Aubin--Talenti bubble, at the explicit rate \(δ_\varepsilon^{2(1-s)}\sim\varepsilon=\frac{n+2}{n-2}-p\) dictated by the competition between the two diffusions. Dually, in every dimension \(n\ge3\) and for \(p>\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\) close to \(\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\), we construct radial solutions which bifurcate from the bubble of \((-Δ)^s\) and vanish by spreading out at the rate \(μ_η^{-2(1-s)}\simη=p-\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\). These results show that this mixed Lane--Emden equation does not admit a critical exponent in the traditional sense.

papers.title: Salvetti complexes for conditional oriented matroids
papers.abstract: We give a new proof of the fact that the complement of the complexification of a real hyperplane arrangement is homotopy equivalent to the Salvetti complex of the associated oriented matroid. Our proof involves no choices, is relatively easy to visualize, and generalizes to the setting of conditional oriented matroids.

papers.title: The Polyhedral Structure of Energy Storage Operations: Convex Hull and Valid Inequalities
papers.abstract: Energy storage models rely on complementarity constraints to prevent simultaneous charging and discharging, which turn them into disjunctive, nonconvex programs. Their linear relaxations, widely used in power system operation and planning, often violate these constraints. This paper studies the polyhedral structure of the multi-period operational set of a storage unit with conversion losses.
