In normalized units, $T_c=2+d_c\approx 2.43674$, where $d_c$ is determined by two transcendental equations. In particular, local controllability fails for $2<T\le T_c$, disproving Coron's conjecture that it holds exactly for $T>2$. For times just above $T_c$, we construct a control that cancels the linear and quadratic terms of the endpoint expansion and apply a fixed point argument. At $T_c$, a weighted comparison with a critical plane curve, combined with estimates along the nonlinear characteristics, gives the obstruction.

papers.title: Approximation numbers of Hankel Operators on Weighted Fock Spaces and the Berger--Coburn Phenomenon
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb{C}^n)$ be a real-valued weight whose real Hessian is uniformly positive definite and bounded. For $0<p<\infty$, $1\le q<\infty$, and possibly unbounded symbols $f$, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for prescribed decay of the approximation numbers of Hankel operators $H_f$ from weighted Fock spaces $F^p(\varphi)$ to weighted Lebesgue spaces $L^q(\varphi)$ in terms of the non-increasing rearrangement of the IDA function of $f$. We also characterize membership in the approximation ideals $\mathfrak A_s(F^p(\varphi),L^q(\varphi))$ and their weak counterparts $\mathfrak A_{s,\infty}(F^p(\varphi),L^q(\varphi))$ for $0<s<\infty$. The symbol criteria involve Lorentz, Lorentz--Zygmund, and Copson--Lorentz spaces. Our approach also yields the converse to the sufficient condition in [15], thereby completing the characterization of prescribed singular value decay for Hankel operators on a broad class of weighted Bergman spaces. For the pair $H_f$ and $H_{\bar f}$ on weighted Fock spaces, we characterize simultaneous decay of their approximation numbers and simultaneous membership in these ideals in terms of the mean oscillation function of $f$. For bounded symbols, we establish the Berger--Coburn phenomenon for both ideals in sharp exponent ranges. A new feature in the case $p<2<q$ is that the Berger--Coburn equivalence holds for $s_0(p,q)<s\le1$, where the sharp threshold $s_0(p,q)$ is strictly less than $1$.

papers.title: Precise Eigenvalue Asymptotics for Electrostatic Layer Potential Operators
papers.abstract: We investigate the eigenvalue asymptotics of electrostatic layer potential operators associated with the Laplace equation on smooth bounded domains in two and three dimensions. In two dimensions, we establish precise eigenvalue asymptotics for the single-layer potential operator, up to a remainder of order $O(j^{-\infty})$. In three dimensions, we obtain refined eigenvalue asymptotics for the single-layer potential operator on arbitrary smooth surfaces and for the Neumann--Poincaré operator on smooth surfaces with everywhere positive Gaussian curvature. Under suitable nonperiodicity assumptions on the associated Hamiltonian flows, the remainder estimates in three dimensions improve to $o(j^{-1})$.

papers.title: Algebraic Vector Fields on Compact Homogeneous Spaces are 2-generated
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact, connected manifold on which a compact Lie group $K$ acts smoothly and transitively. We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields on $M$, i.e., of smooth vector fields whose translates under $K$ span finite-dimensional spaces, is generated by two vector fields. Consequently, the subgroup generated by the flows of these two vector fields is dense in the identity component of the diffeomorphism group of $M$. For spheres, explicit generators are obtained from earlier results on spherical vector fields.

papers.title: Doing Well by Doing Good: Alignment of Revenue and Welfare in Robust Product Line Design through Data-Driven Optimization
papers.abstract: Product line design (PLD) selects product variants for a firm to maximize expected revenue. Candidate assortments are usually evaluated under random utility maximization (RUM), in which choice probabilities stem from the joint distribution of latent consumer utilities. As this utility distribution cannot be directly observed and is estimated from choice data, distributional uncertainty inevitably arises. This paper studies how to hedge PLD decisions against such ambiguity. We construct a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model that maximizes worst-case expected revenue over an l1-Wasserstein ball around a nominal utility distribution. We derive a dual reformulation for general nominal distributions and then specialize to two cases. With independent Gumbel utility shocks, the dual simplifies to a closed-form robust multinomial logit. We derive revenue gap bounds for parameters estimated from finite full-assortment choice data. When the true model structure is unknown beforehand, we adopt a data-driven scheme using the empirical distribution of sampled utility vectors and extend optimality-gap analysis to a general RUM oracle. For the NP-hard empirical problem, we propose Adaptive Parametric Search (APS), an algorithm with certified relative optimality guarantees. Numerical experiments show fast computation and better out-of-sample performance.Dual analysis shows that robustness to preference uncertainty endogenously encourages the firm to raise buyer welfare. This incentive takes distinct forms: robustness supports larger assortments in the unconstrained logit setting, whereas under the empirical nominal, it favors products with lower prices and higher utility relative to the outside option. Numerically, we identify a "doing well by doing good" effect: product lines with higher in-sample buyer welfare attain higher out-of-sample revenue and buyer welfare.

papers.title: Global existence and emergent dynamics of singular Cucker-Smale model on general digraphs
papers.abstract: We investigate the global-in-time dynamics of the Cucker--Smale model under general network topologies with a singular communication weight function $ψ(r) = r^{-α}$, $α>0$. For $α\ge 1$, we establish the global-in-time existence of smooth solutions when network topologies belong to one of several classes of directed graphs. In particular, in one dimension, we present a necessary condition on the network topology for global existence by constructing finite-time blow-up solutions from non-collisional initial configurations. Moreover, we provide a sufficient framework for the emergence of mono-cluster flocking. For certain classes of network topologies, we further show that mono-cluster flocking occurs unconditionally for non-collisional initial configuration when $α=1$.

papers.title: OCP: a greedy projection method for row-sparse representations of minimum-norm solutions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a greedy projection method, termed orthogonal constraint pursuit (OCP), for identifying a small set of rows of a consistent linear system $Ax=b$ whose span contains the minimum-norm solution $x^*$, along with the coefficients of that representation. The method successively activates the most violated constraint, and then projects the iterate onto the intersection of all activated constraints. We prove that OCP is equivalent to OMP applied to the dictionary $A^T$ and the signal $x^*$, and that it terminates in at most rank(A) iterations. When $x^*$ is a linear combination of $s$ rows of a matrix whose rows are independent and uniformly distributed on the unit sphere, OCP identifies those rows in exactly $s$ iterations with probability $1-O(m^{-1})$, provided that $n\ge Cs\ln m$ for a sufficiently large constant $C$. We also derive a variant of OCP with constraint removal for hard-margin support vector machines with regularized bias, which returns the support vectors, along with the multipliers that satisfy the KKT conditions. Numerical results on both real and synthetic problems demonstrate the identification of representing rows and the regime in which it is competitive with Krylov subspace methods.

papers.title: $H_2$-optimal riblet profiles for turbulence suppression in channel flows
papers.abstract: The drag-reducing properties of streamwise-elongated surface corrugations, commonly referred to as riblets, have been extensively studied through experiments, simulations, and reduced-order modeling. Notably, the linearized Navier-Stokes framework introduced by Ran, Zare, and Jovanovic (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 906, 2021) employs volume penalization to model riblet-induced boundary conditions and predict drag reduction. These approaches typically quantify drag reduction as a function of a single geometric parameter, such as spanwise spacing or groove cross-sectional area, evaluated over fixed riblet shapes. As a result, identifying optimal riblet geometries across a broader design space often necessitates exhaustive parametric studies. To address this problem, we propose an optimization framework for the systematic design of optimal riblet shapes. Accordingly, we reformulate the volume penalization term in the linearized dynamics as a structured state-feedback operator. Targeting maximal suppression of turbulence, we pose a composite optimization problem that minimizes the steady-state variance of velocity fluctuations and riblet-induced dynamical augmentations while maintaining a constant bulk-flux. For a fixed spanwise wavelength (riblet spacing), this framework yields optimal wall-normal profiles that achieve maximal turbulence attenuation.

papers.title: $L^p$-norms of holomorphic cusp forms
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal orders of local and global $L^p$-norms of $L^2$-normalized holomorphic cusp forms of large weight on the modular surface, for fixed $2<p\leq\infty$. Both orders are attained by peak forms. For normalized Poincaré series of weight $k$ and index $m$, we obtain an asymptotic formula with an explicit constant, uniformly for $1\leq m\leq c_0k$ with any fixed $c_0<(4π)^{-1}$. We also give sup norm bounds in a wider range of indices.

papers.title: An Explicit Parallelizable Robin-Robin Splitting Scheme for Navier-Stokes-Naghdi Shell Interaction
papers.abstract: We develop a novel explicit Robin-Robin splitting scheme for the system of an incompressible viscous fluid coupled to a time dependent Naghdi shell model. The shell model includes three displacement components and three independent rotation components, accounting for membrane, bending, and transverse-shear deformations. Both Robin conditions depend only on interface data from the previous time step, allowing the fluid and shell subproblems to be solved independently without coupling subiterations. For the fixed-domain Stokes-Naghdi problem, we derive a discrete energy identity that incorporates shell rotational inertia, interface velocities, and interface loads. We prove that the scheme is unconditionally stable for any fixed positive common Robin coefficient under homogeneous external data. Under suitable regularity and initialization assumptions, we establish first-order consistency and an $O(\sqrt{Δt})$ temporal error bound in the mechanical energy norm. Numerical experiments with a moving-domain pressure pulse compare the proposed scheme with the kinematically coupled $β$-scheme and a monolithic solver. To demonstrate its applicability to a more realistic vascular configuration, we simulate a stented artery using a bonded layered shell with stiff strut bands, capturing spatial variations in the arterial wall response.

papers.title: The Nygaard graded piece, the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and regularity criteria
papers.abstract: For a $p$-torsionfree $p$-quasisyntomic ring, we construct a fiber sequence relating the $p$-th Nygaard graded piece of absolute prismatic cohomology to the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex. The latter is an arithmetic analogue of the cotangent complex in which the differential of $p$ need not vanish. We also clarify the relationship between the regularity criterion proved by Mao using the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and the regularity criterion established by Bhatt and Mathew using the Nygaard graded piece. This relationship was anticipated by Bhatt and Mathew.

papers.title: On continuous unitriangular matrices on \(\mathbb R^2\)
papers.abstract: Let \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)\) be the group of complex \(2\times 2\)-matrices with determinant \(1\). We prove that each continuous map \(A:\R^2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)\) can be written in the form \[A=\begin{pmatrix}1&f_1\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\f_2&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&f_3\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\f_4&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&f_5\\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \] where \(f_1,\ldots,f_5:\R^2\to\C\) are continuous functions.

papers.title: More lower bounds for Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers
papers.abstract: We give explicit colourings improving the comparison lower bounds assembled here for several Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers. The main algebraic tool generalises Rabung's power-residue colouring from arithmetic progressions to arbitrary sets. If every translate of a t-element set S in F_p meets at least two classes of the r-th power character, and the integer weights have both parities, then a period-2p one-weight colouring of [t]^p has no monochromatic combinatorial line. The 19 displayed algebraic certificates comprise 18 improvements and one closed-form reproduction; they include HJ(4,3)>=164, HJ(5,4)>=7418, and HJ(5,6)>=34034. The underlying period-p construction also proves kappa_ow(t,r)>=p-1 for the one-weight bracket ceiling, in particular kappa_ow(5,4)>=7416 and kappa_ow(5,6)>=34032. Warm breakout-weighted tabu search on the type simplex gives HJ(3,4)>=51. Whole-colouring local search gives W(8,3)>522, W(11,3)>1193, and W(17,3)>3620. All accepted certificates are available separately and are checked by direct enumeration; unresolved searches are reported as UNKNOWN, not UNSAT.

papers.title: Flocking Time and Graph Volume in Nonlinear Cucker-Smale Models with Dynamic Networks
papers.abstract: This study proposes a Cucker-Smale model incorporating dynamic networks and the discrete $p$-Laplacian ($p \in (1,2)$) and analyzes the relationship between flocking time constraints and graph connectivity from both theoretical and experimental perspectives. We establish that this model achieves flocking within finite time and derive a quantitative relationship between the lower bound of flocking time and graph volume. Based on these results, we observe that imposing sufficiently small flocking time induces an increase in network volume, and that larger initial velocity variance requires greater volume under the same time constraint. In our experiments, we trained a transformer-based PPO policy to select network structures at each time step. Under the most stringent time constraint, the maximum average number of connections increased sharply, confirming a threshold effect. The negative correlation between convergence time and average number of connections reflects the theoretical results well. This study provides quantitative evidence for the phenomenon that time constraints induce connection mobilization.

papers.title: Training Neural Networks to be Locally Adaptive
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks fitted by global empirical risk minimization commit to a single model for the entire covariate space. In a regression problem, if the regression function $f_0$ is inhomogeneous --- varying rapidly in one region, while being nearly flat in another --- no single model can be appropriate everywhere, and the fit degrades where the function varies most rapidly. Here we study an alternative in which, instead of fitting the network globally, we fit it locally. For each query point $x$, a \emph{local neural network} is trained on the $k$ nearest-neighbours of $x$ alone, making the training sample and the fitted function query-dependent. We analyze the performance of the resulting estimator through a localization approach, establishing that the pointwise risk of the estimator with an appropriate choice of $k$ attains the rate $n^{-2α/(2α+d^{*})}$, up to logarithmic factors, when $f_0$ is locally $α$-Hölder with $α\in(0,1]$ and the covariates are supported on a $d^{*}$-dimensional manifold embedded in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. A matching Le Cam lower bound shows that this rate is pointwise minimax optimal. However, the local rate-optimality requires $k$ to be calibrated to the smoothness of $f_0$, which is unknown in practice. We therefore provide a locally adaptive choice of $k$ that makes the neural network adapt to the local Hölder exponent of $f_0$ and to the intrinsic dimension simultaneously, both of which are potentially varying over the covariate domain. An extensive simulation study demonstrates the dominance of the locally adaptive neural network over a globally trained network and several state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Grid-Responsive Pricing of Dynamic Wireless Charging with Coupled Residential Demand
papers.abstract: Dynamic wireless charging (DWC) is an emerging technology that enables electric vehicles (EVs) to recharge while traveling. Its unique operational model creates two revenue streams for DWC operators through lane access tolls and electricity sales. However, these prices influence not only traffic flow and roadway energy delivery but also how much EV charging moves to homes instead, potentially within the same distribution network. Neglecting this coupling can underestimate grid loading and compromise pricing decisions. We develop a coupled traffic, EV energy, driver-response, and AC distribution network model with a model predictive control (MPC) framework that jointly optimizes DWC tolls and charging prices while explicitly accounting for displaced residential charging and network losses. Using 78 days of I-210 West traffic data, we show that conventional MPC exceeds feeder loading limits on 52 days, whereas the proposed residential load aware controller eliminates these violations with only 0.6% lower operator revenue. Under a more constrained feeder configuration, it eliminates 50 overloaded days with a 0.9% revenue reduction. Sensitivity analyses highlight the importance of accurate residential demand estimation and feeder loss modeling, while peak-aware pricing further reduces daily peak loading by 3.7% relative to the base load. These results demonstrate the value of coordinated pricing that captures the interaction between roadway and residential charging.

papers.title: On Threshold Probabilities for the Stability of the Independence Number of a Random Subgraph
papers.abstract: For an arbitrary sequence of graphs $G_n$, we consider a random spanning subgraph $G_{n,p}$ in which each edge of the graph $G_n$ survives independently of the others with probability $p$. We obtain a general upper bound for the independence number $α(G_{n,p})$, from which, for an arbitrary probability $p=p(n)$, we derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability, i.e., for the equality $α(G_{n,p})=(1+o(1))α(G_n)$ asymptotically almost surely, as well as upper bounds for the independence number of the random subgraph, including unconditional ones; for $p=1/2$ they recover A. M. Raigorodskii's results of 2017 and 2026. Under additional conditions on the structure of the independent sets of the graph $G_n$, we find, up to a constant factor, the threshold probabilities for both asymptotic and exact stability (the equality $α(G_{n,p})=α(G_n)$). Special cases include results on the graphs $G(n,r,<s)$ for growing $r$ and $s$, including Kneser graphs for growing $r$; we also give examples of complete multipartite graphs, graphs on the blocks of Steiner systems, and $q$-analogues of Kneser graphs.

papers.title: On Contractibility of Geometric Joins
papers.abstract: The geometric join of a family of sets in $\mathbb R^d$ is the union of the convex hulls of all colorful sets. For every $d \geq 4$, we construct $\lceil\frac{(d-1)^2}{2}\rceil$ sets in $\mathbb R^d$ whose geometric join is not contractible, disproving the conjecture of Bárány, Holmsen, and Karasev that the geometric join of at least $d+1$ sets is contractible.

papers.title: Decision Stability and Model Reduction for Hamilton--Jacobi Navigation in Multiscale Flows
papers.abstract: Autonomous vehicles plan time-optimal routes through flow fields that are known only through reduced, finite-resolution models of an underlying multiscale flow. Classical Hamilton-Jacobi homogenization concerns convergence of the value function as the fine scale vanishes; but what a vehicle commits to is a route, and value accuracy need not imply route accuracy. We study this gap for a fixed-resolution reduction rather than in the homogenization limit. The committed route's dependence on the model-reduction error splits into two regimes. When the optimal route is a unique, nondegenerate minimizer with a regular value-function neighborhood, it depends Lipschitz-continuously on the reduction error, while the extra travel time from acting on the reduced model grows only quadratically with that error. When two routes are tied on the cut locus of the value function, the value remains stable, but an arbitrarily small change in the flow can switch the selected route, making route selection discontinuous in the reduction error. This dichotomy identifies where a reduced model must be accurate: not where the flow error is largest, but where the route choice is fragile. In the regular regime it yields a resolution-allocation principle, while an oracle marginal-regret benchmark illustrates the potential benefit of decision-aware resolution allocation relative to refinement based on flow-error magnitude.

papers.title: A Brownian web invariance principle: Localized disturbance flows and Hastings-Levitov(0)
papers.abstract: We establish a Brownian web invariance principle for localized disturbance flows, providing a criterion that strengthens the weak-flow convergence of [Norris--Turner 2015, Ann. Probab. 43, 935--970] to path-Hausdorff convergence of their full trajectory collections. We apply this approach to the radial, stationary, and cylindrical versions of the Hastings--Levitov$(0)$ aggregation model, proving path-Hausdorff convergence of the full harmonic measure path collections to the (Cylindrical) Brownian web, together with joint convergence of the full gap--finger collections to geometric embeddings of the corresponding double Brownian webs. This extends the radial HL$(0)$ small-particle limits of [Norris--Turner 2012, Commun. Math. Phys. 316, 809--841] for the harmonic measure flow and finite gap--finger collections. In the radial and cylindrical HL$(0)$, we also show that the rescaled one-arm domination time converges to a multiple of the global coalescence time of coalescing Brownian motion on $\mathbb T$, with convergence of expectations. The main new ingredient is a three-point survival estimate, proved via a multiscale stopping-time decomposition.

papers.title: Morse resolutions and applications to lcm powers
papers.abstract: We consider the $r$-th lcm power $I^{\{r\}}$ of a monomial ideal $I$, defined to be generated by the least common multiples of all $r$-element subsets of the set of minimal monomial generators of $I$. Some homological invariants of these ideals are studied. Specifically, we use discrete Morse theory to give sharp upper bounds for the projective dimension and total Betti numbers of these ideals. Moreover, we completely determine the extent to which lcm powers define the homological shift ideals of edge ideals. Finally, we study when the minimal resolution of some ordinary powers and lcm powers are supported on the same CW-complex.

papers.title: Extremal metrics for the $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalues
papers.abstract: We study the $G$-invariant Steklov spectrum of compact connected Riemannian manifolds with boundary, endowed with an effective isometric action of a compact Lie group $G$. Under a mild nontransitivity assumption on the boundary action, we establish that this spectrum consists of an infinite sequence of eigenvalues diverging to infinity. We then investigate extremal metrics for the normalised $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue functionals. Assuming that $\dim G \geq 1$, we prove that none of these functionals admits an extremal $G$-invariant metric. Moreover, when $\dim M \geq 3$, the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue is unbounded above even within a fixed $G$-invariant conformal class. The proof relies on a local model near a boundary orbit and spectral convergence under conformal collapse. Finally, in contrast with the upper bounds obtained by Colbois, Dryden and El Soufi for invariant Laplace eigenvalues of embedded spheres of revolution, we construct, for any $n \geq 3$, a sequence of smooth Euclidean domains of revolution in $\mathbb R^n$, all diffeomorphic to the ball, along which the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue blows up.

papers.title: On the uniqueness of ground states for pseudo-relativistic boson stars
papers.abstract: We establish the uniqueness of both action and energy ground states for the pseudo-relativistic Hartree equation. The latter, for every prescribed mass below the critical stellar mass, proves the Lieb-Yau conjecture. Our approach establishes radial nondegeneracy and a strict monotonicity property of the mass-frequency relation, providing a unified framework for proving uniqueness in both variational settings.

papers.title: Cyclic group actions on K3 surfaces and almost complex structures
papers.abstract: Fintushel, Stern and Sunukjian constructed exotic $\mathbb{Z}_n$-actions on $K3$ for $n=2,3,4$ using twist-rim surgery. We prove that these exotic actions do not preserve any Ricci flat metric or any integrable complex structure. This answers a question of Farb and Looijenga in the negative. In contrast, we prove that any smooth $\mathbb{Z}_n$-action on $K3$ for which the fixed point set has only non-isolated fixed points preserves an almost complex structure with trivial first Chern class. In particular, this applies to the Fintushel-Stern-Sunukjian examples. Lastly, we classify the possible fixed point data and action on cohomology for cyclic group actions on $K3$ of prime order which preserve an almost complex structure with trivial first Chern class.

papers.title: B-Series Theory for Continuous Time Integration Methods
papers.abstract: B-Series are a common tool for constructing numerical integration methods and partitioned variations. In this paper, we expand the operations of B-Series to describe the formal expansion of modified differential equations found in multirate ODE solvers. Typically, such modified differential equations have time dependent approximations using summed fixed constant states. To create the B-Series we introduce a new operation called replacement to induce the constant states and add a time parameterization to the labels of the B-Series. By doing so we introduce new analysis via the permanent and block matrices which provide alternative formulations to composition and substitution. To support the time dependent labels properties are provided, the exact solution is described in Tree Iterated Integrals, and the underlying approximate representations are analyzed.

papers.title: The topology of the mean action spectrum
papers.abstract: We prove that if an area-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed two-disk is neither a pseudo-rotation nor a periodic map, then the closure of its mean action spectrum contains an interval of positive length. This partially answers a question of Hutchings. We do not require any additional assumptions on the area-preserving map, such as non-degeneracy or specific behavior near the boundary.

papers.title: Continuous improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for Gaussian random vectors
papers.abstract: We establish continuous versions of the improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for correlated Gaussian random vectors, where a finite covariance matrix is replaced by a covariance operator acting on a Hilbert space of parameter fields. Under operator comparisons between the covariance and the exponent multiplier, we prove both inequalities and characterize equality in terms of a compatible probability density on the underlying Gaussian space. We further describe this density as a product of independent factors on common eigenspaces and a Gaussian factor whose mean and covariance satisfy explicit algebraic conditions. In the reverse setting, positive and negative exponents may coexist. The continuous product is defined by ordered truncation, allowing zeros in the positive-exponent factors. The equality proof combines an exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup comparison, a spectral gap away from the kernel of the governing operator difference, and characteristic-function deconvolution. We also treat exponential quadratic functions without requiring a uniform positive-definiteness margin on the precision matrices.

papers.title: Finite sample guarantees of MPPI: suboptimality, sample complexity and closed-loop guarantees
papers.abstract: This paper considers model predictive path integral (MPPI) control for nonlinear finite-horizon optimal control problems with bounded inputs, allowing nonconvex and nonsmooth costs. We prove theoretical guarantees that quantify the suboptimality caused by positive temperature and finite sampling on MPPI and establish their implications for closed-loop guarantees. Specifically, we derive a suboptimality bound for infinite-sample MPPI that characterizes the effects of temperature and prior coverage, followed by a high-probability finite-sample approximation error bound that reveals the dependence on sample size, temperature, and cost variability. By incorporating these bounds into a terminal-constraint-free MPC framework, we further establish semi-global practical recurrence of the closed-loop system. Numerical examples involving a four-link planar manipulator illustrate the temperature-sampling tradeoff and the influence of prior quality on approximation accuracy and closed-loop performance.

papers.title: $\mathrm{BMOA}$ and Carleson-homogeneous Denjoy domains
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be a proper closed subset of the extended real line that contains $[-\infty,-1]\cup[1,+\infty]$, and let $F$ be a universal covering of the Denjoy domain $Ω=\overline{\mathbb C}\setminus E$. We prove the conjecture of Huo and Zinsmeister that $E$ is Carleson-homogeneous if $\log F'\in\mathrm{BMOA}(\mathbb D)$. The proof is based on an estimate for the length of $F^{-1}(\mathbb R)$ in terms of the Bloch seminorm of $\log F'$ and a weighted $L^2$ integral of $F''/F'$. From this estimate we deduce that $Ω$ has the Hayman-Wu property, and Carleson-homogeneity then follows from a theorem of Fernández. We also characterize these domains by Carleson measure conditions for the arclength on $F^{-1}(\mathbb R)$ and for the Schwarzian derivative of $F$, and by the $H^\infty$ interpolation property of the inverse images of suitable sequences in ${\mathbb R}\setminus E$.

papers.title: Heat-wave semigroup estimates and the compressible Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: We study the connection between the heat-wave semigroup and the compressible Navier-Stokes (CNS) equations. On one hand, the parabolic-hyperbolic nature of the CNS motivated the study of space-time estimates for the heat-wave semigroup by using recent harmonic analysis development, in particular, the local smoothing estimates for the wave equations; on the other hand, we apply the new estimates to obtain global well-posedness for CNS in the optimal critical Besov spaces. For the latter purpose, we introduce a new iteration framework for CNS that exploits some intrinsic structures of the equations, so that we can successfully apply these estimates.

papers.title: Three Circles in a Unit Disk: Three Solutions to an Extremal Problem
papers.abstract: We place two disks inside the unit disk so that they touch each other and the unit circle. We then insert a disk of the largest possible radius, requiring it to touch both original disks. We show that the smallest possible sum of the three areas is $11π/18$, and find all equality cases. We give three solutions, using Descartes' circle theorem, inversion, and contact-point coordinates. The main difficulty is checking that the third disk is largest among all disks that fit, not only among disks touching the first two.

papers.title: Weak error estimates of a spectral Galerkin approximation to the stochastic Burgers equation driven by rough white noise
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate weak error estimates for a spectral Galerkin approximation to a stochastic Burgers equation driven by rough space-time white noise. The roughness of the driving noise results that the mild solution possesses only $L^\infty$-regularity rather than any positive-order differentiability order regularity. The theory of classical numerical analysis reveals that the convergence rate of numerical solution is determined by the smoothness of the exact solution, and hence $L^\infty$-regularity is insufficient to yield any positive convergence rate. Indeed, De Vecchi et al.\ \cite{DeVecchi2026} studied a spectral Galerkin approximation to such equation and only proved pathwise convergence. However, we aim to derive positive weak convergence rate for the spectral Galerkin approximation, which is determined by the roughness order of noise. To overcome the difficulty caused by the absence of smoothness of the exact solution, we turn to study the differentiability regularity of the first and second order Fréchet derivatives of the solution to a Kolmogorov equation associated with the spectral Galerkin approximation. We manage to prove that they possess nearly second order smoothness, enabling us to derive a positive weak convergence rate for the spectral Galerkin approximation. Finally, we conduct a numerical experiment to illustrate the theortical analysis.

papers.title: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

papers.title: Real-Rootedness and Log-Concavity of Zigzag Eulerian Polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that the zigzag Eulerian polynomials have only real, negative, simple zeros, and hence strictly log-concave coefficients, settling the first two parts of a conjecture of Petersen and Zhuang. Real-rootedness in combinatorics is usually proved inside a single algebraic framework, such as interlacing or stability. Our proof rests on a different premise: different parts of a zero set become visible in different representations of the same polynomial, and classical tools suffice once each part is viewed in the right one. The bridge between representations is a local rule. Forgetting the order in which a bounded-jump path visits positions leaves only a nearest-neighbor condition on sorted gaps, which makes an encoding via a transfer matrix much simpler to see. From there the argument passes to complex analysis. The sizes of the matrix's eigenmodes locate the zeros at the two ends of the negative axis, through Rouché's theorem. In a logarithmic coordinate the generating function becomes a combination of derivatives of the hyperbolic secant, akin to the classical derivative polynomials, and the arguments of its nearest poles produce a sine that fixes the signs between consecutive central zeros. The zeros are thus read off from the poles of an associated kernel. More broadly, the proof suggests that combinatorial polynomials defined by local constraints carry analytic structure, in their spectra and in the poles of their kernels, that is complementary to the usual algebraic methods and that classical complex analysis can exploit directly.

papers.title: Uniqueness of tangent flows in mean curvature flow (I): smooth minimal cone
papers.abstract: We prove uniqueness of multiplicity-one minimal-cone tangent flows in mean curvature flow when the cone has a smooth embedded two-sided link and satisfies strict Hardy stability, radial Gaussian nonresonance, and weighted stationary rigidity. We also establish a discrete Lojasiewicz inequality, polynomial convergence rates, and rigidity among smooth self-shrinkers. In particular, these conclusions hold for all Simons cones $\mathcal C_{p,q}$ with $p,q \geq 1, p+q\geq 6$.

papers.title: Directed triangles in oriented graphs without a directed cycle of length $3t$
papers.abstract: For integers $k,\ell\ge 3$, let $\operatorname{ex}(n,\Cdir_k,\Cdir_\ell)$ denote the maximum number of directed cycles of length $k$ in an $n$-vertex oriented graph containing no directed cycles of length $\ell$. Grzesik, Jaworska, Kielak, Kuc and Ślusarczyk~\cite{GJ} systematically studied the generalized Turán problem for directed cycles and conjectured that, for every fixed integer $t\ge 2$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,\Cdir_3,\Cdir_{3t})=\frac{t-1}{4}n^2+o(n^2)$. They proved this asymptotic formula for $t=2$. In this paper, we prove it for every fixed integer $t\ge 3$, thereby confirming the conjecture.

papers.title: Differentiable High-Order Mesh $r$-Adaptivity
papers.abstract: High-order mesh r-adaptivity typically entails minimizing a nonlinear functional using its gradients and, for Newton-based methods, its Hessian. These derivatives can be expensive to derive, must be updated with any changes to the functional, and errors in the derivatives directly impact the convergence of r-adaptivity. Additionally, derivatives of the r-adaptivity operator are required for consistent sensitivity analysis for inverse problems. This work develops a framework for differentiable r-adaptivity based on the Target-Matrix Optimization Paradigm. Given a pointwise functional defining the local mesh-adaptation objective, the proposed framework uses $\partial$FEM to automatically generate pointwise first- and second-order derivatives. These local derivatives are then assembled into a global gradient vector and a Hessian operator through the finite element operator decomposition. The derivative kernels support portable CPU and GPU execution, with partial assembly and tensor sum factorization enabling matrix-free application of the Hessian operator. The framework also provides consistent sensitivities of the r-adaptivity operator through automatically generated mixed derivatives and implicit differentiation of the mesh stationarity equations. Numerical experiments show GPU solve times comparable to those of hand-derived TMOP implementations on a benchmark problem, improvement in r-adaptivity convergence due to accurate computation of the derivatives, and demonstrate the use of mesh sensitivities for material-interface identification in an inverse heat-conduction problem.

papers.title: A counterexample to the one-supremum conjecture and sharp logarithmic weighted bounds for Calderón--Zygmund operators
papers.abstract: We give a negative answer to the one-supremum conjecture of Hytönen and Lacey~\cite[Remark~1.3]{HL}, in the strong-type form stated by Lerner and Moen~\cite[Conjecture~1.3, formula~(9)]{LM}. The conjecture asks whether the mixed $A_p$--$A_\infty$ characteristics $K_p(w)$ and $K_{p'}(σ)$, with both factors evaluated on the same cube, control Calderón--Zygmund operators without a logarithmic loss. For every $1<p<\infty$, we construct explicit weights for which $K_p(w)+K_{p'}(σ)\eqsim_p m$, but one fixed Hilbert transform has weighted norm at least $m(1+\log m)^{γ_p}$, where $γ_p=\max\{1/p,1/p'\}$. Thus the proposed bound fails even for a fixed singular integral. The counterexample also extends to a fixed Riesz transform in each dimension $n\ge2$. We further establish a logarithmically corrected bound for Calderón--Zygmund operators, with powers $1/p'$ and $1/p$ on the respective one-supremum terms. Together, the lower and upper bounds identify $γ_p$ as the optimal common logarithmic exponent and give the sharp worst-case growth $(1+\log A)^{γ_p}$ under the constraint $[w]_{A_p}\le A$. The results show why information from any one cube cannot fully capture the accumulation of a singular integral across many scales.

papers.title: COSI: A Framework for Robustly Valid Inference
papers.abstract: We introduce COSI (COnfidence from Scale Invariance), a framework for constructing confidence sets for statistical functionals. COSI builds on the HulC (Hull-based Confidence), which uses median unbiasedness to construct confidence sets from batch estimates. COSI uses scale-invariance properties shared by many common estimators. We divide the data into batches, compute an estimate in each batch, and retain each candidate parameter value for which the batch estimates pass a test of scale invariance. The resulting confidence sets are asymptotically valid under weaker assumptions than classical Wald and bootstrap procedures require, and their coverage can be closer to the nominal level in small samples. Applications include robust inference for the mean, regression coefficients in misspecified linear models, tensor norms, and Fréchet means.

papers.title: On the Morse index of some Riemannian homogeneous fibrations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use the technique developed by the first named author in arXiv:2610.07815 to compute the Morse-index of some Riemannian homogeneous fibrations. For the quaternionic (resp. octonionic) Hopf fibration, we compute the index and nullity, where the metric on the $\mathbb{S}^7$ (resp. $\mathbb{S}^{15}$) is the quaternionic (resp. octonionic) Hopf--Berger metric. In particular, for the round metric on the domain, the Morse-index is $45$ (resp. $153$). We also give a spectral formula for the Aloff--Wallach projections. In particular, we obtain that the Konishi $\mathbb{R} P^3$-fibration $N_{1,1}\to\mathbb{C} P^2$ is stable throughout the two-parameter metric family, while the unit tangent sphere bundle $T^1(\mathbb{C} P^2)\to \mathbb{C} P^2$ is stable under some conditions on the metric. We also compute the index and nullity of the Clifford hypersurface in the fiber-squashing range of the quaternionic Berger family. Finally, for the identity map on the quaternionic Hopf--Berger spheres, we determine its Morse--index by an explicit sequence of transition parameters.

papers.title: Toroidal Obstructions with No K_5 Minor
papers.abstract: Finding the complete set of forbidden minors for the torus remains an open problem. We determine the complete list of toroidal minor obstructions with no $K_5$ minor and prove that there are exactly $74$, each with between $10$ and $14$ vertices. Combined with the known classification of toroidal obstructions with no $K_{3,3}$ minor, this determines every toroidal obstruction that excludes one of the forbidden minors for planarity. The proof uses three-vertex cuts to show that, apart from $K_{3,7}$, every three-connected obstruction in this class has two distinct independent triples, each the common neighborhood of at least two degree-three vertices. The classification proceeds by considering the possible intersections of these triples and reduces each case by planarity tests and enumeration of the possible graph forms. From the $74$ minor obstructions we also obtain a complete list of $381$ topological obstructions for the torus with no $K_5$ minor.

papers.title: Enumerating orbits of finite classical groups on their Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We enumerate the orbits of a finite classical group in the adjoint action on its Lie algebra, giving exact generating functions and very good upper bounds. We treat the general linear, unitary, symplectic and orthogonal groups, in both odd and even characteristic. In even characteristic, we get very nice formulas for the number of orbits on nilpotent classes both in the finite and algebraically closed case. We discuss the connection with commuting varieties.

papers.title: Residual-driven lattice Boltzmann equation. Part I: framework and nonlinear solution methods
papers.abstract: We developed a residual-driven framework of the lattice Boltzmann equation (LBE) to integrate general nonlinear iterative methods. The nonlinear residual is constructed directly from the complete LBE collision-streaming update, allowing general nonlinear solvers to be integrated without modifying the original LBE algorithmic structure, i.e., the kernel consisting of collision-streaming, boundary conditions, and various forcing and interaction effects. Sophisticated techniques, such as weighted fixed-point iteration, full approximation scheme (FAS) multigrid, and Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov methods are integrated into the LBE via this framework, and preconditioned LBE is further incorporated as a nonlinear smoother to demonstrate solver composability. Numerical tests validate that FAS and Newton methods do converge to the same discrete steady fixed-point obtained with the primitive LBE iteration. For the 2D lid-driven cavity flow, the FAS scheme reduces the measured solution time by a factor of approximately 44 at Re = 1000 and more than 224 at Re = 5000. Accurate results are also obtained for the steady flows past a cylinder at Re = 20 and the NACA0012 airfoil at Re = 1000. The low Mach-number tests for the flow past a NACA0012 airfoil further show that both the FAS scheme and preconditioning can not only substantially reduce the work required to reach steady solutions, but also mitigate the zero Mach-number crisis.

papers.title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
papers.abstract: We develop neural network methods for the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations at a small viscosity $\varepsilon > 0$, whose accuracy is uniform in $\varepsilon$ and whose residual is evaluated on a grid that does not resolve the vorticity boundary layer. In the vorticity-stream function formulation with the slip boundary conditions, a vorticity layer of width $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ forms along the walls. The trial function of the singular layer Physics-Informed Neural Network (sl-PINN) contains the corrector of the asymptotic analysis, together with the law that fixes its amplitude at the wall. The amplitude is tied to the wall trace of the network itself, so that the method requires no a priori knowledge of the limit solution. The sl-PINN keeps the error uniform in $\varepsilon$ over six decades, for the Stokes and the Navier-Stokes equations alike, although in the latter the wall trace travels with the flow and is not known in advance. An enrichment that uses the thin scale but leaves the profile and the amplitude of the layer free deteriorates as $\varepsilon\to0$. Since the corrector carries the layer analytically, the Laplacian in the residual can be discretized by a finite volume flux difference on a coarse grid. The resulting singular layer Finite Volume Neural Network (sl-FVNN) attains the same uniform accuracy as the sl-PINN, to within the scatter of the random seed, at about half the cost of a training step. The combination of the asymptotic corrector with the coarse-grid finite volume discretization is the main result of this article.

papers.title: Gradient estimates and monotonicity formulae for the $p$-filtration equation on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We derive Li--Yau type estimates on closed Riemannian manifolds and local Hamilton-type gradient estimates on complete manifolds for the $p$-filtration equation $u_t=Δ_pF(u)$. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and a structural condition on $F$, we establish a $\mathcal W$-entropy formula, entropy-power concavity and local entropy rigidity. We also prove a parabolic frequency monotonicity formula without curvature assumptions. The results include homogeneous doubly nonlinear diffusion and extend to nonhomogeneous power sums and the arctangent law.

papers.title: Finite volume neural networks for singularly perturbed boundary value problems
papers.abstract: We develop a singular-layer enhanced Finite Volume Neural Network (sl-FVNN) methodology for solving singularly perturbed boundary value problems. The proposed framework combines flux-conserving finite volume residuals with analytically derived boundary layer correctors, enabling stable and efficient approximation of sharp boundary variations induced by small perturbation parameters. Numerical experiments over a broad range of small perturbation parameters ($10^{-4}$ to $10^{-12}$), demonstrate that the sl-FVNN yields uniformly accurate predicted solutions and significantly improved convergence behavior compared to conventional FVNN methods. Further comparisons with sl-PINNs from (Gie, Hong, Jung, Appl. Anal. 2024) show that our sl-FVNNs attain comparable accuracy for reaction--diffusion and Burgers equations, while achieving significantly improved convergence for convection-dominated nonlinear problems. These results highlight the effectiveness of incorporating asymptotic layer structures into finite volume based neural networks, offering a practical and scalable framework for multiscale PDE learning in stiff regimes.

papers.title: A nonlinear multigrid method for the preconditioned lattice Boltzmann equation
papers.abstract: This work developed a preconditioned lattice Boltzmann equation (PLBE) smoother for the residual-driven full approximation scheme (FAS) multigrid to accelerate steady-state LBE calculations. To overcome the deterioration of LBE smoothing at low viscosity, we used a two- relaxation-time (TRT) collision model together with characteristic-velocity and kinetic precondition- ing to keep the relaxation frequency for the even-order moments within a favorable range, while independently selecting the relaxation frequency for the odd-order moments to reduce their local amplification factor. We further investigated F-, W-, and hybrid V/W-cycles to address residual stagnation observed with V-cycles at high Reynolds numbers. The 2D lid-driven cavity flow was used as a test case. At Re = 5000, TRT-PLBE-FAS achieves an approximately 27-fold speedup over single-grid TRT-PLBE. At Re = 20000 on a 20482 grid, the hybrid V/W-cycle reduces solution time by 14% compared with the W-cycle.

papers.title: Fixed-Point Results and Disequilibrium for Negators of Hyperbolic-Valued Probability Distributions
papers.abstract: Hyperbolic-valued probability distributions provide a probabilistic setting in which mass, order, and uncertainty take values in the positive cone of the hyperbolic algebra. We study the fixed-point structure of hyperbolic probability negators and the behavior of hyperbolic-valued disequilibrium along their iterates. Starting from a hyperbolic-valued metric on each mass stratum, we define the associated disequilibrium as the separation between a distribution and the uniform distribution determined by its hyperbolic mass. We consider the disequilibria induced by the hyperbolic Euclidean, \(\ell_1\), and Jensen--Shannon metrics. Their hyperbolic Schur-convexity is established and sharp lower and upper bounds are obtained. We also characterize the possible fixed-point sets of hyperbolic negators through an order-theoretic condition and derive criteria ensuring uniqueness of the associated uniform distribution. The behavior of disequilibrium along the iterates of hyperbolic negators is then analyzed through two complementary mechanisms. Domination by Yager's negator yields exact decay factors for the Euclidean and \(\ell_1\) disequilibria and a uniform decay factor for the Jensen--Shannon disequilibrium. Independently, Lipschitz conditions for generated negators lead to positive linear comparison maps whose spectral radii control the asymptotic decay of disequilibrium. These results provide structural and quantitative conditions ensuring that hyperbolic-valued disequilibrium converges to zero under repeated probability negation.

papers.title: Positivity in symmetric webs and block permanents
papers.abstract: We use symmetric webs to prove Marcus's block-permanent inequality for up to four blocks of every size, for five blocks of size at least three, and for any fixed number of blocks above an explicit logarithmic bound on the block size. The proof idea is easy: Bending strands in the Schur relation turns the comparison into a calculation with squared norms.

papers.title: Exotic cluster structures on $Sp_{2n}$
papers.abstract: We modify the seeds of Berenstein, Fomin and Zelevinsky attached to reduced words for~$(w_0,w_0)$, for any simply connected simple complex algebraic group and any aperiodic Belavin--Drinfeld pair. In every type, moves of words act on the resulting seeds by mutations. After a change of coordinates introduced by Gekhtman, Shapiro and Vainshtein, the seeds are, for $SL_N$, seeds of the cluster structures of these authors, and for $Sp_{2n}$ they define regular complete cluster structures with the expected properties. This proves the aperiodic version of their conjecture for $Sp_{2n}$, with its uniqueness part in a refined form.

papers.title: Cantor correlations II. Synchronicity and bisynchronicity
papers.abstract: We study synchronous and bisynchronous no-signalling correlations, defined over Cantor topological spaces, from the perspectives of both continuous variable quantum information and operator algebra theories. We focus on strategies, satisfying a natural no-signalling condition across the Cantor space levels, called graded, identifying a universal C*-algebra, whose tracial states of different types characterise synchronous correlations of respective types. The universal C*-algebra for bisynchronous graded correlations is shown to coincide with the C*-algebra of a projective limit of free wreath products of quantum permutation groups, introduced by Bhowmick, Goswami and Skalski, and a type description, analogous to the one in the synchronous case, is provided. Extending results in the finite case, we show that bisynchronous graded correlations canonically give rise to factorisable maps on type I factors, defined via Cantor permutation matrices. We examine non-local games over Cantor topological spaces, with inputs/outputs that are finite words of equal length, define corresponding game algebras, and characterise the perfect strategies of the games via the respective game algebras. In the case of the Cantor graph isomorphism game, we provide equivalent descriptions of the existence of perfect strategies of quantum commuting type, in terms of bigalois correspondences, factorisable maps, Cantor permutation intertwiners and game algebra non-triviality. Our results supply a quantum information interpretation of a notion of a quantum isomorphism of locally finite graphs, introduced by Rollier and Vaes, canonically arising from Cantor graphs.

papers.title: Quantum Born Geometries from Modular Quantization
papers.abstract: A structural link between quantization and "thermal-doubled" non-commutative Born geometry (with its split-quaternionic structure) is uncovered via Tomita-Takesaki first-quantized modular theory for complexified and polarized ortho-symplectic spaces. Implications for the modular algebraic quantum gravity program (arXiv:1007.4094) hint at further deep modifications of the notions of space and geometry (thermal quantum space-time hypothesis) waiting to be further explored. Speculative suggestions in the direction of A.Sakharov and L.Boyle-K.Finn-N.Turok CPT-mirror cosmologies will be mentioned, among several others. The present work is based on the manuscript "Modular Quantization and Non-commutative Space-time" (now on alphaXiv) that has been shared, with a selected number of researchers, since end of April 2026.

papers.title: Radial nodal action ground states with two prescribed masses for coupled Schrodinger equations
papers.abstract: We study normalized nodal solutions of a cooperative system of nonlinear Schrödinger equations with two independently prescribed masses. For sufficiently small positive coupling, we obtain a radial nodal action ground state for every mass pair in a fixed compact subset of the positive quadrant. We first minimize the action on a radial nodal Nehari set at fixed frequencies. We then select both frequencies through an interior minimization of the action level. In this way, we adapt the scalar action approach of De Coster--Dovetta--Galant--Serra (\emph{Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Anal. Non Linéaire}, 2026) to construct solutions whose components both change sign and whose action is minimal among radial nodal solutions at the selected frequencies.

papers.title: Cubic graphs with circumference ratio 21/22 and cyclic connectivity 5
papers.abstract: We construct a cyclically $5$-connected cubic graph of order $22m$ and circumference $21m$ for every $m\geq 3$. Consequently, the shortness coefficient of the class of cyclically $5$-connected cubic graphs is at most $21/22$, improving the previously known upper bound of $24/25$. We also demonstrate how I-reductions, which delete an edge and suppress its two end-vertices, can be used to prove cyclic connectivity.

papers.title: Klarner's sequences have density $0$
papers.abstract: We prove that the set of non-negative integers $n$ which can be obtained from $0$ by repeated application of affine maps $x\mapsto 2x$, $x\mapsto 3x+2$ and $x\mapsto 6x+3$ has density $0$. Moreover, we reach the same conclusion for five other sequences of similar type introduced by D. Klarner. More generally, we establish a criterion excluding stationary measures with bounded density on the profinite group $\mathbb Z_P\cong\prod_{p\mid P}\mathbb Z_p$. A density-to-measure construction using invariant Banach limits and a combinatorial argument involving rational orbits and affine words yield our density-zero results. The criterion also applies to an infinite family of mixed-slope affine semigroups.

papers.title: FunSearch and Structured SAT Search for Weak Schur Partitions
papers.abstract: The weak Schur problem asks how large an interval of consecutive integers can be partitioned into a fixed number of classes with no class containing a monochromatic solution to $a+b=c$ with $a\neq b$. We investigate whether FunSearch, an evolutionary program-search method guided by a large language model, can discover effective construction strategies for this classical combinatorial problem. In our adaptation, FunSearch evolves a priority function used by a fixed greedy solver, while a separate validity check enforces the weakly sum-free condition. This approach matches the known exact values for two, three, and four classes and reaches $WS(5)\geq195$. We then explore a complementary SAT-based approach. Guided by structural information from a 207-element construction communicated by Fred Rowley (Rowley, 2026), our SAT search produces and verifies a distinct valid five-class partition of $\{1,\ldots,207\}$. Thus the strongest construction obtained in this project reaches $WS(5)\geq207$, eleven integers beyond the best published lower bound of 196. The contrast between the two approaches also exposes a limitation of our FunSearch formulation: its greedy solver makes local, irreversible decisions, whereas SAT can enforce global structure across the whole partition.

papers.title: An improved bound on the strong chromatic index via local flag algebras
papers.abstract: A strong edge coloring is an edge coloring where two edges receive different colors if they are incident or joined by a third edge. For a graph $G$, the strong chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $χ'_s(G)$, is the minimum number of colors needed for a strong edge coloring of $G$. In this paper, using a local flag algebra method, we prove that for every graph $G$ of sufficiently large maximum degree $Δ$, $χ'_s(G)\le 1.642Δ^2$, improving the previous best bound $1.73Δ^2$ due to Davey, Hurley, de Joannis de Verclos, Kang, and Volec.

papers.title: New necessary conditions on $h$-vectors of simplicial balls
papers.abstract: Although the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of dimension at most $4$ have been completely characterized, much less is known in dimensions $5$ and higher. We establish new necessary conditions on the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls in these dimensions. Together with the necessary conditions of Billera and Lee and the sufficient conditions of Kolins, our results yield a complete characterization of the $h$-vectors of $5$- and $6$-dimensional simplicial balls. We also give a characterization of $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of any dimension with neighborly boundary.

papers.title: Causal Input--Output Modeling with Prior Information
papers.abstract: We study the problem of inferring a causal input--output model from unpaired marginal observations and a given prior coupling. We formulate this problem using entropic causal optimal transport, which seeks a coupling that preserves the observed marginals, satisfies a one--sided causality constraint, and remains close to the prior. For Gaussian marginals and general quadratic costs, we prove that the optimal coupling is Gaussian and reduce the problem to a finite--dimensional optimization over covariance matrices. Using a Cholesky transformation to simplify the causality constraint, we derive a Lagrangian dual formulation and develop a block coordinate descent algorithm with explicit update formulas. We establish linear convergence of the algorithm, with explicit convergence rates, and prove stability of the optimal coupling under marginal covariance perturbations and derive a statistical error bound. We further show its equivalence to Sinkhorn iterations. Numerical experiments demonstrate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and illustrate the predictive advantages of causal couplings.

papers.title: Single-Vertex Metropolis on Minor-Free Graphs: A General EPTAS
papers.abstract: We consider a class of combinatorial optimization problems where the goal is to find a largest induced subgraph with a prescribed property. We assume that the property is preserved by taking induced subgraphs and disjoint unions, holds for all edgeless graphs, and can be tested in polynomial time. We study the single-vertex Metropolis process for this class of problems. We show that on graphs excluding an arbitrary fixed minor $H$, this process is a randomized efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme. Starting from any feasible solution on a graph with $n$ vertices, it finds a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation within $\exp(O_H(\varepsilon^{-2})) n(n+\log(1/δ))$ steps with probability at least $1-δ$. This includes maximum independent set, maximum induced forest, maximum induced bipartite subgraph, and maximum induced subgraph of degree at most one. The proof uses improving exchanges on one fixed division of the input graph into regions. A recursive separator construction performs each exchange inside a region of size $r$ in at most $2r$ moves, with temporary loss $O_H(\sqrt r)$. We count move sequences through each transition and bound the probability of avoiding all near-optimal states. The general theorem bounds the number of Metropolis steps in terms of the temporary loss along improvement paths. We extend the result to bounded weight imbalance and give a weighted-star obstruction for unrestricted weights.

papers.title: A mechanistic characterization of missingness at random
papers.abstract: The missingness-at-random (MAR) assumption underlying many missing-data methods describes abstract statistical independences, whereas practitioners reason more naturally about the causal mechanisms that generate missingness. To bridge this gap, we provide a mechanistic characterization of MAR in terms of paths in a directed acyclic graph (DAG) modified to allow certain edges to cease to operate when an incomplete variable is missing, a property termed "context-specific causal irrelevance (CSCI)". Under a faithfulness condition, MAR holds if and only if the modified DAG contains no MAR-violating paths. Without CSCI, this condition reduces to a previously established d-separation condition, VMAR; thus, MAR without VMAR requires specific kinds of CSCI, as can occur with monotone dropout. These results shift the burden on investigators from passively invoking MAR to justifying, on substantive grounds, the specific mechanisms it requires. We then consider identification of a target law p(v) of variables V by a MAR-assuming analysis, e.g., multiple imputation, that includes complete auxiliary variables Z (variables not in V). Barring a perfect cancellation, such an analysis recovers p(v) if and only if MAR holds with respect to V and Z jointly. We show that if there exists any set of auxiliaries such that (V, Z) obeys MAR, then the complete candidate auxiliaries that are ancestors of the target variables or their missingness indicators form a sufficient set. Contrary to standard recommendations, not all candidate auxiliaries should be used: even complete auxiliaries can introduce MAR violations that would not otherwise occur. We illustrate these results with simulations and an analysis of sexual identity change in the Stockholm Public Health Cohort, where our results indicate that a candidate auxiliary, income, should be excluded; including it attenuated estimates toward the null.

papers.title: Perfect matching complexes of antiprism graphs and independence complexes of generalized Petersen graphs $GP(n,2)$
papers.abstract: We show that the perfect matching complexes of antiprism graphs and the independence complexes of the generalized Petersen graphs $GP(n, 2)$ are homotopy equivalent to wedges of spheres, and we determine the number and dimensions of the spheres. For the former we compute the initial values of Adamaszek's recursion for the independence complexes of cubes of cycles.

papers.title: Structural functional identifiability of unknown differential equation observation maps
papers.abstract: In many differential equation models of real-world systems, the mechanistic structure of the dynamics is known, but the map from the dynamics to the observations is not. This is potentially problematic, as it can prevent us from e.g. learning model parameter values from data. Examples where this occurs include measuring a fluorescent marker as a proxy for the dynamics of a cellular circuit, and using wastewater measurements to follow the development of an epidemic. The nascent field of hybrid modelling, in which machine learning components (like neural networks) are embedded within mechanistic models, provides the tools to learn such maps. Here, the system's dynamics keep their mechanistic form, while a neural network represents the unknown observation map and is trained alongside any unknown core system parameters. This raises a question of identifiability: when can the true observation map be learnt, and when does one simply learn some map that transforms the dynamics into the available data? Building on previous work, we show how structural functional identifiability analysis can establish whether a model's unknown observation maps and core system parameters are identifiable, i.e. can be uniquely learnt from data. We both prove general results on when models with unknown observation maps are, and are not, identifiable, and demonstrate a general methodology (based on differential algebra) for assessing the identifiability of such models. This paves the way for applying classic differential equation workflows to the many real-world systems that contain such unknown maps.

papers.title: On $U(1)^{2}$-Invariant Cayley $4$-Folds in $\mathbb{R}^{8}$
papers.abstract: We study $ \mathrm{U}(1)^{2} $-invariant Cayley submanifolds in $ \mathbb{R}^{8} $, under the action with weights $ (e^{i θ_{1}}, e^{i θ_{2}}, e^{-i(θ_{1} + θ_{2})}, 1) $ on coordinates $ (z_{1}, z_{2}, z_{3}, z_{4}) \in \mathbb{C}^{4} $. Locally, we can prove that $ N $ can be written as a graph of functions $ u, v, a_{1}, a_{2}: \mathbb{R}^{2} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ (where $ a_{3}= -a_{1}-a_{2} $), where unlike in the special Lagrangian setting, the moment-map parameters are not required to be constant, which gives rise to additional degrees of freedom in the reduced equations. We prove that $ N $ is Cayley if and only if a non-linear, Cauchy-Riemann system of partial differential equations in $ u, v, a_{1}, a_{2} $ holds, with ellipticity away from its degeneracy locus. We investigate the special Lagrangian and coassociative reductions of the system, obtaining potential functions in both cases. For general $ \mathrm{U}(1)^{2} $-invariant Cayley $ 4 $-folds, we derive almost-conservation laws (with clear obstruction terms) involving natural $ S_{3} $-invariant and alternating combinations of the moment-map parameters. These identities exhibit additional source terms, distinguishing the general Cayley system from its special Lagrangian and coassociative reductions.

papers.title: Deformation Quantization of Coisotropic A-branes
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Gukov--Witten proposal that the endomorphism algebra of a coisotropic A-brane should be described by a deformation quantization of its transverse holomorphic symplectic geometry at the perturbative level, we study deformation quantization on transverse holomorphic symplectic manifolds $(M,Ω)$. Extending the approach of Nest--Tsygan to this setting, we show that, under an admissibility condition, equivalence classes of deformation quantizations are in bijection with \[ \hbar H^2\bigl(\operatorname{F}_1Ω^\bullet(M,\mathbb C),d\bigr) [[\hbar]], \] where $\operatorname{F}_1Ω^\bullet(M,\mathbb C)$ is the differential ideal generated by transverse $(1,0)$-forms. We further illustrate this framework through examples arising from mapping tori, $T$-duality, and coisotropic lifts in cotangent bundles. These examples clarify the roles of admissibility and the transverse Atiyah class, as well as the distinction between deformation quantizations and global star products. Finally, for a coisotropic A-brane $M$ induced from a transverse complex manifold $Q$, we use transverse jets and the Fock representation to construct a perturbative level action $End(M)\curvearrowright Hom(M,Q)$ under suitable compatibility assumptions, providing a geometric realization of the brane quantization philosophy.

papers.title: Characterizing nonlocal Sobolev spaces as generalized Bessel potential spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal Sobolev spaces $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $p \in (1,\infty)$, defined via a general class of nonlocal gradients $D^ρ$ associated with a kernel function $ρ$. As our main contribution, we establish three new equivalent characterizations of these spaces. First, we describe $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ in terms of Fourier multipliers involving the symbol of the nonlocal potential associated with $D^ρ$. Second, we give a thorough functional analytic treatment of the nonlocal $ρ$-Laplacian $Δ^ρ$, which allows us to represent general nonlocal Sobolev spaces through its square root $(-Δ^ρ)^{1/2}$. Third, we show that $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ coincides with the image $g_ρ* L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for a suitable convolution kernel $g_ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, which confirms that these spaces are genuine potential spaces. These results generalize the well-known fact that, in the special case of the Riesz kernel, the resulting fractional Sobolev spaces coincide with the classical Bessel potential spaces. In this spirit, the present work can also be viewed as introducing a natural notion of generalized Bessel potential spaces.

papers.title: Decorated lattices: hyperuniformity and limit theorems
papers.abstract: We introduce \emph{decorated lattices}, a point process obtained by placing finite random point configurations in lattice cells. A stationary mark field selects the motif laws and acts as a random environment transmitting dependence between cells, while allowing flexible local arrangements. Using this construction, one can efficiently generate large regions of disordered patterns with desired local behavior while the random environment controls the asymptotic density fluctuations. Under moment and summability assumptions, we derive an explicit decomposition of the Bartlett spectral measure into contributions from conditional motif fluctuations and correlations between marks. This yields criteria for hyperuniformity, or generally $p$-uniformity. Independent, nondegenerate count fluctuations destroy hyperuniformity, whereas suitable dependence governed by the random environment can restore it despite random and unequal cell counts. Once count fluctuations are sufficiently suppressed, motif geometry and its spatial correlations govern the finer order of uniformity. Under mixing assumptions, we also establish central limit theorems for linear statistics, with fluctuations governed by cell counts or, at a finer scale, by the first spatial moments of the motifs.

papers.title: Discontinuity-Aware Solvers for Vapor-Compression Cycles
papers.abstract: Physics-based models of vapor-compression cycles are often formulated as large, stiff DAE systems with derivative discontinuities introduced at the points of phase change. We use an implementation of a discontinuity-aware ODE and DAE solver scheme that uses domain-specific, user-declared information to compute appropriate time steps for more efficient integration. This scheme is made open-source within Julia's DifferentialEquations package. We demonstrate how discontinuity information can be specified symbolically in a declarative modeling language such as Dyad and passed to the solver to address the numerical challenges posed. We apply this discontinuity-aware technique to two applications: first, a scalar ODE with two discontinuities, and then a model of a full vapor-compression cycle. The discontinuity-aware solver yields significantly fewer step rejections and improved solver times, particularly with the Rodas5P solver at loose tolerances, as compared to standard error control, suggesting that exposing physical discontinuity information from equation-oriented models to adaptive solvers can improve practical simulation performance without requiring reassembly of the model.

papers.title: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
papers.abstract: We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4πm,4π(m+1))\times(4πk,4π(k+1))$, then \[ \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k =(1-x)^{χ(M)-1}(1-y)^{χ(M)-1}(1-xy)^{χ(M)}, \] where $χ(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block. At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4π,0)$ and $(8π,4π)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.

papers.title: Subwavelength resonances and localization in finite resonator chains with a size defect
papers.abstract: We study subwavelength resonances of a finite chain of $N\ge2$ close-to-touching spherical resonators in three dimensions with a single radius defect of relative size $τ\in(0,1]$ and gap width $\varepsilon$. Taking the high-contrast limit before the narrow-gap limit, we prove that the positive generalized eigenvalues of the weighted chain coupling matrix with respect to the volume matrix determine the leading relative resonant frequencies. After eliminating the finite tails, we obtain an exact characteristic determinant and identify a unique critical ratio $τ_*\in(0,1)$ at which the largest eigenvalue crosses the upper edge of the homogeneous recurrence band $[0,4]$. For every $0<τ<τ_*$, exactly one eigenvalue lies above this band, and its eigenvector decays geometrically along the tails. As $τ\toτ_*^-$, its recurrence decay length diverges like $(τ_*-τ)^{-1/2}$. As $τ\to0$, exactly one eigenvalue diverges like $τ^{-2}$ and its eigenvector concentrates at the defect; if the defect is interior, one additional positive eigenvalue has order $τ$. For suitably normalized relative resonant modes, the sequential limit of the $\varepsilon$-scaled gradient supremum in each gap equals the absolute difference between adjacent reduced amplitudes. For the largest-eigenvalue mode, this yields defect-adjacent gradient concentration as the defect shrinks.

papers.title: Asymptotic Order of the Minimum Number of Graph-Saturating Edges I
papers.abstract: Given an $H$-free graph $G$, a non-edge $e$ of $G$ is called $H$-saturating if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. The function $f_H(n,m)$ denotes the minimum number of $H$-saturating non-edges over all $n$-vertex $H$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges. In this paper, we fully characterize the asymptotic order of $f_H(n,\operatorname{ex}(n,R)+1)$ for any fixed graph $H$ with $χ(H)\ge χ(R)$, where $R$ is any fixed edge-critical graph, and resolve the conjecture proposed by He et al. (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 159 (2023), 42-60).

papers.title: Maximality of the Došen-Petrić Boolean Category
papers.abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Došen and Petrić, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Every congruence preserved by the operations on morphisms and by uniform formula substitution either is equality or identifies every pair of parallel morphisms. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. We give two proofs that use Boolean Coherence and uniform formula substitution to derive equality of the product projections from an identification of distinct parallel morphisms. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.

papers.title: Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$. More precisely, \[ \mathscr L(L(0,a))=\mathscr L(L(0,1)) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=1, \] while \[ L(0,a)\prec L(0,1) \qquad (a\geq3). \] For $a=0$ and $a=2$, the two spectra are incomparable. The main new containment is \[ L(0,2n)\preceq L(0,1)\qquad(n\geq2), \] which goes beyond the classical parity-preserving nesting relations. A key ingredient is a braid-theoretic criterion: every $T$-link \[ T((r_1,s_1),\ldots,(r_k,s_k)) \] with $s_k\geq2r_k$ is a horseshoe link. This gives a large explicit family belonging to both the Lorenz and horseshoe spectra. In the reverse direction, we construct a horseshoe link which is not Lorenz, thereby disproving the Birman--Kofman conjecture that every horseshoe link is a Lorenz link. For each integer $m\geq6$, we obtain infinitely many horseshoe links of braid index $m$ excluded from every other nonnegative $L(0,a)$. These examples give infinitely many links with any prescribed number of components at least three. In the other direction, for each positive number of components, we give infinitely many links carried by both $L(0,0)$ and $L(0,2)$ and excluded from the horseshoe spectrum.

papers.title: On complemented skew braces
